So, they apply for a mortgage loan (i.e., to borrow money from a bank so that they can buy the flat) and will repay the money plus interest later. Explain why John and Ling need to pay interest to borrow money.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	As John and Ling prefer earlier consumption (to buy a flat even though they do not have enough money now), they need to borrow money for the purchase. 		(1 mark)
•	On the other hand, they have to compensate the lender (e.g., bank) with interest whom sacrifices present consumption and lends them money. 	(2 marks)
•	So, they repay the principal plus interest in the future; the interest is the compensation for deferring consumption of goods.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
'Buying a High-definition television (HDTV) now or later makes no difference if its price remains unchanged.'
Do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer. 	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	No. Goods with the same physical characteristics are not really the same if they are available for consumption at different times. 	(2 marks)
•	As we prefer having goods earlier to later, the option of consuming goods earlier is in itself an economic good.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text: * Some people borrow money from loan sharks (高利貸) while others lend money to people. How would you explain this phenomenon? 	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Different people may have different preferences towards present consumption and future consumption. 	(1 mark)
•	Some people have a stronger preference towards present consumption. They are willing to pay more to buy goods and services by borrowing from loan sharks.		(2 marks)
•	Some people are more willing to postpone their consumption and offer loans in return for interest in order to enjoy a greater future consumption.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Study the conversation below.
'Public library services are a free good as they are provided free of charge,' John said.
'The services are an economic good. The government should not provide them free of charge,' Mary said.
(a)	Identify the positive statement(s) and the normative statement(s) in the above conversation.	(3 marks)
(b)	Explain whether John is correct.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	John's statement is a positive statement.	(1 mark)
	Mary's first statement is a positive statement while her second statement is a normative statement.	(2 marks)
(b)	John is not correct. Public library services are an economic good as more are preferred / it involves costs to provide the services.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Stephy: 'I am too heavy.'
Janice: 'I am heavier than you.'
Which of the above statements is positive? Which of them is normative? Explain your answer. 	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Stephy's statement is normative. It involves value judgment (too heavy) and disagreements cannot be settled by appealing to facts.	(2 marks)
•	Janice's statement is positive. It does not involve value judgment and disagreements can be settled by appealing to facts (weight can be measured and compared).	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Identify whether the following is a positive statement or normative statement.
(a)	In a market economy, people follow government plans and commands in production and consumption.	(1 mark)
(b)	For specialisation to occur, exchange must take place.	(1 mark)
(c)	The government should impose a maximum working hours law.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Positive statement	(1 mark)
(b)	Positive statement	 (1 mark)
(c)	Normative statement 	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
(a)	What are positive statements?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether each of the following is a positive statement.
(i)	The government should enhance the protection of intellectual property rights to maintain Hong Kong's competitiveness.	(2 marks)
(ii)	If the government gives a low-income allowance to the poor, income distribution will be more even.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Positive statements are statements about facts. They do not involve any value judgements. We can test them by checking facts.	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	No. It is a normative statement.	(1 mark)
		It involves a value judgement about what the government 'should' do.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Yes. It is a positive statement.	(1 mark)
		It is about facts. Whether the income distribution will be more even after introducing a low-income allowance can be tested by checking facts.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text: 'Since positive statements are about facts, positive statements must be true.' Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	No. Positive statements can be false.	(1 mark)
•	It is true that positive statements are statements about facts. However, if we find that these statements are inconsistent with facts, we can refute them.	(2 marks)



Structured Questions

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
In September 2014, Apple launched its new iPhone 6. Wherever iPhone 6 was sold,  there were long queues for it. Just as in Australia, more than 1,000 people lined up outside Apple's flagship store in Sydney to wait to buy it. People who did not want to wait in line could hire professional line sitters to wait. In New York, the hourly rates of a professional line sitter can be as high as US$25 (equal to HK$195). Some entrepreneurs have even set up companies to provide waiting services.
(a)	Everyone can wait in line free of charge. Why do people hire line sitters to wait in line? Explain.	(3 marks)
(b)	What is an economic good? With reference to the above information, explain why iPhone 6 is an economic good.	 (4 marks)
(c)	The official price of iPhone 6 (16GB) is $5,688 and its resale price is $10,000. Explain whether the following situations will affect the cost of owning an 
iPhone 6 (16GB).
	(i)	The resale price of iPhone 6 (16GB) rises to $12,000.	(2 marks)
(ii)	All telecommunication service providers raise their monthly service fees.
					(2 marks)
(d)	Explain whether the following statements are positive or normative.
	(i)	The government should prohibit line sitting as this will push up the prices of goods.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	'First-come, first-served' is the fairest criterion for distributing goods.
					(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Some people may have a higher time cost than others.	(1 mark)
	To save on their time cost, they may hire people to wait for them so they don't have to wait in line.	(2 marks)

(b)	An economic good is a good whose quantity available is insufficient to satisfy all people's wants.	(2 marks)
	iPhone 6 is an economic good because people are willing to spend time and money to obtain it / more is preferred to less.	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	The cost of owning an iPhone 6 is its resale price.	(1 mark)
		Thus, the cost of owning an iPhone 6 rises from $10,000 to $12,000.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	This will only affect the cost of using an iPhone 6.	(1 mark)
		The cost of owning an iPhone 6 (the resale value) remains unchanged.	(1 mark)

(d)	(i)	Normative statement	(1 mark)
		Whether the government should prohibit line sitting involves a value judgement.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Normative statement	(1 mark)
		Whether a criterion is fair or not involves a value judgement.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Mark and Janice decide to go to a Friday night concert. Mark has spent $3,000 to buy two concert tickets. On the day of the concert, a typhoon strikes. Although the weather is extremely bad, the concert is held as scheduled. The following phone conversation takes place between Mark and Janice.
'Oh, no! The weather is very bad! I want to stay at home,' Janice said.
'Since I have spent $3,000 for the two tickets, we should go to the concert,' Mark said.
(a)	What is opportunity cost? Do you think Mark is correct? Explain with the concept of opportunity cost.	(4 marks)
(b)	Under the following situations, explain whether the ticket price should be included in Janice's cost of going to the concert.
(i)	Janice does not need to give back to Mark the money he spent to buy the ticket, whether she goes to the concert or not.	(3 marks)
*(ii)	If Janice decides not to go to the concert, she needs to give back to Mark the money he spent to buy the ticket. She does not have to pay if she goes to the concert with Mark.	(3 marks)
(c)	In the end, Mark and Janice go to the concert. Explain whether the following events will affect their cost of going to the concert.
	(i)	Due to the bad weather, they need to spend additional hour to get  to the concert.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	The concert ends one hour earlier.	(2 marks)
(d)	Determine whether the following statements are positive or normative.
	(i)	The concert is entertaining.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Due to the typhoon, fewer people attend the concert.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone.	(2 marks)
	Mark is incorrect. The $3,000 is an irrecoverable past expenditure and should not be considered when deciding whether to go to the concert. 	(2 marks)

(b)	(i)	Not included. In this case, the money Mark spent on the tickets does not affect her value of staying at home (her highest-valued option forgone).	(3 marks)
	(ii)	Included. The cost of going to the concert is the value of not going to the concert. In this case, the value of not going to the concert will decrease as she needs to pay back to Mark the money he spent if she does not go to the concert.
	(3 marks)

(c)	(i)	The cost will increase as they spend more resources (time) to go to the concert.		(2 marks)
	(ii)	The cost will decrease as they spend less time at the concert.	(2 marks)

(d)	(i)	Normative statement	(1 mark)
		Whether the concert is entertaining involves a value judgement.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Positive statement	(1 mark)
The statement is about facts and is refutable. It can be tested by checking the facts.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
The government plans to extend the railway network. Under a development plan for 2018-2026, seven railway projects will be undertaken. The total cost of the railway plan is about HK$110 billion. Most people are in favour of this plan. However, some think that the cost is too high and the government should spend its money on other areas like education and public health.
Suppose the government has the following policy priorities:
1st choice	Transportation	
2nd choice	Education	
3rd choice	Public health	

(a)	Given the following events, explain whether the opportunity cost of extending the railway network will necessarily remain unchanged.
(i)	It is expected that greenhouse gas emissions will fall by 4% a year when the new lines are completed.	(2 marks)
(ii)	It is expected that there will be a shortage of construction workers and the construction period will have to be extended.	(3 marks)
*(iii)	The chance of an Ebola (伊波拉病毒) outbreak in Hong Kong increases.
		(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose the government decides to provide the railway service to the public free-of-charge. Explain whether the free railway service provided by the government is a free good.	(3 marks)
(c)	Explain whether the following activities are production or consumption.
(i)	Samuel, a courier, takes the train to deliver business letters to other companies.		(2 marks)
	(ii)	Morris takes the train to go on a picnic with his girlfriend.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Yes. It will only affect the value of extending the railway network and the value of the highest-valued option forgone remains unchanged.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	No, it will increase the opportunity cost. The shortage of construction workers will increase the wages of construction workers. The money cost may increase. The extension of the construction period will increase both the expenditure on the construction and the time cost.	 (3 marks)
	(iii)	No, as the value of the third choice (public health) increases, it is possible that the value of the third choice will become higher than that of the second choice. The cost of extending the railway network may change from the value of spending the money on education to the value of spending it on public health. 
				(3 marks)

(b)	Not a free good.	(1 mark)
	More is preferred to less. / Providing the services involves a cost.	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	Production as	(1 mark)
		Samuel provides courier services.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Consumption as	(1 mark)
		this satisfies Morris's desire to go on a picnic with his girlfriend.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Mr Chan is a taxi driver who owns his taxi. 
(a)	Define opportunity cost. What is Mr Chan's cost of driving his own taxi?	(4 marks)
(b)	Give an example where Mr Chan's opportunity cost of driving his own taxi increases. Explain your answer.	(2 marks)
(c)	If Mr Chan is frequently robbed when driving his taxi at night, does this increase his cost of driving his own taxi? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.					(2 marks)
	•	Mr Chan's cost of driving his own taxi is the income that can otherwise be obtained if he does not choose to drive his own taxi.	(2 marks)

(b)	Any correct example with explanation.	(2 marks)
Example: If the income from renting out the taxi increases, the cost to Mr Chan of driving his own taxi will increase as his forgone income increases.

(c)	•	No, this will only affect the value of driving his own taxi.	(1 mark)
	•	But the value of his highest-valued option forgone is not affected.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Mr Chan is a fisherman. He owns his fishing boat.
(a)	Define opportunity cost. What is Mr Chan's cost of renting out his fishing boat?
				(4 marks)
(b)	Explain how Mr Chan's cost of renting out his fishing boat will change during fishing moratoria (休漁期).	(2 marks)
(c)	Suppose his fish catch decreases tremendously due to pollution. Explain how this will affect Mr Chan's cost of renting out his fishing boat.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.		(2 marks)
	•	Mr Chan's cost of renting out his fishing boat is giving up the fish catch he could have had using his own fishing boat.	(2 marks)

(b)	During fishing moratoria, Mr Chan's cost of renting out his fishing boat decreases. This is because the catch of fish he could have had using his own fishing boat decreases.	(2 marks)

(c)	Mr Chan's cost of renting out his fishing boat decreases because the catch of fish he could have had using his own fishing boat falls due to pollution.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Joe is searching for a job. He has three options from which to choose: being a teacher, a management trainee or a sales executive. Suppose the monthly incomes of the three jobs are the same. Joe's preferences for the jobs are as follows:

1st choice: Teacher
2nd choice: Management trainee
3rd choice: Sales executive	

Finally, Joe chooses to be a teacher.
(a)	(i)	Define opportunity cost.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	What is his cost of choosing to be a teacher? Explain.	(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose later Joe finds out the workload of a teacher is very heavy. Will this change his cost of choosing to be a teacher? Explain.	(3 marks)
(c)	At the beginning of a school year, Joe receives free textbooks from local publishers.
	(i)	Define free goods.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Are these books free goods? Explain.	(3 marks)
(d)	Classify the following items into consumption and production. Explain your answer.
	(i)	Joe prepares notes for students at home; and	(3 marks)
	(ii)	Joe takes his class to a country park at Tai Po for a school picnic.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.					(2 marks)
	(ii)	His cost of choosing to be a teacher is the forgone option of being a management trainee. 	(3 marks)

(b)	No, this will only lower the value of being a teacher. Since the value of the highest-valued option forgone, that is, the option of being a management trainee, remains unchanged, the cost remains unchanged.	(3 marks)

(c)	(i)	Free goods are goods whose available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all our wants (Or: more of them are not preferred).	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	No, they are not free goods. Reasons:	(1 mark)
		•	People want more free textbooks. / There is a cost involved in the production of those free textbooks.	 (2 marks)

(d)	(i)	•	It is production.	(1 mark)
		•	Because he uses his labour, computer and printer to produce notes for his class.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	It is production.	(1 mark)
		•	Because Joe provides educational services.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Ming is choosing pets. He can choose one of the following: a dog, a cat and a snake. Suppose the prices of the three pets are the same. Ming's preferences for the pets are as follows:

1st choice: Snake
2nd choice: Cat
3rd choice: Dog	

(a)	(i)	Define opportunity cost.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	What is Ming's cost of choosing a snake?	(1 mark)
(b)	Suppose Ming later finds out that the snake is poisonous. Explain whether this will affect his cost of choosing a snake.	(3 marks)
(c)	Ming's uncle gave him a cat and a dog this summer vacation.
	(i)	Define scarcity.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	'Ming does not have to face scarcity anymore as his wants for a cat and a dog are satisfied.'
		Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
(d)	Classify the following items into consumption and production. Explain your answer.
	(i)	Ming trains his pets to perform on a TV show.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	Ming sleeps with his pets at home.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.					(2 marks)
	(ii)	His cost of choosing a snake is giving up a cat.	(1 mark)

(b)	No, this will only affect the value of choosing a snake. Since the value of the highest-valued option forgone, that is, a cat, remains unchanged, the cost remains unchanged.	(3 marks)

(c)	(i)	Scarcity means we want more than we have. When our resources are insufficient to produce goods and services to satisfy our unlimited wants, scarcity exists.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Ming still has to face scarcity, because he will have new wants when his wants for pets are satisfied.	(3 marks)

(d)	(i)	•	It is production.	(1 mark)
		•	Because he uses his labour to train his pets.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	It is consumption.	(1 mark)
		•	Because he enjoys sleeping with his pets.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Alan has recently won a $3 million lottery prize. His order of preference in spending the money is as follows:

I	Buying an apartment in Ma On Shan
II	Starting a business
III	Buying stocks and bonds	

(a)	What is opportunity cost? What is his opportunity cost of buying an apartment in Ma On Shan?	 (4 marks)
(b)	Suppose Alan later finds commuting to and from Ma On Shan inconvenient. Will this affect his cost of buying the apartment? Explain your answer.	(2 marks)
(c)	Suppose the estate in which Alan lives provides free shuttle bus service from Ma On Shan to Diamond Hill MTR station.
	(i)	Define free goods.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Is the bus service a free good? Explain your answer.	(3 marks)
(d)	Soon after Alan purchases the apartment, Ma On Shan Rail commences services. This has caused an increase in property prices and rent in Ma On Shan. Will this affect (i) Alan's cost of buying the apartment and (ii) his cost of living in his own apartment? Explain your answer.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.					(2 marks)
	•	His cost of buying the apartment is the option of starting a business.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	No.	(1 mark)
	•	Since the value of the highest-valued option forgone, that is, the value of starting a business, remains unchanged, the cost of buying the apartment remains unchanged.	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	Free goods are goods whose available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all our 
wants (Or: more of them are not preferred). 	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	It is not a free good.	(1 mark)
		•	Because costs are involved in providing them / we want more bus services.				(2 marks)

(d)	(i)	•	After he has purchased the apartment, he has already spent the $3 million.
				(1 mark)
		•	The increase in property prices in Ma On Shan will not affect the amount spent on buying the apartment. Thus, the cost of buying the apartment will not change.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	The cost of living in his own apartment increases as the forgone income from renting out his apartment increases.	(2 marks)
		(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
A university has recently received a $1,000,000 donation from a rich person. Its order of preference for spending the money is as follows:

I	Building a new residence hall
II	Hiring Professor Chan, a famous scholar
III	Setting up a scholarship	

(a)	What is opportunity cost? What is the opportunity cost of building a new residence hall?	(4 marks)
(b)	Suppose the university later finds out that the occupancy rate of the new residence hall is very low. Explain whether this will affect the cost of building the new residence hall.	(2 marks)
(c)	Suppose the university provides free residence service to all graduate students (研究生).
	(i)	Define free goods.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Is the free residence service a free good? Explain your answer.	(3 marks)
(d)	Suppose Professor Chan announces that he is not going to accept the offer due to the university's poor academic standard. Explain whether this will affect the cost of building the new residence hall.	 (4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.					(2 marks)
	•	Its cost of building a new residence hall is the option of hiring Professor Chan.					(2 marks)

(b)	•	No, this will only affect the value of the chosen option.	(1 mark)
	•	Since the value of the highest-valued option forgone, that is, the value of hiring Professor Chan, remains unchanged, the cost remains unchanged.			(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	Free goods are goods whose available quantities are sufficient to satisfy all our wants (Or: more of them are not preferred).	(2 marks)
	(ii)	It is not a free good.	(1 mark)
		Reasons:
		•	Providing the residence hall involves cost.
		•	More residence halls are preferred.
		(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answer. 2 marks)

(d)	Since the option of hiring Professor Chan is no longer available, the cost of building a new residence hall becomes the option of setting up a scholarship. Since the value of setting up a scholarship is lower than that of hiring Professor Chan, the cost of building a new residence hall decreases.	(4 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
James owns a factory which suffered a great loss last year. Recently, he borrowed $100,000 from a bank. James's order of preference of using the money is shown below:

First preference: Purchasing advanced equipment
Second preference: Paying workers' wages
Third preference: Investing in stocks	

(a)	Define opportunity cost.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose the government forbids investing the money borrowed from banks in stocks. Explain whether James's cost of choosing to pay the workers' wages would change.	(2 marks)
(c)	James's friend, Lily says, 'James should not borrow from the bank as he needs to pay interest to borrow money from the bank, which will worsen the financial position of the factory.' Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
(d)	After learning that James's factory suffered a great loss last year, the bank raises the interest rate on the $100,000 they lend to James. How will this affect production costs at James's factory?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.			(2 marks)

(b)	•	In this case, when James chooses to pay the workers' wages, the opportunity cost is purchasing advanced equipment.	(1 mark)
	•	In other words, whether the third preference (i.e., investing in stock) is available or not, the cost remains unchanged. 	(1 mark)

(c)	•	It depends. 
	•	To a borrower, interest is the cost of earlier availability of goods or resources.	(1 mark)
	•	If James finds that the benefit of borrowing money (e.g., he can increase his profit by purchasing more advanced machines for production) is greater than the cost of borrowing (e.g., the interest payment), he should borrow money from the bank.	(2 marks)

(d)	•	As the interest rate increases, the cost of obtaining capital increases.	(1 mark)
	•	Therefore, the production cost at James's factory increases.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Alan has been a tutor at a tutorial centre for many years. He is considering quitting his job and starting his own business. However, he is still deciding whether he should start his own tutorial centre or a restaurant.
(a)	Define opportunity cost.	(2 marks)
(b)	Besides the salary forgone, does Alan's resignation incur any other cost? Explain briefly with the concept of full cost.	(3 marks)
Finally, Alan starts his own tutorial centre and runs his business in an office leased from a relative free of charge.
(c) Alan says, 'The government should subsidise people like me who start their business for the first time.'
	Is the statement above a normative or positive statement? Explain.	(2 marks)
(d)	'The office provided by Alan's relative is a free good to Alan.' Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone in making a choice.			(2 marks)

(b)	Yes, the full cost of quitting his job includes the salary forgone and non-monetary returns such as the job satisfaction from being a tutor. (Accept any other reasonable answers.)	(3 marks)

(c)	•	Normative statement	(1 mark)
	•	This is because his statement involves a value judgement, i.e., 'the government should'.	(1 mark)

(d)	•	Disagree.	(1 mark)
	•	More office space is preferred. / The office has alternative uses.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Mandy recently participated in a promotional event on Facebook and was awarded a free, one-day Disneyland ticket, which costs $450. Suppose the ticket is transferable and the resale price on the internet is $182.
(a)	Mandy says, 'Although the ticket is free-of-charge, it is NOT a free good.' Is she correct? Explain.	(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose Peter, Mandy's friend, offers to buy Mandy's ticket for $200. How will this affect Mandy's cost of using the ticket?	(3 marks)
(c)	This morning, Disney announced that the promotional event on Facebook was unauthorised (未獲授權) and that the free tickets given out are therefore invalid (無效的).
	(i)	Explain how Mandy's cost of visiting Disneyland will change.	(5 marks)
	(ii)	Mandy is interviewed by a news reporter and asked to describe the course of events. Does this belong to consumption or production? Explain.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Yes, the free ticket is not a free good because:	(1 mark)
	•	The available quantity of free tickets is insufficient to satisfy all human wants for them. 
	•	We prefer to have more of the free tickets. 
	•	People are willing to pay a cost to obtain the free tickets. For example, some people spend time taking part in the Facebook event, and some offer to buy the tickets.
	(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answers. 2 marks)

(b)	•	The cost will increase.	(1 mark)
	•	Since the free ticket is transferable, Mandy's cost of using the ticket is the income from reselling the ticket.	(1 mark)
	•	As Peter is willing to buy the ticket for a price higher than that on the internet, Mandy has to give up more money if she uses the ticket.	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	•	The cost will increase.	(1 mark)
		•	Originally, Mandy could use the free ticket and thus her cost of visiting Disneyland would be the resale price of the ticket (i.e., $182), plus her time cost.	(2 marks)
		•	However, since the free ticket became invalid, she must pay $450 to visit Disneyland. Hence, her cost of visiting Disneyland would be the ticket price, plus her time cost, which is greater than before.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	Production.	(1 mark) 
		•	This is because the interview helps transform her story and personal feelings (inputs) into news reports (outputs).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch101 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Last year, Paul purchased a tablet computer and paid for it on a 12-month interest-free instalment (免息分期付款) plan. The value of the tablet was $3,888. Without the instalment plan, Paul would have had to wait one year to save enough money to buy the tablet.
*(a)	Paul said, 'As I bought the tablet and paid in interest-free installments, it involved a zero interest cost.' Do you agree? Explain.	(5 marks)
(b)	Paul has installed many apps on his tablet. Some are available free-of-charge. Are these free apps free goods? Explain.	(3 marks)
(c)	Explain whether each of the following activities belongs to consumption or production.
	(i)	Paul watches YouTube videos on his tablet for leisure.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Paul makes a presentation to his client with the tablet.	(2 marks)
(d)	How will each of the following events affect his cost of using the tablet?
	(i)	An interesting app is available for free download.	(3 marks)

	*(ii)	The tablet is infected with a virus and Paul has to pay $1,500 to have it fixed before he can use or resell it.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Disagree.	(1 mark)
	•	Interest is the compensation for deferring consumption of goods. If Paul can save money and purchase the tablet one year from now, he can earn interest from his savings.	(2 marks)
	•	Hence, when Paul chose to buy the tablet one year earlier by paying in instalments, he gave up the interest income, which can be considered as his interest cost.	(2 marks)
(Merely mentioning the definition of interest without further explanation: 1 mark)

(b)	No.			(1 mark)
	•	The available amount of free apps is insufficient to satisfy all human wants for them. 
	•	We prefer to have more of these free apps. 
	•	People are willing to pay a cost (e.g., time cost of downloading the apps) to obtain them.
	(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answer. 2 marks)

(c)	(i)	•	Consumption because	(1 mark)
		•	this directly satisfies Paul's wants for entertainment.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	•	Production because	(1 mark)
		•	Paul transforms his labour and capital (i.e., the tablet) into presentation services (output).	(1 mark)

(d)	(i)	•	The cost will remain unchanged.	(1 mark)
		•	The free app only increases the value of using the tablet. The highest-valued option forgone of using the tablet is unaffected.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	The cost will remain unchanged.	(1 mark)
		•	Paul has to pay $1,500 to fix the tablet whether he chooses to use or resell the tablet.	(1 mark)
		•	Hence, to use the tablet, he still has to give up the income from reselling the tablet.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
More tourists are using public swimming pools in Hong Kong and some of the swimming pools are crowded during the summer. Some people suggest that the government build more public swimming pools. The suggestion is mainly related to the __________ problem in economics.
A.	'what to produce'
B.	'how to produce'
C.	'for whom to produce'
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
More tourists are using public swimming pools in Hong Kong and some of the swimming pools are crowded during the summer. Some people suggest charging swimmers who do not have a Hong Kong identity card double when they use public swimming pools. The suggestion is related to the __________ problem(s) in economics.
A.	'what to produce'
B.	'how to produce'
C.	'for whom to produce'
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
A rich man employs farmers in a poor village to plant rice. Part of the rice is kept to sell to local villagers at a low price. The above case illustrates how the __________ problem(s) in economics is solved.
A.	'what to produce'
B.	'how to produce'
C.	'for whom to produce'
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
A coastal village in Japan is famous for its sea urchins (海膽). According to the village tradition, the sea urchins are collected by female free divers (徒手潛水員). The above tradition is related to the __________ question(s) in economics.
A.	'what to produce'
B.	'how to produce'
C.	'for whom to produce'
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
An airline company in Germany has decided to buy two Airbus A380s to increase the number of its flights between Frankfurt and Tokyo.
Which of the following economic problems is/are related to the above case?
A.	'What to produce'
B.	'For whom to produce'
C.	'What to produce' and 'how to produce'
D.	'How to produce' and 'for whom to produce'
questions.answerText: The choice of aircraft is related to 'how to produce'. The increase in the number of flights on a route is related to 'what to produce'.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
A property developer has announced it will provide more small, low-priced flats in the near future to meet the needs of young couples. This is related to the __________ question(s) in economics.
A.	'what to produce'
B.	'for whom to produce'
C.	'how to produce' and 'for whom to produce'
D.	'what to produce' and 'for whom to produce'

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Ming owns a small factory that produces traditional snacks. As traditional snacks have become less popular, Ming decides to lay off half of his workers to reduce output. Which of the following economic questions are involved?
(1)	What to produce
(2)	How to produce
(3)	For whom to produce
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The government plans to employ female workers to provide free childcare service for single parent families. Which of the following economic questions are involved?
(1)	What to produce
(2)	How to produce
(3)	For whom to produce
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In which of the following situations is the problem of 'what to produce' NOT involved?
	(1)	Living in a world without scarcity
	(2)	A bank manager plans to hire more staff
	(3)	A store owner chooses between selling apples or oranges
A.	(2) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(1) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText: Option (1): If there is no scarcity, the problem of 'what to produce' does not exist since people can get anything they want.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT a 'what to produce' question?
A.	What types of shoes a factory should produce.
B.	What time a factory should ship its products overseas.
C.	What kind of coffee a café should serve.
D.	How many socks a factory should produce.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following does NOT illustrate the 'what to produce' question? 
A.	How many meal boxes a restaurant should produce
B.	Which types of ice cream an ice cream shop should provide
C.	Which types of cuisines (菜式) a restaurant should provide
D.	When a restaurant should deliver its food

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following illustrates the 'how to produce' question?
A.	A garment factory decides to produce a new fashion.
B.	Mary decides to buy a new MP3 player.
C.	A manager decides to set up a new plant in Guangdong.
D.	A publisher (出版商) decides to publish more books about globalisation.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following illustrates the 'how to produce' question? 
A.	A publishing company decides to publish more books for children.
B.	A businessman decides to close all his shops and switch to selling goods via the internet. 
C.	Keung decides to buy a new laptop computer.
D.	A watch factory decides to produce a new watch.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following illustrates the 'how to produce' question?
A.	Mrs Chan buys vegetables at a market.
B.	Miss Lau performs acrobatics (雜技) at the annual dinner.
C.	Mr Lee decides to publish a computer magazine.
D.	Mr Chow types notes for his students with a laptop computer.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following illustrates a solution to a 'for whom to produce' question?
A.	Some parents would not let their children go to school because of their fear about the Ebola virus (伊波拉病毒).
B.	The United Nations sent hygiene kits to villagers in Western African countries.
C.	More advertisements about hygiene were produced during the Ebola virus outbreak.
D.	Pharmaceutical companies accelerated their research into a vaccine for the Ebola virus.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is made for resolving the 'for whom to produce' question? 
A.	The government decides to carry out mosquito-killing actions in public housing estates when dengue fever (登革熱) becomes widespread. 
B.	Some farmers stop farming when dengue fever becomes widespread. 
C.	Shops sell more mosquito coils (蚊香) when dengue fever becomes widespread. 
D.	Mosquito repellent spray (驅蚊水) producers try to boost sales by reducing prices when dengue fever becomes widespread.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following involves the 'for whom to produce' question?
(1)	The government allocates public housing units according to household income.
(2)	Universities allocate places according to students' HKDSE results.
(3)	Accident and emergency departments (急症室) determine the priority of treatment according to the seriousness of conditions.
(4)	Mr Leung reserves goods for frequent customers (常客).
A.	(1) only
B.	(2) and (3) only
C.	(1), (2) and (4) only
D.	(1), (2), (3) and (4)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The manager of a factory is considering whether to employ more workers or install an expensive new machine. Which of the following economic problems is directly addressed?
A.	What to produce
B.	How to produce
C.	When to produce
D.	For whom to produce

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
A university has decided to organise an orientation programme for its freshmen (新生). Which of the following problems does the university directly address?
	(1)	What to produce
	(2)	How to produce
	(3)	For whom to produce
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(1) and (3) only
D.	(2) and (3) only

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
One big fitness club launches a yoga programme. What economic problem is involved in this case?
A.	What to produce
B.	How to produce
C.	For whom to produce
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText: In the question, the fitness club decides on the type of services to be provided (yoga programme). Therefore, it is involved in the 'what to produce' question.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
To reduce production cost, a garment factory decided to fire (辭退) skilled workers and replaced them by hiring more semi-skilled workers. What economic problem is involved in this case?
A.	What to produce
B.	How to produce
C.	For whom to produce
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText: A change in production methods (from relying more on skilled workers to relying more on semi-skilled workers) concerns the 'how to produce' question.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Both Alex's father and grandfather are teachers. After Alex graduates from university, he decides to follow his father and grandfather in his choice of career. What economic problem(s) is (are) involved in this case?
A.	What to produce
B.	How to produce
C.	For whom to produce
D.	What and how to produce
questions.answerText: Choice of career is about the types of services to be provided. Therefore, it involves the 'what to produce' question.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is most likely an example of solving economic problems by customs and traditions?
A.	In ancient times, European merchants imported Chinese-made products via the Silk Road to earn a profit.
B.	Priests (祭司) in a primitive tribe receive more agricultural products than farmers during a harvest.
C.	In an ancient empire, it was illegal to produce salt privately.
D.	None of the above is the example

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a planned economy,
A.	most resources are owned by the state.
B.	most economic decisions are made by the government.
C.	most goods are distributed according to government commands.
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Compared to a planned economy, a market economy
A.	is more modernised (現代化).
B.	has more resources controlled by private enterprises.
C.	has less even income distribution.
D.	has fewer government officials.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
When a planned economy is transformed into a market economy,
A.	the government will intervene less in production.
B.	people can consume more goods.
C.	more resources will be wasted.
D.	there will be social unrest.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
A planned economy 
A.	does not have any customs and traditions.
B.	does not have currency.
C.	must eventually be transformed into a market economy.
D.	has a larger portion of its resources owned by the state than a market economy does.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Star City is famous for its high-quality medical services. However, the medical services are mainly in private hospitals. To meet the needs of the poor, public hospitals also provide cheap medical services. The above example shows that Star City is most likely a
A.	traditional economy.
B.	planned economy.
C.	market economy.
D.	mixed economy.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
North Korea is often regarded as a planned economy because
(1)	its per-capita (人均) consumption is relatively low.
(2)	the government distributes most goods and services.
(3)	workers' occupations are assigned by the government.
(4)	famine (飢荒) occasionally occurs.
A.	(1) and (4) only
B.	(2) and (3) only
C.	(1), (2) and (3) only
D.	(2), (3) and (4) only

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a country, the army assigns retired air force pilots to jobs at airline companies. This is an example of solving the problem of ___________ by __________.
A.	'for whom to produce' … government command
B.	'how to produce' … the market mechanism
C.	'how to produce' … government command
D.	'what to produce' … the market mechanism

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Andy originally owned a toy factory. He found that his profits from toys were declining. He decided to close the factory and open a restaurant from which he thought he could earn greater profits. This is an example of tackling the economic problem of __________ by ___________.
A.	'what to produce' … customs and traditions
B.	'what to produce' … the market mechanism
C.	'how to produce' … customs and traditions
D.	'how to produce' … the market mechanism

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Lincoln owns a parcel of land in Country Z. He built a music studio there. Last year, the Ministry of Agriculture (農業部) expropriated (徵用) the land and tore down Lincoln's studio to build a farm. This is an example of tackling the economic problem of __________ by __________.
A.	'what to produce' … government command
B.	'what to produce' … the market mechanism
C.	'for whom to produce' … government command
D.	'for whom to produce' … the market mechanism

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In some East Asian countries, married people give red packets to juniors (後輩) during festivals. This is an example of solving the question of _________ by __________.
A.	'how to produce' … customs and traditions
B.	'how to produce' … the market mechanism
C.	'for whom to produce' …customs and traditions
D.	'for whom to produce' … the market mechanism

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Suppose the Airport Authority announces the construction of a third runway to expand the capacity of the airport and provide job opportunities. This is an example of tackling the economic problem of __________ by __________.
A.	'what to produce' … government command
B.	'for whom to produce' … government command
C.	'how to produce' … the market mechanism
D.	'how to produce' … customs and traditions

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is an example of a price system?
A.	Students are told by teachers to perform at a ceremony.
B.	Students are awarded scholarships based on their academic results.
C.	Students pay for private tuition services.
D.	Students have to make a booking with their school before using a classroom after school.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a command economy,
A.	production decisions are made by a dictator (獨裁者).
B.	there is no discrimination.
C.	price signals are suppressed.
D.	costs and benefits are irrelevant in making decisions concerning resource allocation.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Compared to a planned economy, a market economy
A.	practises a higher level of specialisation.
B.	has more uneven income distribution.
C.	has more government intervention.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a command economy,
A.	there will be no problem of scarcity.
B.	government commands replace price signals in solving the problems of resource allocation.
C.	there will be no competition.
D.	there will be no problem of unequal income distribution.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following situations is most likely to be found in a command economy?
A.	The government provides subsidies to some industries.
B.	People can inherit (承繼) the properties of their ancestors.
C.	Students are assigned by the labour department to work in different positions after graduation.
D.	Prices of agricultural products have been very stable in recent years.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of following is most likely to exist in a command economy?
A.	The government owns all resources.
B.	Firms can earn huge profits because there is no competition.
C.	Workers' jobs are assigned.
D.	Price competition does not exist.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about a market-oriented economy is correct?
A.	The three basic economic problems are solely solved by the market mechanism.
B.	The living standard is higher than in a planned economy.
C.	All resources are owned by private enterprises.
D.	Most firms follow price signals in making their decisions.
questions.answerText:
•	Even in a market-oriented economy, some economic problems are solved by government commands or traditions. Option A is incorrect. 
•	Living standard is not necessarily higher in a market-oriented economy. Option B is incorrect.
•	Even in a market-oriented economy, some resources are owned by the government. Option C is incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following would affect the allocation of resources in a mixed economy?
(1)	Parental advice
(2)	Government officials' decisions
(3)	Consumer preferences
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText: In a mixed economy, features of more than one type of economy (i.e. traditional, planned and market economies) are present. Therefore, parental advice, government officials' decisions and consumer preferences all affect resource allocation.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Compared to a market economy, a planned economy must
A.	have a lower economic growth rate.
B.	have more even income distribution.
C.	have less output available for consumption.
D.	rely less on the market mechanism to allocate resources.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following about a command economy is correct?
A.	All resources are owned by the government.
B.	All markets are monopolised by government departments.
C.	Non-price competition is common.
D.	Production pattern fully reflects what consumers want.
questions.answerText:
•	Even in a command economy, some resources may be owned by private enterprises. Option A is incorrect. 
•	Even in a command economy, private enterprises may still exist in some industries. Option B is incorrect.
•	Since production is directed by government commands, and government officials do not necessarily know what consumers want, the production pattern may not reflect what consumers want. Option D is incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is a feature of a market-oriented economy?
A.	The problem of scarcity is more serious.
B.	There is price competition only.
C.	Resources are allocated according to the will of government officials. 
D.	Most productive resources are privately owned.
questions.answerText:
•		Scarcity means that our resources are insufficient to satisfy all our wants. In all types of economies, scarcity exists. The difference between different types of economies lies in their different methods to solve the three basic economic problems.
•	In a market-oriented economy, there are some resources which are not allocated by price mechanism. Other forms of competition replace price competition to decide who gets these resources.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
When a command economy is transformed into a market economy,
A.	more resources will be owned by private enterprises.
B.	the problem of income inequality will improve.
C.	the total output of goods and services will decrease.
D.	all production decisions will be made by private individuals.
questions.answerText:
•	In a market economy, income distribution is mostly determined by the price mechanism. There is no guarantee that the price mechanism distributes income more equally. Option B is incorrect. 
•	Compared with a command economy, a market economy does not have less total output of goods and services. In many cases, the total output of goods and services increases when a command economy changes into a market economy. Option C is incorrect. 
•	Even in a market economy, not all production decisions are made by private individuals. Some types of goods and services are provided by the government. Option D is incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following will NOT be found in a command economy?
	(1)	Production activities
	(2)	Opportunity costs
	(3)	The three basic economic problems
	(4)	Scarcity
A.	(2) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(3) and (4) only
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about a market economy is correct?
A.	All resources are privately owned.
B.	Competition is so intense that firms will get loss.
C.	Most workers can choose their jobs freely.
D.	Non-price competition is absent.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about a market economy is correct?
A.	The standard of living of its citizens is higher than that in a command economy.
B.	People are free to make consumption and production decisions without any restrictions.
C.	All property is privately owned.
D.	Resources are mostly allocated by the price mechanism.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about a market economy is INCORRECT? 
A.	People's standard of living in a market economy is not necessarily higher than that in a command economy. 
B.	People's consumption and production are free from government intervention.
C.	Most resources are privately owned.
D.	Some resources are allocated by a non-price mechanism.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a market economy,
A.	the problem of scarcity does not exist.
B.	market signals are substituted for government commands in resolving the problems of resource allocation.
C.	competition may not exist.
D.	income is evenly distributed.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is most likely to exist in a market economy? 
A.	The government imposes sewage charges on some industries.
B.	The government provides water supply.
C.	Private property rights are protected by law.
D.	Product prices are stable.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
When a country is transforming itself from a market economy into a command economy, we expect
	(1)	a more limited scope of private ownership of property.
	(2)	lower commodity prices.
	(3)	a less important role for price as a mechanism for allocating resources.
	(4)	more control over wage rates and prices of goods.
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (3) and (4) only

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
When a country changes from a command economy to a market economy, 
	(1)	fewer resources will be owned by the government.
	(2)	product prices will drop. 
	(3)	market prices will serve as signals in guiding production and consumption.
	(4)	wage rates and product price fluctuations will increase.
A.	(1) only 
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (3) and (4) only

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following situations is most likely a way to solve economic problems by customs and traditions?
A.	Only females can inherit property from their ancestors.
B.	Income earners need to pay taxes.
C.	People follow production orders that come from the ruling party (執政黨).
D.	Merchants sell products where they can make a greater profit.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is LEAST likely a way to distribute goods and services by customs and traditions?
A.	Only women have the right to distribute goods and services.
B.	During festivals, free Ping-on rice (平安米) is distributed on a 'first-come, first-served' basis.
C.	Antiques are sold to the highest bidder (投票者) at auctions (拍賣).
D.	When a ship is sinking, male passengers let female passengers escape first.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
'In order to protect people from the rising prices of daily necessities, we have decided to implement a series of policies. First, we will regulate the price of rice to be…,' said a government spokesperson. 
Which of the following can best be used to describe the above solution for rising prices?
A.	The market mechanism.
B.	Government commands.
C.	Traditions
D.	Market competition

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
'Our ancestors (祖先) have told us not to catch fish on this lake,' said a village headman (村長).
This statement best describes a
A.	closed economy.
B.	command economy. 
C.	market economy. 
D.	traditional economy.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Most of the resources in Economy X are privately owned and most of the questions of resource allocation are solved by the price mechanism. Economy X is most likely
A.	a market economy.
B.	a command economy.
C.	a traditional economy.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In Economy A, most resources are owned by the government and people have to follow government plans in consumption and production. Yet, some resources are still allocated by the price mechanism. Economy A is a
A.	traditional economy.
B.	command economy.
C.	market economy.
D.	developing country.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is correct?
A.	Scarcity can be eliminated in a pure market economy.
B.	Since there is scarcity, we cannot solve the three basic economic problems.
C.	There is no pure market economy in the real world.
D.	People in a command economy face no scarcity as they have no choice.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Hong Kong is a ________ because _____________.
A.	market economy; all resources are controlled by private enterprises
B.	planned economy; its government spends a huge amount of money on infrastructure
C.	traditional economy; many indigenous villages in the New Territories allow only males to inherit land
D.	mixed economy; market forces, government commands and traditions are all used to tackle economic problems

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
'Since the price of flour has increased substantially, we have to raise the price of our bread…….'
The above bakery is most likely operating in a ____________ economy.
A.	market
B.	command
C.	traditional
D.	mixed
questions.answerText: The above bakery makes its pricing decisions according to price signals. This most likely happens in a market economy.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The United States of America is often regarded as a market economy because
(1)	its per-capita (人均) consumption is high.
(2)	market forces allocate most consumer goods.
(3)	its workers can choose their occupations freely.
(4)	it has many billionaires (億萬富豪).
A.	(1) only
B.	(2) and (3) only
C.	(1), (2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
•	Options (2) and (3) are an indication that market mechanism is relied on to allocate resources (consumer goods and labour). 
•	In a market economy, the price mechanism does not guarantee a high per-capita consumption: people may choose to have more investment rather than consumption.
•	The presence of a large number of billionaire does not indicate that the US is a market economy. A command economy where the government deliberately (故意地) grants monopolies or privileges (特權) to individuals may also have many government-created billionaires.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The mainland of China is a _______________ as ______________.
A.	market economy; all property is privately owned
B.	command economy; the government plays an important role in the economy
C.	traditional economy; many people in the countryside follow customs and traditions
D.	mixed economy; it contains the features of all three types of economies

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Japan is a ____________, because _______________.
A.	mixed economy; government commands, the market mechanism, and customs and traditions are used to tackle economic problems
B.	planned economy; the government plays an important economic role in controlling the exchange rate of the Japanese Yen
C.	traditional economy; many people follow gender-based customs and traditions
D.	market economy; most resources are owned by households and private enterprises

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
__________ is/are a prerequisite (先決條件) for __________.
	(1)	Specialisation … exchange
	(2)	Exchange … specialisation
	(3)	Well-defined private property rights … market exchange
	(4)	Well-defined private property rights … competition
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(3) and (4) only

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about exchange is INCORRECT?
A.	Market exchange does not exist in a command economy.
B.	Exchange is not possible in a one-man economy.
C.	Exchange enhances living standards.
D.	Market exchange may take place if private property rights are clearly defined.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
* Which of the following is correct?
A.	We cannot satisfy all our wants because of greed (貪念).
B.	Scarcity implies shortage.
C.	Specialisation (專門化) is needed only when there is scarcity.
D.	Opportunity cost exists when there is more than one want.
questions.answerText: If there is no scarcity, people can satisfy all their wants with their resources. Therefore, they need not increase output by practising specialisation.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following rights are included in private property rights?
A.	The exclusive right to use the good.
B.	The exclusive right to generate income from the use of the good.
C.	The exclusive right to transfer the good.
D.	All of the above.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Private property is a resource or a good
A.	that people do not want more of.
B.	from which only its owner has the right to use, transfer and generate income.
C.	that must be owned by one person.
D.	that must be distributed by the market mechanism.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is/are the right(s) that a taxi driver can exercise over a taxi if the taxi is rented from a taxi company?
(1)	Exclusive right to use the taxi.
(2)	Exclusive right to sell the taxi.
(3)	Exclusive right to lease (出租) the taxi to his/her friend.
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In economics, the existence of discrimination implies
A.	that scarce resources are distributed through competition.
B.	the poor are unfairly treated.
C.	violence must be used to allocate resources.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The existence of competition implies that
A.	there are no free goods in the real world.
B.	resources are distributed by the market mechanism.
C.	scarcity can be eliminated.
D.	some people must be discriminated against.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following about scarcity is correct?
A.	Scarcity is a universal phenomenon.
B.	When there is a market price for a good, the good must be scarce.
C.	In a society, competition for scarce goods cannot be avoided.
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT an example of non-price competition?
A.	A baby catches the attention of his mother from his sister.
B.	Passengers look for seats in a train.
C.	People bid for an ancient vase in an auction (拍賣).
D.	Athletes compete at the Olympic Games (奧運會).

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In Hong Kong, the general out-patient service (普通門診服務) provided by public hospitals is allocated by
	(1)	price.
	(2)	first-come, first-served.
	(3)	customs and traditions.
	(4)	government commands.
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Hong Kong public libraries' book borrowing service is allocated
	(1)	by price.
	(2)	on a first-come, first-served basis.
	(3)	by customs and traditions.
	(4)	by government commands.
A.	(1) only
B.	(2) only
C.	(3) and (4) only
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a private housing estate, clubhouse (俱樂部) service is allocated
(1)	by price.
(2)	on a first-come, first-served basis.
(3)	by customs and traditions.
(4)	by government commands.
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText: In private housing estates, residents have to pay for some clubhouse services. Moreover, some of the services require reservations and are allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
A tutorial centre that specialises in teaching economics accepted only 100 people out of 600 applicants. Which of the following allocation methods involves discrimination?
A.	Only those who got an A in their school exam would be considered
B.	First-come, first-served
C.	By drawing lots
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The manager of a Hong Kong entertainment company is now formulating the company's development plan. Briefly explain which economic problem is being tackled in each of the following situations.
(a)	'Fans in the mainland are spending more now. Our artists should visit the mainland more frequently to gain greater publicity there,' said the manager.
			(3 marks)
(b)	'Our artists should not go to overseas studios to record CDs anymore. Local studios are good enough and much cheaper,' said the manager.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	'For whom to produce'.	(1 mark)
	The company decides to provide more services to fans in the mainland.	(2 marks)
(b)	'How to produce'.	(1 mark)
	The company decides to use a less costly method to produce CDs.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The CEO of a film production company in America must make certain decisions. Briefly explain which economic problem is being tackled in each of the following situations.
(a)	'Superhero movies have been popular in recent years. We should film a trilogy (三部曲) about a battle between two legendary superheroes,' said the manager. 				(3 marks)
(b)	'India has a huge audience. We should have relationships with more cinemas in India so that more of our films can be shown there,' said the manager.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	'What to produce'.	(1 mark)
	The company decides on the quantity and type of films to be produced.	(2 marks)
(b)	'For whom to produce'.	(1 mark)
	The company decides to provide more services to audiences in India.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Identify the problems of resource allocation illustrated in each of the following situations:
(a)	Public hospitals suspend the provision of obstetrical and gynaecological (婦產科) services to non-resident pregnant women.
(b)	A restaurant decides to introduce a vegetarian menu.
(c)	A farmer decides to keep a cow to help in farming.
(d)	A factory decides to lay off some workers and use more machines.
(e)	A cinema decides to show more Korean movies.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	For whom to produce question	(1 mark)
(b)	What to produce question	(1 mark)
(c)	How to produce question	(1 mark)
(d)	How to produce question	(1 mark)
(e)	What to produce question	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which basic economic problem is involved in each of the following situations?
(a)	A herbal tea shop decides to sell sandals (涼鞋) as well.
(b)	A bookshop decides to change and to sell via the Internet.
(c)	A publishing company decides to develop computer software for teaching and learning.
(d)	An ice cream shop decides to produce more fat-free ice-cream.
(e)	A government launches policies to deal with intergenerational poverty (跨代貧窮).	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	What to produce question	(1 mark)
(b)	How to produce question	(1 mark)
(c)	What to produce question	(1 mark)
(d)	What to produce question	(1 mark)
(e)	For whom to produce question	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a factory, managerial staff have to make decisions. Identify which question of resource allocation is being tackled in each of the following cases.
(a)	The production manager says, 'Since the wage rate of skilled workers in Hong Kong is too high, we should move the plant to Shenzhen.'	(2 marks)
(b)	The marketing manager says, 'A survey shows that this type of T-shirts becomes popular and we should produce more of it.'	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	How to produce question	(2 marks)
(b)	What to produce question	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The management of a publishing company has to make decisions on resource allocation. Identify which question of resource allocation is being tackled in each of the following situations.
(a)	'We should hire more editors from the mainland because the wage rate of local senior editors is too high,' said the publishing manager.	(2 marks)
(b)	'According to market research, our books have been the market leader in Hong Kong for many years. We can prepare to enter the Chinese market in the coming year to let the mainland readers buy our books,' said the sales manager. 	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	How to produce question	(2 marks)
(b)	For whom to produce question	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
'Hong Kong is a pure market economy where only the market mechanism is used.' 
Do you agree with this statement? Give TWO examples to explain your answer.	
				(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
No.				(1 mark)
Customs and traditions are used. For example, in some indigenous villages in the New Territories, only males can inherit land to build houses.	(2 marks)
Government commands are also used. For example, the government builds public estates for those who cannot afford private housing.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Explain whether the following are examples of allocating resources by customs, government command, or the price system in Hong Kong.
(a)	Eddie buys and sells shares on the stock market.	(2 marks)
(b)	Every year, organisations distribute free rice to people, usually the elderly, during the last day of the Yu Lan Festival (盂蘭節).	(2 marks)
(c)	Eligible households can apply for public housing provided by the Housing Authority.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Price system	(2 marks)
(b)	Customs	(2 marks)
(c)	Government command	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Explain how a market economy tackles the three basic questions in economics. 	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The 'What to produce' question: market prices serve as signals in deciding what goods to produce and in what quantities.	(2 marks)
•	The 'How to produce' question: producers find the lowest cost method of production. Factor prices guide them in their choice of production methods.	(2 marks)
•	The 'For whom to produce' question: people's ability to pay determines the quantity of goods they can get. 	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Explain how a command economy tackles the three basic economic questions. 				(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The 'What to produce' question: the government makes decisions on what goods are to be produced and in what quantities. The decisions are then sent to production units in the form of a command.	(2 marks)
•	The 'How to produce' question: the government decides on the method of production and allocates productive resources to production units to fulfill production targets.			(2 marks)
•	The 'For whom to produce' question: the government controls people's wage rates and prices. It also rations the limited quantity of goods to its people.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Compare market and command economies in terms of (a) ownership of property and (b) the way to tackle the how to produce question.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Most property is privately owned in a market economy while most resources are owned by the state in a command economy.	(3 marks)
(b)	In a market economy, producers find the least costly method of production. Factor prices guide them in their choice of production methods. On the other hand, the 'how to produce' question is determined by central planning in a command economy.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Compare market and traditional economies in terms of the way to tackle the (a) 'what to produce' question and (b) 'how to produce' question.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	In a market economy, market prices serve as signals in guiding what goods to produce and in what quantities.
In a traditional economy, people follow their ancestors in deciding what to produce.	(3 marks)
(b)	In a market economy, producers find the lowest-cost production method; factor prices guide them in their choice of production methods.
In a traditional economy, people follow their ancestors' ways in deciding how to produce.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Name THREE features which indicate that the economy of the mainland is transforming into a market economy.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	More widespread private ownership of property
•	More freedom in making consumption and production decisions
•	More prices are determined by the market mechanism
•	Fewer state-owned enterprises 
(Any THREE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Suppose the government builds some residential units and sells them to residents. Buyers of those units cannot sell or lease their units for the first five years after their purchase.
(a)	Explain whether the buyers have full private property rights over the units they buy in the first five years after their purchase.	(3 marks)
(b)	Would the price of units sold by private developers be higher or lower than those sold by the government? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.			(1 mark)
	In the first five years, buyers do not have the right to generate income from the units by selling or leasing them.	(2 marks)
(b)	Higher.		(1 mark)
	As the buyers of units sold by private developers have full private property rights over the units, people would be more willing to offer a higher price for them.	
				(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
(a)	What is specialisation?	(2 marks)
(b)	'Specialisation can take place even without exchange.' Do you agree? Explain.
			(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Specialisation is a way of organising production. It takes place when different people or economies concentrate on the production of a particular good or a particular production stage of a good.	(2 marks)
(b)	No. Without exchange, people have to produce everything they need by themselves. They cannot specialise in the production of a particular good.
		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Is the smartphone you bought in an electronics shop your private property? Explain by referring to the three rights associated with private property.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The smartphone is my private property.	(1 mark)
•	Exclusive right to use the good: I can exclude others from using the smartphone, and decide what to do with it. For example, I can use it to make a phone call or play games with it.	(2 marks)
•	Exclusive right to receive income generated by the use of the good: I can use the smartphone to earn income for myself by, for example, lending it to others to earn interest.	(2 marks)
•	Right to transfer the good: I can give the smartphone to any person I want.
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: What is the relationship between specialisation and exchange?	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Exchange (or trade) is a precondition for specialisation. With specialisation, people and economies do not produce everything they need. In order to enjoy goods they do not produce, they have to engage in exchange.			(2 marks)
•	Without exchange, specialisation is not possible. People and economies have to produce everything they need by themselves.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
(a)	What are private property rights?	 (3 marks)
(b)	What role do they play in facilitating exchange and specialisation? 	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a) The private property rights of a good consist of the following rights:
	•	exclusive right to use the good;	(1 mark)
	•		exclusive right to receive income generated by the use of the good;	 (1 mark)
	•	the right to transfer the good.	(1 mark)
(b) •	If private property rights to a good do not exist, the good becomes a common property. Since everyone may use it, no one would be willing to pay for its use. As a result, exchange would not take place.	(2 marks)
•	Exchange is a precondition for specialisation. Without exchange, specialisation is not possible. People and economies have to produce everything they need by themselves.	(2 marks)
	•	Therefore, clear delineation of private property rights is an important condition for exchange and hence specialisation.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Does a tenant have the private property rights to the apartment he/she has leased from the owner? Why?	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	No. A tenant does not have private property rights to a leased apartment.	(1 mark)
•	Although the tenant has the exclusive right to use the apartment, he/she has no right to transfer the apartment to others.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: 'An economy where private property rights to goods or resources do not exist can never be a market economy.' Do you agree with this statement? Explain.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	In a market economy, most resources are owned by private individuals. Resources are allocated by the market mechanism.	(1 mark)
