•	If private property rights to resources do not exist, no one can sell the resources as no one owns them; and no one will pay for the resources as they cannot be owned. No voluntary market transaction would take place.	(2 marks)
•	Therefore, resources will be allocated by non-price methods (e.g., violence, direction of the authority). 	(1 mark)
•	So, an economy where private property rights do not exist cannot be a market economy.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Explain whether people would compete for seawater.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
No.	(1 mark)
Seawater is not a scarce good.	(1 mark)
People do not prefer more of it, hence they are not willing to pay any costs to compete for seawater.	(2 marks)
(Accept any other reasonable answer)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Explain whether the following statements about competition are correct:
(a)	Since resources in a command economy are allocated by government plans and commands, there is no competition in a command economy. 	(4 marks)
(b)	In general, the types of discriminated people change with the forms of competition.		(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Incorrect.
	•	Scarcity means we want more than we have. In a society (where there is more than one person), scarcity implies competition. We have to compete for the use of scarce resources.	(2 marks)
	•	Therefore competition exists in every economic system (i.e., traditional, planned and market economies). Although price competition is suppressed in a command economy, there is still non-price competition, e.g., competition through political power. 	 (2 marks)
(b)	•	Correct.
	•	The aim of competition is to decide who can get the resources and how much they get. Rules are designed to discriminate (or distinguish) among who can get the resources. A given set of rules favours certain types of people and discriminates against others. 	(2 marks)
	•	When new rules are used to discriminate between competitors, the types of people who are able to get the resources will be different. 	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Alex: 'When there is scarcity, there is competition.'
Mary: 'Even when there is scarcity, there may not be competition.'
Explain why both of them can be correct.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Mary is correct when she refers to a one-man economy. In such an economy, a person may want more than he has, but there is no one to compete with him for the scarce resources. Therefore, there is scarcity but no competition in a one-man economy.	(2 marks)
•	Alex is correct when he refers to a society. In a society (where there is more than one person), scarcity implies competition.	(2 marks)


Structured Questions

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Air pollution is serious in City J. This is mainly caused by the combustion (燃燒) of diesel fuel as the city has a huge amount of vehicles. The mayor (市長) wants to find ways to improve the city's air quality.
(a)	Identify the economic problem tackled and the methods used in each of the following situations.
(i)	The mayor and officials decide to limit the number of driving licenses issued each month to control the number of new vehicles on the roads.	(2 marks)
(ii)	The city's railway company lowers its fares during rush hours to attract more workers into using its services.	(2 marks)
(iii)	The government orders the postal service providers to use more bicycles instead of vehicles to deliver the mails.	(2 marks)
(b)	To encourage the use of bicycles in the city, the government provides bicycles at some railway stations. Residents can borrow the bicycles to travel locally. 
	(i)	Explain whether the bicycles are free goods.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	'As residents do not need to pay to use the bicycles, there is no competition for the bicycles.' Do you agree with this statement? Explain.		(3 marks)
	(iii)	Explain whether users have full private property rights to the bicycles.		(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	'What to produce'	(1 mark)
		Tackled by government command.	(1 mark)
(ii)	'For whom to produce'	(1 mark)
	Tackled by the market mechanism.	(1 mark)
(iii)	'How to produce'	(1 mark)
	Tackled by government command.	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	No.		(1 mark)
		They are scarce goods because more of them are preferred.	(2 marks)
(ii)	No.	(1 mark)
	Although users do not need to pay, they may engage in non-price competition (e.g., first-come, first-served) to use the bicycles.	(2 marks)
(iii)	No.	(1 mark)
	Users have the right to use the bicycles.	(1 mark)
	However, they do not have the right to transfer the bicycles.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The government is studying the feasibility of adopting electronic textbooks (電子教科書), called e-textbooks, in primary and secondary schools. It is suggested that the use of e-textbooks can improve the effectiveness of teaching and learning. Currently, some printed textbooks are accompanied with CDs that containing digital learning materials, such as interactive games and exercises.
(a)	State the THREE basic economic problems. Give ONE example for EACH problem from the above case.	(6 marks)
(b)	To stimulate the development of e-textbooks, the government subsidises (資助) non-profit institutions to develop e-textbooks. The subsidy will be granted only if the applicants' proposals meet the government's requirements. Some profitmaking publishers complain that this scheme discriminates against them and violates the principles of a market economy.
	(i)	In which way does the above scheme violate the principles of a market economy?	(2 marks)
	(ii)	From an economics viewpoint, why does discrimination exist? Explain.
			(4 marks)
	(iii)	Do applicants in the above subsidy scheme face discrimination? Explain.
		(3 marks)
	(iv)	It is reported that scheme participants have to hand over all of the e-textbook materials to the government if they cannot complete the product by the deadline. How does this affect the attractiveness of the scheme? Explain using the concept of private property rights.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	What to produce.	(1 mark)
	•	Example: Publishers have to decide whether they should produce more e-textbooks and fewer printed textbooks.	(1 mark)
	•	How to produce.	(1 mark)
	•	Example: Teachers have to decide whether e-textbooks should be used to replace printed textbooks.	(1 mark)
	•	For whom to produce.	(1 mark)
	•	Example: Publishers have to decide whether they should develop e-textbooks for primary students or secondary students.	(1 mark)
	(Accept other relevant examples.)


(b)	(i)	In a market economy, resource allocation is guided by the market mechanism. However, resources for this scheme are allocated by the government.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	Discrimination exists whenever there is competition.	(2 marks)
		•	Competition exists because there is scarcity.	(2 marks)
	(iii)	•	Yes.	(1 mark)
		•	The government has decided rules to discriminate among those who can obtain the subsidy.	(2 marks)
	(iv)	•	The attractiveness will decrease.	(1 mark)
		•	This is because the e-textbooks developers' private property rights are not guaranteed. They face the risk of losing their property to the government after making a huge investment.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Mr Lee lives in West Kowloon. Due to the development of the West Kowloon Cultural District, he could either move to the New Territories or accept resettlement in the same district.
(a)	What is Mr Lee's cost of moving to the New Territories?	(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose the government compensates Mr Lee if he moves to the New Territories. Explain whether this would affect his opportunity cost of moving.	(3 marks)
(c)	The government once proposed the inclusion of a canopy covering (天篷) over at least 55% of the development area in the core facilities. Identify what basic economic question is involved. 	(1 mark)
(d)	Suppose the private developers involved in the project will charge fees on some of the facilities to increase their profits. What type of economy usually practises such a mechanism? List another feature of this type of economy.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Mr Lee's cost of moving to the New Territories was the expense of moving to the New Territories and the option of resettlement in the same district.	(3 marks)

(b)	This will only increase the value of moving to the New Territories and will not affect its cost.	(3 marks)

(c)	'What to produce' question	(1 mark)

(d)	•	Price setting (or production decisions) by private companies is usually practised in a market economy.	(2 marks)
	•	Another feature: most of the resources are privately owned.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch102 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Mr Szeto is a teacher. Because of the reduction in the number of school-age children, he is considering whether he should continue teaching or retire earlier.
(a)	What is Mr Szeto's cost of choosing to continue teaching?	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose the government is willing to provide an 'early retirement gratuity' (提早退休酬金) for Mr Szeto. Explain whether this would affect his cost of choosing to continue teaching.	(3 marks)
(c)	The government had once considered launching a scheme under which one teaching post would be shared by two teachers. Identify what basic economic question is involved.	(1 mark)
(d)	Some tutoring centres attract experienced teachers to be tutors by offering high wage rates. In which type of economy does this practice usually occur? List another feature of this type of economy. 	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Mr Szeto's cost of choosing to continue teaching is the option of early retirement.					(2 marks)

(b)	If the government is willing to provide an 'early retirement gratuity' for Mr Szeto, his cost of choosing to continue teaching will increase. This is because he has to give up his extra gratuity for early retirement.	(3 marks)

(c)	'How to produce' question	(1 mark)

(d)	•	Resolving resource allocation problems by adjusting prices and wages is common in a market economy.	(2 marks)
	•	Another feature: most resources are privately owned.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following are kept constant along a demand curve?
(1)	Quantity demanded
(2)	Price
(3)	Consumers' income
(4)	Weather
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(3) and (4) only

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
While deriving the demand for a good, which of the following factors have to be kept constant?
(1)	Price of the good
(2)	Prices of related goods
(3)	Buyer's preference for the good
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following persons has a demand for a tablet computer?
A.	Sara wants to buy a tablet computer to watch dramas, but she has used up her pocket money.
B.	Felicity wants to buy a tablet computer to help her with her work and her boss will pay for it.
C.	Laurel can buy 100 tablet computers but she does not want to buy it.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following is/are held constant along the same demand curve for the iPhone??
	(1)	The price of the iPhone
	(2)	Buyer's income
	(3)	The prices of Android phones
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText: The prices of related goods (i.e., Android phones in this case) would affect the demand for the iPhone. Therefore, the prices of Android phones should be held constant along the same demand curve for the iPhone.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about demand is correct?
A.	Demand can be expressed in the form of a demand schedule.
B.	The time period needs to be specified when we describe the demand for a good.
C.	Demand shows the relationship between the price and the quantity demanded.
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Mr Lee has a demand for an apartment on the Peak if
A.	his family thinks the Peak is an ideal place to live.
B.	he wants to have his own apartment there.
C.	he has won the Mark Six lottery recently and is able to pay for it.
D.	he is willing and able to buy one.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about want and demand is correct?
A.	Since wants are unlimited, demand is unlimited too.
B.	The rich have more wants than the poor.
C.	Wants must be supported by purchasing power.
D.	Wants exist even if we cannot satisfy them.
questions.answerText:
•	Wants are unlimited, while demand is limited by purchasing power. Therefore, Option A is incorrect.
•	Both the rich and the poor have unlimited wants, so we cannot say the rich have more wants than the poor. Therefore, Option B is incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about demand is INCORRECT?
A.	Demand reflects the purchase plan of a consumer at different prices.
B.	Demand is the quantities a person is willing and able to buy at various prices.
C.	Demand is the quantity a person will buy at the market price.
D.	Demand is desire supported by purchasing power.
questions.answerText: Demand refers to the purchase plan or the quantities a person is willing and able to buy at various prices. It does not tell us the quantity a person will actually buy at a particular price. Therefore, option C is incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following persons has demand for a Gucci handbag priced at $15,000?
A.	A bankrupt (破產者) who wants the handbag very much
B.	An economics professor with a monthly income over $60,000 who hates branded products
C.	The wife of a rich businessman who is fond of the bag and can afford it
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
•	The bankrupt wants the Gucci handbag very much but cannot spend money on luxuries. Therefore, he or she does not have a demand for it.
•	Although the professor has the money to buy the handbag, he or she is not willing to buy it. Therefore, he or she has no demand for it. 
•	Only when the person has the ability and willingness to buy the handbag will the demand for it exist. Therefore, only the wife of a rich businessman has the demand for it.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Tommy is a student who is fond of smartphone games. This month, after spending 95% of his pocket money on in-game items, he used the remaining 5% for lunches.
A.	Tommy has demand for in-game discs only.
B.	Tommy has demand for both in-game items and lunches.
C.	Tommy does not have demand for either in-game items or lunches.
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText:
•	The fact that Tommy has actually spent money on both in-game items and lunches implies that he has demand for both. 
•	Although Tommy spends only 5% of his money on lunches, he still has a demand for lunches.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Under which of the following conditions will Mrs Cheung have demand for brand name handbags?
A.	She wants a brand name handbag. 
B.	She wants to buy a brand name handbag and she can afford it.
C.	Her husband thinks that the quality of brand name handbags is very high. 
D.	She has just been promoted and received a pay rise. Her monthly salary is sufficient for her to buy several brand name handbags.

questions.answerText: The fact that Shawn has a demand for meals at Pizza Hut simply means he is willing and able to purchase meals at Pizza Hut over a period of time. A.	Her demand for sunglasses is 30 pairs per year.
B.	At a price of $3, her demand for sunglasses is 6 pairs per year.
C.	At a price of $5, her quantity demanded of sunglasses is 2 pairs per year.
D.	Her demand for sunglasses violates the law of demand.
questions.answerText:
•	Demand refers to the quantities a person is willing and able to buy at various prices. It is not equal to the sum of all the quantities demanded at various prices (30 = 10 + 8 + 6 + 4 + 2). Therefore, Option A is incorrect.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements about a market demand curve is correct?
A.	A market demand curve shows the total quantity demanded of all consumers at a given price.
B.	A market demand curve can be derived from individual demand curves via horizontal summation.
C.	The market demand curve cannot violate the law of demand.
D.	A market demand curve alone can determine the equilibrium price.
questions.answerText:

C.	A market is in equilibrium when there is no tendency for the price to change.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose the market price of Good X is initially set at P1. What will happen if the market price decreases?
A.	The excess supply will increase.
B.	The excess supply will disappear.
C.	The excess supply will decrease.
D.	An excess demand will appear.
questions.answerText:
•	At P1, there is an excess supply of Good X. When the price decreases, the excess supply will decrease. Therefore, Option A is incorrect while Option C is correct.
•	However, the extent of the price decrease may not be sufficient to eliminate the excess supply. Therefore, Option B may not be correct.
•	Moreover, only when the price decreases to a level below the equilibrium level will an excess demand appear. Therefore, Option D may not be correct.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
*To increase tourism, Country A decides to lower the Air Passenger Departure Tax (飛機乘客離境稅): the tax charged on passengers who depart Country A by plane will decrease from $1,000 to $100. Which of the following statements is correct?
A.	The average length of air journeys will tend to fall.
B.	More senior citizens and children will travel.
C.	More foreigners will go to Country A.
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
•	After the tax cut, the relative price of short-distance journeys (in terms of long-distance journey) will decrease. According to the law of demand, there will be relatively more short-distance journeys. Hence, Option A is correct.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Explain whether the law of demand can illustrate the following phenomenon.
(a)	During an economic boom, both the price and quantity transacted of new cars increase.	(4 marks)
(b)	Although the price remains unchanged, more people have lunch at Restaurant X now because it serves meals faster than before.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.			(1 mark)
	The law of demand states that the price and quantity demanded of a good are inversely related, holding other factors constant.	(2 marks)
	The change described is caused by a change in a factor other than the price.
				(1 mark)
(b)	Yes.		(1 mark)
	In addition to the money price, the full price consists of the non-money price. In this case, the non-money price (i.e., time cost) decreases. Hence, the full price decreases.	(2 marks)
	This shows an inverse relationship between the quantity demanded and the full price.		(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	State the law of demand.	(2 marks)
(b)	In the past, there were no fitness centres near Victoria's home. She had to travel to a fitness centre in another district to exercise. After a new fitness centre opens near her home, Victoria exercises more than before. Use the law of demand to explain this.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The law of demand states that the lower (higher) the price of a good, the greater (smaller) its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	(2 marks)
(b)	To Victoria, the full price of exercising involves the money price and time cost.
	(1 mark)
	After a new fitness centre opens near her home, her time cost and the full price of exercising decreases. According to the law of demand, the lower full price will lead to her higher quantity demanded of exercising.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	State the law of demand.	(2 marks)
(b)	A drug addict said, 'I will buy the same amount of heroin (海洛英) regardless of the price.' Is his behaviour consistent with the law of demand? Explain.	 (4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The law of demand states that the lower (higher) the price of a good, the greater (smaller) its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	 (2 marks)
(b)	•	No.	 (1 mark)
•	Since the quantity demanded for heroin remains unchanged when the price changes, it violates the law of demand.	 (3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
*A girl said, 'I spend $1,000 buying Bird of Paradise's records every year regardless of the price.' Is her behaviour consistent with the law of demand? Explain. 
(Hint: Total spending = Price × Quantity demanded)	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Consistent	(1 mark)
•	To keep the total spending constant, her quantity demanded for Bird of Paradise's records must be inversely related to the price.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
In recent years, more and more mainlanders have come to Hong Kong to buy Apple products. It has been reported that the prices of Apple products are much lower here.
(a)	State the law of demand.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether the above phenomenon can be explained by the law.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The law of demand states that the lower (higher) the price of a good, the greater (smaller) its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	 (2 marks)
(b)	•	Yes.	(1 mark)
	•	Mainland buyers buy the products in Hong Kong at lower prices instead of in the mainland at higher prices.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
In recent years, more and more people from the mainland have come to Hong Kong to buy baby formula (嬰幼兒配方奶粉). This is because they believe that the quality of the baby formula sold in Hong Kong is far better than that in the mainland. This has led to the increase in the prices of baby formula in Hong Kong.
(a)	State the law of demand.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether the above phenomenon can be explained by the law.	 (3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The law of demand states that the lower (higher) the price of a good, the greater (smaller) its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	(2 marks)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
	We cannot use the law of demand to explain the above phenomenon in which the number of visitors increase with the quality of baby formula sold, which is a factor other than price. This is because the law of demand tells only the relationship between the price and the quantity demanded of a good.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is the difference between quantity demanded and demand?	(4 marks)
(b)	Mr. Chan and Miss Wong have the same quantity demanded for Good X at every price. Is it correct to conclude that they have the same demand for Good X? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Quantity demanded refers to the quantity a buyer is willing and able to buy at a particular price over a period of time.	(2 marks)
	•	Demand refers to the quantities a buyer is willing and able to buy at different prices over a period of time. 	(2 marks)
(b)	No, it depends on the length of the period.	 (1 mark)
•	If the period of Mr. Chan's demand is longer, his demand is actually smaller than that of Miss Wong.
•	If the period of Mr. Chan's demand is shorter, his demand is actually greater than that of Miss Wong.
(Any ONE of above, 2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is the difference between quantity supplied and supply?	 (4 marks)
(b)	Firm A and Firm B have the same quantity supplied of Good Y at every price. Explain whether we can conclude that they have the same supply of Good Y.	 	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Quantity supplied refers to the quantity a seller is willing and able to sell at a particular price over a period of time.	 (2 marks)
	•	Supply refers to the quantities a seller is willing and able to sell at different prices over a period of time.	 (2 marks)
(b)	No, we need to consider the length of the period:	 (1 mark)
•	If the period of Firm A's supply is longer, its supply is actually smaller than that of Firm B.
•	If the period of Firm A's supply is shorter, its supply is actually greater than that of Firm B.
(Any ONE of the above, 2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	State the law of supply.	(2 marks)
(b)	In recent years, the price of portable hard disks has kept decreasing while the quantity sold has increased. Explain whether this phenomenon can be illustrated by the law of supply.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The law of supply states that the higher (lower) the price of a good, the greater (smaller) its quantity supplied, other factors being constant.	(2 marks)
(b)	No.			(1 mark)
	The changes in the quantity supplied and the price go in different directions. This is caused by factors other than the price.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is the difference between scarcity and shortage?	(4 marks)
(b)	What is the similarity between scarce goods and goods in shortages?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Scarcity means human wants can never be fully satisfied by limited resources.					(2 marks)
	A shortage means that the quantity demanded is larger than the quantity supplied at a price below the equilibrium.	(2 marks)
(b)	People prefer to have more scarce goods and goods in shortages.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is excess supply?	(2 marks)
(b)	What is implied by the phenomenon that some workers are unemployed at the minimum wage? Draw a supply-demand diagram to describe this phenomenon.			(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Excess supply refers to a situation where the quantity supplied is greater than the quantity demanded when the price is set above the equilibrium price.	(2 marks)
(b)	The phenomenon implies that the minimum wage (W) is higher than the equilibrium wage (We), leading to an excess supply of workers.	(2 marks)
	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Minimum wage > Equilibrium wage	(1 mark)
	(	Excess supply	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The illegal sale of permits for sports facilities provided by the Leisure and Cultural Department (LCSD) is a serious problem. The permits are sold on the internet for a higher price than the original fees charged by the LCSD. What economic concept is illustrated in this example? Explain with the aid of a supply-demand diagram.
		(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Verbal elaboration:
(	The example shows that an excess demand (or shortage) exists in the market for LCSD sports facilities.	(2 marks)
(	Excess demand (or a shortage) refers to a situation where the quantity demanded is greater than the quantity supplied when the price (P) is set below the equilibrium price (Pe).	(2 marks)
Indicate on the diagram:
(	Price < Equilibrium price	(1 mark)
(	Excess demand	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The following are the demand and supply schedules for Good X.

Unit price ($)	2	3	4	5	6	7	
Quantity demanded (units)	90	76	65	52	43	35	
Quantity supplied (units)	43	54	65	74	83	96	

(a)	Find the equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity of Good X.	 (2 marks)
(b)	Calculate the amount of excess supply at a price of $7.	 (2 marks)
(c)	What is the quantity transacted at a price of $7? Explain.	 (2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The equilibrium price is $4 and the equilibrium quantity is 65 units.	 (2 marks)
(b)	At a price of $7, Excess supply = Quantity supplied - Quantity demanded
	= (96 - 35) units	 (1 mark)
	= 61 units	 (1 mark)
(c)	•	At a price of $7, the quantity supplied is greater than the quantity demanded.	 			(1 mark)
•	In this case, the quantity transacted is equal to quantity demanded, i.e., 35 units.	 (1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The following are the demand and supply schedules for dictionaries.

Unit price ($)	100	150	200	250	300	350	
Quantity demanded (units)	10	8	6	4	2	0	
Quantity supplied (units)	2	4	6	8	10	12	

(a)	What are the equilibrium price and quantity transacted of dictionaries?	(2 marks)
(b)	Calculate the amount of excess demand at a price of $150.	(2 marks)
(c)	What is the quantity transacted at a price of $300? Explain.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The equilibrium price is $200 and the quantity transacted is 6 units.	(2 marks)
(b)	At a price of $150, Excess demand = Quantity demanded - Quantity supplied 
= (8 - 4) units	(1 mark)
	= 4 units	(1 mark)
(c)	•	At a price of $300, the quantity supplied (10 units) is greater than the quantity demanded (2 units).	(1 mark)
	•	In this case, the quantity transacted is equal to the quantity demanded, i.e. 2 units.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
To celebrate its 3rd anniversary, a restaurant sells 300 lunch boxes at a discounted price every day. A long queue is found outside the restaurant.
(a)	Show the phenomenon mentioned on a supply-demand diagram.	(3 marks)
(b)	Does the above case illustrate scarcity? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Suppose the price of a lunch box is P.
	(2 marks)
	•	Since P is lower than the equilibrium price (Pe), a shortage exists.	(1 mark)
(b)	•	Yes.	(1 mark)
	•	Scarcity means we want more than we have.	(1 mark)
	•	In the above case, the discounted lunch boxes available are insufficient to satisfy everyone's wants, so scarcity exists.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: Suppose the government imposes a fixed tax amount on each cigar. Explain the effect of the tax on the average length of cigars.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The price of a long cigar is higher than the price of a short cigar.	(1 mark)
•	When the tax is imposed, the percentage increase in the price of a long cigar is smaller than the percentage increase in the price of a short cigar.	(2 marks)
•	The relative price of a long cigar (in terms of short cigars) decreases.	(1 mark)
•	According to the law of demand, relatively more long cigars are sold in the market.
				(1 mark)
•	Hence, the average length of cigars increases.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: Country N is famous for its tuna. Suppose the transportation costs of each unit of high-quality tuna and low-quality tuna are the same. Compare the average qualities of exported tunas and tunas consumed by local consumers in Country N.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:

•	When the transportation cost is added during export, the percentage increase in the price of high-quality tuna is smaller than the percentage increase in the price of low-quality tuna.	(2 marks)
•	The relative price of exported high-quality tuna (in terms of low-quality tuna) is lower than that of high-quality tuna consumed by local consumers.	(1 mark)
•	According to the law of demand, relatively more high-quality tunas are exported.
				(1 mark)
•	Hence, the average quality of exported tunas is higher than that of tunas consumed by local consumers.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: There are many flower sellers at the Lunar New Year Fair. Suppose the sellers cut the prices of all flowers by the same amount at the last night of the fair. What is the effect on the average quality of flowers sold?	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The price of high-quality flowers is higher than the price of low-quality flowers.
		(1 mark)
•	After the uniform price cut, the percentage decrease in the price of high-quality flowers is smaller than the percentage decrease in the price of low-quality flowers.	
			(2 marks)
•	The relative price of high-quality flowers (in terms of short cigars) increases.
				(1 mark)
•	According to the law of demand, relatively fewer high-quality flowers are sold.	
			(1 mark)
•	Hence, the average quality of flowers sold decreases.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The prices below show the cost of a DVD and a Blu-ray Disc in two countries.

	Country X	Country Y	
Blu-ray Disc	$180	$200	
DVD	$60	$100	

(a)	What are the relative prices of a Blu-ray Disc in terms of DVDs in the two countries, respectively?	(4 marks)
(b)	In which country will people consume relatively more Blu-ray Discs? Explain.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The relative price of a Blu-ray Disc in terms of DVDs in Country X 
	=  = 3 DVDs	(2 marks)
	The relative price of a Blu-ray Disc in terms of DVDs in Country Y
	=  = 2 DVDs 	(2 marks)
(b)	The relative price of a Blu-ray Disc in terms of DVDs in Country Y is lower than that in Country X. By the law of demand, people in Country Y will buy relatively more Blu-ray Discs.	(2 marks)

(b)	Explain the change of the relative price of an apartment in terms of cars. Show your steps. 	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Percentage change of the nominal price of an apartment
		 (1 mark)

	 	(1 mark)

questions.text:
Study the following table and answer the following questions.

(b)	Explain the change in the relative price of a can of spiced pork cube (in terms of cans of pork luncheon meat) between 2009 and 2014. Show your steps.
		(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Percentage change in the nominal price of a can of pork luncheon meat
		(1 mark)
	= 50%	 (1 mark)
	Percentage change in the nominal price of a can of spiced pork cube
		(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
*'Suppose the taxi fare for the first two kilometres increases from $18 to $30, holding other things constant, the average length of trips per ride will increase.' Do you agree with this statement? Explain.	 (6 marks)
(Hint: 1.	Average length equals the total length of all trips divided by the number of trips.
2.	Assume there are only 2 types of passengers: passengers taking long distance trips and passengers taking short distance trips.)
questions.answerText:
•	If the taxi fare for the first two kilometres increases, the relative price of long distance trips (in terms of the number of short distance trips) falls. 	(1 mark)
•	According to the law of demand, the quantity demanded of long distance trips will increase relative to that of short distance trips. 	(1 mark)
•	On the other hand, the increase in the taxi fare for the first two kilometres will increase the money prices (fares) for both long distance trips and short distance trips, therefore, the quantity demanded of both long distance trips and short distance trips (i.e., the number of trips) decreases. 	(2 marks)
•	The average length of trips per ride increases as the quantity demanded of long distance trips increases relative to that of short distance trips.	 (2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: A cake shop sells two types of freshly baked cakes each day: premium Cheese Cake and standard Cheese Cake. The former is $200 per cake while the latter is $150 per cake. The owner of the shop has recently decided to charge $20 per cake for packing. Explain how this affects the ratio of premium Cheese Cake to standard cheese Cake sold by applying the concept of the law of demand. 	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
The relative price of premium Cheese Cake in terms of standard Cheese Cake before the packing charge
= $200 ÷ $150
= 1.33	(1 mark)
The relative price of premium Cheese Cake in terms of standard Cheese Cake after the packing charge
= $220 ÷ $170
= 1.29	(1 mark)
The relative price of premium Cheese Cake in terms of standard Cheese Cake decreases from 1.33 to 1.29, thus according to the law of demand, relatively more premium Cheese Cake will be purchased. 	(1 mark)
Therefore, the ratio of premium Cheese Cake to standard Cheese Cake sold increases.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: Suppose the government provides a $15 unit subsidy on every can of baby formula. Using the law of demand, explain the change in the average size of cans of baby formula sold.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
After providing the unit subsidy, the prices of both large-sized and small-sized baby formula cans would decrease by an equal amount. The percentage decrease in the price of large-sized baby formula cans would be smaller than the percentage decrease in the price of small-sized baby formula.	(2 marks)
The relative price of large-sized baby formula cans (in terms of small-sized baby formula cans) increases.	(1 mark)
According to the law of demand, relatively fewer large-sized cans of baby formula would be sold.	(1 mark)
Hence, the average size of baby formula cans sold would decrease.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose a Japanese buffet restaurant offers the following sets to customers.

Standard set
$250
Choose from 90 dishes		Premium set
$330
Choose from 130 dishes	
(+ $50 for both sets on Saturdays and Sundays.)

Using the law of demand, explain whether a large portion of customers would choose the premium set on Saturdays and Sundays (than on weekdays).	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
On Saturdays and Sundays, the prices of both standard and premium sets would increase by $50. The percentage increase in the price of the premium set is smaller than the percentage increase in the price of the standard set.	(2 marks)
The relative price of the premium set (in terms of the standard set) on Saturdays and Sundays is less than it is on weekdays.	(1 mark)
According to the law of demand, relatively more customers would choose the premium set on Saturdays and Sundays.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
A telecommunication service provider provides the following monthly data plans to local residents and foreign domestic helpers.

	For local residents	For foreign domestic helpers	
	3G plan	4G plan	3G plan	4G plan	
Monthly charge	$150	$300	$80	$120	
Maximum usage	5 GB	

(a)	Calculate the relative price of a monthly 4G plan (in terms of monthly 3G plans) for local residents and foreign domestic helpers, respectively.	(2 marks)
(b)	Compared with local residents, would there be a larger proportion of foreign domestic helpers who would choose a 4G plan? Explain your answer using the law of demand.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Relative price of 4G plan for local residents
	= $300 ÷ $150 = 2 months of 3G plan	(1 mark)
	Relative price of 4G plan for foreign domestic helpers
	= $120 ÷ $80 = 1.5 months of 3G plan	(1 mark)
(b)	Yes.	(1 mark)
	The relative price of a 4G plan for foreign domestic helpers is lower than that for local residents. According to the law of demand, a larger proportion of foreign domestic helpers would choose a 4G plan.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: A Hong Kong superstar holds a concert in Central Harbourfront. The tickets sell out quickly. It is reported that overseas fans account for nearly 60% of the seats close to the stage while they only take up 20% of the seats far from the stage. Explain this phenomenon with the law of demand.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Besides the ticket prices, overseas fans need to pay travel-related fees to come to Hong Kong and watch the concert.	(1 mark)
After adding up the travelling fees, the relative price the overseas concertgoers pay for seats close to the stage (in terms of a seat far from the stage) is lower than the relative price paid by local fans.	(2 marks)
The law of demand states that the lower the price of a good, the greater its quantity demanded, other factors being constant. Therefore, relatively more overseas fans would book seats closer to the stage.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: Suppose the government charges every air passenger a uniform airport construction surcharge of $100. The surcharge is included in the ticket price. Using the law of demand, explain whether the proportion of passengers choosing business class instead of economy class will increase or decrease.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
After adding $100, the percentage increase in the ticket price for business class is smaller than the percentage increase in the ticket price for economy class.	(2 marks)
The relative price of business class (in terms of economy class) decreases.	(1 mark)
According to the law of demand, the lower the price of a good, the greater the quantity demanded of the good, other factors being constant. Therefore, relatively more passengers would choose business class. The proportion of passengers choosing business class would increase.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Some online stores charge customers a shipping fee for each order, regardless of the quantity of goods purchased.
'An increase in the shipping fee will raise the average quantity of goods purchased per order from these online stores.' Explain the above phenomenon using the law of demand.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
The law of demand states that the lower the price of a good, the greater its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	(2 marks)
When the shipping fee increases, large-quantity orders become relatively cheaper than small-quantity orders. The relative price of large-quantity orders in terms of small-quantity orders decreases. People will place more large-quantity orders relative to small-quantity orders, resulting in an increase in the average quantity of goods per order.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
A restaurant has long queues for lunch. However, the waiting time decreases after the restaurant sets up a counter for takeaway customers.
Explain, with the law of demand, how the introduction of a takeaway counter affects the average order amount at the restaurant.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
The law of demand states that the lower the price of a good, the greater its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	(2 marks)
The introduction of a takeaway counter lowers the time cost of queueing at the restaurant. This lowers the relative price of small orders in terms of large orders. People will place more small orders relative to large orders, lowering the average order amount.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose the same unit surcharge is imposed on every imported mobile phone. Explain the following with the law of demand.
(a)	The change in the number of mobile phones imported	(2 marks)
(b)	The change in the average quality of mobile phones imported	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	As the surcharge will increase the price of imported mobile phones, the quantity demanded of imported mobile phones decreases. Thus, the number of mobile phones that are imported decreases.	(2 marks)
(b)	After the surcharge is imposed, the relative price of high-quality imported mobile phones in terms of low-quality imported mobile phones decreases. Consumers tend to buy relatively more high-quality imported mobile phones, improving the quality of mobile phones imported.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
To attract customers, shops usually offer discounts on selected goods. Evaluate the following two discounts in terms of the effect on the total number of customers and the average quality of goods sold.
(a)	A 20% discount	(4 marks)
(b)	A lump-sum discount of $100 for items priced over $500	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Total number of customers increases when the price is lowered.	(2 marks)
	Average quality of goods sold remains unchanged as the relative price between high-quality goods and low-quality goods remains unchanged.	(2 marks)
(b)	Total number of customers increases as the price for items priced over $500 is lowered.	(2 marks)
	Average quality of goods sold decreases as the relative price of low-quality goods in terms of high-quality goods decreases.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text: Compared with local residents, tourists tend to consume higher priced wonton noodles (雲吞麵). Explain this phenomenon using the law of demand.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
The law of demand states that the lower the price of a good, the greater its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	(2 marks)
The travelling cost of tourists is higher than those for local residents. Therefore, the relative price of higher priced wonton noodles (in terms of lower priced wonton noodles) is lower for tourists. Tourists tend to consume higher priced wonton noodles.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The problem of obesity (癡肥) in Country U is serious. Many people suffer from illnesses due to their weight. As fast food is very popular in the country, many international fast food chains want to open branches there. Seeing fast food as the major cause of obesity, the government has imposed a fixed surcharge on each set of meals sold in fast food restaurants.
(a)	What method does Country U use to tackle the basic economic problems? Explain.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose a fast food restaurant sells a standard pizza and a large pizza (which is more expensive). How does the average size of pizzas sold at the restaurant change after the imposition of the fixed surcharge?	(6 marks)
(c)	By the law of demand, explain how the surcharge helps alleviate the problem of obesity.	(4 marks)
(d)	After a few years, people in Country U become more cautious about their diets and less interested in fast food. How does Country U's fast food market change?
				(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)		The market mechanism has been used in the country since international fast food chains opened branches there to pursuit higher profit.	(2 marks)

(b)	The price of a large pizza is higher than the price of a standard pizza.	(1 mark)
	After the imposition of the fixed surcharge, the percentage increase in the price of the large pizza is smaller than the percentage increase in the price of a standard pizza.		(2 marks)
	The relative price of a large pizza (in terms of standard pizzas) decreases.
				(1 mark)
	According to the law of demand, relatively more large pizzas are sold.	(1 mark)
	Hence, the average size of pizzas sold in the restaurant increases.	(1 mark)

(c)	The surcharge increases the price of fast food.	(1 mark)
	According to the law of demand, the quantity demanded of fast food decreases when the price increases.	(2 marks)
	Hence, since less fast food is consumed, the obesity problem will improve.
				(1 mark)

(d)	The event will decrease the demand for fast food. Both the market price and quantity transacted of fast food will decrease.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The following shows Ming's demand schedule for Good X.

 Unit price ($)	50	100	150	200	250

(a)	Is Ming's demand schedule consistent with the law of demand? Explain.	 (4 marks)

50	375	330	450

	(i)	Suppose the market consists of only four buyers: Ming, Joan, Joe and Jane. Draw a table showing the market demand schedule.	(4 marks)
* (ii)	Based on your answers in parts (a) and (b)(i), must every person's individual demand satisfy the law of demand for the law of demand to hold for the market demand?	(4 marks)
(c)	The following is an importing firm's supply schedule for Good X.

 Unit price ($)	50	100	150	200	250	
 Quantity supplied (units)	900	1,065	1,230	1,395	1,560	
	
	(i)	Explain if the importing firm's behaviour is consistent with the law of supply.		(4 marks)
	(ii)	Suppose the firm is the only supplier of Good X. Find the equilibrium price and equilibrium quantity of Good X.	(2 marks)

questions.answerText:
(a)	•	No. The law of demand states that the lower (higher) the price of a good, the greater (smaller) its quantity demanded, other factors being constant.	 	(2 marks)

(b)	(i)
 Unit price ($)	50	100	150	200	250	
 Market quantity demanded (units)	1,455	1,065	945	720	540	
	 (4 marks)

(c)	(i)	•	Yes. The law of supply states that the higher (lower) the price of a good, the greater (smaller) its quantity supplied, other factors being constant.		(2 marks)

 Unit price ($)	50	100	150	200	250

questions.topic: B1 · Ch103 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
It is popular for families in Country A to hire domestic helpers to do the housework. In general, there are two types of domestic helpers: foreign domestic helpers (外籍家庭傭工) and local domestic helpers (本地家務助理).  
(a)	Define opportunity cost.	 (2 marks)
(b)	Use the concept of opportunity cost to explain why some families hire domestic helpers to do the housework.	(4 marks)
(c)	The following table shows the average prices (wages) of foreign domestic helpers and local domestic helpers in Country A: 

Year	Average wages (per month)	
	Local domestic helpers	Foreign domestic helpers	
1999	$5,500	$5,000	
2014	$3,000	$2,500	
 
(i)	What were the changes in the nominal wage of local and foreign domestic helpers between 1999 and 2014?	(4 marks)
(ii)	What was the change in the relative wages of local domestic helpers (in terms of foreign domestic helpers) between 1999 and 2014?	(3 marks)
(d)	Suppose the government of Country A provided a fixed $100 cash subsidy (津貼) to families who hire domestic helpers, regardless of their nationality. The average wages of local and foreign domestic helpers become $2,900 and $2,400, respectively. Assuming that each family only employs one domestic helper, apply the law of demand to explain
	(i)	the change in the quantity demanded of domestic helpers;	(2 marks)
	(ii)	the ratio of local domestic helpers to foreign domestic helpers employed.		(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Opportunity cost is the highest-valued option forgone.	(2 marks)
(b)	•	The cost of family members doing the housework themselves includes the income forgone from being employed, while the cost of hiring domestic helpers to do the housework is the amount paid for domestic helpers.
	 (2 marks)
	•	If the cost of doing housework themselves (the amount of income forgone) is greater than the cost of hiring domestic helpers (the amount paid for the domestic helpers), these families may hire domestic helpers to do the housework.	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	•	Nominal wages are wages measured in terms of money. The nominal average wage of local domestic helpers decreased by $2,500 (= $5,500 － $3,000) between 1999 and 2014.	(2 marks)
		•	The nominal wages of foreign domestic helpers decreased by $2,500 (= $5,000 － $2,500) between 1999 and 2014.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	Relative wage is the wage of a worker expressed in terms of another worker.	(1 mark)
		•	The relative wage of local domestic helpers (in terms of foreign domestic helpers) increased from 1.1 (= $5,500 / $5,000) in 1999 to 1.2 (= $3,000 / $2,500) in 2014.	(2 marks)

(d)	(i)	From the viewpoint of the households, the cash subsidy lowers the wage of domestic helpers, thus according to the law of demand, the quantity demanded of domestic helpers increases, holding other factors constant.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	After providing a cash subsidy, the relative wage of local domestic helpers in terms of foreign domestic helpers increases from 1.2 to 1.21.	(1 mark)
		•	Since the relative price of local domestic helpers increases, households will hire relatively less local domestic helpers.	(1 mark)
		•	Therefore, the ratio of local domestic helpers to foreign domestic helpers employed decreases.	(1 mark)
		OR
		•	After providing a cash subsidy, the relative wage of foreign domestic helpers in terms of local domestic helpers decreases from 0.833 to 0.828.
				 (1 mark)
		•	Since the relative price of foreign domestic helpers decreases, households will hire relatively more foreign domestic helpers.	(1 mark)
		•	Therefore, the ratio of local domestic helpers to foreign domestic helpers employed decreases.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following factors will affect the demand for Samsung smartphones?
(1)	A change in people's income
(2)	A change in the price of iPhones
(3)	A change in the price of Samsung smartphones
(4)	A change in the production cost of smartphones
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(2) and (3) only
C.	(3) and (4) only
D.	(1), (2), (3) and (4)
questions.answerText:
:
•	Options (1) and (2) affect the demand for Samsung smartphones.
•	Option (3) affects the quantity demanded of Samsung smartphones only.
•	Option (4) has nothing to do with the demand for Samsung smartphones. It affects the supply of all smartphones, including Samsung smartphones.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose the demand curve for a tour package to Korea is downward sloping. Which of the following CANNOT be constant when we move from one point to another on the demand curve?
A.	The price of the tour package to Korea
B.	The price of a tour package to Japan
C.	People's income
D.	The price of a travel guidebook to Korea
questions.answerText:
:
A good's demand curve shows the relationship between the price and quantity demanded of the good, assuming other factors remain unchanged. questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Cocoa is a major ingredient of chocolate. In recent years, the cocoa harvest was adversely affected by severe droughts in cocoa growing countries in West Africa. As a result,
A.	the supply of chocolate milk would decrease.
B.	the quantity demanded of chocolate bars would increase.
C.	the demand for chocolate bars would decrease.
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText:
:
When the cocoa harvest decreased in West Africa, the world supply of cocoa decreased. As a result, the price of cocoa would increase. Since cocoa is an ingredient used to make chocolate milk and chocolate bars, the cost of producing them would increase. The supply of chocolate milk and chocolate bars would then decrease. Therefore, only Option A is correct.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
The following diagrams show the effect of an increase in the price of Good X on Good Y.

Good X and Good Y are most likely __________ and ___________, respectively.
A.	mutton (羊肉) … pork
B.	roast goose (燒鵝) … goose down (鵝絨)
C.	computer games … computers
D.	milk … cheese
questions.answerText:
:
(	In the above diagrams, an increase in the price of Good X leads to an increase in the quantity supplied of Good X and an increase in the supply of Good Y. This is a case of joint supply.
(	Option A refers to a case of competitive demand.
(	Computer games and computers are complements. Therefore, the two goods in Option C are in joint demand.
(	In Option D, milk is an input for cheese. When the price of milk increases, the supply of cheese will decrease.
(	In slaughtering geese for roasting, goose down is collected at the same time. Therefore, the goods in Option B are in joint supply.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following will lead to an increase in the supply of gasoline?
A.	An increase in the price of crude oil (原油).
B.	A decrease in the price of jet fuel (航空煤油).
C.	A war occurring in the Middle East.
D.	A new cost-saving method of producing gasoline is discovered.
questions.answerText:
:
(	An increase in the price of crude oil (Option A) will increase the cost of producing gasoline. Therefore, the supply of gasoline will decrease.
(	A decrease in the price of jet fuel (Option B) will lower the quantity supplied of jet fuel. Since jet fuel and gasoline are in joint supply, the supply of gasoline will decrease too.
(	Wars in the Middle East (Option C) will disrupt oil production there. Therefore, the supply of crude oil and gasoline will decrease.
(	The new cost-saving production method will lead to a lower production cost of gasoline. Therefore, the supply of gasoline will increase. Option D is the answer.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
* Which of the following will lead to a rightward shift of the supply curve for residential units in Hong Kong?
A.	There is a fall in people's income.

C.	Property developers expect the price of property to fall in the future.
D.	Property developers give discounts to married couples who purchase property for the first time.
questions.answerText:
:
(	A fall in people's incomes will lead to a fall in the demand for residential units only.
(	The fact that more people can migrate to Hong Kong by investing in property in Hong Kong will only raise the demand for residential units in Hong Kong. 
(	The discounts given by property developers to these couples will only raise the quantity demanded of residential units in Hong Kong.
(	If property developers expect property prices to fall in future, they will supply more flats now. Hence, the supply of residential units increases.

questions.answerText:
:

(	In Option B, a decrease in the price of laptops with built-in equipment for wireless internet connection will increase the quantity demanded of these types of laptops. Since these types of laptops and wireless internet service are complements for each other, the demand for wireless internet service will increase. Therefore, there will be more usage of wireless internet service.
(	If the government provides free Wi-Fi service at more spots, using wireless internet service will be more convenient than before. As a result, the demand for wireless internet service will increase. There will be more usage of wireless internet service.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
It is a European tradition to have turkey (火雞) for Christmas dinner. In the winter of 2014, there was an outbreak of avian influenza in Europe. Much poultry was destroyed. It was found that the price of turkey in Europe increased during Christmas. Which of the following can explain this?
A.	The demand for turkeys increased.
B.	The supply of turkeys decreased.
C.	The increase in demand was greater than the decrease in supply.
D.	Both the increase in demand and the decrease in supply contributed to the increase in the price.
questions.answerText:
:
(	After the outbreak of avian influenza, some turkeys were destroyed and the supply of turkeys decreased. On the other hand, the demand for turkeys increased during Christmas. 
(	Both the increase in demand and the decrease in supply would contribute to a rise in price. Hence, the effect on price does not depend on the magnitudes of the increase in demand and the decrease in supply.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Nowadays, Hong Kong parents are more willing to spend on their children's study tours. Moreover, more firms are providing study tours for children in Hong Kong. Which of the following statements is correct?
A.	The price of study tours will increase.
B.	The price of study tours will decrease.
C.	The quantity transacted of study tours will increase.
D.	The quantity transacted of study tours will decrease.
questions.answerText:
:
(	Since Hong Kong parents are more willing to send their children on study tours, the demand for study tours increases. On the other hand, an increase in the number of firms providing study tours will increase the supply of study tours. 
(	The increases in both demand and supply will lead to an increase in quantity transacted. Therefore, the quantity transacted of study tours will increase. 
(	On the other hand, an increase in demand tends to increase price whereas an increase in supply tends to decrease price. Therefore, the combined effect on the equilibrium price is uncertain, depending on the relative magnitudes of the two effects.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
* Suppose the government has imposed stricter regulations on the beauty industry. Slimming companies are required to employ doctors to monitor and carry out the therapies. However, the price of slimming therapies has decreased. Which of the following can explain this?
A.	Slimming companies have installed better quality equipment.
B.	People are more concerned about their body shape.
C.	After several accidents related to slimming therapies, people are afraid of these therapies and the resultant change in demand is greater than the change in supply.
D.	The government has banned TV advertisements for slimming companies and the resultant change in demand is smaller than the change in supply.
questions.answerText:
:
(	Stricter regulations will lower the supply of slimming therapies. An increase in the quality of equipment (Option A) will drive up production costs and further decrease the supply. The decrease in supply will increase the price.
(	Option B has the effect of increasing demand. The increase in demand will increase the price.
(	In Option C, fear about the therapies will decrease the demand. Only when the decrease in demand is greater than the decrease in supply will the price increase. Therefore, Option C is correct.
(	In Option D, the ban on TV advertisements will lower the demand for the therapies. However, when the decrease in demand is smaller than the decrease in supply, the price will increase. Therefore, Option D is incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
* Suppose the price of imported Blu-ray discs increases while the quantity supplied decreases. Which of the following can explain this?
	(1)	There is an improvement in the technology of Blu-ray disc production.
	(2)	There is a fall in the price of Blu-ray disc players.
	(3)	More people love to watch movies.
	(4)	There is an increase in the production cost of Blu-ray discs.
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(4) only
questions.answerText:
:
(	(1) will increase the supply of Blu-ray discs. Hence, the price will decrease while the quantity supplied will increase.
(	(2) will increase the quantity demanded of Blu-ray disc players. Since Blu-ray disc players and Blu-ray discs are complements, the demand for Blu-ray discs will increase. Hence, both the price and quantity supplied will increase. In equilibrium, quantity transacted = quantity demanded = quantity supplied.
(	(3) will increase the demand for Blu-ray discs. Hence, both the price and quantity supplied will increase.
(	(4) will reduce the supply of Blu-ray discs. Hence, the price will increase while the quantity supplied will decrease. Option D is the answer.

In Hong Kong, it was reported that many university graduates could not find jobs in the education sector; while there was a labour shortage in the engineering sector. Which of the following measures can reduce unemployment in the education sector?

	(2)	Increasing the wage rate in the engineering sector
	(3)	The government implements a small-class teaching policy. 
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
:
(	(1) increases the cost of being a teacher, therefore, the labour supply in the education sector decreases.
(	(2) will also reduce labour supply in the education sector.
(	(3) will increase labour demand in the education sector.
(	At the same wage rate, (1), (2) and (3) will reduce the amount of the excess supply of labour in the education sector. Therefore, (1), (2) and (3) will reduce unemployment in the education sector.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose the price of Android phones decreases.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the effects on the price and quantity transacted of Android applications.	(5 marks)
(b)	With the aid of another diagram, explain the effects on the price and quantity transacted of iPhones.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Rightward shift in demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Increases in price and quantity transacted	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
	Android phones and Android applications are complements.	(1 mark)
	When the price of Android phones decreases, the demand for Android applications increases from D1 to D2.	(1 mark)
	Hence, the price increases from P1 to P2 and the quantity transacted increases from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:

	(	Decreases in price and quantity transacted	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
	Android phones and iPhones are substitutes.	(1 mark)
	When the price of Android phones decreases, the demand for iPhones decreases from D3 to D4.	(1 mark)
	Hence, the price decreases from P3 to P4 and the quantity transacted decreases from Q3 to Q4.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Farmer A says, 'When the price of beef increases, people will buy less of it.'
Farmer B says, 'No, I cannot agree with you. What I observed was that the price of beef and the quantity bought increase at the same time.'
Explain with the aid of separate diagrams why both of them can be correct.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
(	Farmer A refers to a movement along a demand curve.	(1 mark)
(	Law of demand: When the price of beef increases, the quantity demanded of beef decreases, ceteris paribus.	(1 mark)

		(2 marks)

(	Farmer B refers to increases in the demand for beef.	(1 mark)
(	When there is an increase in the demand for beef, both the equilibrium price and the quantity transacted increase.	(1 mark)

		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
A citizen says, 'When the price of flats decreases, more people will buy flats.'
A government official says, 'Recently, the property market has been buoyant (行情看漲). Both the price and the quantity transacted of flats have increased.'
Can both of them be correct?	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(	The citizen refers to a movement along a demand curve.	(1 mark)
(	Law of demand: When the price of flats decreases, the quantity demanded for flats increases, ceteris paribus. 	(1 mark)
(	The government official refers to an increase in the demand for flats.	(1 mark)
(	When there is an increase in the demand for flats, both the price and the quantity transacted increase.	(1 mark)
(	Therefore, the two statements refer to two different situations and can both be correct.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Peter says, 'When the price of Good X increases, the price of Good Y increases.'
Mary says, 'I find something contradictory. When the price of Good A increases, the price of Good B decreases.'
Is there any contradiction between the findings of Peter and Mary? Explain.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(	No, there is no contradiction between the observations made by them.	(1 mark)
(	Peter's finding refers to the case where Good X and Good Y are substitutes for each other.	 (1 mark)
(	When the price of Good X increases, the quantity demanded of Good X decreases; people substitute Good Y for Good X and the demand for Good Y increases, leading to an increase in the price of Good Y (two separate diagrams explaining the same situation should also be accepted).	 (2 marks)
(	Mary's finding refers to the case where Good A and Good B are complements.				(1 mark)
(	When the price of Good A increases, the quantity demanded of Good A decreases; people at the same time buy less of Good B and the demand for Good B decreases, leading to a drop in the price of Good B (two separate diagrams explaining the same situation should also be accepted).	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Fun says, 'When my wage rate increases, I will buy more of Good A.'
Keung says, 'When my wage rate increases, I will buy less of Good A.'
Does Fun's and Keung's behaviour violate the law of demand? Explain.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(	Their behaviour does not violate the law of demand.	(1 mark)
(	To Fun, Good A is a normal good. Her demand for Good A will increase when her wage income increases.	(2 marks)
(	To Keung, Good A is an inferior good. His demand for Good A will decrease when his wage income increases.	(2 marks)
OR
(	Law of demand: When the price of a good increases (decreases), its quantity demanded decreases (increases), ceteris paribus.	(2 marks)
(	What they refer to is the relationship between wage rate and quantity demanded.		(2 marks)
(	Therefore, their behaviour does not violate the law of demand.	(1 mark)
(Accept other reasonable explanations.)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Country P was an ancient empire. Every time Country P conquered a nation, it enslaved people in the defeated nation. Slaveholders (奴隸主) could trade slaves in the market.

	Do you agree with him? Explain briefly.	(3 marks)
(b)	Many slaves worked as rice farmers in Country P. If the population in Country P increased, explain briefly how the equilibrium price and quantity of slaves would change.	(3 marks)
(c)	An industrial revolution took place in Country P. The use of machines became more common in production. At the same time, a number of conquered nations successfully revolted against the rule of Country P and gained independence. With the aid of a diagram, explain under what circumstances the price of slaves in Country P would decrease. 	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.			(1 mark)
	Although the rich man did not have to pay wages, he had to satisfy the slave's basic needs (e.g., giving him food) to keep him alive and working. So, costs were involved.	(2 marks)

(b)	When the population increased, the demand for rice increased.	(1 mark)
	The demand for slaves increased because it was derived from the demand for rice.					(1 mark)
	Both the equilibrium price and quantity of slaves would increase.	(1 mark)

(c)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift in demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Leftward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Decreases in price	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	When more machines were used in production, the demand for slaves decreased from D0 to D1.	(1 mark)

questions.text:

questions.text:

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:

questions.answerText:

			(2 marks)
	(	Since the assumption of ceteris paribus does not hold, this does not violate the law of supply.	(2 marks)

(c)	(	Quantity transacted refers to the quantity actually bought and sold while quantity supplied refers to the quantity sellers plan to sell.	(2 marks)
	(	When the market price is at or below equilibrium (( P0), the quantity transacted is equal to the quantity supplied.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch104 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:

questions.answerText:
:
(	
( % change in quantity demanded = Ed × % change in price

Option A is the answer.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch105 · Price elasticity of demand and supply

2	500	
4	500

questions.answerText:
:
(	Since her total expenditure does not change with the price, her demand must be unitarily elastic.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch105 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:

questions.answerText:

questions.topic: B1 · Ch105 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose when Genki Sushi raises the unit price of its sushi from $10 to $12, its quantity transacted decreases by 50%. Which of the following statements about this is correct?
A.	The percentage decrease in quantity transacted is smaller than the percentage increase in price. 
B.	The seller can increase total revenue by increasing the price.
C.	The elasticity of demand for its sushi is -2.78.
D.	A fall in price will lead to a less than proportionate increase in quantity transacted.
questions.answerText:
:
(	The percentage change in price is 18% (). Option A is incorrect.
(	Since the percentage change in quantity transacted is -50%, the elasticity of demand is -50% / 18% = -2.78. Option C is the answer. 
(	When demand is elastic, a price change will lead to a more than proportionate change in quantity demanded. Option D is incorrect. 
(	When demand is elastic, total revenue changes inversely with price. Therefore, the seller cannot increase total revenue by increasing the price. Option B is incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch105 · Price elasticity of demand and supply

D.	The demand for diamonds is inelastic.
questions.answerText:
:
(	The discovery of a huge deposit of diamonds will increase the supply of diamonds. When the supply increases, the price decreases. Moreover, quantity transacted, which is equal to quantity demanded and quantity supplied at equilibrium, increases. Options A and B are incorrect.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch105 · Price elasticity of demand and supply

questions.answerText:
:
(	Since Shakespeare has passed away, the supply of his poems is perfectly inelastic.

questions.answerText:
:

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Study the following data for luncheon meat (午餐肉) imported from the mainland:

Unit price ($)	4	8	12	16	20	24		Quantity supplied (cans)	1,000	2,000	3,000	4,000	5,000	6,000		Quantity demanded (cans)	5,000	4,000	3,000	2,000	1,000	0

B.	$36,000
C.	$48,000
D.	$64,000
questions.answerText:
:

Therefore, the quantity transacted and the market price remain the same at 3,000 cans and $12, respectively. Total revenue = $12 × 3,000 = $36,000.

The amount of time that customers need to wait to buy an iPhone 6 will be longer if 
A.	Apple employs more factories to produce the iPhone 6.
B.	the price of the iPhone 6 Plus increases.
C.	many users complain about the camera on the iPhone 6.
D.	retailers increase the price of the iPhone 6.
questions.answerText:
:

Option B: iPhone 6 Plus is a close substitute for the iPhone 6. Thus, when the price of the iPhone 6 Plus increases, the demand for the iPhone 6 will increase. This will increase  excess demand and  the waiting time.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
To combat inflation (通脹), suppose the Hong Kong Government imposes an effective price ceiling on food imported from the mainland. Which of the following are possible consequences?
	(1)	The equilibrium price of imported food decreases.
	(2)	The quantity of food imported decreases.
	(3)	A black market may emerge in which people pay a price higher than the legal maximum.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
:
If the government imposes an effective price ceiling on imported food from the mainland, the market price rather than the equilibrium price will decrease. Moreover, the quantity imported will decrease. At the reduced quantity imported, consumers are willing to pay a price higher than the legal maximum, so a black market may emerge.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
If a government removes an effective price ceiling on rental housing, which of the following will increase?
	(1)	The equilibrium rent
	(2)	The number of rental transactions
	(3)	Rental income for landlords as a whole
A.	(2) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
:
If a government removes an effective price ceiling on rental housing, the market rent will increase back to its equilibrium level, which is not affected by the imposition or removal of the price ceiling. The quantity transacted will also increase back to its original equilibrium level. Since both the market price and quantity transacted increase, total rental income will increase.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Suppose the demand for red wine is perfectly inelastic. If the government imposes an effective maximum price on red wine, which of the following is correct?
