B.	The market price of red wine will remain unchanged.
C.	Consumers will spend less on red wine overall.
D.	The quality of red wine will increase.
questions.answerText:
:
If the government imposes an effective price ceiling on red wine, both the market price and the quantity transacted will decrease. Options A and B are not correct.
Since both the market price and the quantity transacted decrease, the total expenditure on red wine will decrease. Option C is correct.
At the controlled price level, red wine sellers do not have an incentive to improve the quality of red wine. Option D is not correct.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
To prevent the price of rice from rising to an unaffordable level, the government imposes a price ceiling on rice. It has been reported that rice is often sold out. Which of the following can alleviate (減輕) this problem?
A.	Raising the price ceiling
B.	Lowering the price ceiling
C.	Increasing the quality
D.	Increasing the price of noodles
questions.answerText:
:
If the rice is often sold out, the price ceiling must have been set at a level below the equilibrium price so as to create excess demand. To reduce excess demand, we can increase the price to its equilibrium level. However, increasing the quality and increasing the price of noodles will only increase the demand and, hence, excess demand for the rice.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
In 2013, a Japanese ramen (拉麫) restaurant opened its first branch in Hong Kong. Despite the hot weather, customers queued for up to four hours to try the ramen during the first few days after the restaurant opened. Which of the following can explain this phenomenon?
A.	The restaurant must be very small.
B.	The ramen must be very delicious.
C.	The price of the ramen must be set below the equilibrium level. 
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText:
:
Since long queues formed outside the restaurant, there was excess demand for the ramen and the price must have been set at a level below the equilibrium level. Options A and B would not lead to excess demand for the ramen if the price were set at the corresponding equilibrium levels.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
In 2013, a Japanese ramen (拉麫) restaurant opened its first branch in Hong Kong. Despite the hot weather, customers queued for up to four hours to try the ramen during the first few days after the restaurant opened. Which of the following could reduce customers' waiting time?
A.	The restaurant improves the service quality of the waiters.
B.	The restaurant raises the price of its ramen.
C.	The restaurant reduces the number of seats.
D.	The restaurant airs a TV advertisement.
questions.answerText:
:
Options A and D: Improving the service quality and advertising on TV will increase  demand and excess demand, making the waiting time even longer. Option C: Reducing the number of seats means a decrease in the supply. This will also increase  excess demand, making the waiting time even longer than it was.
Option B: Raising the price can reduce the quantity demanded, thus decreasing the excess demand and the waiting time. So Option B is the answer.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Which of the following causes the quantity demanded of a good to be larger than its quantity transacted?
A.	The market price is fixed below the equilibrium level.
B.	The market price is fixed at the equilibrium level.
C.	The market price is fixed above the equilibrium level.
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText:
:
Whenever quantity demanded is not equal to quantity supplied, the quantity transacted is equal to the smaller of the two quantities. In this question, the quantity transacted must be equal to the quantity supplied. As the quantity demanded is larger than the quantity supplied, the market price must be fixed below the equilibrium level. It is also important to note that neither Qd nor Qs can be smaller than the quantity transacted.

The following table shows the demand and supply schedules of imported labour:

questions.text:
* An economic researcher comes up with the following data about Good X:

Price ($)	10	12	14	16	18	
Quantity transacted (units)	100	200	300	250	200	

If the demand curve for Good X is downward-sloping and the supply curve for it is upward-sloping, what is the equilibrium price?
A.	$10
B.	$12
C.	$14
D.	$16
questions.answerText:
:
At the equilibrium price (Pe), Qd = Qs = Qt, given that demand curve is downward sloping and supply curve is upward sloping. When the market price is above the equilibrium price, Qd falls while Qs rises; Qt equals Qd because whenever Qd is not equal to Qs, Qt is equal to the smaller of the two quantities. Similarly, when the market price is smaller than the equilibrium price, Qd rises while Qs falls; Qt equals Qs. Hence, Qt is the largest at the equilibrium price. Therefore, the equilibrium price from the above table is the one with the largest Qt, i.e., $14.

questions.text:
* The government has imposed a quota on the number of taxi licences in Hong Kong. Suppose the taxi fare remains unchanged. Which of the following will occur when the economy turns bad?
	(1)	Taxi drivers' total income will decrease
	(2)	There will be a surplus of taxi services
	(3)	The price of taxi licences will decrease
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
:
Option (3) is correct. When the income generated from a taxi licence decreases, the demand for taxi licences will decrease. As a result, the price of taxi licences will decrease.

questions.text:

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Suppose the European Union decreases the quota for textile products from China. Which of the following statements is correct?
A.	The price of Chinese textile products in Europe decreases.
B.	The price of European textile products in Europe increases. 
C.	The quantity of Chinese textile products imported into Europe increases.
D.	If the demand for European textile products in Europe is inelastic, European consumers' expenditure on European textile products will decrease.
questions.answerText:
:
When the European Union decreases the quota for textile products from China, the supply curve changes from Sq1 to Sq2. The price will increase from P1 to P2. On the other hand, the quantity imported of Chinese textile products decreases from Q1 to Q2. Since European textile products are close substitutes for Chinese textile products, an increase in the price of the latter will result in an increase in the demand for the former, leading to the increase in the price, the quantity transacted and consumers' expenditure on European textile products.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT an effect of an increase in the quota of imported professionals from the mainland?
A.	The market wage rate of these imported professional falls.
B.	If the demand for these imported professionals is elastic, total income for them will increase.
C.	The wage rate of local professionals falls.
D.	The employment of these professionals decreases.
questions.answerText:
:
When there is an increase in the quota of imported professionals from the mainland, the supply curve changes from Sq1 to Sq2. The wage rate of these professionals decreases while their employment increases. Moreover, since these professionals are close substitutes for local professionals, the demand for local professionals decreases and leads to a fall in their wage rate. The change in the total income for these professionals depends on the elasticity of demand for them. If the demand is elastic, their total income will increase.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:

questions.answerText:

	(	Increase in price and decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	(	Increase in total expenditure < Decrease in total expenditure	(2 marks)

	The price increases from P1 to P2 and the quantity transacted decreases from Q1 to Q2.			(2 marks)

questions.text:
Suppose the government of Thailand announces a rice support programme. questions.answerText:

questions.text:

	(2 marks)

(d)	Coal is commonly used to produce electricity in China. If there is no price ceiling, how will the price for electricity change when the price for coal increases? Explain your answer with the aid of a diagram.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Price ceiling below the equilibrium price	(1 mark)
(	Shortage at the price ceiling	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
The price ceiling will create a shortage of electricity. As the quantity demanded is greater that the quantity supplied, some factories cannot obtain enough electricity.	(2 marks)

(b)	Since both the price and quantity transacted decrease, the total revenue decreases.			(2 marks)

(c)	During hot summers, the demand for electricity increases (e.g., more people use air conditioners) and so the excess demand for electricity increases.	(2 marks)

(d)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Supply curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
(	Price increases and the quantity transacted decreases.	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
	(	When the price for coal increases, the cost of generating electricity increases. Thus, the supply of electricity will decrease.	(2 marks)
	(	The electricity price will increase from P1 to P2 and the quantity transacted will decrease from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
There are three cross-harbour tunnels in Hong Kong. They are the Cross-Harbour Tunnel, the Western Harbour Tunnel and the Eastern Harbour Tunnel. Suppose the government plans to construct a fourth cross-harbour tunnel.

questions.answerText:

	(	Traffic congestion increases travel time and hence the value of the highest-valued option forgone. So the cost of using the Cross-Harbour Tunnel will increase.	(2 marks)

(b)	The utilisation rate of the Western Harbour Crossing is far below its maximum capacity because the toll is set above the equilibrium. Hence, excess supply exists.				(2 marks)
		(2 marks)

(c)	(	Since the Eastern Harbour Crossing is at equilibrium, lowering the toll will result in a shortage (Q2 - Q1). 	(2 marks)
	(	The utilisation rate will remain unchanged (Q1). Therefore, a decrease in toll will lower the total revenue from P1 × Q1 to P2 × Q1.	(2 marks)

		(2 marks)

questions.answerText:
(a)	(	As many visitors went to Incheon, the demand for hotel accommodation increased (D0 ( D1).	(1 mark)
	
				(2 marks)
	(	Both the rental rate and the quantity transacted would increase.	(1 mark)
	(	Therefore, the total rental income would increase.	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	(	Since the fixed ticket price (P0) of some unpopular games was above the equilibrium (P1),	(1 mark)
		(	there would be excess supply, i.e., vacant seats  (= Q1 - Q0).	(1 mark)
		(2 marks)

		(	there would be excess demand, i.e., people asked for more tickets 
(= Q2 - Q1).	(1 mark)
		(2 marks)

			(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Sochi (索契), in Russia, hosted the Winter Olympic Games in 2014. Many people visited Sochi during that period. This led to a drastic increase in the demand for hotel accommodation in Sochi.

questions.answerText:
(a)	(	Since the supply of hotel accommodation was fixed, the supply curve was vertical at the fixed quantity (Q0).	(1 mark)
		Since the rental rate was fixed and uniform, the increase in demand (D0(D1) would lead to excess demand (= Q1 - Q0).	(2 marks)
		(3 marks)

(b)	(i)	(	Because the event would decrease the demand for hotel accommodation.					(1 mark)

					(3 marks)
(	Since the supply and rental rate were both fixed, there would be excess supply, i.e., vacant rooms might be found (= Q0 - Q2).	(2 marks)
	(ii)	(	Agree. When the rental rate is determined by market demand and supply, the decrease in demand will cause the rental rate to decrease to P2.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch106 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Suppose the public's income has been falling in recent years and some people are urging the government to lower the effective minimum wage rate of foreign domestic helpers.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the effect of the proposed reduction in the minimum wage rate on the total income of foreign domestic helpers.	(6 marks)
(b)	What are the combined effects of the decline in the public's income and the fall in the minimum wage rate on the employment and the total income of foreign domestic helpers? Explain your answer.	(5 marks)
(c)	Suppose the government rejects the proposal to lower the minimum wage rate of foreign domestic helpers. On the other hand, local domestic helpers have agreed to a lower wage rate for their services.
	(i)	In what kind of demand are foreign domestic helpers and local domestic helpers?	(1 mark)
	(ii)	What are the effects of the fall in the wage rate of local domestic helpers on the employment and the total income of foreign domestic helpers? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(5 marks)
(d)	To solve the problem of the high unemployment rate among unskilled workers, a government official suggests retraining unskilled workers to become local domestic helpers. What are the effects of the retraining programme on the wage rate, employment and the total income of local domestic helpers? Briefly explain WITHOUT the aid of a diagram.	 (4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Suppose the government lowers the effective minimum wage rate from W0 to W1.
	(	The effect of lowering the minimum wage rate on the total income of foreign domestic helpers depends on the price elasticity of demand for them.	(2 marks)
	(	If the demand is elastic (Ed > 1), the lower wage rate will lead to an increase in total income. / If the demand is inelastic (Ed < 1), the lower wage rate will lead to a fall in total income. / If the demand is unitarily elastic (Ed = 1), the lower wage rate will not lead to any change in total income.	(Any ONE, 2 marks)
		
					(2 marks)

(b)	(	The fall in the public's income will reduce the demand for foreign domestic helpers.	(1 mark)
	(	The fall in the public's income will tend to decrease the employment of foreign domestic helpers while the fall in the minimum wage rate will tend to increase their employment.	(2 marks)
	(	The overall effect on employment is uncertain, depending on the magnitude of the reduction in demand and the fall in the minimum wage rate.	(1 mark)
	(	Thus, although the wage rate has fallen, the effect on total income is uncertain as the effect on employment is uncertain.	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	They are in competitive demand / substitute demand.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	(	The fall in the wage rate of local domestic helpers will reduce the demand for foreign domestic helpers (D0(D1).	(1 mark)
		(	As a result, the employment of foreign domestic helpers will fall (L0(L1).	(1 mark)
		(	Since the minimum wage rate remains unchanged at W0 and employment falls, the total income of foreign domestic helpers will fall.	(1 mark)

			(2 marks)

(d)	(	The retraining programme will increase the supply of local domestic helpers.			(1 mark)
	(	The wage rate of local domestic helpers will drop.	(1 mark)
	(	Employment will increase.	(1 mark)
	(	Thus, the effect on total income is uncertain, depending on the price elasticity of demand. 	(1 mark)

questions.text:
Refer to the following supply-demand diagram of a good. The equilibrium price is $26.

B.	2:3
C.	1:1
D.	2:1
questions.answerText:
:
After the imposition of the $12 unit tax, the supply curve shifts upward by $12. The market price will increase from $26 to $34. Hence, the amount of unit tax borne by consumers is $8. The amount of unit tax borne by producers is $4. As a result the ratio of the consumers' tax burden to the producers' tax burden = $8 : $4 = 2:1.

Refer to the following supply-demand diagram of a good. The equilibrium price is $80.

If the government provides a $20 unit subsidy on the good, what will be the ratio of the consumers' share of the subsidy to the producers' share of the subsidy?
A.	1:4
B.	2:3
C.	3:2
D.	4:1
questions.answerText:
:
After the provision of the $20 unit subsidy, the supply curve shifts downward by $20. The market price will decrease from $80 to $72. Hence, the amount of the unit subsidy enjoyed by consumers is $8. The amount of the unit subsidy enjoyed by producers is $12. As a result, the ratio of the consumers' share of the subsidy to the producers' share of the subsidy = $8 : $12 = 2:3.

questions.text:
Suppose parents' demand for textbooks is perfectly inelastic. If the government gives out a per-unit subsidy on textbooks, 
A.	the market price of textbooks will increase.
B.	the quantity transacted will increase.
C.	consumers get all the benefit of the subsidy.
D.	total revenue, including the subsidy, will decrease.
questions.answerText:
:
When the government gives out a per-unit subsidy to textbook producer, the market price will fall by the amount of the subsidy. However, the quantity transacted will remain unchanged. Consumers will get all the benefit as the price they pay decreases by the unit subsidy. Total revenue, including the subsidy, will remain unchanged as the fall in total revenue is fully compensated for the total amount of the subsidy.

questions.topic: B1 · Ch107 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
The problem of deforestation (濫伐林木) is serious in Country B. Therefore, the government imposes a unit tax on timber (木材).
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain how the unit tax can deal with the problem of deforestation.	(5 marks)
(b)	Some people think that other measures of government intervention in the timber market can also deal with the problem of deforestation. With reference to your diagram in (a), suggest TWO measures that can achieve the goal.	(2 marks)
(c)	Given that the demand for furniture is elastic. With the aid of another diagram, explain how the unit tax on timber affects the total expenditure on furniture.
				(7 marks)
(d)	Suppose there is an increase in the demand for timber. WITHOUT the aid of the diagram, explain how the tax revenue of the unit tax on timber will change.
				(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Upward shift of the supply curve by the amount of the unit tax	(1 mark)
	(	Increase in price and decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	Due to the unit tax, the supply of timber decreases from S0 to S1 by the amount of the unit tax.	(1 mark)
	The price increases and the quantity transacted decreases.	(1 mark)
	As the consumption of timber decreases, fewer trees will be cut down. Hence, the problem of deforestation can be alleviated.	(1 mark)

(b)	(	Setting a price ceiling at P2
	(	Setting a price floor at P1
	(	Setting a quota at Q1
	(Any TWO of the above. 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(c)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift of supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Increase in total expenditure < Decrease in total expenditure	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B1 · Ch107 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Country T exports shoes to foreign countries. Country T decides to provide a unit subsidy on its exported shoes. Shoe producers in importing countries object to this policy.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain under what condition shoe exporters in Country T will enjoy more of the subsidy than consumers in importing countries.	(6 marks)
(b)	With the aid of another diagram, explain how the export subsidy will affect the total revenue of shoe producers in the importing country.	(6 marks)
(c)	Suppose both high-quality shoes and low-quality shoes will be granted the same amount of the unit subsidy. Explain how the provision of the subsidy will affect the average quality of shoes exported from Country T.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Downward shift of supply curve by the amount of the unit subsidy	(1 mark)
	(	Decrease in price and increase in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	(	Consumers' share of subsidy < Producers' share of subsidy	(2 marks)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	If the demand for Country T's exported shoes is more elastic than the supply, shoe exporters in Country T will enjoy more of the subsidy than consumers in importing countries.	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift of demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Decrease in total revenue	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	The export subsidy will lower the price of Country T's shoes in importing countries.	(1 mark)
	As Country T's shoes and shoes produced in importing countries are close substitutes, the export subsidy will decrease the demand for shoes produced in importing countries.	(1 mark)
	Both the price and quantity transacted of shoes produced in importing countries will decrease.	(1 mark)
	Hence, the total revenue of shoe producers in importing countries will decrease.					(1 mark)

(c)	The price of high-quality shoes is higher than the price of low-quality shoes.					(1 mark)
	After the provision of the export subsidy, the percentage decrease in the price of high-quality shoes will be smaller than the percentage decrease in the price of low-quality shoes.	(2 marks)
	The relative price of high-quality shoes (in terms of low-quality shoes) will increase.	(1 mark)
	According to the law of demand, relatively fewer high-quality shoes will be exported.	(1 mark)
	Hence, the average quality of shoes exported from Country T will decrease.					(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch208 · Ownership of firms
questions.text: What are the TWO major forms of private ownership that have unlimited liability? Explain TWO differences between them.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Sole proprietorship and partnership	(2 marks)
The differences between them are as follows:
•	A sole proprietorship is owned by only one owner but a partnership is owned by more than one owner.
•	A partnership can have a wider scope of specialisation.
•	Partners bear collective responsibility and higher risks than sole proprietors.
•	Partners can have consultations among themselves, which may result in better decisions. However, consultations may delay decision making and decrease flexibility.
•	A sole proprietor can freely transfer his business but partners need to have the consent of all partners before the transfer of ownership.
•	A sole proprietor bears all the risks of his business and enjoys all the profit from it. Partners share the risks of loss as well as the profit.
(Any TWO of the above. 2 marks ( 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
When the percentage contribution of secondary production to the total value of production increases,
A.	the percentage contribution of primary production to the total value of production must decrease.
B.	the percentage contribution of tertiary production to the total value of production must decrease.
C.	the total percentage contribution of primary and tertiary production to the total value of production must decrease.
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
•	The total percentage contribution of the three types of production to the total value of production must add up to 100%. Therefore, when the percentage contribution of secondary production to the total value of production increases, the total percentage contribution of primary and tertiary production must decrease. 
Option C is the answer.
•	However, we cannot conclude that the percentage contribution of primary production or the percentage contribution of tertiary production must decrease. Options A and B are incorrect.

questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT an advantage of division of labour?

B.	Workers' productivity increases.
C. 	Total output increases.
D. 	Workers become more satisfied with their jobs.

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Which of the following is a disadvantage of specialisation?
A.	Required training time increases. 
B.	Workers have limited skills.
C.	The standard of living declines.
D.	The required expenditure on buying capital goods increases.

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Which of the following about specialisation is correct?
A.	It can stimulate workers' morale.
B.	It can make workers become more skilful at their jobs.
C.	It can cater to the needs of different consumers.
D.	It can enhance workers' job satisfaction.

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Which of the following can have the highest degree of division of labour?
A.	Singing a song
B.	Writing a novel
C.	Hunting a rabbit
D.	Making a car

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
For which of the following activities would it be most difficult to carry out division of labour?
A.	Making a pencil

C.	Playing football

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about division of labour is INCORRECT?
A.	Division of labour can increase the competitiveness of goods in the international market.
B.	The nature of products will affect the practice of division of labour
C.	Market size will affect the practice of division of labour.
D.	There must be a greater extent of division of labour when the market size increases.
questions.answerText: Sometimes complex division of labour is not practised even when the market size increases. This happens when production requires individual creativity. Option D is the answer.

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Which of the following statements is correct?
A.	A command economy cannot practise division of labour.

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	What is production?	(2 marks)
(b)	Mary sells fruit in her shop. In what type of production is she involved?	
				(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Production is an activity through which resources are transformed into goods and services.	(2 marks)

(b) Tertiary production	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	What is production?	(2 marks)
(b)	Peter, the monitor of class 5A, collects homework from his classmates for the teachers. Is there any production involved? Explain your answer.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Production is an activity through which resources are transformed into goods and services.	(2 marks)

(b) Yes, he provides homework collection services for teachers as well as classmates.				(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Explain whether the following activities belong to consumption or production.
(a)	Chi Wai represents the Hong Kong Football Team when it participates in a football match held in Britain.	(3 marks)
(b)	Chi Keung watches live football broadcasts at home.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Production	(1 mark)
	•	Because Chi Wai provides factor services to the Hong Kong Football Team.		(2 marks)

(b)	•	Consumption.	(1 mark)
	•	Because this can satisfy Chi Keung's wants of watching football matches.		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	A flower can be a consumer good. Explain with an example.	(2 marks)
(b)	A flower can also be a producer good. Explain with an example.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Consumer goods are goods used to satisfy wants. If a girl buys a flower for her enjoyment, the flower is a consumer good.	(2 marks)

(b)	Producer goods are goods used to help production. If a restaurant owner buys flowers to decorate the restaurant, the flowers are a producer good.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	What is a consumer good?	(2 marks)
(b)	Is a pineapple bun a consumer good or a producer good? Explain with examples.					(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A consumer good is a good used to satisfy wants.	(2 marks)

(b)	A pineapple bun can either be a consumer good or a producer good, depending on its uses:
	•	It is a consumer good if it is used to satisfy wants.	(1 mark)
		Any reasonable example, e.g., a hungry person buys a pineapple bun to eat.
				(1 mark)
	•	It is a producer good if it is used to help production.	(1 mark)
		Any reasonable example, e.g., a tea restaurant sells the pineapple bun for profits.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Agatha Christie was an English crime novelist. Some of her famous works include Murder on the Orient Express and Curtain.
(a)	People can borrow the books from the library for free. Are these books free goods?				(2 marks)
(b)	Give ONE example in which her novels would be capital goods.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A free good is something we prefer to have some of but not more of, but people want to have more of the books rather than less. Therefore, these books are economic goods, not free goods. 	(2 marks)
	
(b)	A hair salon owner buys the books to entertain customers.	(1 mark)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	What is a producer good?	(2 marks)
(b)	A car can either be a consumer good or a producer good. Explain with examples respectively.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A producer good is a good used to help production.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	A car is a consumer good if it is used to satisfy wants.	(1 mark)
		Any reasonable example, e.g., a car bought by an individual for the pleasure of driving	(1 mark)
	•	A car is a producer good if it is used to help production.	(1 mark)
		Any reasonable example, e.g., a car bought by a firm to transport people or goods	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	What is a consumer good?	(2 marks)
(b)	Is a fire engine a producer good or a consumer good? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A consumer good is a good used to satisfy wants.	(2 marks)

(b)	A fire engine can either be a producer good or a consumer good, depending on its uses:
	•	It is a producer good if it is used for firefighting.	(2 marks)
	•	It is a consumer good if it is used to satisfy wants, e.g., for collection and appreciation.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Classify the following two items into consumer goods and producer goods. Explain your answers.
(a)	Photocopiers at school	(3 marks)
(b)	Snacks at home	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Producer goods	(1 mark)
	•	They are used to help production, e.g., provide photocopying services for teachers and students to facilitate the provision of educational services.			(2 marks)

(b)	•	Consumer goods	(1 mark)
	•	They are used to satisfy wants, e.g., the desire for food or enjoyment from the way they taste.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Classify the following items into consumer goods and producer goods. Explain your answers.
(a)	Professional digital cameras at newspaper publishers	(3 marks)
(b)	Professional digital cameras at home	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Producer goods	(1 mark)
	•	They are used to help production, e.g., the taking of news photos.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	Consumer goods	(1 mark)
	•	They are used to satisfy wants, e.g., the pleasure of photography.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text: Everyone can use the law of demand. Explain whether the use of the law of demand is a public good.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
Yes				(1 mark)
(	The use of the law is non-rival. A person's use will not reduce the amount available to others.	(1 mark)
(	The use of the law is non-excludable. It is not possible to exclude others from using it.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Explain whether the music composed by Franz Schubert (舒伯特) is a public good.	
				(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
Yes				(1 mark)
(	The music is non-rival in consumption. A person's consumption will not reduce the amount available to others.	(1 mark)
(	The music is non-excludable in consumption. It is not possible to exclude others from consuming it.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	To what type of production does a school belong?	(1 mark)
(b)	What are the other two types of production? Give ONE example of each.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Tertiary production	(1 mark)

(b)	Primary production. Example: farming.	(2 marks)
	Secondary production. Example: canned fish manufacturing.	(2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Identify the type of production in which each of the following people is engaged. Briefly explain your answers.
(a)	A miner working in a quarry	(2 marks)
(b)	A fireman	(2 marks)
(c)	A construction worker	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Primary production;	(1 mark)
	•	Because he is involved in activities (mining) that extract resources (stone) provided by nature.	 (1 mark)

(b)	•	Tertiary production;	(1 mark)
	•	Because he is involved in the provision of services (fire prevention and rescue services).	 (1 mark)


(c)	•	Secondary production;	(1 mark)
	•	Because he is involved in activities which turn raw materials (e.g., cement, bricks, steel bars and water pipes) into semi-finished products and finished products (e.g., a building).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Identify the type of production in which each of the following people is engaged. Explain your answers.
(a)	Paparazzi (「狗仔隊」)	(2 marks)
(b)	Coal mine supervisors	(2 marks)
(c)	Dim sum makers	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Tertiary production;	(1 mark)
	•	Because they are involved in the provision of services (photo-taking and video-shooting services).	(1 mark)

(b)	•	Tertiary production;	(1 mark)
	•	Because they are involved in the provision of services (supervising).	(1 mark)

(c)	•	Secondary production;	(1 mark)
	•	Because they are involved in activities which turn raw materials (ingredients) into finished products (dim sum).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
As Hong Kong develops towards a knowledge-based economy, the demand for information technology (IT) professionals has increased tremendously. This has resulted in a serious shortage of IT professionals in Hong Kong.
(a)	Identify the type of production IT is involved in.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain why Hong Kong has experienced a shortage of IT professionals.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Tertiary production	(2 marks)

(b)	The wage rates for Hong Kong IT professionals are below equilibrium.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text: Mr Wong runs a bakery where he produces bread for sale. Explain what type(s) of production Mr Wong's bakery is involved in.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Secondary and tertiary production:
•	Turning raw materials into bread is secondary production.	(2 marks)
•	Selling bread is tertiary production.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text: Mr Hui runs a Chinese medicine clinic where he provides medical advice together with herbal medicine to patients. He also makes and sells Tieh Ta Wine (跌打酒) there. Explain what types of production Mr Hui's clinic is involved in.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Secondary and tertiary production:
•	Making Tieh Ta Wine is secondary production.	(2 marks)
•	Providing medical services is tertiary production.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
(a)	What is tertiary production?	(2 marks)
(b)	Ming is the head prefect at his school. He is responsible for maintaining order during recess. Is Ming a tertiary producer? Explain.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Tertiary production refers to activities which provide services.	(2 marks)

(b)	Yes, because he provides his teachers and schoolmates with the service of maintaining order.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Identify and explain the type of division of labour that is involved in each of the following cases:
(a)	The US invents a lot of high technology products and Thailand exports a lot of agricultural products.	(2 marks)
(b)	A father is responsible for cooking and a mother is responsible for cleaning.			(2 marks)
(c)	A nurse cleans the wound of a victim and a doctor performs the surgery.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Regional division of labour;	(1 mark)
	Because different countries specialise in producing different goods.	(1 mark)

(b)	Simple division of labour;	(1 mark)
	Because each specialises in producing a particular good or service.	(1 mark)

(c)	Complex division of labour;	(1 mark)
	Because each specialises in a particular role and works in a team.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Identify and explain the type of division of labour that is involved in each of the following cases:
(a)	Mary chooses to be a fashion designer while her brother chooses to be a doctor.		(2 marks)
(b)	An international accounting firm has set up different departments to help provide accounting services.	(2 marks)
(c)	Japan exports televisions to Hong Kong while Hong Kong exports garments to Japan.		(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Simple division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because a person specialises in producing a particular good or service.		(1 mark)

(b)	•	Complex division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because different people in the firm specialise in different production stages.		(1 mark)

(c)	•	Regional/international division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because different regions or countries specialise in the production of different goods.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Identify and explain the type of division of labour that is involved in each of the following cases:
(a)	Mary's mother works outside and her father does the housework.	(2 marks)
(b)	An anaesthetist (麻醉師) gives patients anaesthetics and a surgeon (外科醫生) performs medical operations on patients.	(2 marks)
(c)	In Hong Kong, Cheung Sha Wan is an industrial district while Causeway Bay is a business district.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Simple division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because each specialises in producing a particular good or service.	(1 mark)

(b)	•	Complex division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because different people in the firm specialise in different production stages.			(1 mark)

(c)	•	Regional division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because different districts specialise in the production of different goods or services.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Identify and explain the type of division of labour that is involved in each of the following cases:
(a)	Susanne sings and David acts in a show staged at the Hong Kong Cultural Centre.	(2 marks)
(b)	In a family, the sister is responsible for preparing meals while the brother is responsible for tidying up the house.	(2 marks)
(c)	Ethiopia concentrates on growing coffee beans while Switzerland concentrates on roasting coffee beans.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Complex division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because each specialises in a particular role and works in a show.	(1 mark)

(b)	•	Simple division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because each concentrates on the production of a particular good or service.		(1 mark)

(c)	•	Regional division of labour;	(1 mark)
	•	Because different countries specialise in different production stages of a good.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Tammy and Yummy open a cake shop. Tammy specialises in making cake bases and Yummy specialises in cake decorating. One day, Tammy was sick and could not make cake bases. As a result, the cake shop had no cakes to sell because Yummy did not know how to make cake bases.
(a)	In what type of division of labour is involved? 	(1 mark)
(b)	What are the two disadvantages of the division of labour shown in the above case? Explain your answer.			(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Complex division of labour	(1 mark)

(b)	•	Over-interdependence: Disruption in Tammy's work hinders Yummy's work.
				(2 marks)
	•	Limited skills of workers: Yummy only knows how to decorate the cakes but does not know how to make the cake bases.	(2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
A bank has tellers, security guards and relationship managers.
What economic principle is illustrated by the above phenomenon? List THREE reasons why the principle can increase labour productivity.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Division of labour	(1 mark)
Reasons:
(	Assigns the right person to do the right job
(	Practice makes perfect
(	Save workers from shifting between different tasks
(Accept any other reasonable answers. 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Ben and David are the owners of a goldfish shop. Ben is responsible for selling goldfish and David is responsible for selling tortoises. Both bear unlimited liability.
(a)	To what type of business ownership does the shop belong? List TWO features of this type of business ownership.	(3 marks)
(b)	Explain TWO advantages of the division of labour shown in the above case.			(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Partnership	(1 mark)
	Features:
	(	The firm is not a legal entity.
	(	The firm does not need to disclose its financial accounts to the public.
	(	The firm enjoys a lower profits tax rate.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers. 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(b)	•	Assigns the right person to do the right job: Ben and David may be familiar with different types of goldfish and tortoises, respectively.	(2 marks)
	•	Saves workers from shifting between different tasks: They can remain at fixed locations in the shop to sell the pets. 	(2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Mr Chan runs a garment factory in Cheung Sha Wan. In his factory, there are managers, clerks and workers in different production processes.
(a)	In which type of production is Mr Chan involved?	(1 mark)
(b)	Identify the type of division of labour found in Mr Chan's factory. Explain TWO advantages of division of labour to Mr Chan.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Secondary production	(1 mark)

(b)	Complex division of labour	(1 mark)
	Advantages:
	•	Assigning the right person to do the right job
	•	Practice makes perfect
	•	Saving time in training workers
	•	Saving workers' time in shifting between different tasks
	•	More workers have capital goods to use
	•	Capital goods are used efficiently
	•	Mechanisation is stimulated
	(Any TWO of the above with explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
After she retired, Ms Tsui opened a seafood restaurant on Cheung Chau. She has no workers and does everything on her own.
(a)	In which type of production is Miss Tsui involved?	(2 marks)
(b)	Identify the type of division of labour found in Miss Tsui's restaurant. Explain TWO disadvantages of such a production arrangement.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Secondary and tertiary production	(2 marks)

(b)	Simple division of labour (because she specialises in the supply of seafood dishes)			(1 mark)
	Disadvantages:
	•	Required training time increases.
	•	More time is spent in moving around jobs.
	•	Miss Tsui cannot make full use of capital goods.
	(Explain any TWO of the above, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Kent runs a garage. He employs some workers to work with him at the garage. Each of them specialises in a different task.
(a)	In what type of production is Kent involved?	(1 mark)
(b)	Explain TWO reasons why division of labour helps raise the productivity of labour.		(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Tertiary production	(1 mark)

(b)	•	Assigning the right person to do the right job
	•	Practice makes perfect
	•	Saving time in training workers
	•	Saving workers' time in shifting between different tasks
	•	More workers have capital goods to use

	•	Mechanisation is stimulated
	(Any TWO of the above with explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Miss Cheung runs a fitness centre. She hires different fitness specialists to teach customers of different ages and gender.
(a)	In which type of production are those fitness specialists involved?	(1 mark)
(b)	Suggest ONE reason to explain why division of labour can raise productivity in this case.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Tertiary production	(1 mark)

(b)	•	Assigning the right person to do the right job
	•	Practice makes perfect
	•	Saving time in training workers
	•	Saving workers' time in shifting between different tasks
	(Explain any ONE of the above, 2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
News companies usually employ different editors and reporters for different types of news. For example, they have people focusing only on local, financial, entertainment or sports news.
(a)	State the economic principle behind this arrangement.	(2 marks)
(b)	List TWO reasons to explain how the economic principle mentioned above raises the productivity of editors and reporters.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Division of labour / specialisation	(2 marks)

(b)	Reasons for raising productivity are:
	•	Assigning the right person to do the right job
	•	Practice makes perfect
	•	Saving time in training workers
	•	Saving workers' time in shifting between different tasks
	(Any TWO of the above, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
In the US, military forces consist of the army, navy, air force, marine corps and coast guard. Each branch is responsible for different duties.
(a)	What principle has been used in the above arrangement?	(2 marks)
(b)	Suggest TWO reasons to explain why that principle can help increase the power of military forces.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Division of labour / specialisation	(2 marks)

(b)	Reasons:
	•	The military can choose the most suitable person for a job.
	•	Time is saved in training soldiers.
	•	Saving time in shifting between different tasks
	•	Practice makes soldiers become more skilful at their jobs.
	•	Less equipment is needed and hence the military forces can equip solders with sufficient equipment.
	(Any TWO of the above, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
'Whenever there is a large market for a product, division of labour will be carried out to a large extent.'
Do you agree with this statement? Explain your answer with an example.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	No, this is true only when the nature of the goods or services permits division of labour.		(1 mark)
•	If the goods or services require some highly specialised skills which can only be found in one person, division of labour is impossible.	(1 mark)
•	Any reasonable example	(2 marks)
	e.g., In writing a novel, division of labour is impossible as the styles of different authors differ.

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
'Firms should practise division of labour as long as the nature of the product permits,' said Ming.
Do you agree? Explain with ONE reason.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Disagree.		(1 mark)
•	If the market is small, a small output is sufficient to satisfy market demand. Division of labour will become unnecessary.
•	If there are many trade barriers, regional division of labour will be limited.
•	Trade barriers also reduce the volume of trade, limiting the extent of division of labour.	
(Any ONE of the above, 2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the contribution of various economic activities in different years to the total value of production on Iron Island.

(a)	Give an example of tertiary production.	(1 mark)
(b)	How did the contribution of secondary production to the total value of production change over the years?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Insurance (Accept other reasonable answer.)	(1 mark)

(b)	Since the contribution of primary production to the total value of production had been decreasing and that of tertiary production remained unchanged, the contribution of secondary production to the total value of production had been increasing.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Suppose there are only two countries, Country A and Country B. Study the table below about the two countries:

Types of production	Percentage share of total employment	
	Country A	Country B	
Primary	62%	1%	
Secondary	15%	64%	
Tertiary	23%	35%	

(a)	Is there evidence of division of labour from the table above? Explain.	(2 marks)
(b)	Sam says, 'Country A must be more reliant on Country B as secondary production is more important.'
	Do you agree? Explain	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Yes. Division of labour can be found in both countries.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	Disagree. The three types of production are interdependent.	(1 mark)
	•	Country A is reliant on Country B because secondary production provides producer goods (e.g., machines) for primary production.	(1 mark)
	•	Country B is also reliant on Country A because primary production provides raw materials for secondary production.	(1 mark)



Structured Questions

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Louis catches fish and Natalie sells the fish at the market. They discover that when the price of meat increases, more people will buy the fish.
(a)	In which types of production are Louis and Natalie involved?	(2 marks)
(b)	Are fish and meat in substitute demand or complementary demand?	(1 mark)
(c)	When fishing is suspended, Louis cannot find another job because he can only catch fish. Give ONE disadvantage of division of labour in this case.	(2 marks)
(d)	Explain TWO other disadvantages of division of labour.	(4 marks)
(e)	Is the fish an economic good or a free good?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Louis is involved in primary production and Natalie is involved in tertiary production.	(2 marks)

(b)	Substitute demand	(1 mark)

(c)	•	Limited skill of workers	
	•	Greater risk of unemployment
	(Any ONE of the above. 2 marks)

(d)	•	Work can become boring: As workers repeat a simple task, their work becomes boring.
	•	Loss of job satisfaction: Workers specialise in a tiny aspect of a product. It is difficult for them to feel job satisfaction.
	•	Over-interdependence: Production is separated into different stages. Disruption in one hinders the others.
	•	Excessive standardisation of products: Production procedures cannot be frequently changed. Products are standardised under mass production.
	(Any TWO of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

(e)	The fish is an economic good because people prefer to have more of it rather than less.		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Cathy, Kelly and Mag are three hair stylists. Now they have formed a partnership and own a salon. Cathy cuts hair, Kelly washes hair and Mag cleans the floor. 
(a)	In which type of production are they involved?	(1 mark)
(b)	Identify and explain the type of division of labour involved.	(3 marks)
(c)	Give TWO advantages of a partnership relative to a sole proprietorship.	(2 marks)
(d)	Explain TWO disadvantages of division of labour.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Tertiary production	(1 mark)

(b)	•	Complex division of labour	(1 mark)
	•	Different people specialise in different stages in the provision of hair cutting services.	(2 marks)

(c)	•	More sources of capital	(1 mark)
	•	Can have some degree of specialisation	(1 mark)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

(d)	•	Work becomes boring
	•	Loss of job satisfaction
	•	Over-interdependence
	•	Limited skills of workers
	•	Greater risk of unemployment
	•	Excessive standardisation of products
	(Any TWO of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Jack writes novels and Kate sells the novels in a book store. Kate discovers that they sell more books when the economy is bad.
(a)	In which type of production are Jack and Kate involved?	(2 marks)
(b)	Why is it difficult for Jack to have division of labour with other people in writing the novels?	(2 marks)
(c)	Without Kate, Jack has to go to the book store and sell his books after he finishes writing them. Now he can just stay at home and write the novels. What kind of advantage of division of labour is shown in this case?	(2 marks)
(d)	Explain TWO other advantages of division of labour.	(4 marks)
(e)	Are the novels normal goods or inferior goods in this case? Explain	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Both are involved in tertiary production.	(2 marks)

(b)	Because writing novels requires individual creativity.	(2 marks)

(c)	Saving workers' time in shifting between different tasks	(2 marks)

(d)	•	Assigning the right person to do the right job
	•	Practice makes perfect
	•	Save time in training workers
	•	More workers have capital goods to use
	•	Capital goods are used efficiently
	•	Mechanisation is stimulated
	(Any TWO of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

(e)	The demand for the novels increases when people's incomes decrease. Therefore, the novels are inferior goods.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch209 · Production and division of labour
questions.text:
Suppose an economy consists of only two persons, Mary and Peter, and they survive on only rice and potatoes. Mary produces only rice and Peter produces only potatoes.
(a)	In the above situation, what should Mary and Peter do in order to consume both rice and potatoes?	(1 mark)
(b)	Which economic principle is illustrated by the above situation?	(1 mark)
(c)	If Mary and Peter can each produce both rice and potatoes on their own, why would they still choose to produce only one food? Explain.	(4 marks)
(d)	What role do private property rights play in facilitating exchange and specialisation in the above case? Explain.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	They should engage in exchange. 	(1 mark)

(b)	Simple division of labour / specialisation 	(1 mark)

(c)	It is because specialisation can increase their productivity. This will increase their total output and living standards.	(2 marks)
	Specialisation can increase productivity because:
	•	The right person can be assigned to do the right job.
	•	Practice makes perfect.
	•	Saving workers' time in shifting between different tasks.
	(Briefly explain any ONE of the above, 2 marks)

(d)	•	If private property rights to a good do not exist, the good becomes a common property. Since everyone may use it, no one would be willing to pay for its use. As a result, exchange would not take place.	(2 marks)
	•	Exchange is an important condition for specialisation. Without exchange, specialisation is not possible. Mary and Peter have to produce everything they need by themselves.	(2 marks)
	•	Therefore, a clear delineation of private property rights is an important condition for exchange and hence specialisation.	(1 mark)

	(1)	Its average labour productivity in 2019 is higher than that in 2014.
	(2)	Its average labour productivity in 2019 is lower than that in 2014.
	(3)	The labour supply in 2019 is higher than that in 2014.
	(4)	The labour supply in 2019 is lower than that in 2014.

D.	(2) and (4) only

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
* Study the following production information about Country A and Country B.

	Country A	Country B	
 Labour force	3 million	2 million	
 Output (units)	600	400	

Which of the following descriptions must be correct?
	(1)	The labour supply of Country A is higher than that of Country B.
	(2)	The quality of labour in Country A is higher than that of Country B.
	(3)	The average labour productivity of Country A is the same as that of Country B.
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(1) and (3) only
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText:
•	While labour supply is positively related to the size of the labour force and the average working hours of workers, the latter may be much higher in Country B.
•	The labour force usually includes both employed and unemployed persons. On the other hand, (average) labour productivity is measured by the output produced per working hour of labour. As we do not have information on the latter, we cannot conclude which country has a higher average labour productivity.

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
(a)	Define labour.	(2 marks)
(b)	An office assistant said, 'In economics, both office assistants and managers are labour.' Is he correct? Explain your answer.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Labour is the human effort, both mental and physical, that can be used in production.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	Yes, both office assistants and managers provide human effort in production though their tasks are different.	(2 marks)
	•	Managers provide mainly mental effort in the management of companies; office assistants provide both mental and physical effort in providing supporting services for others in offices.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Study the following table carefully:

	Labour force	
Country X	300,000	
Country Y	200,000	

Explain if we can draw the following conclusions based on the above information:
(a)	The labour supply in Country X is higher.	(2 marks)
(b)	Labour productivity in Country X is higher.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No. We also have to consider the number of working hours of workers.	(2 marks)

(b)	No. Labour productivity is measured by output produced per working hour of labour. We can't draw conclusion about their productivity just based on the size of their labour force.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Explain how each of the following policies affects labour supply.
(a)	Setting the maximum number of working hours	(2 marks)
(b)	Increasing the number of university places	(2 marks)
(c)	Increasing the retirement age of civil servants	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Setting the maximum number of working hours will reduce the working hours of labour. This implies the labour supply will decrease.	(2 marks)

(b)	Increasing the number of university places will reduce the size of labour force, so the labour supply will decrease.	(2 marks)

(c)	Increasing the retirement age of civil servants will enable civil servants who should retire initially to continue to work, so the labour supply will increase.		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Although labour costs in China, India and Thailand are cheaper, some companies are building new manufacturing plants in the US because of its higher labour productivity.
(a)	What is labour productivity?	(2 marks)
(b)	How can a government raise labour productivity? Give TWO examples.
				(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Labour productivity is measured by output per unit of labour. It is equal to total output divided by the total number of working hours.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	Raise the educational level of workers by providing free education.
	•	Improve the health of workers by providing more medical services or improving a city's air quality.
	(Accept other reasonable answers. 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Louis owns a toy factory. The labour productivity of his factory is higher than the industrial average.
(a)	How is labour productivity measured?	(2 marks)
(b)	Briefly explain TWO possible reasons why Louis's factory has above-average labour productivity. 	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Labour productivity is measured by output per working hour of labour.	(2 marks)

(b)	The possible reasons are as follows:
•	Healthier workers: His factory has healthier workers who can concentrate on their work and produce efficiently.	
•	Better education and training: His workers receive better education and training which improves the intelligence of workers and develops their skills. Both enhance labour productivity.	
•	Higher level of mechanisation and technology: With the help of machinery and advanced technology, workers can produce more output per working hour.	
•	Better working environment: A better working environment helps increase output.
•	Better management: If his managers can assign workers to appropriate tasks, achieve good teamwork and maintain high morale, labour productivity can be higher.
•	Greater incentive to work: If more productive workers are rewarded with higher wage rates or better job prospects, workers will be motivated to work more efficiently.
(Any TWO of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Some foreign high-tech companies invest in Hong Kong since they believe that the labour productivity in Hong Kong is higher.
(a)	Define labour productivity.	(2 marks)
(b)	Give THREE suggestions to the government or firms on how to raise labour productivity.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Labour productivity is measured by output produced per working hour of labour.		(2 marks)


(b)	•	Raising their educational level and providing more training
	•	Improving the health of workers
	•	Raising the quantity and quality of capital as well as the technological level
	•	Improving the method of organising labour
	•	Improving working conditions
	•	Improving the incentive to work
	(Any THREE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Nick Cheung Ka Fai is a Hong Kong actor who was formerly a Hong Kong Police officer. After quitting his job, he started his acting career.
(a)	To what factor of production does the police officer belong?	(1 mark)
(b)	What is the occupational mobility of labour? Give TWO factors that may affect it.
		(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Labour		(1 mark)

(b)	It refers to the willingness and ease of labour to change from one occupation to another.	(2 marks)
	Factors:
	•	Market obstacles: If the government or professional associations raise entrance requirements, occupational mobility will decrease.
	•	Market information: If workers have more market information, their occupational mobility will increase.
	(Accept other reasonable answers. 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Susan was a bank manager but she was laid off last month. She is planning to change her occupation.
(a)	What is occupational mobility?	(2 marks)
(b)	Give TWO suggestions as to how Susan can increase her occupational mobility.		(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Occupational mobility refers to the willingness and ease of a factor to change from one occupation (or use) to another.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	Reducing her income requirement
	•	Learning new skills other than banking
	•	Searching for market information
	(Any TWO of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
(a)	What is geographical mobility?	(2 marks)
(b)	Give TWO reasons to explain an increase in the geographical mobility of labour.		(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Geographical mobility refers to the willingness and ease of a factor to move from one area to another.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	Transport costs decrease
	•	Improvement of the transport network
	•	Economic conditions worsen
	•	The political environment becomes unstable
	•	The government relaxes its immigration and emigration policy
	•	Availability of market information
	(Briefly explain any TWO of the above, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text: Tutors at private tutorial centres are usually paid a basic salary, plus a commission. Suggest and explain ONE reason why this payment method is adopted.	(4 marks)

This payment method reduces the need for supervision.	(2 marks)
(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text: Masseuses and masseurs perform massages on customers. Suggest ONE payment method for them. Explain your answer.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Basic salary plus tips	(2 marks)
They directly provide services to customers. Their performance influences the firm's profit but is difficult to monitor. Therefore, tips are employed.
A basic salary can stabilise workers' income.	(2 marks)
(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text: Amy employs a private tutor to teach her son Economics and pays the tutor according to his working hours. Suggest and explain ONE advantage and ONE disadvantage of this payment method to Amy.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Advantage:
•	Without the need to measure the tutor's extra contribution, the cost of calculating wage payments is reduced.	
•	The tutor can pay more attention to teaching quality.
(Any ONE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks)
Disadvantage:
•	The tutor may shirk as his income does not directly depend on his contribution. Productivity may decline.
•	More supervision is needed. Amy has to monitor the work of the tutor closely. Therefore, the administrative cost may be higher.
(Any ONE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks)

questions.text: The workers in supermarkets are paid on a time rate. Suggest and explain ONE reason why this payment system is adopted.	(2 marks)

•	It enables the workers to earn a more regular income.
(Any ONE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Study the following recruitment advertisement.

MiChi Company
Recruitment
(1) Salespersons
Monthly salary of $6,000 + commission
(2)	One cleaning worker
Monthly salary of $5,000

questions.answerText:

•	The output of a cleaning worker is difficult to measure. Paying him/her by time rate is simple and easy to administer.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text: Workers at Mr Lee's toy factory are paid on a piece rate basis. Please suggest ONE advantage of this payment method for the company and workers, respectively.		(4 marks)
questions.answerText:

	this payment method increases workers' incentive to work and their productivity;
	OR
	the employer can save on the cost of supervising the workers against shirking. 		(2 marks)
•	The advantage to the workers: hard-working workers can earn more.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text: Mr Chan is the owner of a toy factory. He is going to hire a packaging worker and an accounting clerk. Explain separately which wage payment methods Mr Chan should adopt to hire these two employees.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Packaging worker: Piece rate should be adopted. This is because it can increase the worker's incentive to work and save Mr Chan the cost of monitoring the worker.	(2 marks)
•	Accounting clerk: Time rate should be adopted. This is because the output of an accounting clerk is difficult to measure. This wage payment method is simple and easy to administer. Moreover, the accounting clerk can pay more attention to product quality.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch210 · Factors of production
questions.text:
Salespeople at mobile phone shops are given a basic salary plus a certain percentage of revenue as commission.
Explain ONE advantage to the employer and ONE disadvantage to the employees of this payment system. 	 (4 marks)
questions.answerText:
