questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	List TWO characteristics of perfect competition.	(2 marks)
(b)	What will happen if a seller in a perfectly competitive market sets his price higher than the market price? What if he sets his price lower than the market price?
			(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	A large number of sellers
	•	Homogeneous products
	•	Free entry
	•	Perfect information
	•	Sellers are price takers.
	•	Sellers do not engage in non-price competition.
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(b)	If the seller sets his price higher than the market price, he will lose all his customers because the customers know that they can buy the goods at a lower price elsewhere.	(2 marks)
	If the seller sets his price lower than the market price, he will lose money.
		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: In Hong Kong, the same brand of chocolate is sold at different prices in different retail outlets. Give TWO reasons to explain why some retail outlets can charge higher prices without losing all their customers.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The services of different retail outlets are heterogeneous (e.g., some shops are more convenient).	
•	Buyers have imperfect information.	
(Accept other reasonable answers. 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	List TWO characteristics of perfect competition.	(2 marks)
* (b) 'Under perfect competition, an individual seller has no influence on the market. Therefore, even if all sellers reduce their output, they will still be unable to influence the market price.'
	Is this statement true? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	A large number of sellers
	•	Homogeneous products
	•	Free entry
	•	Perfect market information
	•	Sellers are price takers
	•	No non-price competition
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(b)	•	The first half is correct. Under perfect competition, a seller cannot affect the market price by his behaviour. This is because his output is too small to affect the market supply. Moreover, his product is the same as that of many other sellers and everyone has perfect market information.	(2 marks)
	•	However, the second half is incorrect. If all sellers reduce their output, the total contraction in output will have a significant effect on the market supply and hence the market price. 	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: Why are sellers price takers in perfectly competitive markets?	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	There are many sellers who are small and not associated with each other. An individual seller's output is so small that any change in his supply cannot affect the market supply and the market price.	(2 marks)
•	Sellers supply homogenous products and buyers have perfect information. Any seller who charges a higher price would lose all his customers.	 (2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: Briefly explain THREE reasons why the newspaper publishing industry in Hong Kong does NOT belong to perfect competition.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Some sellers have a large market share.
•	Newspapers are heterogeneous.
•	Non-price competition (e.g., advertising, free gifts) exists.
•	Information is imperfect.
•	Entry is difficult as huge capital investment is required.
•	Sellers are price searchers.
(Any THREE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: Tsim Sha Tsui has many hotels. Give TWO reasons to explain why the market structure of hotels is NOT perfect competition.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Sellers provide heterogeneous services, e.g., different locations.
•	Market information is imperfect, e.g., information about the quality of services.
•	Sellers engage in non-price competition, e.g., advertisements.
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: Briefly give THREE reasons why the television broadcasting industry in Hong Kong does NOT belong to perfect competition.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	There are only a few television stations.
•	Television stations provide heterogeneous programmes.
•	Market information is imperfect.
•	Entry is difficult as a huge capital investment is required.
•	Sellers are price searchers. They can affect the price of advertisements.
•	Sellers engage in non-price competition.
(Any THREE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
'Local computer retailers operate under perfect competition.'
Do you agree with the above statement? List THREE reasons to support your answer.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	No.		(1 mark)
Reasons:
•	Sellers provide heterogeneous services.
•	Market information is imperfect.
•	Entry is not totally free: some computers are sold by particular agents so computer retailers cannot deal with the producers directly.
•	Sellers are price searchers.
•	Sellers engage in non-price competition.
(Any THREE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	List TWO common features among all types of imperfect competition.	(2 marks)
(b)	'Under imperfect competition, goods are heterogeneous.'
	Is this statement true? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Information about the market is imperfect.
	•	Sellers are price searchers.
	•	Sellers may engage in non-price competition.
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(b)	•	No.	(1 mark)
	•	Oligopolists may sell homogeneous goods.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	What is perfect competition?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain TWO features of the retail flower industry in Hong Kong that resemble perfect competition.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Perfect competition is a market structure which has the following features:
	•	It has a large number of sellers who are small and not associated with each other.
	•	The market allows free entry of sellers.
	•	The sellers supply homogeneous products.
	•	Buyers and sellers have perfect market information.	(2 marks)
(b)	•	There are a large number of buyers and sellers.	(2 marks)
	•	The market allows free entry of sellers.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: In 2014, many people bought smart TV boxes to watch HKTV's television programmes. It was found that one smart TV box model was sold in many shops but at different prices. Give TWO reasons to explain why there was such a price difference.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Heterogeneous services, e.g., the shops are located at different locations, and some are more convenient.
•	Imperfect information, e.g., buyers do not know the prices in other shops.
(Accept other reasonable answers, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: What is the market structure of watch retailing in Hong Kong? State THREE features of this type of market structure.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Monopolistic competition	(1 mark)
Features:
(	many sellers
(	free entry
(	heterogeneous products
(	imperfect information
(	non-price competition
(	sellers are price searchers
(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	What is monopolistic competition?	(2 marks)
*(b)	'Under perfect competition, the fact that there are many sellers and free entry ensures all sellers are price takers; under monopolistic competition, although there are many sellers and free entry, the sellers are price searchers.'
	Account for the difference between perfect competition and monopolistic competition.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopolistic competition is a market structure which has the following features:
	•	There are a large number of sellers who are small and not associated with each other.
	•	The market allows free entry of sellers.
	•	The sellers supply heterogeneous products.
	•	No buyers or sellers have perfect market information.	(2 marks)
(b)	•	The goods are heterogeneous in a monopolistically competitive market but they are homogeneous in a perfectly competitive market.	(2 marks)
	•	The information in a monopolistically competitive market is imperfect while that in a perfectly competitive market is perfect.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	To what type of market structure do local Chinese restaurants belong? List THREE features of this market.	(4 marks)
(b)	Suggest THREE methods of competition among Chinese restaurants.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopolistic competition	(1 mark)
	•	A large number of sellers who are small and not associated with each other
	•	Free entry
	•	The products sold are heterogeneous.
	• 	Imperfect information about the market
	•	Price searching
	•	Engaging in non-price competition
	(Any THREE of the above, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)
(b)	•	Lowering prices or offering discounted dishes
	•	Improving the services of their waiters/waitresses
	•	Improving the environment of the restaurant
	•	Improving the quality of their food
	•	Advertising
	•	Offering free gifts
	(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: City F has only two bus companies. State the market structure of bus services in this city and list TWO features of this kind of market structure.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Oligopoly	(1 mark)
Features:
•	a few dominant firms
•	sellers are price searchers
•	interdependent in pricing policies
•	product can be homogeneous or heterogeneous
•	non-price competition
•	not easy to enter the market
•	imperfect information
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: Why do the prices in an oligopolistic market tend to be rigid?	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(	When an oligopolist cuts its price, others may follow so as to maintain their market shares. Consequently, all sellers may suffer a great drop in profits without increasing their market shares.	(2 marks)
(	When an oligopolist raises its price, others may not follow in hopes of seizing its market share. Consequently, the former may lose a significant portion of its market share.	(2 marks)
(	Hence, oligopolists are cautious about changing prices.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: WhatsApp, WeChat and LINE are the most popular instant messaging applications on smartphones. What is the market structure of instant messaging apps? State THREE features of this type of market structure.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Oligopoly	(1 mark)
Features:
•	a few dominant firms
•	sellers are price searchers
•	interdependent in pricing policies
•	product can be homogeneous or heterogeneous
•	non-price competition
•	not easy to enter the market
•	imperfect information
(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Study the following information about mobile phone services industry in City H. All providers and their basic plans are as follows.

Service provider	Airtime 
(basic voice minutes)	Local data usage	Monthly fee 
($)	
A	1,000	200 Mb	98	
B	1,000	200 Mb	80	
C	1,000	400 Mb	80	
D^	1,400	400 Mb	80	
E^	1,200	800 Mb	88	
F	1,200	800 Mb	85	
G^	1,200	1 Gb	85	
	^ D, E and G are owned by the same company.

(a)	Identify the market structure of City H's mobile phone services industry. Explain your answer with reference to the above table.	(3 marks)
(b)	List TWO features of the market structure other than that in (a).	(2 marks)
*(c)	Service provider G provides a plan for $35, but the plan provides fewer extra services. Other competitors do not reduce their prices accordingly. Explain whether this phenomenon can still be consistent with the market structure suggested in (a).	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	•	Several service providers dominate the market since there are at most seven sellers in the market.	(2 marks)
(b)	•	Entry is restricted, e.g., a huge capital investment.
	•	Mobile phone services are heterogeneous.
	•	Information is imperfect.
	•	The service providers are price searchers.
	•	The service providers are interdependent.
	•	Prices tend to be rigid. A price cut may lead to a price war.
	•	Price leadership occurs.
	•	Non-price competition is common.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(c)	•	Yes. The phenomenon can be consistent with the market structure.	(1 mark)
	•	As an oligopolist, service provider G may try to differentiate its product by providing different plans.	(1 mark)
	•	This does not mean that service provider G has lowered its price (i.e., the fee per minute remains unchanged).	(1 mark)
	•	Thus, the strategy of service provider G does not lead to a price war.	(1 mark)
	•	Market price still tends to be rigid.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Recently, a dominant private housing estate developer in Hong Kong has begun the process of subscription (認購). Flat prices were set lower than for similar flats in the same area. Later, other large property developers also lowered the prices of their flats.
(a)	Identify the market structure of private housing development in Hong Kong. Explain your answer with the information provided.	(5 marks)
(b)	Explain TWO other behaviours of the firms under the market structure in (a).		(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	•	There are several dominant private developers.	(1 mark)
	•	The sellers in the market are interdependent.	(1 mark)
	•	A price cut from one developer leads to a price war.	(1 mark)
	•	There is price leadership.	(1 mark)
(b)	•	Non-price competition is common.	(1 mark)
	•	Price searching	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Recently, a textbook publisher gave away to its customers free exercise books with detailed answers. Later, other publishers also attached free exercise books to their products.
(a)	Identify the market structure of the textbook publishing industry. List TWO features of the market structure.	(3 marks)
(b)	What form of competition is illustrated by the above event? Suggest TWO more examples of this form of competition.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	•	A few textbook publishers dominate the market.
	•	Products are heterogeneous.
	•	Market information is imperfect.
	•	The oligopolists are interdependent.
	•	Prices tend to be rigid. A price cut may lead to a price war.
	•	Price leadership occurs.
	•	Non-price competition is common.
	•	Publishers are price searchers.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(b)	•	Non-price competition	(1 mark)
	•	Any two examples of non-price competition, e.g., improving print quality, giving away free student learning CDs, more free teaching materials for teachers	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	What is an oligopoly?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain TWO examples of oligopolistic behaviour in the Hong Kong loan market.		(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	An oligopoly is a market structure where several sellers dominate the market.				(2 marks)
(b)	•	Price wars: banks lower lending rates to attract more customers
	•	Sellers are interdependent: when an oligopolistic bank initiates a promotional programme, others will follow.
	•	Non-price competition: banks advertise and offer privileged terms to attract more customers.
	•	Any other reasonable examples
	(Any TWO of the above with explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
There are many brands of digital cameras on the market, such as Canon, Sony and Panasonic.
(a)	To what type of market structure does digital camera production belong? List TWO features of the market structure. 	(3 marks)
(b)	To what type of market structure does digital camera retailing belong? List TWO features of the market structure.	(3 marks)
(c)	Explain why a firm that operates under perfect competition does NOT need to advertise.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	•	A few digital camera producers dominate the market.
	•	Products are heterogeneous.
	•	Market information is imperfect.
	•	The oligopolists are interdependent.
	•	Prices tend to be rigid. A price cut may lead to a price war.
	•	Price leadership occurs.
	•	Non-price competition is common.
	•	The producers are price searchers.
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(b)	Monopolistic competition	(1 mark)
	•	A large number of sellers who are small and not associated with each other
	•	Free entry
	•	The goods sold and the services provided are heterogeneous.
	•	Imperfect market information
	•	The retailers are price searchers.
	•	Both price and non-price competition may occur.
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(c)	Reasons:
	•	Products are homogeneous.	(1 mark)
	•	Market information is perfect.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
In Hong Kong, most karaoke establishments are run by 'Neway' and 'RedMR'.
(a)	What is the market structure of the karaoke services industry? List TWO features of this market structure.	(3 marks)
(b)	In what competition other than price competition will karaoke service providers engage? Suggest an example of this type of competition.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	•	A few service providers dominate the market.
	•	The services offered are heterogeneous.
	•	Market information is imperfect.
	•	The oligopolists are interdependent.
	•	Prices tend to be rigid. A price cut may lead to a price war.
	•	Price leadership occurs.
	•	Non-price competition is common.
	•	The service providers are price searchers.
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(b)	•	Non-price competition	(1 mark)
	•	Examples: advertising; improving the environment of the establishments
		(Any ONE of the above examples or any other relevant example, 1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	'In Hong Kong, major travel agencies usually provide tours of highly similar routes. Therefore, they compete under perfect competition.'
	Is this statement correct? Give TWO reasons to support your answer.	(5 marks)
(b)	Suppose a travel agency introduces a new tour. What will be the reaction of other travel agencies?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.		(1 mark)
	Reasons:
	•	Although travel agencies provide tours of highly similar routes, their arrangements for the tours are different; or tour guides of different travel agencies provide heterogeneous services.
	•	Market information is imperfect.
	•	Several travel agencies account for a large market share. They can affect the market.
	(Any TWO of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

(b)	Other travel agencies will probably introduce a tour of a highly similar route.		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	To what type of market structure do supermarkets in Hong Kong belong? State THREE behaviours of supermarkets which are related to this type of market structure.	(4 marks)
(b)	'If PARKnSHOP merged with Wellcome and monopolised the market, it would not face any competition.' Do you agree? Explain.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	•	The market is dominated by two major sellers.
	•	The supermarkets are interdependent.
	•	When an oligopolist lowers its prices, this may trigger a price war.
	(Accept other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)
(b)	No.		
	•	It had to prevent newcomers from entering the market and to avoid being taken over by other firms.
	•	It had to compete with sellers of substitutes (e.g., convenience stores) for customers.
	•	It had to compete with other producers for resources.
	(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answers, 2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
The Hong Kong and China Gas Company (Towngas) is the only supplier of gas in Hong Kong.
(a)	What is the market structure for gas supply in Hong Kong?	(1 mark)
(b)	Does Towngas face any competition? Explain.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopoly	(1 mark)
(b)	Yes.	(1 mark)
Towngas has to compete for customers with other energy suppliers in Hong Kong. For example, people may use electricity instead of gas when they cook.	(2 marks)
Towngas also has to compete with energy suppliers for factors of production.
			(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text: MTRC is the only provider of underground mass transit services in Hong Kong. Give TWO types of competition it faces.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(	It competes with bus and minibus companies, which provide public transit services above ground.
(	It competes with other companies for labour and capital.
(Accept other reasonable answers, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	What is a monopoly?	(2 marks)
(b)	Does a monopolist face any competition? Explain with an example.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopoly is a market structure with only one seller whose products have no close substitutes.	(2 marks)
(b)	Yes, under scarcity, it faces competition.	(2 marks)
	Example:
	•	MTRC is a monopolist of underground railway services but it still faces competition from sellers of substitutes, such as buses or minibuses.
	•	KMB is a monopolist of bus services in some parts of Kowloon but it still has to compete with other bus companies for experienced drivers.
	(Any ONE of the above or other relevant example with brief explanation, 
2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA) is the only international airport in Hong Kong.
(a)	Identify the market structure of international airport services in Hong Kong.		(1 mark)
(b)	Give TWO features to the market structure identified in part (a).	(2 marks)
(c)	What competition does Hong Kong International Airport face? Explain with an example.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopoly	(1 mark)
(b)	•	The market allows no entry.
	•	HKIA's services have no close substitutes, e.g., air cargo and passenger services.
	•	No one has perfect information about the market.
	•	The HKIA is a price searcher.
	•	The HKIA may engage in non-price competition.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(c)	•	Hong Kong International Airport faces competition from sellers of its substitutes.	(2 marks)
	•	Examples: Shenzhen International Airport and Macau International Airport: domestic travellers may travel by air at other airports. 
		(Any relevant example, 1 mark)
	OR
	•	Hong Kong International Airport needs to compete with other airports for factors of production.	(2 marks)
	•	Example: management executives	
		(Any relevant example, 1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
The Hongkong Electric Company, Limited (HEC) is the only company which supplies electricity to Hong Kong Island.
(a)	What is the market structure of the electricity supply on Hong Kong Island?		(1 mark)
(b)	The government does not grant a franchise to HEC. Give TWO reasons to explain why there are no other suppliers of electricity on Hong Kong Island.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopoly	(1 mark)
(b)	•	HEC enjoys economies of scale as its output is large. Its average cost is so low that a new company finds it difficult to compete with it.	(2 marks)
	•	Huge capital investment is required when entering the market. Small companies cannot afford it.	 (2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
In Hong Kong, the MTR Corporation is the only provider of underground railway services.
(a)	Identify the market structure of underground railway services in Hong Kong.		(2 marks)
(b)	In 2013, the MTR Corporation issued a limited edition 'MTR × Storm Riders' souvenir ticket set. The Storm Riders are popular Kung Fu and martial arts comic heroes created by Hong Kong animator Ma Wing-shing. Which type of competition is this? Suggest ONE more example of this type of competition. 				(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopoly	(2 marks)
(b)	•	Non-price competition.	(2 marks)
	•	Examples: increasing the frequency of train services; extending its network
		(Any relevant examples, 2 marks)


Structured Questions

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Two stores sell food and drinks on a beach. They are both located in the middle of the beach.
(a)	State the market structure of retailing services on the beach and list TWO features of this kind of market structure.	(3 marks)
(b)	The owners of the stores are sole proprietors. State THREE features of this type of		ownership.	(3 marks)
(c)	Give ONE example of variable costs that the stores incur. Explain your answer.
			(2 marks)
(d)	One of the stores opens a restaurant in the city. Explain TWO advantages of this expansion.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	Features:
	•	a few dominant firms
	•	sellers are price searchers
	•	interdependent in pricing policies
	•	product can be homogeneous or heterogeneous
	•	non-price competition
	•	not easy to enter the market
	•	imperfect information
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(b)	•	Simple set-up procedure
	•	Not a legal entity
	•	Lack of continuity
	•	Unlimited liabilities
	•	Narrow source of capital
	•	No specialisation in management
	•	Strong incentive to improve efficiency
	(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

(c)	Cost of buying food and drinks / Wages of part-time workers	(1 mark)
	Because the expenses for these items will increase with output.	(1 mark)
	(Accept other reasonable examples)

(d)	•	Enjoy economies of scale
	•	Extend its brand name to other products
	•	Spread risk through product diversification. Loss in one business may be compensated for by gains in another.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
In large shopping malls, there is usually one floor where different brands of cosmetic shops are located. Many cosmetics brands can be found in Hong Kong. No brand has a high market share.
(a)	What is the market structure of cosmetics products in Hong Kong? Give an example of non-price competition found in this industry.	(2 marks)
(b)	A cosmetics shop finds that when other cosmetics shops open on this floor, its average cost decreases. What economic principle is involved?	(2 marks)
(c)	Salespeople at cosmetics shops are usually paid a basic salary plus a commission. Explain TWO advantages of this method of wage payment to employers.
		(4 marks)
(d)	The lipstick effect suggests that during an economic downturn, consumers will buy fewer luxury coats but more premium lipsticks, thus the sales of premium lipsticks can represent an indicator of economic performance.
	According to this theory, is lipstick a normal good or an inferior good? Why?
			(2 marks)
(e)	Give ONE situation where a lipstick is a consumer good and ONE situation where it is a producer good.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Monopolistic competition	(1 mark)
	Advertising (Accept other correct example)	(1 mark)

(b)	External economies of scale	(2 marks)

(c)	By offering a basic salary, employers can retain staff and save on the cost of recruitment.	(2 marks)
	By offering a commission, employers can increase staff's work incentive.			(2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers)

(d)	Inferior good because when income decreases, sales of lipsticks increase.
	(2 marks)

(e)	When a consumer buys a lipstick to satisfy wants, it is a consumer good.		(2 marks)
	When a makeup artist buys a lipstick to provide makeup services, it is a producer good.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Suppose the government of City H grants Company A the franchise to sell beef. Company A finds that when the price of pork decreases, the quantity transacted of beef decreases if it does not change the price of beef.
(a)	(i)	What is the market structure of beef retailing in City H?	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Suggest TWO characteristics of this type of market structure besides the number of sellers.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain why the quantity transacted of beef decreases when the price of pork decreases.	(2 marks)
(c)	If the government imposes a unit tax on pork, how will the prices of pork and beef change? Explain your answer with TWO diagrams. (For simplicity, assume that the market for beef and pork are perfectly competitive.)	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Monopoly	(1 mark)
	(ii)	•	The market allows no entry.
		•	Both buyers and the monopolist have imperfect information.
		•	The monopolist is a price searcher.
		•	The monopolist engages in both price and non-price competition.
		(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(b)	This is because the two goods are substitutes for each other.	(1 mark)
	When the price of pork decreases, the demand for beef decreases.	(1 mark)

(c)	Indicate on the diagrams:
	•	The supply curve of pork shifts upwards.	(1 mark)
	•	The price of pork increases.	(1 mark)
	•	The demand curve of beef shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
	•	The price of beef increases.	(1 mark)
	
	

	Verbal elaboration:
	When the government imposes a unit tax on pork, the price of pork increases. Since pork and beef are substitutes, the demand for beef increases, so the price of beef increases.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
In a city, only two companies sell hamburgers. Company A later combines with a beef farm and Company B later combines with a Chinese restaurant.
(a)	(i)	What is the market structure for hamburgers in the city above?	(1 mark)
	(ii)	List TWO characteristics of this type of market structure.	(2 marks)
(b)	To which type of expansion does the combination of Company A with the beef farm belong? How about the combination of Company B with the Chinese restaurant? Answer from the perspective of Company A and Company B and explain your answers.	(4 marks)
(c)	What are the benefits of the above expansion? Suggest TWO benefits to Company A and Company B, respectively.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	(ii)	•	A few sellers dominate the market.
		•	Entry is restricted.
		•	Sellers provide heterogeneous products.
		•	Buyers and sellers have imperfect information.
		•	Sellers are price searchers.
		•	Sellers are interdependent.
		•	Prices tend to be rigid.
		•	There may be price leadership.
		•	Non-price competition is common.
		(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(b)	Combination of Company A with the beef farm: vertical backward expansion
Reason: The production of beef is the preceding stage of hamburger production.	
			(2 marks)
	Combination of Company B with the Chinese restaurant: lateral expansion
Reason: The Chinese restaurant produces related but not competing products.
			(2 marks)

(c)	To Company A:
	•	Enjoy economies of scale
	•	Extend its brand name to other products
	•	Secure the supply of inputs
	•	Reduce expenses in transactions
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)


	To Company B:
	•	Enjoy economies of scale	
	•	Extend its brand name to other products
	•	Reduce risk through product diversification
	•	More efficient use of resources held by the Chinese restaurant
	•	Attract customers from its competitors by offering various related products.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
(a)	What is the market structure of the banking industry in Hong Kong?	(2 marks)
(b)	State THREE characteristics of this type of market structure.	(3 marks)
(c)	Suppose a large bank provides a new loan service which attracts many customers. What will the reaction of other banks be? Explain your answer.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Oligopoly	(2 marks)

(b)	• 	A few banks dominate the market.
	•	The services offered are heterogeneous.
	•	Market information is imperfect. 
	•	The oligopolists are interdependent.
	•	Prices tend to be rigid. A price cut may lead to a price war.
	•	Price leadership occurs.
	•	Non-price competition is common.
	•	The banks are price searchers.
	(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks) 

(c)	Other banks will probably provide similar or even better loan services to customers.	(2 marks)
	Reasons for the reaction:
	•	Banks are interdependent, i.e., banks will consider their competitors' strategies when deciding on their business policies.	(1 mark)
	•	To retain its own customers and attract customers from other banks	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Miss Chan runs a boutique in Mongkok. Since the premises are Miss Chan's property, she does not have to pay any rent.
*(a)	Suppose the premises are the only fixed factors in the boutique. Is the boutique's fixed cost equal to zero? Explain.	(2 marks)
(b)	Miss Chan plans to open a branch in Tsim Sha Tsui. She wants to employ a shop manager and two salespeople. Which methods should Miss Chan use in calculating the wages for the manager and the salespeople? Suggest ONE reason for each method.	(6 marks)
(c)	In what ways does the fashion retailing industry resemble perfect competition? In what ways is it different from perfect competition?	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Miss Chan must pay the rates, which is a fixed cost.	(1 mark)
	•	Hence, the boutique's fixed cost is not zero.	(1 mark)

(b)	Miss Chan should pay the manager on a time rate.	(1 mark)
	Reasons:
	•	The work of the manager is not standardised. Using a time rate saves on the cost of calculating wage payments.
	•	The manager can pay more attention to the quality of his services as he does not have to hurry.
	(Any ONE of the above, 2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers)
	Miss Chan should pay the salespeople on a basic salary plus commission scheme.	(1 mark)
	Reasons:
	•	The salespeople will have a higher incentive to work and their productivity will increase.
	•	Miss Chan can save on the costs of supervising the service standard of the salespeople.
	(Any ONE of the above, 2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers)

(c)	Features that resemble perfect competition:
	•	A large number of sellers who are small and not associated with each other
	•	Free entry
	(1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
	Features that differ from perfect competition:
	•	Heterogeneous goods and retailing services
	•	Imperfect market information
	•	Sellers are price searchers.
	•	Sellers may engage in non-price competition.
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
In Hong Kong, the use of mobile phones is popular. Despite continuous significant improvement in telecommunications technology, the price of mobile phone service was still high before 1999. Since 1999, all mobile phone users have been able to keep their existing telephone numbers when changing mobile phone service suppliers. A price war then broke out between the major mobile phone service suppliers.
(a)	(i)	Identify the market structure of Hong Kong's mobile phone services industry. Explain ONE feature of the market structure which helps you identify the market structure.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	Explain TWO features of the market structure other than that in (a)(i).		(4 marks)
*(b)	Economist A said, 'This new policy that all mobile phone users can keep their existing phone numbers when changing suppliers is responsible for starting the price war between major mobile phone service suppliers.' Explain this statement.			(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
		•	A few firms dominate the market.
		•	The oligopolists are interdependent.
		•	The emergence of a price war
		•	Any other reasonable features
(Any ONE of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks)
	(ii)	•	Products tend to be heterogeneous.
		•	Entry into the industry is restricted.
		•	Information is imperfect.
		•	Prices tend to be rigid.
		•	Price leadership occurs.
		•	Non-price competition is common.
		(Any TWO of the above with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

(b)	•	Before 1999, mobile phone users could not keep their telephone numbers when changing service suppliers. As a result, consumers bore a high cost (informing all their friends and relatives) when changing their service suppliers. Hence it was difficult for service suppliers to seize customers from others unless they cut their prices to an unprofitable level to compensate customers' costs.	(2 marks)
	•	Since 1999, customers have been able to retain their phone numbers when changing mobile phone service suppliers and, as a result, the cost of changing service suppliers is much lower. Service suppliers found that it was still profitable for them to seize customers from others by cutting prices.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Suppose recently a Hong Kong property developer tried to boost its sales by selling new flats in Tseung Kwan O at a price 20 percent below the market level. Later, another property developer also lowered the price for its new flats in Tai Kok Tsui to 30 percent below the market level.
(a)	(i)	Identify the market structure of private residential development. Explain ONE of the features of the market structure illustrated by the above event.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	Suggest TWO features of the market structure other than that in (a)(i).		(4 marks)
(b)	(i)	Property agent A: Property developers lowered their prices because the number of completed private residential units increased considerably.
		Explain the opinion of property agent A (No need to draw a diagram).	
	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Property agent B: Apart from an increase in the number of completed private residential units, a fall in Hong Kong people's incomes was another factor in the decrease in property prices.
		Explain the opinion of property agent B (No need to draw a diagram).		(2 marks)
	(iii)	Compare the effects on the quantity transacted and the total revenue of private residential units under cases (b)(i) and (b)(ii).	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	•	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
		•	Sellers are interdependent.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	A few firms dominate the market.
		•	The firms supply heterogeneous products.
		•	Entry into the industry is difficult.
		•	Information is imperfect.
		•	Prices tend to be rigid. A price cut may lead to a price war.
		•	Price leadership occurs.
		•	Non-price competition is common.
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable features with brief explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

(b)	(i)	Supply increases when the number of completed private residential units increases. As a result, the price decreases.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Demand for private residential units decreases when consumers' income falls. Hence, the price of private residential units falls.	(2 marks)
	(iii)	•	Quantity transacted:
			In case (b)(i), the quantity transacted must increase. In case (b)(ii), the demand and the supply change in the opposite direction. Thus, the quantity transacted may increase, decrease or remain unchanged.	(2 marks)
		•	Total revenue:
			In case (b)(i), the total revenue may increase, decrease or remain unchanged, depending on the price elasticity of demand; in case (b)(ii), the demand and the supply change in the opposite direction. Thus, the total revenue may increase, decrease or remain unchanged, depending on the magnitude of the changes in demand and supply.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
The following is the price list of a firm Chan, Lam and Kwok, Solicitors.

Chan, Lam and Kwok, Solicitors	
	Fees	
Divorce	$5,000	
Mortgage	$1,800	

(a)	(i)	Name the type of business ownership of this firm.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	List THREE features of this business ownership.	(3 marks)
(b)	Identify the market structure of legal services in Hong Kong. Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Partnership	(2 marks)
	(ii)	•	It can have a minimum of two partners.
		•	It has no separate legal identity.
		•	Each partner's decision is binding on all other partners.
		•	Partners bear unlimited liability.
		•	There are regulations on the admission and withdrawal of partners.
		•	There is a lack of continuity.
		•	The setting up procedure is simple.
		(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable features, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

(b)	Monopolistic competition	(1 mark)
	Reasons:
	•	There are many legal firms in Hong Kong.
	•	The services provided by different firms are regarded as heterogeneous by consumers.
•	Information is imperfect.
	(Accept other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Mr Wong runs a clinic in Tung Chung in the form of a sole proprietorship. Recently, a large medical centre opened nearby. The medical centre has a full range of facilities and provides a variety of services.
(a)	Suppose Mr Wong's consulting fee remains unchanged. With the aid of a diagram, explain how Mr Wong's income from medical services will be affected by the opening of the medical centre.	(6 marks)
(b)	The medical centre is owned by several doctors in the form of a partnership. They specialise in different medical services. Explain TWO distinctive features of the medical centre's business ownership in comparison with Mr Wong's clinic.				(4 marks)
(c)	'In Hong Kong, entry to the private medical services industry is restricted as a doctor must obtain a licence before practising. Hence, private clinics in Hong Kong compete under an oligopoly.'
	Is this statement correct? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Medical services provided by the medical centre are close substitutes for that of Mr Wong.	(1 mark)
	•	The demand for Mr Wong's medical services will decrease (D0 ( D1).		(1 mark)
	•	If the consulting fee remains unchanged, the quantity transacted will decrease (Q0 ( Q1).	(1 mark)
	•	His income from medical services decreases (P0Q0 ( P0Q1).	(1 mark)
	
			(2 marks)

(b)	• 	With more than one owner
	•	With wider sources of capital
	•	With specialisation in management
	•	With sharing in cost and risk
	•	Lower flexibility in decision making
	•	Difficult to transfer ownership (The consent of all partners is required.)
	(Any TWO of the above with explanation, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

(c)	•	An oligopoly is a market structure in which several sellers dominate the market.	(2 marks)
	•	There is no dominant private clinic in Hong Kong.	(1 mark)
	•	Therefore, the statement is incorrect.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch213 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Suppose a group of three university students successfully invented a new energy source that could be a substitute for crude oil. The group collectively starts a firm in the form of a partnership selling this energy source.
(a)	List THREE characteristics of this form of business ownership.	(3 marks)
(b)	What is the market structure of the firm? Explain.	(2 marks)
(c)	Does the firm face any competition? Explain.	(3 marks)
(d)	What will the market structure be if the group breaks up and each of the three individuals starts his/her own firm selling the same energy source? Explain.		(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Not a legal entity
	•	Unlimited liability
	•	Strong incentive for efficient management
	•	Lack of continuity
	•	Minimum of two owners
	•	Not necessary to disclose financial accounts to public
	(Any THREE of the above or other correct characteristics, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

(b)	•	Monopoly	(1 mark)
	•	The group forms a single seller of a product for which there are no close substitutes.	(1 mark)

(c)	Yes.	(1 mark)
	•	Compete with others for the right to be the sole seller in the market, e.g., against potential entrants
	•	Compete with producers of substitutes for customers
	•	Compete with other producers for resources
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(d)	•	Oligopoly	(1 mark)
	•	A few sellers (three) dominate the market in supplying the same product.		(1 mark)

questions.topic: B2 · Ch214 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
(a)	What is profit maximisation? 	(2 marks)
(b)	What TWO approaches are used to determine the profit-maximising output? Briefly explain the conditions for profit maximisation. 	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Profit maximisation means the pursuit of the largest net receipts, which is equal to the difference between total revenue and total cost.	(2 marks)
(b)	The two approaches are the total revenue and total cost approach, and the marginal revenue and marginal cost approach.	(2 marks)
	•	According to the total revenue and total cost approach, the profit-maximising output is the output at which there is the greatest difference between total revenue and total cost.	(1 mark)
	•	According to the marginal revenue and marginal cost approach, the profit-maximising output is the output at which the marginal revenue is equal to the marginal cost.	(1 mark)

(b)	Suppose both the price and the fixed cost decrease by $1. Find the new profit-maximising output and the change in profit.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When output = 5 units, marginal cost = price = $13. Therefore, the profit-maximising output is 5 units.	(1 mark)

The following table shows the data for a firm operating in a price-taking market.

Output
(units)	Marginal cost
($)	
0	―	
1	7	
2	8	
3	9	
4	10	
5	11	
6	12	

Suppose the product price is $10 and the fixed cost is $2.
(a)	Find the profit-maximising output for the firm and the corresponding total profit. Show your work.	(4 marks) 
(b)	If the fixed cost increases by $2, will the profit-maximising output and the corresponding total profit in (a) change? Explain your answer.	(3 marks)
(c)	Suppose the government provides a unit subsidy of $2. Find the firm's new profit-maximising output and the corresponding total profit.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The profit-maximising output is 4 units where P = MR = MC (= $10).	(2 marks)
	Total profit at 4 units of output 
	= $(10 - 7) + $(10 - 8) + $(10 - 9) - $2	(1 mark)
	= $4		(1 mark)

(b)	As the fixed cost does not affect the marginal cost of the firm, the profit-maximising output remains unchanged at 4 units,	(2 marks)
	Total profit at 4 units of output will change from $4 to $2.	(1 mark)


(c)	After the provision of the unit subsidy, the marginal cost of each unit of output decreases by $2 (except for zero unit of output). The effects are shown in the table below.

Output
(units)	Old MC
($)	New MC (= Old MC - Unit subsidy) ($)	
0	―	―	
1	7	5 (= 7 - 2)	
2	8	6 (= 8 - 2)	
3	9	7 (= 9 - 2)	
4	10	8 (= 10 - 2)	
5	11	9 (= 11 - 2)	
6	12	10 (= 12 - 2)	
	(2 marks for new marginal cost)
	The profit-maximising output is 6 units where P = MR = MC (=$10) and the total profit is $13 [= ($10 - $5) + ($10 - $6) + ($10 - $7) + ($10 - $8) + ($10 - $9) - $2].	(2 marks)

A.	marginal benefit may still be positive.

questions.text:
The following table shows the production cost of a price-taking firm.

Total output (units)	1	2	3	4	5	
Marginal cost ($)	2	4	6	8	10	
Average variable cost ($)	2	3	4	5	6	
Fixed cost ($)	2	2	2	2	2	

If the product price is $8,
A.	the firm will produce 5 units of output to maximise its profit.
B.	the maximum profit the firm can make is $10.
C.	the average cost is $5 when the firm maximises its profit.
D.	the producer surplus is $10.
questions.answerText:
:
If the product price is $8, the profit maximising output is 4 units where the marginal cost is equal to the price. At this output, the producer surplus is $12 [= ($8 × 4) - ($5 × 4)], while the profit is $10 [= ($8 × 4) - ($5 × 4) - $2]. The average cost is $5.5 
[= $22 / 4].

When the market price is $3, the quantity supplied is __________ and the producer surplus is __________.

B.	4 units … $5
C.	5 units … $4
D.	5 units … $5
questions.answerText:
:
When the price is $3, the profit-maximising output is 4 units where the marginal cost is equal to the price. At this output, the total variable cost is $7 (= $8 - $1). As a result, the producer surplus is $5 [= ($3 × 4) - $7].

questions.text:
The schedule below shows the marginal benefit of consumers.

3	80

Suppose the market price is $90. Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?
(1)	At this market price, the consumer surplus is maximised when two units of the good are consumed.
(2)	We cannot find the consumer surplus since we do not have information about the marginal cost.
(3)	If there is an increase in supply so that the price decreases to $70, the consumer surplus will increase by $60.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
:
Option (3) is incorrect. The old consumer surplus is $10 (= $100 + $90 - $180). The new consumer surplus is $60 (= $100 + $90 + $80 + $70 - $280). Thus, the consumer surplus will increase by $50 (= $60 - $50).

B.	The new producer surplus is more than $6.

questions.answerText:
:
Original equilibrium price = $6

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: Stephy said, 'If there is a difference between marginal benefit and marginal cost at the quantity transacted, the total social surplus is not maximised. But if the total social surplus is maximised, the total benefit is equal to the total cost.' Comment on Stephy's statement.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
The first part of Stephy's statement is correct. Whenever there is a difference between the marginal benefit (MB) and marginal cost (MC) at the quantity transacted, total social surplus can be increased either by raising production or cutting production to the point where MB = MC. 	(2 marks)
The second part of her statement is not correct. The condition for maximising total social surplus is MB = MC, which does not imply that the total benefit equals the total cost. The total social surplus is equal to the total benefit minus the total variable cost. It can be greater than zero.	 (2 marks)
(Note: Even if the total benefit is equal to the total cost, the total social surplus is greater than zero if the fixed cost is greater than zero.)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: * A farmer who studied Economics said, 'Under a competitive market, the price of each apple must be the same as the marginal cost for each apple. Thus, there is no difference between the price and marginal cost, and the amount I can receive is exactly my cost of production. Thus, a competitive market is not good for farmers.' Do you agree? Explain your answer.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
No.	(1 mark)
Under a competitive market, only the marginal cost of the last unit of apples is the same as the price. Thus, farmers can still gain a producer surplus equal to the sum of the difference between the price and the marginal cost for all units sold.	(2 marks)

questions.answerText:

The profit will be $0 [∵Profit = Total revenue - Total cost = $12 ( 3 - $12 ( 3 = $0].	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: 'Under a perfectly competitive market, when the total social surplus is maximised, both the consumer surplus and producer surplus will be maximised too.' Do you agree? Explain your answer.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Agree.		(1 mark)

questions.text: Musical talent is considered necessary for children to enrol in popular kindergartens. Explain how this raises the producer surplus of piano classes. (Diagram is NOT required.)	(4 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: A representative of restaurant owners said, 'As the price of seafood falls, our customers can gain.' WITHOUT the aid of a diagram, explain this statement using the concept of consumer surplus.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Seafood is an input for restaurants in providing their services. As the price of seafood falls, the supply of restaurant services increases.	(1 mark)
As a result, the price of restaurant services decreases while the quantity of the services increases.	(2 marks)
Since customers can enjoy more services at a lower price, their consumer surplus increases. They can gain from it.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
Suppose more Southeast Asians are living in Shenzhen. This increases the demand for basmati rice (印度大米). Explain the function of price performed in the following cases.

	As the relative price of basmati rice increases, more resources are allocated to bring basmati rice to Shenzhen.	(1 mark)
(b)	Rationing function	(1 mark)
As the price of basmati rice increases, only those who are willing and able to pay the price can get basmati rice in Shenzhen.	(1 mark)

The following table shows the cost schedule of a price-taking firm which has no fixed cost.

Suppose the product price is $23.

(b)	If the price decreases by $2, calculate the change in profit.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When output = 4 units, marginal cost = price = $23. Therefore, the profit-maximising output is 4 units.	(1 mark)

	Change in profit = ($21 × 2) - $(20 + 21) - $6 = $1 - $6 = -$5	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:

questions.answerText:

	(	Increase in demand for computer games	(1 mark)

	(	Increase in price	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
	The demand for game playing broadcasts is a derived demand from the demand for computer games.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
Both Mary and Sally like candy very much. Tom does not like candy at all.
(a)	'Mary has eaten six pieces of candy and Sally has eaten three pieces. As a result, Mary enjoys a greater consumer surplus than Sally.'
	Comment on the statement.	(4 marks)
(b)	Under what condition will Mary's total expenditure on candy decrease when the price decreases? Explain your answer with the aid of a diagram.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Consumer surplus refers to the difference between the total maximum amount a consumer is willing to pay and the total amount he actually pays for a given quantity of a good.	(2 marks)
	Since their marginal benefit curves (or demand curves) are different, we cannot conclude that Mary enjoys a greater consumer surplus than Sally simply based on the fact that Mary consumes more candy than Sally.	(2 marks)
	(Graphical explanation is also accepted.)

(b)	If Mary's demand for candy is inelastic, the percentage decrease in price is greater than the percentage increase in quantity demanded. In this case, her total expenditure will decrease.	(2 marks)
	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Price decreases while quantity demanded increases.	(1 mark)
(	The decrease in total expenditure caused by the decrease in price is greater than the increase in total expenditure caused by the increase in quantity demanded.	(2 marks)

*(c)	To encourage traders to stop doing business, what would the minimum amount of compensation to the traders be? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)

	(3 marks)

(b)	The decrease in supply would lead to an increase in price while the decrease in demand would lead to a decrease in price. Thus, the overall effect on price would be uncertain.	(2 marks)

(c)	The amount of compensation should at least cover the cost of ceasing to do business. The cost of not selling is equal to the value of selling live chickens.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
Traditionally, when prices are rising, people will buy more gold as a store of value (價值儲藏). Thanks to global inflation, demand for gold has increased rapidly. In addition, as income levels in China increase, demand for gold jewellery is increasing sharply. This trend is expected to continue. However, as the costs of gold exploration and mining are increasing rapidly, the supply of gold is declining.
(a)	With reference to the above information, explain why gold prices may continue to increase.	(4 marks)
(b)	If the quantity transacted of gold decreases, what will the change in the total social surplus be? Draw a diagram to show your answer.	(3 marks)
(c)	Paul has $1 million. He can either choose to deposit his money into banks to earn interest or buy gold. Explain whether the cost will change in the following cases if he chooses to buy gold.
(i)	Interest rates increase rapidly.	(2 marks)
(ii)	A financial crisis occurs again. There are massive bank runs (擠提) in the country.	(2 marks)
(iii)	There is a rumour that the price of gold will decrease.	(2 marks)
(iv)	After Paul has bought gold, interest rates increase and the price of gold dramatically decreases.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Some demand for gold is derived from the demand for gold jewellery. Thus, the increase in the demand for gold jewellery will lead to an increase in the demand for gold. The increase in the demand for gold will lead to an increase in the price of gold.	(2 marks)
The increase in the cost of gold exploration and mining will lead to a decrease in the supply of gold. This will lead to an increase in the price of gold.	(2 marks)

(b)	The total social surplus will decrease from Triangle BAC to Triangle B'A'C'.
		(1 mark)

	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	If Paul chooses to buy gold, he will forgo the opportunity to earn interest. Thus, if interest rates increase, his cost will increase.	(2 marks)
(ii)	As the risk that banks cannot repay depositors' money increases, the expected value of depositing money into a bank decreases. Thus, the cost of buying gold will decrease.	(2 marks)
(iii)	The change in expectations about the price of gold will not affect the value of depositing money into the bank (which is the highest-valued option forgone). Thus, the cost will remain unchanged.	(2 marks)
(iv)		When an action has been taken, nothing can affect the cost of the action. When measuring the cost of an action, we only consider the options available within the decision-making period. Thus, an increase in interest rates will not be counted in the cost of buying gold. The cost of buying gold (which is a sunk cost or historical cost now) will not change.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch315 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
Due to climate change, dry areas have become drier and water shortages have worsened. Less land can be used to produce barley, a key ingredient of beer. Thus, it is expected that barley production will decline and so will beer. Some breweries are looking for new varieties of barley, which can better cope with climate change.
(a)	Using the concept of consumer surplus, explain why beer drinkers will suffer as a result of climate change. Show your answer using a diagram.	(6 marks)
(b)	Suppose some breweries find a new variety of barley which can be grown on dry land at a very low cost. How will this discovery affect the quantity transacted and price of beer? With the aid of a diagram, explain how drinkers and breweries will benefit.	(7 marks)
(c)	Suppose, because of climate change, the quality of barley declines so that the demand for beer decreases. What change will there be in the quantity transacted, price, consumer surplus, producer surplus and total social surplus in the beer market? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Climate change will lead to a decrease in the supply of barley.	(1 mark)
The price of beer will increase from P0 to P1 and the quantity of beer transacted will decrease (from Q0 to Q1). People will drink fewer beers and pay a higher price.	(2 marks)
Therefore, the consumer surplus, which measures the gain from consumption, will decrease (from Triangle CP0A to Triangle CP1A').	(1 mark)

	(2 marks)

(b)	The discovery of the new variety of barley will lower the cost of producing beer. This will lead to an increase in the supply of beer.	(1 mark)
	The quantity transacted will increase (from Q1 to Q2). 	(1 mark)
	The price will decrease (from P1 to P2).	(1 mark)
	The consumer surplus will increase from Area CP1A to AreaCP2A'.	(1 mark)
	The producer surplus will increase from Area P1BA to Area P2B'A'.	(1 mark)

	(2 marks)

(c)	The quantity transacted will decrease from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)
	The price will decrease from P1 to P2.	(1 mark)
	The consumer surplus will decrease from AreaCP1A to Area C'P2A'.	(1 mark)
	The producer surplus will decrease from Area P1BA to Area P2BA'.	(1 mark)
	The total social surplus will decrease from Area CBA to Area C'BA'.	(1 mark)

	(2 marks)

questions.text:
* Which of the following imply that resource allocation is efficient?
(1)	The total social surplus is maximised.
(2)	Producers produce up to a point where MB = P = MC.
(3)	Both consumers and producers try to maximise their own interests.
(4)	The consumer surplus is maximised.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(3) and (4) only
questions.answerText: Option (3) is not the answer. It is the basic assumption of the behaviour of consumers and producers. Even if both consumers and producers try to maximise their own interests, this does not guarantee that the market is efficient. For example, in a monopoly, both consumers and producers will also maximise their gains. However, the market is still inefficient.

questions.answerText: Option D is incorrect. If the increase in output is large enough so that there is an overproduction (instead of an underproduction), it is possible that the total social surplus will decrease.

questions.text:
* Refer to the diagram below.

When the output level is at Qf, there is a deadweight loss because
A.	the market price is at Px, which is lower than the equilibrium price.
B.	Pf > Px, which implies that there is a potential loss from an increase in the output level.
C.	Pf > Px, which implies that total social surplus can be increased by producing more.
D.	the market price is at Pf, which implies that producers do not maximise their producer surplus.
questions.answerText: Pf is the price after the imposition of a price floor, which is also equal to the marginal benefit at Qf. Px is the marginal cost at Qf. Thus, Pf > Px implies that the marginal benefit is greater than the marginal cost at Qf. In other words, the marginal social surplus (= MB - MC) is greater than zero. There is a potential gain from an increase in the output level.

(3)	The total social surplus after the provision of the subsidy is equal to Triangle AEB minus Triangle EHI.

questions.answerText:
Option (3) is correct. From the viewpoint of producers, the subsidy can reduce their cost of production by Area BCIH. However, from the viewpoint of society, the subsidy is just a transfer as Area BCIH (which is equal to the government's subsidy) is the production cost borne by the government. Thus, the new TSS is equal to 
Area AIC - Area BHIC = Area AEB - Area EHI.

questions.text:
(a)	What is the condition for efficiency in resource allocation?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain how consumers and producers interact in a perfectly competitive market to achieve efficiency in resource allocation	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Efficiency in resource allocation is attained when the total social surplus is maximised.	(1 mark)
	The total social surplus is maximised when MB = MC.	(1 mark)
(b)	In a perfectly competitive market, the total social surplus is equal to the sum of the consumer surplus and the producer surplus.	(1 mark)
	To maximise their gains, consumers keep buying until P = MB and producers keep selling until P = MC.	(2 marks)
	In equilibrium, the condition MB = MC is satisfied and efficiency in resource allocation is attained.	(1 mark)
