(a)	Uncertain. The surplus will change from Area HIFB to Area GIEA. The change in the surplus is uncertain. It depends on the relative size of Area GHCA and 
Area CEFB.	(2 marks)
(b)	Loss. The number of foreign domestic helpers employed will decrease from Q1 to Q2 as the minimum wage increases.	(1 mark)
(c)	Gain. The surplus that each of the employed helpers earned will increase from $300 ($3,500 - $3,200) to $400 ($3,600 - $3,200).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text: With the aid of a diagram, explain the effect of reducing an effective quota on economic efficiency.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
(	Decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
(	Increase in deadweight loss	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
When the effective quota decreases, quantity transacted decreases.	(1 mark)
Hence, the deadweight loss increases by the shaded area.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Suppose the government increases the unit tax on cigarettes.
(a)	Explain the effect on economic efficiency, with the aid of a diagram.	(4 marks)
(b)	Tom said, 'As the unit tax increases, the cigarette tax revenue must increase.' 
Do you agree with him? Explain briefly.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Upward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Increase in deadweight loss	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	When the government increases the unit tax, the quantity transacted will decrease.
				(1 mark)
	The deadweight loss will increase by the shaded area.	(1 mark)
(b)	No.			(1 mark)
	Although the unit tax increases, the quantity of cigarettes sold decreases. Therefore, the change in the cigarette tax revenue is uncertain.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Refer to the following table about a perfectly competitive market.

Quantity (units)	Marginal benefit ($)	Marginal cost ($)	
1	8	2	
2	7	3	
3	6	4	
4	5	5	
5	4	6	

Suppose a unit tax of $2 is imposed.
(a)	What will the quantity transacted and the price be after the tax is imposed?	
		(4 marks)
(b)	How will the tax affect the consumer surplus?	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The following table shows the marginal costs after tax:
Quantity (units)	Marginal cost after tax ($)	
1	4	
2	5	
3	6	
4	7	
5	8	
		(2 marks)
	The quantity transacted will be 3 units (where MB = MC = $6).	(1 mark)
	The price will be $6.	(1 mark)
(b)	The original quantity transacted and price are 4 units and $5, respectively.
		(1 mark)
	The original consumer surplus = $(8 + 7 + 6 + 5) - ($5 × 4) = $6	(1 mark)
	The new consumer surplus = $(8 + 7 + 6) - ($6 × 3) = $3	(1 mark)
	The consumer surplus decreases by $3 (= $6 - $3).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
In Country A, the government decides to remove the environmental levy of $500 per unit of cars imported. Country A does not produce cars.
Suppose the supply of imported cars is perfectly elastic. What will the effects of the removal of the environmental levy be on the following items? 
(a)	The price of imported cars	(2 marks)
(b)	The number of cars imported	(1 mark)
*(c)	The consumer surplus and the producer surplus	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	As the supply of imported cars is perfectly elastic, the entire levy will be borne by consumers. Thus, the removal of the levy will decrease the price of imported cars by the amount of the levy (i.e., $500).	(2 marks)
(b)	The number of cars imported will increase as the price has decreased.	(1 mark)
(c)	The consumer surplus will increase as consumers can buy more cars at a lower price. The producer surplus will remain at zero as the marginal cost curve is horizontal.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text: * A government initially provided a unit subsidy to Good Y. Now, the government decides to set a price ceiling for Good Y at the market price under the subsidy and to abolish the subsidy. With the aid of a diagram, explain the changes in the consumer surplus and the producer surplus.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
(	Upward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
(	Decreases in the consumer surplus and the producer surplus	(2 marks)

Verbal elaboration:
As the government abolishes the unit subsidy, the supply of Good Y decreases from S to S'.			(1 mark)
The quantity transacted decreases from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)
Both the consumer surplus and the producer surplus decrease.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
(a)	Define deadweight loss.	(2 marks)
(b)	A government provides a unit subsidy for the provision of ferry services. Use a diagram to show the deadweight loss.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Deadweight loss is the loss in total social surplus, or the potential gain not being captured, when the marginal benefit is not equal to the marginal cost.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Supply curve shifts downwards	(1 mark)
(	Deadweight loss (= Area BCE)	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Mary: 'If the government provides a unit subsidy, the sum of the consumer surplus and the producer surplus will increase.'
Peter: 'If this is the case, then a subsidy must benefit society as a whole.'
(a)	Do you agree with Mary? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(4 marks)
(b)	Do you agree with Peter? Use the diagram in (a) to explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Supply curve shifts downwards.	(1 mark)
(	Increase in the sum of the consumer surplus and the producer surplus 
(Area P2BEG)	(1 mark)
	
Verbal elaboration:
(	Yes.	(1 mark)
(	The sum of the consumer surplus and the producer surplus will increase from ABP2 to AEG.	(1 mark)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
	The total government subsidy equals Area P2CEG, which is greater than the increase in the sum of the consumer surplus and the producer surplus 
(Area P2BEG). Therefore, there is a deadweight loss in Area BCE.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Suppose you are the Chief Executive of Country A and would like to increase the total social surplus in a perfectly competitive market. Would you agree to the following suggestions? Why?
(a)	Setting a minimum price control	(2 marks)
(b)	Setting a quota	(2 marks)
(c)	Providing a unit subsidy	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No. An effective minimum price control will lead to underproduction and a deadweight loss. Thus, this policy will decrease the total social surplus.	(2 marks)
(b)	No. An effective quota will lead to underproduction and a deadweight loss. Thus, this policy will decrease the total social surplus.	(2 marks)
(c)	No. The provision of a unit subsidy will lead to overproduction and a deadweight loss. Thus, this policy will decrease the total social surplus.	(2 marks)
(Accept any other reasonable answers)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Suppose you are the Chief Executive of Country A and your target is to increase the total social surplus in a perfectly competitive market. Would you agree to the following suggestions? Why?
(a)	Lower the level of an effective maximum price control (which is still effective after the change) 	(2 marks)
(b)	Removal of an effective quota	(2 marks)
(c)	Increase a unit subsidy	(2 marks)
(d)	Removal of a unit tax	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No. As the maximum price set by the government decreases, the problem of underproduction will worsen. The quantity transacted will be lower and the deadweight loss will increase. Thus, the total social surplus will decrease.
		(2 marks)
(b)	Yes. After the removal of the effective quota, the output level will increase to its efficient level and the market price will decrease. The total social surplus will increase. 	(2 marks)
(c)	No. An increase in the unit subsidy will increase the deadweight loss. The total social surplus will decrease.	(2 marks)
(d)	Yes. After the removal of the unit tax, the output level will increase to its efficient level and the market price will decrease. The total social surplus will increase.
	(2 marks)
(Accept any other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
To promote music, governments occasionally sell music festival tickets to the public at affordable prices. This attracts many people to queue for tickets, which can then be resold for more than the official price.

With the aid of the above diagram, explain how governments should adjust ticket prices to improve efficiency.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Official ticket price (P0), which is below market equilibrium (P1)	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in deadweight loss / Increase in total social surplus after price increase (shaded area)	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
As governments fix the price below the market equilibrium, the marginal benefit is higher than the marginal cost at the quantity transacted.	(1 mark)
There is a deadweight loss from underproduction.	(1 mark)
The deadweight loss can be reduced / Total social surplus can be raised by increasing ticket prices.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Wheat is the staple food in Country N. Some people have complained that the wheat price is too high. Therefore, the government has imposed an effective price ceiling on wheat.

(a)	On the above diagram, indicate the price and quantity transacted of wheat under the price ceiling as Pc and Qc, respectively.	(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose the wheat harvest is poor. With the aid of the above diagram, explain how the price, quantity transacted and consumer surplus will be affected.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Effective price ceiling	(1 mark)
	•	Price (Pc)	(1 mark)
	•	Quantity transacted (Qc)	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Leftward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	No change in price and decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in consumer surplus	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	Due to a poor harvest, the supply of wheat decreases from S to S'.	(1 mark)
	The price remains unchanged at Pc due to the price ceiling.	(1 mark)
	The quantity transacted deceases from Qc to Q1.	(1 mark)
	The consumer surplus decreases by the shaded area.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the demand for and supply of Good X, which is an inferior good in Country A.

Suppose Country A's consumer income has decreased recently.
(a)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain the change in price and quantity transacted of Good X.	(4 marks)
(b)	To maintain price stability, the government fixes the price of Good X at P0. Using the same diagram in (a), indicate the deadweight loss that results from the price control.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Increase in demand	(1 mark)
•	Increase in price and quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	
Verbal elaboration:
As Good X is an inferior good, a decrease in consumer income raises its demand. Both the price and quantity transacted increase.	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Effective price ceiling at P0	(1 mark)
•	Deadweight loss (shaded area)	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the market for etextbooks. The government initially imposed a price ceiling at P1.

Suppose the government raises the price ceiling to P2. With the aid of the above diagram, explain the effect of the change on economic efficiency.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Increase in price	(1 mark)
•	Increase in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in deadweight loss	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The effective price ceiling (P1) becomes ineffective (P2).	(1 mark)
The quantity transacted increases from Q1 to the efficient level (Q2) where marginal benefit is equal to marginal cost.	(1 mark)
Therefore, deadweight loss no longer exists and economic efficiency improves.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The government has provided leisure facilities like basketball and badminton courts for the public at a low booking charge, but many people have complained that they were unable to book the facilities.
Suppose the government raises the charge from P1 to P2.
(a)	Indicate the change in consumer surplus and producer surplus on the diagram below.	(2 marks)
	

(b)	Explain whether total social surplus will increase and the problem of a shortage will lessen.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Loss in consumer surplus = Gain in producer surplus (Area P2abP1)	(2 marks)
	
(b)	There is no change in total social surplus because the quantity transacted remains unchanged.	(1 mark)
	The problem of a shortage lessens because the quantity demanded decreases.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the market for seafood in Country C which has a price floor.

(a)	Explain whether the price floor is effective.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose Country C has recently invaded some islands, and the country's fishermen can now fish in the seas around the islands. With the aid of the above diagram, explain whether the market is efficient after the above change.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The price floor is ineffective as it is not set above the equilibrium price.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Rightward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Deadweight loss	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	As fishermen can fish in a larger area, the supply of seafood increases from S to 
S'.	(1 mark)
	Due to the price floor, the price and quantity remain unchanged at Pf and Q1, respectively.	(1 mark)
	The market is not efficient because a deadweight loss (the shaded area) exists.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Suppose the government imposes an effective price floor on gasoline to promote energy conservation.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain under what situation producers' total revenue will increase.	(5 marks)
(b)	With the aid of the same diagram, explain whether consumers gain or lose after the imposition of the price floor.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Effective price floor	(1 mark)
	•	Increase in total revenue > Decrease in total revenue	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	Due to the price floor, the price increases from P1 to Pf and the quantity transacted decreases from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)
	If the demand is inelastic, the percentage decrease in quantity transacted is smaller than the percentage increase in price. In this case, producers' total revenue increases.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Decrease in consumer surplus	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	Consumers lose because the consumer surplus decreases (by Area PfabP1).
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The government of Country K imposes a minimum wage (W1) on foreign domestic helpers from Country G as shown in the following diagram.

Recently, the income level in Country G has increased and more workers have chosen to stay in the country.
(a)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain under what situation the minimum wage will become ineffective.	(5 marks)
(b)	With the aid of the same diagram, explain whether Country K's employers of foreign domestic helpers will gain or lose under the situation in (a).	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Leftward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Increase in wages (higher than the minimum level)	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	The number of foreign domestic helpers from Country G will decrease as more workers choose to stay in Country G.	(1 mark)
	The supply of foreign domestic helpers in Country K will decrease from S to S'.
	(1 mark)
	If the equilibrium wage increases to a level higher than W1 (e.g., W2), the minimum wage will become ineffective.	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Decrease in consumer surplus	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	After the decrease in supply, employers will lose because the consumer surplus decreases by the shaded area.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
An effective minimum wage has been imposed in the property management industry. With the aid of a diagram, explain how an improvement in job prospects in the property management industry will affect the industry's economic efficiency.
	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Effective minimum wage	(1 mark)
•	Increase in supply	(1 mark)
•	Correct position of the increase in deadweight loss (Area abcd)	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The supply of labour for the industry will increase.	(1 mark)
With the same minimum wage, the quantity transacted remains unchanged.	(1 mark)
The gap between the marginal benefit and the marginal cost increases, leading to a greater deadweight loss.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
A government imposes an effective quota in the petroleum market.
(a)	Explain, with the aid of a diagram, the effect of the quota on the price and quantity transacted of petroleum.	(4 marks)
(b)	With new technology, petroleum producers can now use solar energy to replace coal in extracting crude oil (原油). Explain, with the aid of the diagram you have drawn in (a), how the new technology affects the producer surplus if the quota is still effective.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Effective quota	(1 mark)
•	Increase in price and decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	
Verbal elaboration:
Under the effective quota, the supply curve becomes kinked. The price increases while the quantity transacted decreases.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Downward shift of supply curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in producer surplus (shaded area)	(1 mark)
	
Verbal elaboration:
The new technology lowers production costs. The supply of petroleum increases.
	(1 mark)
With the same effective quota and demand, the price remains unchanged (at Pq). The lower marginal cost implies an increase in the producer surplus.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text: The government has imposed an effective quota (Qq) on Good X. Using the following diagram, indicate the change in deadweight loss if demand increases.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Rightward shift of demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in deadweight loss (Area abcd)	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the market for a good with a quota at Q1.

(a)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain the effects of the quota on the price and quantity transacted of the good.	(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose the quota is lowered to Q2. With the aid of the same diagram, explain how the efficiency of the market is affected.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Correct price (P0) and quantity transacted (Q0)	(1 mark)
Verbal elaboration:
The quota is ineffective as it is greater than the equilibrium quantity (Q0).
	(1 mark)
The price and quantity transacted are at the equilibrium levels (P0 and Q0, respectively).	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Supply curve under the new quota at Q2	(1 mark)
•	Increase in price	(1 mark)
•	Deadweight loss	(1 mark)
Verbal elaboration:
The quota becomes effective when it is lowered to Q2.	(1 mark)
At Q2, the marginal benefit is higher than the marginal cost.	(1 mark)
Therefore, a deadweight loss from underproduction emerges and the market is inefficient.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text: With the aid of a diagram, explain the effect of reducing the quota on imported lobsters on the total social surplus in the market.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Decrease in quota	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in total social surplus	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
When the government reduces the quota from Q1 to Q2, the supply of imported lobsters decreases from S1 to S2.	(1 mark)
The total social surplus decreases as the quantity transacted of imported lobsters decreases.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the market for steel with a quota.

Suppose the government increases the quota (assuming the new quota is still effective).
(a)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain how the price and quantity transacted of steel change.	(5 marks)
(b)	With the aid of the same diagram and referring to the consumer surplus, explain whether consumers gain.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Increase in effective quota	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in price	(1 mark)
	•	Increase in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	As the quota increases, the quantity transacted increases from Q1 to Q2 and the price decreases from P1 to P2.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Increase in consumer surplus	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	After the increase in the quota, consumers gain because the consumer surplus increases by the shaded area.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the market for ginseng (人蔘) in Country H.

Suppose the government imposes a unit tax on ginseng.
(a)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain the effects of the unit tax on the price and quantity transacted of ginseng in Country H.	(4 marks)
(b)	Mr Fong said, 'As the tax paid by producers and consumers is collected by the government, society as a whole would not lose due to the unit tax.' With the aid of the same diagram, explain whether Mr Fong is correct.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Upward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in price and decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
Verbal elaboration:
The supply of ginseng decreases from S to ST due to the imposition of the unit 
tax.	(1 mark)
The price increases from P1 to P2 and the quantity transacted decreases from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Deadweight loss	(1 mark)
Verbal elaboration:
He is not correct.	(1 mark)
Due to the unit tax, the production of ginseng (Q2) is lower than the efficient level (Q1).	(1 mark)
Society would lose as a deadweight loss emerges / total social surplus decreases.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Country A's government has imposed a per-unit sales tax on Good X.
(a)	Under what condition will producers bear a greater tax burden than consumers?
	(2 marks)
(b)	Will the removal of the tax improve efficiency? Explain your answer with the aid of a diagram.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Producers' tax burden will be greater if the elasticity of demand is greater than the elasticity of supply.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Increase in supply	(1 mark)
•	Increase in total social surplus (Area abc)	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
There is no underproduction for the market of Good X. Efficiency is improved as the deadweight loss is eliminated / total social surplus increases.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
* The following diagram shows the market supply and demand curves of alcohol. Suppose the government either imposes a per-unit tax (t) or a price floor (P1) on alcohol to reduce drunk driving.

With the aid of the above diagram, explain the difference in producer surplus between these two government interventions.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Correct position of quantity transacted after both interventions (Q1)	(1 mark)
•	Correct position of the price received by producers net of tax (P2)	(1 mark)
•	Correct position of the difference in producer surplus (Area P1abP2)	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The quantity transacted will decrease to Q1 under both government interventions.
	(1 mark)
The price that producers receive under the per-unit tax (P2) is smaller than that under the price floor.	(1 mark)
Compared with the price floor, the producer surplus is lower under the per-unit tax. The difference becomes government tax revenue.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Suppose Country G's government provides a per-unit subsidy to electric vehicle producers. With the aid of a diagram, explain the change in consumer surplus.
	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Downward shift of supply curve	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in price and increase in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
•	Increase in consumer surplus (Area P0XYP1)	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The government subsidy lowers the cost of producing electric vehicles.	(1 mark)
Therefore, the supply of electric vehicles increases, leading to a decrease in price and an increase in quantity transacted.	(1 mark)
Consumer surplus will increase.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
* The following diagram shows the market for vitamin pills in Country J where the government provides a unit subsidy on the good. S1 is the supply under subsidy.

Suppose the government abolishes the unit subsidy.
(a)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain the changes in the price paid by consumers, the price received by producers and the quantity transacted of vitamin pills in Country J.	(5 marks)
(b)	Naomi said, 'Both consumers and producers suffer a loss from the abolition of the subsidy. Therefore, society as whole loses.'
	(i)	Indicate the changes in consumer surplus and producer surplus in the above diagram.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Explain whether Naomi is correct.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Upward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in price paid by consumers, decrease in price received by producers and decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
Verbal elaboration:
The supply of vitamin pills decreases from S1 to S2 due to the abolition of the unit subsidy.	(1 mark)
The price paid by consumers increases from P1 to P3. The price received by producers decreases from P2 to P3. The quantity transacted decreases from Q1 to Q2.	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Decrease in producer surplus	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in consumer surplus	(1 mark)
(ii)	She is not correct.	(1 mark)
The reduced government expenditure on the subsidy is larger than the decreases in producer surplus and consumer surplus.	(1 mark)
Therefore, society would gain as a whole.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
* To protect the interests of low-income coffee farmers, some suggest granting the farmers a per-unit subsidy (s) while some suggest setting a minimum purchase price at P1.

With the aid of the above diagram, compare the per-unit subsidy and the minimum purchase price in terms of farmers' total income and the deadweight loss.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Correct position of total income (including subsidy) under a per-unit subsidy 
(= P1 × Q2)	(1 mark)
•	Correct position of total income under a minimum purchase price (= P1 × Q1)
	(1 mark)
•	Correct position of the deadweight loss under a per-unit subsidy (Area cde)
	(1 mark)
•	Correct position of the deadweight loss under a minimum purchase price (Area abc)	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
Farmers' total income is higher under the per-unit subsidy. For receiving the same price (including a subsidy), farmers can enjoy a higher income as they can sell more coffee beans.	(2 marks)
There is a deadweight loss from overproduction (Area cde) under a per-unit subsidy and a deadweight loss from underproduction (Area abc) under a minimum purchase price.	(2 marks)

Structured Questions

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Air pollution is serious in Province Jin. This is mainly caused by coal mining activities. The government decides to impose an effective price ceiling on coal to improve air quality in the province.

(a)	Refer to the above diagram. Should the government set the price ceiling at PA or PB? With the aid of the above diagram, explain how the goal can be achieved.
	(4 marks)
(b)	A government official said, 'We can also improve air quality by imposing a unit tax on coal instead of a price ceiling.' 
	(i)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain how a unit tax can achieve the goal. Assume that the effect of the unit tax on the price is the same as the price ceiling.	(4 marks)
	*(ii)	Explain the effects of changing the price ceiling to a unit tax on consumers, producers and the government.	(3 marks)
(c)	A coal mine owner said, 'Both the price ceiling and the unit tax will lead to inefficiency in the coal market.'
	(i)	Explain why he is correct.	(2 marks)
	*(ii)	Suggest ONE reason to explain why it is worthwhile for the government to intervene in the market.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Decrease in quantity	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	The price ceiling should be set at PB.	(1 mark)
	Under the effective price ceiling, the quantity transacted of coal will decrease from Q0 to Q1.	(1 mark)
	As less coal is mined, air quality will improve.	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	Indicate on the diagram:
		(	Upward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
		Verbal elaboration:
		When the government imposes a unit tax, the supply of coal decreases from S to ST.	(1 mark)
		The quantity transacted of coal decreases from Q0 to Q1.	(1 mark)
		As less coal is mined, air quality will improve.	(1 mark)
(ii)	Consumers will lose since the consumer surplus decreases from Area UVYPB to Area UYPA.	(1 mark)
	Producers will not gain or lose since the producer surplus remains unchanged at Area PBYZ.	(1 mark)
	The government will gain since it can earn tax revenue which equals to Area PAVYPB.
	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	With the price ceiling or the unit tax, the quantity transacted of coal (Q1) is lower than the efficient level (Q0).	(1 mark)
		There is a deadweight loss caused by underproduction.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Reason: The benefit of improvement in air quality outweighs the loss due to underproduction. (Accept other reasonable answers)	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
Suppose a government imposes an effective quota on the amount of sea fish caught in order to conserve fishery resources.
(a)	Are the sea fish supplied by fishermen a free good? Explain.	(3 marks)
(b)	'The quota will increase the fishermen's producer surplus.' 
Comment on the statement with the aid of a diagram.	(6 marks)
(c)	Under what situation will the fishermen's total revenue increase after the imposition of the quota? Explain.	(3 marks)
(d)	(i)	Define deadweight loss.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Suppose sea fish are a normal good. How will the deadweight loss caused by the quota change when people's income increases? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.	(1 mark)
	The available quantity is insufficient to satisfy all human wants. / People want to have more sea fish. / Costs are involved in catching sea fish. / The quantity demanded for sea fish is greater than the quantity supplied at zero price.	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	A quota which is below the equilibrium quantity	(1 mark)
(	Increase in the producer surplus	(1 mark)
(	Decrease in the producer surplus	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
(	The statement is incorrect.	(1 mark)
(	The producer surplus changes from Area 0P1C to Area 0P2BF. Whether the producer surplus increases or not depends on Area P1EBP2 and Area CEF.
	(2 marks)

(c)	The demand is inelastic (elasticity < 1).	(1 mark)
	In this case, the percentage increase in price is greater than the percentage decrease in quantity demanded. / The gain in revenue due to the increase in price is greater than the loss in revenue due to the decrease in quantity demanded.
	(2 marks)

(d)	(i)	Deadweight loss is the loss in total social surplus, or the potential gains not being captured, when the marginal benefit is not equal to the marginal cost.
	(2 marks)

(ii)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Demand curve shifts rightwards	(1 mark)
(	Increase in deadweight loss	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
(	When people have more income, their demand for sea fish (a normal good) increases.	(1 mark)
(	Deadweight loss increases from Area BCF to Area AEF.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
To ensure that rice farmers earn a respectable income, Country A imposes an effective price floor on rice.
(a)	Tommy says, 'Rice farmers' producer surplus may decrease as a result of the price floor.' Do you agree? Explain your answer with the aid of a diagram.	(6 marks)
(b)	Now the government provides a unit subsidy to rice farmers instead of imposing a price floor.
	(i)	Indicate the new producer surplus on a diagram that shows the result of the subsidy. How does the producer surplus change (when compared to the situation without any government intervention)?	(3 marks)
	(ii)	If you were a rice farmer, would you prefer a price floor or a subsidy? Explain your answer by referring to the producer surplus.	(3 marks)
	(iii)	From the viewpoint of society, is a price floor or a subsidy better? Use your answers above to explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	A price floor above the equilibrium price	(1 mark)
(	Increase in the producer surplus	(1 mark)
(	Decrease in the producer surplus	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
(	Agree.	(1 mark)
(	The producer surplus decreases when Area CEF is greater than Area P1EBP2.	(2 marks)

(b)	(i)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	The supply curve shifts downwards.	(1 mark)
(	Producer surplus after subsidy	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The producer surplus increases from Area P1BF to Area P2EG.	(1 mark)
(ii)	A subsidy.	(1 mark)
The producer surplus must increase if the government provides a subsidy, but the change in the producer surplus is unclear in the case of a price floor.	
	(2 marks)
(Accept other reasonable answers.)
	(iii)	None of them is necessarily better than the other.	(1 mark)
		Both will result in a deadweight loss. It is possible that either one will have a greater deadweight loss.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The government in City X finds that the prices of school textbooks rose to a record high last year. Some textbook publishers claim that the increase in the price was caused by the increase in the cost of paper and other production costs.
(a)	Explain why the total social surplus will decrease when paper prices increase. Illustrate your answer with a diagram.	(5 marks)
(b)	Suppose a unit subsidy is given to textbook publishers. Who will gain and who will lose from the provision of the subsidy, parents or publishers? Does society gain from the unit subsidy? Explain your answer with a diagram.	(6 marks)
(c)	Suppose more overseas students come to study in City X. Explain how the total amount of subsidy granted by the government and the producer surplus will change.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Decrease in total social surplus	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
	The increase in the price of paper will lead to a decrease in the supply of textbooks. The supply curve will shift leftwards from S1 to S2.	(1 mark)
As a result, the total social surplus will decrease by the dotted area as indicated on the diagram.	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Downward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Deadweight loss	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
	Both parents and publishers will gain from the subsidy. The consumer surplus will increase from Area AP0E to Area AP2I. The producer surplus will increase from Area P0BE to Area P2CI.	(2 marks)
Since the increase in CS and PS (Area BCIE) is smaller than the total amount of the subsidy provided by the government (Area BCIH), there is a deadweight loss and society will lose.	(2 marks)

(c)	The increase in the number of students increases the demand for textbooks.
	(1 mark)
	The quantity transacted of textbooks will increase.	(1 mark)
	As the unit subsidy remains unchanged, the total amount of the subsidy granted will increase.	(1 mark)
	Since both the price and quantity transacted increase, the producer surplus will increase.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
In a study carried out by the Housing Authority in 2016, the income index of public housing tenants increased by 16.1% from 2013 to 2015. The authority decided to raise public housing rents by 10% in September 2016.

(a)	Suppose the number of public housing units is fixed at Q0 and the original rent is R0. With the aid of the above diagram, explain the effect of the increase in rent on the consumer surplus.	(4 marks)
(b)	Explain the effect of increasing public housing rents on Hong Kong's post social transfer Gini coefficient.	(3 marks)
(c)	Suppose the government increases the number of public housing units by reducing the average size of the units to reduce the waiting time.
	(i)	With the aid of the same diagram in (a), explain the change in total social surplus.	(4 marks)
	(ii)	Explain the effect of increasing the number of public housing units on the rents of subdivided flats (劏房).	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Increase in rent	(1 mark)
	(	Decreases in consumer surplus	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	The rent increases from R0 to R1, while the number of public housing units remains at Q0.	(1 mark)
	As a result, the consumer surplus decreases by Area A.	(1 mark)

(b)	Public housing tenants mainly belong to the lower income group.	(1 mark)
	The increase in rents lowers their post social transfer income while the income of the higher income groups is not affected.	(1 mark)
	Income distribution will become more uneven and Hong Kong's post social transfer Gini coefficient will increase.	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	Indicate on the diagram:
		(	Rightward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
		(	Increases in total social surplus	(1 mark)
		Verbal elaboration:
		The number of public housing units increases from Q0 to Q1.	(1 mark)
		As a result, total social surplus increases by Area (B+C+E).	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Public housing units are substitutes for subdivided flats.	(1 mark)
		When the supply of public housing units increases, the demand for subdivided flats will decrease.	(1 mark)
		Hence, the rents of subdivided flats will decrease.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the supply and demand curves for mooncakes around Mid-Autumn Festival.

Suppose the harvest of lotus seeds (蓮子) is bad this year.
(a)	With the aid of the above diagram, explain the changes in the price and quantity transacted of mooncakes.	(5 marks)
(b)	(i)	Explain under what condition the total expenditure on mooncakes would increase.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Suggest ONE reason to explain the price elasticity of demand for mooncakes implied in part (i).	(2 marks)
(c)	Chi Wa says, 'The government should grant a unit subsidy to mooncake producers before the Mid-Autumn Festival. Both producers and consumers would gain from the subsidy and hence economic efficiency would improve.' Explain whether he is correct.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Increase in price and decrease in quantity transacted	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	As the harvest of lotus seeds is bad, the input cost of mooncakes increases.
	(1 mark)
	The supply of mooncakes decreases from S to S'.	(1 mark)
	The price increases from P1 to P2 and the quantity transacted decreases from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	If the demand for mooncakes is inelastic, the percentage increase in price is larger than the percentage decrease in quantity transacted. As a result, total expenditure increases.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	It is a tradition to have mooncakes during the Mid-Autumn Festival. People would hardly reduce consumption even when the price increases.	(2 marks)
(c)	No.	(1 mark)
	The total subsidy paid by the government would be greater than the increase in the sum of the consumer surplus and producer surplus. Hence, there would be a deadweight loss.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch316 · Competition and efficiency
questions.text:
The Chinese government adopted a minimum purchase price scheme for corn before 2016. According to the scheme, the government maintained corn prices at a certain level (i.e., P1) and bought any excess supply on the market. China had the world's highest corn inventory in 2016.
	

(a)	(i)	With the aid of the above diagram, indicate the excess supply and the Chinese government's total expenditure on corn. Briefly explain your answer.
	(5 marks)
	(ii)	Label the producer surplus on the same diagram. Briefly explain whether society would gain from the scheme.	(3 marks)
(b)	In 2016, the Chinese government cancelled the scheme and started to auction its corn inventory each week. With the aid of the above diagram, explain the effect on corn prices in China.	(4 marks)
(c)	Corn is commonly used to feed livestock. Explain the effect of the cancellation of the scheme on the price of livestock in China.	(3 marks)
(d)	Explain under what circumstance consumers' total expenditure on corn would increase after the cancellation of the scheme.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Indicate on the diagram:
		(	Excess supply	(1 mark)
		(	Government total expenditure	(1 mark)
		Verbal elaboration:
		At P1,the quantity demanded (Q1) was lower than the quantity supplied (Q2).
	(1 mark)
		Hence, there was excess supply (Q2 - Q1) of corn.	(1 mark)
		The government bought the excess supply at P1. Therefore, its total expenditure was equal to the shaded area.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Indicate on the diagram:
		(	Producer surplus (Area P1AB)	(1 mark)
		Verbal elaboration:
		Society would not gain because the government's total expenditure was larger than the increase in the sum of consumer surplus and producer surplus.
	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Rightward shift in supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Decrease in price	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	As the government auctioned its corn inventory, the supply of corn increased from S to S'.	(1 mark)
	Due to the cancellation of the scheme, the price would decrease from P1 to the new equilibrium price, P2.	(1 mark)


(c)	As corn is an input for raising livestock, 	(1 mark)
	the decrease in corn prices will lead to an increase in the supply of livestock.
	(1 mark)
	Thus, the price of livestock will decrease.	(1 mark)

(d)	If the demand for corn is elastic, the percentage decrease in price will be smaller than the percentage increase in quantity demanded, so consumers' total expenditure will increase.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Under which of the following cases does the problem of externalities NOT exist?
(1)	A famous tenor sings in an opera house in London and is fully compensated.
(2)	Eddie buys a diamond ring as a gift for his girlfriend but receives nothing in return from his girlfriend.
(3)	Tony studies Finance at a university. He pays all the educational expenses by himself.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Externalities exist when a party's action affects other parties but there is no _____________ or ____________.
A.	increase in output; decrease in price
B.	compensation paid; payment received
C.	tax paid; subsidy received
D.	production cost paid; profits earned

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
________ externalities exist when a party's action _______ other parties but no compensation is paid to the other parties.
A.	Beneficial; benefits
B.	Positive; involves
C.	Harmful; harms
D.	Negative; negates

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A negative externality exists if there is a divergence between ________ in the market.
A.	private and social costs
B.	total cost and total benefit
C.	private and social benefits
D.	social benefit and social cost

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A positive externality exists if there is a divergence between __________ in the market.
A.	average and social benefits
B.	private and social benefits
C.	total cost and total benefit
D.	social benefit and social cost

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is an example of a divergence between private and social benefits?
A.	A full-time teacher teaches his students during the summer holidays without receiving payment from his students.
B.	On Mother's Day, a mother receives a kiss from her daughter free of charge.
C.	Coco cooks and her neighbours enjoy the smell.
D.	Janice sings in a charity show and is fully compensated.
questions.answerText: Option A is not correct. If the economic agent is paid according to his contribution, there is no beneficial externality. In this case, the teacher receives compensation from his school to teach his students.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Externality exists when 
A.	a tutor receives his salary.
B.	a consumer buys clothes at a discount.
C.	Mary enjoys the music played by her neighbour free-of-charge.
D.	a company pays dividends to its shareholders.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is an example of positive externality?
A.	pollution
B.	new knowledge
C.	traffic congestion
D.	overfishing

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A famous women's volleyball player visits Hong Kong. Which of the following are her private benefits?
(1)	The payment she receives for attending functions in shopping malls
(2)	The increase in the popularity of her national volleyball team
(3)	The increase in her image royalties (肖像使用費)
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is an external cost of a fireworks show organised by the government?
A.	Payment to fireworks manufacturers
B.	Increase in revenue of nearby shops
C.	Police manpower employed to maintain order in the area
D.	Light pollution

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is NOT an external benefit of maintaining a residential building?
(1)	The increase in the price of the building
(2)	Reduction in the building's insurance fee as the external walls pose less danger to passersby
(3)	The comfort of the residents in the building (residents have paid their maintenance fee)
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
There is a long queue outside a newly opened snack shop. Which of the following is an external cost of its opening?
A.	Extra wages to hire more workers to cater to the unexpected queue
B.	The amount already paid to purchase food ingredients
C.	Loss of business at a neighbouring shop as the queue blocks its entrance
D.	The profit earned by the snack shop

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
John opens a factory. Which of the following may be included in his private costs?
(1)	Rent on the factory premises
(2)	Interest on his start-up capital borrowed from a bank
(3)	Damage that the production process imposes on the health of his workers
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText: Option (3) may be included in his private cost because this may reduce his workers' productivity.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Social cost includes the cost borne by
(1)	the government.
(2)	the economic agent taking the action.
(3)	individuals who are affected by the action.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
* Suppose Ming only considers the private cost of having lunch at McDonald's. Which of the following is correct?
A.	Inefficiency must exist as he does not consider the social cost.
B.	There will be a divergence between private cost and social cost because the wages for McDonald's staff are too low.
C.	The government should intervene as the social cost will be greater than the private cost.
D.	Ming's action can be efficient.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is a divergence between private and social costs,
A.	inefficiency may exist due to underproduction.
B.	an external benefit must exist.
C.	the difference between the costs is the external cost.
D.	the government must take action to correct it.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If all drivers considered the external costs they imposed on other drivers, then
A.	no one would drive.
B.	travel time would be shortened.
C.	the road must not be fully utilised.
D.	society would suffer a loss.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
The socially optimal output level will be attained when
A.	private cost equals social cost.
B.	marginal private cost equals marginal private benefit.
C.	total social benefit equals total social cost.
D.	there is no deadweight loss.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
From the viewpoint of economics, the efficient level of timber harvesting (砍伐林木) is the level at which
A.	there is no timber harvesting at all.
B.	the total social cost of timber harvesting is at a minimum.
C.	the total social benefit from timber harvesting equals the total social cost of timber harvesting.
D.	the marginal social benefit from timber harvesting equals the marginal social cost of timber harvesting.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Given the quantity transacted, marginal social benefit equals marginal private cost in the market. Which of the following are correct?
(1)	If there is no negative externality, efficiency will be attained.
(2)	If there is an external cost, a deadweight loss exists.
(3)	If there is no external cost, inefficiency exists.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
* Suppose there is no external benefit. The efficient output level is attained if
A.	the marginal social benefit is equal to the marginal private benefit.
B.	the marginal social cost is equal to the marginal private benefit.
C.	the marginal social benefit is equal to the marginal private cost.
D.	Insufficient information to determine

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Society will experience overconsumption if the
A.	marginal social benefit is greater than the marginal private cost.
B.	marginal private cost is greater than the marginal private benefit.
C.	marginal private benefit is greater than the marginal social cost.
D.	marginal social cost is greater than the marginal social benefit.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Overproduction occurs when
(1)	there is an external cost.
(2)	there is an effective quota.
(3)	there is a unit subsidy.
A.	(1) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Andy loves to sing at midnight. This is an example of
A.	a negative externality.
B.	an external benefit if Andy's neighbourhood loves his songs and he does not receive any payment.
C.	an external cost as it is illegal to sing at midnight.
D.	an external benefit because this will help Andy become an excellent singer.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is a deadweight loss,
A.	underproduction must exist.
B.	overproduction must exist.
C.	marginal social surplus must not be zero.
D.	marginal social benefit must not be equal to marginal private cost.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Suppose a divergence between private and social costs exists, and economic agents only consider their own benefits and costs. Which of the following statements is correct?
A.	There is underproduction.
B.	There is excess supply.
C.	Total social benefit equals total social cost.
D.	The external cost is greater than zero.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Under which of the following situations will underproduction most likely occur?
A.	Ann talks loudly and disturbs other colleagues.
B.	Bob studies hard and gets full marks on his examination.
C.	Cathy, a web designer, builds a website for her client.
D.	Donald volunteers to do magic tricks in Victoria Park every Sunday to entertain pedestrians.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is an external cost, taxation may be used to correct the market because taxation can decrease the output level by
A.	decreasing the marginal social benefit.
B.	increasing the marginal private cost.
C.	increasing the marginal social cost.
D.	decreasing the marginal external benefit.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Under which of the following situations may taxation help improve efficiency?
A.	The excellent performance of Hong Kong athletes at the East Asian Games improves the image of Hong Kong.
B.	Some people watched the fireworks free of charge during the opening ceremony at the East Asian Games.
C.	Drinkers in Lan Kwai Fong (蘭桂芳) disrupt pedestrians.
D.	Some restaurants provide special offers at Christmas.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
From the viewpoint of society, which of the following can be the benefits of imposing a pollution tax to correct negative externalities?
(1)	Tax revenue from the pollution tax can be used to reduce pollution.
(2)	The deadweight loss decreases to zero.
(3)	Factories cut their output level to an efficient level.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is a possible way to narrow the divergence between private and social benefits in Hong Kong?
A.	Tobacco duty
B.	Grant to university students
C.	Levy on plastic bags
D.	Introduction of emissions trading

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A highway creates noise and disturbs residents nearby. Which of the following can lessen the problem of external cost?
(1)	Collecting charges from highway users
(2)	Subsidising nearby residents to install soundproof windows
(3)	Privatising the highway
A.	(1) only
B.	(2) only
C.	(1) and (2) only
D.	(2) and (3) only

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is a positive externality, which of the following measures may be used by the government to correct the problem?
A.	Taxation
B.	Price ceiling
C.	Quota
D.	Subsidy

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A subsidy may be used to correct the problem of externalities because it can
A.	reduce external cost.
B.	increase external benefit.
C.	reduce marginal private cost.
D.	reduce the output level.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If marginal social benefit is greater than marginal private benefit, then
A.	market exchange will not work.
B.	a subsidy must be provided to correct the market.
C.	an external benefit must exist.
D.	there is an overproduction.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
* Under which of the following situations can a subsidy help improve efficiency?
A.	An economics teacher shares his teaching materials with the public free of charge.
B.	Pirate Bay provides BitTorrent files free of charge (BitTorrent is an internet file sharing method).
C.	Internet search engine providers provide web searches free of charge.
D.	Baidu (百度) provides free MP3 song downloads.
questions.answerText: In Options B, C and D, the firms are usually paid by advertisers and the pay is positively related to the websites' number of hits. Hence, to increase their websites' hit rates, the firms will provide different services free of charge. Subsidising those activities may lead to a decrease in efficiency, instead of an increase in efficiency.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is a harmful externality, then the government may
A.	subsidise economic agents which generate the external costs.
B.	restrict the output level to reduce the deadweight loss.
C.	do nothing because the market will always solve the problem itself.
D.	take over all private firms because only public firms can produce without generating an external cost.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Recently, the Chinese government tore down some illegal cement plants because the plants could not meet environmental protection requirements. This intervention is an example of
A.	taxation and subsidisation.
B.	public ownership.
C.	market exchange.
D.	restriction or removal by regulation.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
In Hong Kong, some primary and secondary schools are owned and run by the government. This is an example of
A.	market exchange.
B.	integration.
C.	free goods.
D.	public ownership.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is an example of market solutions to the problem of externalities?
A.	The government subsidises firms which generate an external benefit.
B.	The government taxes firms which generate an external cost.
C.	The government restricts output to a certain level.
D.	The government defines private property rights for scarce resources and thus market exchange emerges to reduce overproduction.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following are examples of market solutions to the problem of externalities?
(1)	Firms trade with each other for quotas to emit pollutants.
(2)	A factory, which pollutes a nearby farm, combines with the farm.
(3)	The government builds a tunnel.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
* The government may reduce pollution by issuing pollution permits because
A.	the government knows the efficient output level and can implement the permit system efficiently.
B.	the marginal cost of producing the goods will increase as the producers must buy permits to increase production.
C.	the permits will justify pollution and increase the output level.
D.	the permits are given to firms exercising social responsibility and cannot be traded.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If pollution permits are granted and can be traded freely, then
A.	the pollution level must increase because pollution is legal now.
B.	the socially optimal output level must not be attained because a government cannot measure the amount of pollution accurately.
C.	firms will earn higher profits because they can pollute unrestrictedly if they can pay for the permits.
D.	the marginal private cost of production will increase so that the output level will decrease.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is traffic congestion,
A.	there is a divergence between private and social costs.
B.	the government should increase the gasoline tax.
C.	charging a toll for the use of the road must be efficient.
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A textile factory discharges pollutants into a river, threatening the health of downstream residents. Which of the following is true?
A.	Market transaction could solve the problem of pollution, regardless of the transaction cost involved.
B.	A tax should be imposed to limit the factory's production.
C.	Relocating the factory may be efficient.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Some people watch a football match from the roofs of nearby buildings without paying. Which of the following is correct?
A.	The government should intervene since it is dangerous to stand on building roofs.
B.	There is a divergence between private and social benefits.
C.	The football clubs should find ways to charge the people who watch from the roof.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Beekeeper's bees help pollinate fruit trees in a nearby orchard. At the same time, the bees collect honey from the fruit trees. Which of the following is correct?
A.	As there are external benefits, there is underproduction.
B.	The beekeeper should be paid for his pollination services.
C.	The government should subsidise the orchard owner to improve economic efficiency.
D.	There may be no divergence between private and social benefits.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If the cost of monitoring pollutant emissions is extremely high, then
A.	the introduction of emission trading may not solve the problem of externality.
B.	the introduction of emission trading will be efficient.
C.	the government must intervene to stop pollution.
D.	the level of pollutant emissions must be equal to the level permitted.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is a transaction cost, then the market exchange for correcting the negative externality
A.	must not work because the transaction cost must lead to a failure of market exchange.
B.	must work because the market solution is always the best solution.
C.	may still work when the transaction cost is small.
D.	may still work when the gain from market exchange is greater than the transaction cost.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Internalisation means that
A.	firms solve externalities via their internal divisions.
B.	firms reduce or remove harmful externalities through integration with each other.
C.	firms or people involved in harmful externalities will find their own ways to reduce or remove externalities.
D.	firms or people gain from internal economies of scale.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
In Hong Kong, some bus operators try to reduce air pollution by buying new bus models which emit fewer pollutants. This is an example of
A.	market exchange.
B.	integration.
C.	self-restraint.
D.	government intervention.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A cattle raiser erects a fence to prevent the cattle from damaging his neighbour's crops. This is an example of
A.	subsidisation.
B.	substitution.
C.	integration.
D.	internalisation.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
The problem of externality can be solved by combining separate firms into one under the same ownership because
A.	the combined firm will enjoy economies of scale.
B.	private costs become external costs.
C.	the combined firm must be under public ownership and so it will be concerned about society.
D.	the new firm will try to maximise the total gain from all activities under its control.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
There is emission trading (排污交易) between Country A (a developing country) and Country B (a developed country). Which of the following is correct?
A.	To achieve efficiency, most of the pollution permits should be assigned to Country A as it does not have money to buy the permits.
B.	It is fair for Country A to have more pollution permits as the pollution level in Country A should be lower.
C.	If the transaction costs are negligible, the initial assignment of pollution permits will not affect the result of resource allocation.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
To attract more customers, a stall at a book fair employs a young model to distribute its free gift. Which of the following is correct?
A.	To achieve efficiency, all other stalls at the book fair should pay the stall mentioned as they enjoy the external benefits from the employment of the young model.
B.	As the stall mentioned attracts customers from other stalls, it should compensate other stalls for their losses.
C.	The activity mentioned is just a means of non-price competition. Thus, no externality exists.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
To attract more customers, a stall at a book fair employs a young model to distribute its free gift. This attracts a group of amateur photographers to take photographs of the young model. Some stalls claim that the photographers disturb their business operation. Which of the following is correct?
A.	The stall which employs the young model should pay compensation to the affected stalls.
B.	If the transaction cost of obtaining compensation is extremely high, the affected stalls may choose to do nothing.
C.	If the affected stalls have the right to compensation, the problem of harmful externality must be solved.
D.	There is a divergence between private and social costs as the group of amateur photographers can take photographs of the young model free of charge.
questions.answerText: Option D is not correct. The reason for the existence of the divergence between private and social costs is not based on the price charged for taking photographs. Even the photographers need to pay a positive money price, if their actions harm other parties but if they do not pay compensation to the affected parties, the divergence between private and social costs will exist.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
To attract more customers, a stall at a book fair employs lots of young models to distribute its free gift. This attracts a group of amateur photographers who take photographs of the young models. Some stalls claim that the photographers disturb their business operations. Suppose the transaction costs involved are negligible and property rights are well-defined. Which of the following is correct?
A.	If the photographers have the right to take photographs and do not need to compensate the affected stalls, then they will take more photographs at the book fair.
B.	If the affected stalls have the right to compensation from the photographers, no photographer will appear at the book fair.
C.	Regardless of the assignment of the property right, the problem of harmful externality can be solved by market exchange.
D.	Regardless of the assignment of the property right, the affected stall will be efficient and receive the same amount of compensation.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Suppose there is no beneficial externality and the transaction costs involved are negligible. A factory's production now pollutes a fish farm. Which of the following is correct?
A.	The production will not be efficient if the potential gain from correcting the externality is small.
B.	The factory will stop polluting the fish farm.
C.	However the property rights are assigned, if the rights are well-defined, the production will be efficient.
D.	If the factory has the right to pollute, it will ignore the fish farm and continue to emit pollutants. This leads to deadweight loss.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Andy owns a factory that pollutes a small pool. Which of the following statements is correct?
A.	This is an example of a public good as the small pool can be used by all individuals at the same time.
B.	Inefficiency exists because the government does not impose a regulation to restrict Andy's behaviour.
C.	Nearby residents can request compensation from Andy.
D.	The problem of harmful externalities may not exist if Andy owns the pool.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Government intervention is justified if
A.	the market fails to allocate resources efficiently.
B.	the resource allocation favours the rich.
C.	it can increase income levels.
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText: Option A is incorrect. Government intervention may not be efficient if the cost of government intervention is greater than its benefit.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Even if there is a problem of externalities, it is not necessary for the government to intervene. This is because
A.	government intervention involves a high cost.
B.	a market solution is preferred by the public.
C.	government intervention may not be the least costly method.
D.	it is impossible for the government to allocate resources efficiently.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
When there is a negative externality,
A.	the private cost is higher than the social cost.
B.	the government must intervene.
C.	the government can subsidise production.
D.	output is higher than the efficient level.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
If there is a divergence between private and social benefits,
A.	the private benefit is smaller than the external benefit.
B.	an external cost exists.
C.	inefficiency may exist due to underproduction.
D.	the government must take action to correct it.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following statements is correct?
(1)	When tackling the problem of externalities, market solutions are preferred to government intervention.
(2)	The cost of government intervention may be greater than the reduction in deadweight loss due to the government intervention.
(3)	Market solutions to the problem of externalities cannot take place if private property rights are not well-defined.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A private good is
A.	owned by private individuals.
B.	produced by private enterprises.
C.	rival in consumption.
D.	a positive-priced good.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A public good is
A.	a good with an excess supply at zero price.
B.	a good whose consumption involves zero cost.
C.	a good that is difficult to prevent non-payers from using.
D.	All of the above

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is true?
A.	A private good is a consumer good.
B.	A public good is not scarce.
C.	A private good can only be consumed by the buyer.
D.	A public good can be consumed concurrently by many people.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is INCORRECT?
A.	A private good is scarce.
B.	A public good is scarce.
C.	There is no competition in the provision of public goods.
D.	There may be no competition in the consumption of public goods.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Private goods are goods of which
A.	one's consumption reduces the amount produced.
B.	one's consumption increases the amount available for others' consumption.
C.	one's consumption will not increase the amount available for others' consumption.
D.	one's consumption reduces the amount available for others' consumption.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Public goods are goods which are
A.	provided by the government.
B.	distributed freely.
C.	consumed by the public.
D.	non-rival and non-excludable in consumption.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is a private good provided by public enterprises?
A.	Public hospital services
B.	National defence
C.	TV programmes provided by the government
D.	An article written by Bill Gates

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:

B.	A bottle of distilled water

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following comes closest to a private good?

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is the closest to a public good?
A.	A Jan Lamb (林海峰) talk show
B.	The manuscript prepared for Jan Lamb's talk show

D.	Souvenirs sold at Jan Lamb's talk show

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following comes closest to a public good?
A.	A hot dog
B.	Beatles' songs
C.	A television set
D.	A public fish pond

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following comes closest to a private good?
A.	A TV programme
B.	Wi-Fi wireless internet access services
C.	Newspapers distributed at MTR stations
D.	An advertisement on a bus

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Stephy has dinner with her boyfriend and pays the bill. This is an example of
A.	an externality because Stephy's boyfriend does not pay for his dinner.
B.	a free good because Stephy's boyfriend can have his dinner for free.
C.	a public good because Stephy shares her money with her boyfriend.
D.	distributing output by prices because Stephy enjoys her dinner and pays the bill.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Public goods are goods which are
A.	rival and excludable.
B.	rival and non-excludable.
C.	non-rival and excludable.
D.	non-rival and non-excludable.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
A public computer in a library is a _____________ because ____________.
A.	private good … it is produced by private firms
B.	private good … it is rival in consumption
C.	public good … it is placed in public areas
D.	public good … everyone can use it

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
National defence is an example of a public good because
A.	all citizens are willing to pay for it.
B.	it can be consumed by all citizens at the same time.
C.	it is paid for with public funds.
D.	it is provided by the government.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Suppose an MP3 song by Andy Lau is now downloadable at his official website free of charge, and Andy Lau announces that all his fans may freely distribute the song to anyone. Which of the following is correct?
A.	The song is not a public good because it can only be freely shared on the internet.
B.	The song can be regarded as a private good because Andy Lau holds the private property rights to it.
C.	The song is a public good as it can be consumed by nearly all individuals at the same time.
D.	The song is a private good because a computer is needed to store it and play it.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
We would NOT regard a good as a 'public good' if
A.	it is not provided by the government.
B.	it is not consumed by the public.
C.	it is not financed by public funds.
D.	rivalry exists in its consumption.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
The City Forum (城市論壇) in Victoria Park can be regarded as a public good because
A.	the audience can participate free of charge.
B.	the speakers do not receive any payment.
C.	only a few individuals are interested in the Forum.
D.	it can serve many individuals at the same time.

questions.topic: B3 · Ch317 · The roles of government (I): market failure
questions.text:
Which of the following is the best example of public goods?
A.	Computers in a public library
B.	A public park
C.	An apple tree
