b.	Explain why the above stock transaction will increase Hong Kong's GDP.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
a.	i.	No, because it does not involve production.	(2 marks)
	ii.	No, because it does not involve production.	(2 marks)
b.	The value of services provided by the local investment company will be counted in Hong Kong's GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Explain which expenditure components of GDP may be affected by the following activities.
(a)	Sandy buys bottled water for her own consumption.	(3 marks)
(b)	The Hong Kong Police Force buys bottled water for the police.	(3 marks)
(c)	A foreign politician donates money to a domestic political party.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Private consumption expenditure will increase because it is a domestic household's expenditure on the consumption of a final product.	(3 marks)
(b)	The Hong Kong Police Force is a government department which is not engaged in market activities. Thus, its expenditure on final products should be included in government consumption expenditure. As a result, government consumption expenditure will increase.	(3 marks)
(c)	The donation is a transfer payment and should not be included in any expenditure components of GDP. However, as the political party has more money to spend, it may consume more goods. As a result, private consumption expenditure may increase.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
The government of Country A introduces unemployment benefits this year.
(a)	Explain whether unemployment benefits should be included in the current GDP.
	(3 marks)
(b)	Ka Ming is unemployed. He has received $5,000 in unemployment benefits and spent all the money on his basic needs. Explain whether Country A's GDP will necessarily increase by $5,000.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.	(1 mark)
	Unemployment benefits are transfer payments, which are not payments for current production.	(2 marks)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
	The goods and services that Ka Ming purchased may be imported / produced by non-resident producing units / not currently produced.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text: What are intermediate products? Explain why their values should NOT be counted in the calculation of GDP.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Intermediate products are inputs used up to produce goods and services for sale.
	(2 marks)
•	To cover costs, producers of final products would include the values of intermediate products in the values of their final products. Thus, their values should not be counted to avoid double counting.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text: Explain why the value of imported goods and services should be deducted from the total expenditure to find GDP.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Imported goods and services are not produced by local resident producing units.
	(2 marks)
•	However, they have already been included in private consumption expenditure, gross domestic capital formation and government consumption expenditure. So their value has to be deducted when we calculate GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Explain whether the value of the following activities is included in current GDP:
(a)	The sale of second-hand textbooks produced this year	(3 marks)
(b)	The sale of books unsold last year	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.	(1 mark)
The values of second-hand textbooks had been counted when they were sold for the first time. Thus, if their values were counted in the current GDP, there would be double counting.	(2 marks)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
Decreases in inventories are not included in current GDP because they represent sales of goods that are not currently produced.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Explain why the following items should NOT be counted in the current GDP.
(a)	The values of second-hand computers	(2 marks)
(b)	Expenditure on purchasing newly issued shares	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The values of second-hand computers had been counted when they were sold for the first time. Thus, if their values were counted in the current GDP, there would be double counting.	(2 marks)
(b)	The expenditure on purchasing financial assets (i.e., newly issued shares) is actually a provision of capital for firms in return for future incomes. The payment is not an expenditure on current production of goods and services.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Explain whether the following items should be included in GDP.
(a)	The commission paid to an insurance agent	(3 marks)
(b)	Expenditure on the purchase of government bonds	(3 marks)
(c)	The subsidy for child education provided to a civil servant by the government
	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Yes.	(1 mark)
This is because the commission represents the value of the services provided by an insurance agent.	(2 marks)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
This is because the transaction only represents a transfer of wealth without any corresponding production activity being involved.	(2 marks)
(c)	Yes.	(1 mark)
This is because the subsidy is a part of the reward to a civil servant for his services.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Explain whether the following items should be included in GDP.
(a)	The interest received by a depositor	(3 marks)
(b)	Expenditure on the purchase of shares in the Tracker Fund (盈富基金) of Hong Kong	(3 marks)
(c)	The repayment of principal on a home mortgage	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Yes.	(1 mark)
This is because the interest represents the reward to a depositor for his factor services (providing capital goods for production).	(2 marks)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
This is because the transaction only represents a transfer of wealth without any corresponding production activity being involved.	(2 marks)
(c)	No.	(1 mark)
The principal repayment is a transfer of money and so should not be included in GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Suppose there is an outbreak of bird flu (禽流感). The government destroys all chickens in Hong Kong. It provides compensation to the chicken farmers for their losses.
Is the value of the destroyed chickens included in Hong Kong's GDP? Explain with TWO reasons.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Not included.	(1 mark)
Reasons:
•	The destroyed chickens do not contribute to any increase in the amount of goods or services for people's consumption, nor are they counted as a change in stocks held by the chicken farmers.	(2 marks)
•	Even though the government compensates the chicken farmers for their losses, the amount of compensation is not counted in GDP as it does not have any corresponding production of equal value.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Suppose after reports of cases of hand, foot and mouth disease (手足口病) in Hong Kong, the government tells all kindergartens to close temporarily for cleaning. The cleaning expenditures are financed by the government and the cleaning services are provided by a local cleaning company.
Explain if the cleaning expenditures should be included in Hong Kong's GDP.
	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Included.	(1 mark)
The expenditures are used to buy final services.	(1 mark)
As they involve current production of a resident producing unit, they should be counted in GDP, regardless of who pays for them.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
At the beginning of last year, Mr Chan employed an interior designer to design the interior of his new home. The designer finished the design work in the first half of last year. Then, Mr Chan employed a local home furnishing company to furnish his new home. The furnishings were completed at the end of last year but the payment was made in the current year.
Explain whether the following statements are true or not:
(a)	The payment for the designer's services was included in last year's GDP.
	(3 marks)
(b)	The expenditure on furnishings should be counted in the current GDP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	True.	(1 mark)
The payment for the designer's services involves a corresponding production of equal value within the year.	(2 marks)
(b)	False.	(1 mark)
The expenditure on furnishings reflects the value of production of a resident producing unit in the last year. Thus, it should be counted in last year's GDP, regardless of when the payment was settled.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
At the beginning of this year, Mr Chan employed a local interior designer to design the interior of his new home. The designer finished the design work during the first half of this year. Then, Mr Chan employed a local home furnishing company to furnish his new home. The furnishings will be completed next year.
'The expenditure on the design work will be included in this year's GDP while the expenditure on furnishings will only be included in next year's GDP.' 
Explain whether this statement is correct.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
The first part of the statement is correct. 	(1 mark)
The designer is a resident producing unit and the value of its production this year should be included in this year's GDP.	(1 mark)
The second part of the statement is not correct.	(1 mark)
The wages for workers and other factor payments involved this year were counted in this year's GDP even though the furnishings had not yet been completed. / The value of production involved this year was counted in this year's GDP when the furnishing was carried out.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Publishing Company A employed an experienced editor to edit a new book in 2014. The editor finished the editorial work in two years. The book was then printed locally and published overseas in 2016. Explain whether the following statements are true or not:
(a)	No part of the payment for the editor's services was included in the 2014 GDP.		(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose the book is 100% locally produced and involves no imports. Both the printing cost and total sales revenue of the book would be counted in the 2016 GDP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	False.	(1 mark)
Although the editorial work had not yet been completed by the end of 2014, the value of the contribution made by the editor during the year was counted in that year.	(2 marks)
(b)	False.	(1 mark)
The printing service is an intermediate product and its value should not be counted to avoid the problem of double counting.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text: Recently, during the Bun Scrambling Competition (搶包山), many local people and foreign tourists travelled to Cheung Chau. The demand for Ping An Buns (平安包) was so great that sales reached $1,000,000. To make Ping An Buns, Cheung Chau bakers imported flour in bulk from the mainland which cost $100,000. Explain which expenditure component(s) of GDP is/are involved and how this event affected Hong Kong's current GDP.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The expenditures of domestic households on Ping An Buns are included in private consumption expenditures while the expenditures of foreign tourists on Ping An Buns are included in exports of services.	(2 marks)
•	The value of imported flour is included in imports of goods.	(1 mark)
•	Hong Kong's current GDP increased by $900,000 (= $1,000,000 - $100,000).
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Meya Company is a shop in Hong Kong selling Japanese cosmetics and local skincare products. Its revenue was $10 million last year.
(a)	Explain why Meya Company's contribution to Hong Kong's GDP was less than $10 million last year.	(4 marks)
(b)	Tammy is a Meya Company employee who needs to visit Japan frequently to search for new products. Explain if her income is included in Hong Kong's GDP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	To find Meya Company's contribution, the value of Japanese cosmetic products should be deducted from the sales revenue as it is not the value of production of Hong Kong's resident producing units.	(2 marks)
•	To find Meya Company's contribution, the value of skincare products purchased from other companies should be deducted from the sales revenue as it belongs to the value of intermediate consumption.	(2 marks)
(b)	•	Yes.	(1 mark)
•	This is because Tammy is employed by a resident producing unit (Meya Company) of Hong Kong.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Florence is a famous artist in Hong Kong. She sold her earlier paintings to her friend Freda for a low price five years ago when she was not famous. Recently, Freda sold her paintings and received $5,000,000.
Florence said, 'Why did you sell my paintings?'
Freda replied, 'You know, this can contribute to Hong Kong's economy! Due to this transaction, Hong Kong's current GDP increased by $5,000,000.'
Explain with THREE reasons why Freda is INCORRECT.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The value of the transaction should not be included in GDP as the value of the paintings was counted when they were sold for the first time.	(2 marks)
•	As the paintings were not produced in the current period, the value of the paintings should not be included in Hong Kong's current GDP. 	(2 marks)
•	Capital gains are not included in GDP as no current production is involved.		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Chia Yi is a Taiwanese who is the sole owner of a restaurant in Hong Kong. She normally stays in Taiwan. Ronald is also a Taiwanese. He has been the chef at the restaurant for more than 10 years. Explain whether each of the following statements is correct.
(a)	As Chia Yi is not a resident of Hong Kong, the output of her restaurant should not be counted in Hong Kong's GDP.	(3 marks)
(b)	Ronald's salary should be included in Hong Kong's GNP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Incorrect.	(1 mark)
	It is true that Chia Yi is not a resident of Hong Kong. However, Chia Yi's restaurant is a resident producing unit of Hong Kong (this does not depend on the residence status of the owner). Therefore, the output of her restaurant should be included in Hong Kong's GDP.	(2 marks)
(b)	Correct.	(1 mark)
	Ronald is a resident of Hong Kong as his major economic activities take place in Hong Kong. Therefore, his salary should be included in Hong Kong's GNP.
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Refer to the following gross domestic product information about Country K.

	$ billion	
Private consumption expenditure	80	
Gross domestic fixed capital formation	70	
Increase in inventories	10	
Depreciation	6	
Government consumption expenditure	14	
Domestic exports of goods	26	
Re-exports of goods	30	
Imports of goods	40	
Net exports of services	20	
Indirect taxes	5	
Subsidies	3	

(a)	Calculate Country K's GDP at market prices and GDP at factor cost.	(4 marks)
(b)	Recently, Ka Ming bought a second-hand textbook from a bookstore in Mong Kok. Explain how this would affect Hong Kong's GDP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP at market prices = $(80 + 70 + 10 + 14 + 26 + 30 - 40 + 20) billion	(1 mark)
             = $210 billion	(1 mark)
GDP at factor cost = $(210 - 5 + 3) billion 	(1 mark)
               = $208 billion	(1 mark)
(b)	Hong Kong's GDP would increase as the value of retailing services provided by the bookstore is included in Hong Kong's GDP.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
In 2014, the government of Country Q gave $9,000 to every household.
(a)	Explain the effect on Country Q's GDP.	(2 marks)
(b)	Keung remitted the $9,000 to his mother in Canada. Explain whether this would cause a difference between Hong Kong's GDP and GNP.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Every household has more money to spend and so private consumption expenditure would increase.	(1 mark)
	Therefore, Country Q's GDP would increase.	(1 mark)

(b)	No.	(1 mark)
	The remittance was a transfer payment instead of income distributed to a factor of production. Hence, it was not factor income paid abroad.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Dr Banner is a famous medical expert in America. He was invited to be the guest lecturer at a medical conference at the University of Hong Kong. The conference lasted for a week. Explain whether Dr Banner's remuneration from the conference should be counted in Hong Kong's
(a)	GDP, and	(3 marks)
(b)	GNP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Counted in Hong Kong's GDP.	(1 mark)
The remuneration was derived from the production of a resident producing unit in Hong Kong (the University of Hong Kong).	(2 marks)
(b)	Not counted in Hong Kong's GNP.	(1 mark)
Dr Banner is not a resident of Hong Kong. His remuneration should be counted as Hong Kong's factor income paid abroad.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Explain in what situation the GDP of a country would be greater than its GNP.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText: When the 'net factor income from abroad' of the country is negative (i.e. factor income paid abroad is larger than the factor income from abroad), its GDP will be greater than its GNP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text: * 'Since GNP is the sum of GDP and net factor income from abroad, the GNP and GDP of an economic territory will be the same if all the resident producing units only employ residents of the territory.' Do you agree? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	When resident producing units of an economic territory only employ residents of the territory, factor income paid abroad will be equal to zero (i.e., non-residents earn no factor income within the economic territory.)	(2 marks)
•	However, residents may still provide factor services outside the economic territory so that factor income from abroad will be positive. As a result, GDP is not the same as GNP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Refer to the following gross domestic product information about Country A.

	$ billion	
Private consumption expenditure	100	
Gross domestic fixed capital formation	90	
Decrease in inventories	10	
Government consumption expenditure	20	
Domestic exports of goods	30	
Re-exports of goods	80	
Imports of goods	40	
Exports of services	70	
Imports of services	110	
Indirect taxes	5	
Subsidies	3	
Net factor income from abroad	-1	

(a)	Calculate the GDP and GNP of Country A.	(3 marks)
(b)	Which approach have you used in (a) to measure GDP?	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP = $(100 + 90 - 10 + 20 + 30 + 80 - 40 + 70 - 110) billion	(1 mark)
= $230 billion	(1 mark)
GNP = $(230 - 1) billion = $229 billion	(1 mark)
(b)	Expenditure approach	(1 mark)



Structured Questions

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Duland is a country with well-developed heavy industries. The following shows a production chain of vehicles in Duland.

*(a)	Calculate the contribution of the above production chain to Duland's GDP at factor cost by the production approach.	(3 marks)
*(b)	Calculate the contribution of the above production chain to Duland's GDP at market prices by the expenditure approach.	(3 marks)
(c)	To which of the components in the expenditure approach do the following items in the above production chain belong?
	(i)	The value of the vehicles for the disabled	(1 mark)
	(ii)	The value of the buses	(1 mark)
	(iii)	The value of the private cars bought by Duland consumers	(1 mark)
	(iv)	The value of the private cars sold to foreign car wholesalers	(1 mark)
	(v)	The value of raw materials	(1 mark)
(d)	Explain whether the following items are included in Duland's gross national product (GNP).
	(i)	The dividend distributed by the local car manufacturer to a foreign investor
	(2 marks)
	(ii)	The salary of Mr Simpson, a foreign engineer working for the local car manufacturer under a three-year contract	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Duland's GDP at factor cost (by the production approach)
= $[(3,000 + 2,500 + 4,500 + 5,500 - 500) - 1,900] + $(6,500 - 4,500)	(1 mark)
= $15,100	(2 marks)

(b)	Duland's GDP at market prices (by the expenditure approach)
= $(3,000 + 2,500 + 6,500 + $5,500 - 1,900)	(1 mark)
= $15,600	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	Private consumption expenditure	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Gross investment expenditure	(1 mark)
	(iii)	Private consumption expenditure	(1 mark)
	(iv)	Exports (of goods)	(1 mark)
	(v)	Imports (of goods)	(1 mark)

(d)	(i)	No.	(1 mark)
		It is factor income paid to a non-resident.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Yes.	(1 mark)
		Mr Simpson is a resident of Duland as he intends to stay in Duland for more than a year. Thus, his income should be included in Duland's GNP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
City M's economy relies heavily on the gambling industry.
(a)	Explain whether the following items will contribute to City M's GDP. 
	(i)	The money won by a gambler in a casino 	(2 marks)
	(ii)	The BBQ pork rice (叉燒飯) lunch boxes made by a casino and distributed to the public free of charge	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether each of the following items is included in City M's GNP.
	(i)	The expenditure on dinner spent by a tourist	(2 marks)
	(ii)	The remuneration paid to a foreign consulting company	(2 marks)
	(iii)	The wages paid to a foreign violist (中提琴手) who performs at a hotel in City M for three weeks	(2 marks)
(c)	A boutique in City M has bought clothes from a wholesaler in City H. Some of the clothes are sold to domestic consumers. The boutique stores the remaining clothing. Under the expenditure approach, how are these items recorded in City M's GDP?	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	No.	(1 mark)
		The money is not paid for production.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Yes.	(1 mark)
		The lunch boxes are produced by the casino, which is a resident producing unit of City M.	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	Tourists' consumption should be included in the GNP because it belongs to exports of services.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	The value of the consulting service belongs to imports of services and should not be included in the GNP.	(2 marks)
	(iii)	As the violist is not a resident of City M, his/her wage income should not be included in the GNP.	(2 marks)

(c)	The total value of clothes bought from City H is recorded as imports.	(1 mark)
	The total market value of the clothes sold to consumers is recorded as private consumption expenditure.	(1 mark)
	The total market value of unsold clothes is recorded as gross investment expenditure (an increase in inventories).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Because of political instability in Country H, some foreign investors have withdrawn their funds from Country H's stock market.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain how the above event affects stock prices and the stock trading volume (成交量) in Country H.	(6 marks)
*(b)	Explain how the above change in the stock market will affect Country H's GDP.
		(3 marks)
(c)	To stabilise the political environment, Country H's government introduces the following policies. Explain how each of the following policies may affect Country H's GDP.
	(i)	The government gives $10,000 to each resident.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	The education department increases its expenditure on civil education.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When foreign investors withdraw their funds, demand for stocks decreases.
	(1 mark)
Both stock prices and the stock trading volume decrease.	(2 marks)
	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Decrease in demand	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in stock prices	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in the stock trading volume	(1 mark)


(b)	When the trading volume decreases, the demand for financial services derived from stock transactions will decrease. Thus, Country H's GDP will decrease.
	(3 marks)

(c)	(i)	This will increase people's disposable income. As people have more money to spend, they will consume more. Thus, private consumption expenditure will increase and so will Country H's GDP.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	This will increase government consumption expenditure and Country H's GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
In Country A, many people can download MP3 songs from the internet through peer-to-peer sharing (點對點分享). Most do not pay for the copyrights and no related laws protect the copyrights.
(a)	(i)	Explain with TWO reasons whether the 'free' songs downloaded through peer-to-peer sharing are free goods.	(3 marks)
(ii)	Because the songs are free, the sales revenue of the original CDs producers decreases greatly. To compensate for the decreased sales revenue, some of the producers plan to lower the prices of their CDs. With the aid of a diagram, explain whether their attempt to increase their total revenue will be successful if demand for the original CDs is inelastic.	(4 marks)
(b)	Suppose the government implements a new measure to punish people who download songs from the internet without paying for the copyrights.
	Without the aid of a diagram, explain the effects of this new measure on the equilibrium price, the quantity transacted and the total revenue of the original CDs.	(6 marks)
(c)	Suppose some online Hong Kong businesses sell original CDs which are produced in the mainland. Explain whether the above activity would increase Hong Kong's GDP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	No.	(1 mark)
Reasons:
•	People want more free songs.	(1 mark)
•	The resources involved in the production of free songs have alternative uses.	(1 mark)
(ii)	•	As the demand is inelastic, the total revenue decreases as the gain in revenue (due to an increase in quantity demanded) is smaller than the loss in revenue (due to a decrease in price).	(1 mark)
•	Thus, their attempt to increase their total revenue will not be successful.
	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

(b)	•	If the users of the free songs are punished, the demand for the free songs will decrease.	(1 mark)
•	Since the free songs from the websites and the songs from the original CDs are substitutes for each other, the demand for the original CDs will increase.
	(2 marks)
•	Both the equilibrium price and quantity transacted will increase.	(2 marks)
•	Since both the equilibrium price and the quantity transacted increase, the total revenue will increase.	(1 mark)

(c)	•	Yes.	(1 mark)
•	Although the CDs are not produced in Hong Kong, the related retailing services are currently provided by online Hong Kong businesses. The value of the retailing services should be included in Hong Kong's GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Suppose Country A's government constructed a new highway connecting Area F and an urban area so as to develop Area F. The construction started in Year 2. It was estimated that the construction would cost $5 billion and the work would be completed in Year 4.
(a)	(i)	Explain the effects of the construction of the highway on Country A's GDP for Year 2.	(2 marks)
(ii)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the effect of this construction on the price of flats in Area F.	(4 marks)
*(iii)	Explain whether the change in the price of the flats in Area F is reflected in the GDP of Year 2.	(4 marks)
(b)	Suppose Country A's government imported construction workers from Country H on a two-year contract basis in Year 2. Explain whether the wage payment of the imported construction workers should be included in the GDP and GNP between Year 2 and Year 4.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Although the construction of the highway will not be completed in Year 2, the wages of the workers and other factor payments involved in Year 2 will be counted in the GDP for that year.	(2 marks)
(ii)	•	Since travelling to and from Area F will be more convenient in the near future, the demand for flats in the area will increase.	(1 mark)
•	Therefore, the equilibrium price of flats in Area F will increase.	(1 mark)

Indicate on the diagram:
•	Increase in demand	(1 mark)
•	Increase in price	(1 mark)

(iii)	•	For flats built before Year 2, the increase in market prices when they are sold in that year is classified as a capital gain and will not be counted in the GDP for Year 2.	(2 marks)
•	For flats built in Year 2, the increase in price will increase the profit margin of real estate developers, which is counted as gross fixed investment.	(2 marks)

(b)	•	The workers work for resident producing units in Country A.	(1 mark)
•	Since GDP measures the value of output produced by all resident producing units, their wage payments are included in Country A's GDP.	(1 mark)
•	Since imported workers are employed on a two-year contract basis, they are treated as residents of Country A.	(1 mark)
•	Since GNP measures the total income of all residents, their wage payments are included in Country A's GNP.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch501 · What is economics?
questions.text:
Study the following cat food production chain.

(a)	What is a market?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether the following statement is correct.
'As online shops do not have physical locations, no market is involved in their transactions.'	(2 marks)
(c)	What is the contribution of the above production chain to Country B's GDP? Find your answer by the expenditure approach.	(2 marks)
(d)	A new movie about Garfield the Cat (加菲貓) has been shown in Country C and received an enthusiastic response from fans. The demand for cats has increased greatly in Country C. Suppose all of its cat food is imported from Country B.
(i)	With the aid of a diagram, explain how the above event affects the equilibrium price and quantity transacted of cat food in Country C.	(6 marks)
(ii)	Explain how the above event affects Country B's GDP and which expenditure components will be directly affected. 	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A market is any arrangement which enables transactions of a good or service to take place.	(2 marks)

(b)	Incorrect.	(1 mark)
A market may not involve a physical location.	(1 mark)

(c)	The contribution of the above production chain to Country B's GDP
	= $9,000 + $4,000- $3,000	(1 mark)
= $10,000	(1 mark)

(d)	(i)	The demand for cat food is in derived demand with cats.	(1 mark)
The increase in the demand for cats will lead to the increase in demand for cat food.	(1 mark)
Both the equilibrium price and quantity transacted of cat food will increase.
	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)
(ii)	As both the price and quantity transacted of cat food in Country C increase, the total revenue of cat food exporters (online shops) in Country B increases.
	(1 mark)
The exports of Country B increase.	(1 mark)
To sell more cat food, cat food wholesalers import more cat food from Country A.	(1 mark)
The imports of Country B increase.	(1 mark)
The increase in exports is greater than the increase in imports (Otherwise, wholesalers and online shops will not increase their output level).	(1 mark)
Country B's GDP increases as net exports increase.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following descriptions about real GDP is correct?
A.	Real GDP can reflect the average output enjoyed by every individual of an economy.
B.	A change in real GDP implies a change in the amount of total output.
C.	Real GDP is a better measure than nominal GDP in reflecting economic growth as the former includes the effects of changes in prices but the latter does not.
D.	Real GDP reflects the total cost of production in an economy.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about nominal GDP and real GDP is correct?
A.	Nominal GDP is also called GDP at current market prices while real GDP is also called GDP at factor costs.
B.	Nominal GDP covers more goods and services than real GDP.
C.	Nominal GDP and real GDP may change in different directions.
D.	A change in quantities of output causes changes in real GDP but not in nominal GDP.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following descriptions about nominal GDP is correct?
A.	It is also called GDP at current market prices.
B.	It can accurately reflect the living standard of a country.
C.	If there is an increase in nominal GDP, there must be an increase in the aggregate output.
D.	Its value is negatively related to the price level.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about real GDP is INCORRECT?
A.	It is also called GDP at constant market prices.
B.	It is the only indicator which can measure the standard of living accurately.
C.	It is measured at market prices in the base period.
D.	Its changes reflect the change in the aggregate output of an economy in a specified period.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about real GDP is correct?
A.	It measures the total income received by factors of production.
B.	It is always smaller than GDP at factor cost.
C.	It cannot be equal to nominal GDP.
D.	Its changes reflect the change in the volume of aggregate output of an economy in a specified period.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following descriptions about GDP is correct?
A.	Nominal GDP can measure the real output of a country.
B.	Measuring GDP at base-year prices can eliminate the effect of price changes on GDP.
C.	If nominal GDP decreases at a smaller rate than price level, real GDP will drop.
D.	Per capita nominal GDP must be higher than per capita real GDP.
questions.answerText: Option C is not correct. Percentage change in real GDP ~ Percentage change in nominal GDP - Percentage change in price level. If the percentage decrease in nominal GDP is smaller than the percentage decrease in the price level, the percentage change in real GDP will be positive, i.e., real GDP will rise.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following will decrease Hong Kong's nominal GDP?
A.	Fewer children who help their parents with household chores (家庭雜務)
B.	Fewer households which make their own meals
C.	Fewer people who participate in volunteer services
D.	Fewer farmers who produce agricultural products

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following will lead to an increase in Hong Kong's nominal GDP?
A.	More and more firms wind up
B.	More and more visitors come to Hong Kong.
C.	More and more leisure time is available to people
D.	More and more pollutants are emitted

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Which of the following can boost Hong Kong's real GDP?
A.	Ocean Park builds a new waterfront.
B.	Some primary schools cease operation due to insufficient student intake.
C.	More Hong Kong residents buy flats in Guangzhou.
D.	More Hong Kong residents change their travel destinations from Japan to Korea.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Country B is a closed economy which only produces fish and chips. The following table shows production information about Country B.

Year	Quantity of fish	Unit price of fish	Quantity of chips	Unit price of chips		1	50 units	$10	100 units	$25	
4	60 units	$5	200 units	$10	

Suppose Year 1 is the base year and the population of Country B has changed from 1,000 persons to 2,000 persons. Which of the following statements about Country B is INCORRECT?
A.	Its general price level has decreased from Year 1 to Year 4.
B.	Its nominal GDP has increased from Year 1 to Year 4.
C.	Its real GDP has increased from Year 1 to Year 4.
D.	Its per capita real GDP has decreased from Year 1 to Year 4.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
* If the GDP deflator has increased, which of the following statements is correct?
A.	The nominal GDP must be rising.
B.	The real GDP must be rising.
C.	Nominal GDP must not be equal to real GDP.
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText: Option C is incorrect. If the GDP deflator in the preceding period is lower than 100 and the GDP deflator in the current period increases to 100, nominal GDP will be equal to real GDP.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In Country A, the GDP deflator falls but CPI (A) merely increases. Which of the following can help explain this phenomenon?

C.	The economy is growing rapidly.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
* If Country A's implicit price deflator of GDP has decreased, which of the following is INCORRECT?
A.	Country A's nominal GDP may not fall. 
B.	Country A's consumer price indices may not fall.
C.	Country A's GDP deflator may not be less than 100. 
D.	The prices for all the goods and services included in Country A's GDP have decreased.
questions.answerText:
Option A is correct and so not the answer. If the percentage increase in the real GDP is greater than the percentage decrease in the implicit price deflator of GDP, the nominal GDP will increase.
Option B is correct and so not the answer. As the coverage of the implicit price deflator of GDP is different from the coverage of consumer price indices, it is possible that they have different directions of change.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
(a)	What is the difference between nominal GDP and real GDP?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain why real GDP is a better measure of aggregate output than nominal GDP.	(2 marks)
(c)	China's real GDP has surpassed Japan's real GDP. Does this imply that the general living standard of people in China is better than that in Japan? Explain your answer.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Nominal GDP is GDP measured at market prices in the current period while real GDP is measured at market prices in the base period.	(2 marks)
(b)	In the compilation of real GDP, the effect of price changes in different years is eliminated. A change in real GDP must imply a change in the volume of aggregate output.	(2 marks)
(c)	No.	(1 mark)
	As the population of China is larger than that of Japan, the average output shared by each citizen in China is less than that in Japan. (Accept other reasonable answers.)	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:

(b)	'Nominal GDP is always greater than real GDP.' Explain whether this statement is correct.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP is the total value of production of all resident producing units of an economy in a specified period.	(2 marks)
Nominal GDP is GDP measured at market prices in the current period.	(1 mark)
Real GDP is GDP measured at market prices in the base period.	(1 mark)
(b)	The statement is incorrect.	(1 mark)
When the price level (or GDP deflator) of the current period is smaller than or equal to 100, nominal GDP will be smaller than or equal to real GDP.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Study the following table about an economy:
Type of goods	Output in Year 2	Unit price in Year 2	Unit price in Year 1	
Good X	500 units	$20	$10	
Good Y	100 units	$100	$50	
Suppose the economy only produces Good X and Good Y.
(a)	Use Year 1 as the base year to calculate nominal GDP and real GDP in Year 2.
	(2 marks)
(b)	Use Year 2 as the base year to calculate nominal GDP and real GDP in Year 2.
	(2 marks)
(c)	Are the results in (a) and (b) the same? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Nominal GDP in Year 2 = (500 × $20) + (100 × $100) = $20,000	(1 mark)
Real GDP (at market prices in Year 1) in Year 2 = (500 × $10) + (100 × $50)
= $10,000	(1 mark)
(b)	Nominal GDP in Year 2 = $20,000	(1 mark)
Real GDP (at market prices in Year 2) in Year 2 = Nominal GDP in Year 2
= $20,000	(1 mark)
(c)	The results of nominal GDPs in (a) and (b) are the same as the same prices are used to value the same quantities.	(2 marks)
The results of real GDPs in (a) and (b) are different as different prices are used to value the same quantities.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Explain why real GDP is a better measure of aggregate output than nominal GDP.
	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
A change in nominal GDP in different periods can be caused by a change in quantities and/or a change in prices.	(1 mark)
Therefore, we do not know whether an increase in nominal GDP implies an increase in quantities, in prices or in both.	(1 mark)
However, in the measurement of real GDP, quantities of outputs in different periods are all valued at the same base-period prices. The effect of price changes in different years is eliminated.	(1 mark)
A change in real GDP must imply a change in the volume of aggregate output.
	(1 mark)
Hence, real GDP is a better measure of aggregate output.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
(a)	Define GDP.	(2 marks)
(b)	Show the relationship between GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices.
		(2 marks)
(c)	Explain under what situation GDP at market prices and GDP at factor cost are the same.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP is the total value of production of all resident producing units of an economy in a specified period.	(2 marks)
(b)	GDP at factor cost = GDP at market prices - Indirect taxes + Subsidies	(2 marks)
(c)	If indirect taxes are equal to subsidies (or both indirect taxes and subsidies are equal to zero), GDP at factor cost will be equal to GDP at market prices.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
(a)	Define GDP.	(2 marks)
(b)	Show the relationship between per capita GDP and GDP.	(1 mark)
(c)	Explain why per capita GDP is a better measure of economic welfare than GDP.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP is the total value of production of all resident producing units of an economy in a specified period.	(2 marks)
(b)	Per capita GDP = GDP ÷ Population	(1 mark)
(c)	When there is an increase in population, the average output enjoyed by each person will be lower. Per capita GDP eliminates the effect of population size. Thus, per capita GDP is a better measure of economic welfare than GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
(a)	Define GDP.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain under what situation GDP will be equal to full employment GDP.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP is the total value of production of all resident producing units of an economy in a specified period.	(2 marks)
(b)	When all resources of an economy are used efficiently, its GDP will be equal to its full employment GDP.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Identify THREE major uses of national income statistics.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	To assess the economic performance of an economy
•	To reflect the economic welfare of an economy
•	To facilitate international comparison
•	To provide information to the government in formulating economic policies
•	To help firms make production and investment plans
(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable answers. 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
State THREE limitations of per capita real GDP as an indicator of economic welfare.
	(6 marks)

questions.text: Suggest THREE situations when national income statistics may underestimate the economic welfare of a country.	(6 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: State THREE situations when real GDP may overestimate the economic welfare of a country.	(6 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Does per capita real GDP underestimate or overestimate the economic welfare of a country under the following cases? Explain your answers.
(a)	Many retired people work for charitable organisations as volunteers.	(3 marks)
(b)	The country's GDP is higher than the global average level due to the country's industrious workers whose working hours are much longer than the global average.	(3 marks)
(c)	Hundreds of thousands of new immigrants have recently flooded into the country.
	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Underestimate	(1 mark)
	Volunteer services are unpaid so they are not included in GDP. However, these kinds of unpaid services actually increase a country's economic welfare.	(2 marks)
(b)	Overestimate	(1 mark)
	Longer working hours reduce workers' leisure time and hence affect their living standards. This is not reflected by the GDP.	(2 marks)
(c)	Neither underestimate nor overestimate	(1 mark)
	The inflow of new immigrants increases the population of the country. However, the effect of changes in the population is eliminated in the calculation of per capita real GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: If the per capita real GDP of Country X increases, can we conclude that the general living standard of the country has improved during the period? Explain, giving TWO reasons.	(5 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: Explain why high per capita real GDP does not mean a high standard of living. Give THREE reasons.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
This is because per capita real GDP does not reflect the following:
•	The extent of income inequality
•	Uses of output
•	The value of unpaid services produced by households for self-consumption
•	Undesirable effects of production
•	The value of leisure
(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable explanations. 2 marks ( 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following table shows the GDP components of a country in Year 7 and Year 8.

	Year 7	Year 8	
Private consumption expenditure ($ billion)	50	8	
Gross domestic capital formation ($ billion)	15	52	
Government consumption expenditure ($ billion)	10	10	
Net exports ($ billion)	5	20	
Population (billion)	0.3	0.5	

(a)	Calculate the nominal GDP in Year 7 and Year 8.	(4 marks)
(b)	Based on your answers in (a), can you conclude that the general living standard has improved? Suggest TWO reasons to support your answer by using the information in the table.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Nominal GDP in Year 7 = $(50 + 15 + 10 + 5) billion	(1 mark)
= $80 billion	(1 mark)
Nominal GDP in Year 8 = $(8 + 52 + 10 + 20) billion	(1 mark)
= $90 billion	(1 mark)
(b)	No, we cannot.	(1 mark)
This is because:	
•	the population in Year 8 is higher and per capita GDP in Year 8 is lower:
	(1 mark)
Year 7 is $266.7; Year 8 is $180.	(1 mark)
•	the composition of GDP is different. Private consumption takes up a smaller proportion in Year 8:	(1 mark)
Year 7: 100% = 62.5%
Year 8: 100% = 8.9%	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following gives information about Country S in 2014.

GDP at factor cost	$3,975,000	
GDP deflator	125	
Population	8,400	

(a)	The amounts of indirect taxes and subsidies in 2014 are $150,000 and $70,000, respectively. Calculate Country S's GDP at market prices in 2014.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose the GDP deflator in 2010 was 105. Calculate Country S's real GDP in 2014, using 2010 as the base year.	(2 marks)
(c)	(i)	Calculate per capita real GDP in 2014. What does this figure reflect?	(3 marks)
	(ii)	Jacky said, 'Since the per capita real GDP in 2014 is higher than that in 2010, the economic welfare of everyone in Country S has improved.' Explain why he may NOT be correct.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP at market prices
	=	GDP at factor cost + Indirect taxes - Subsidies
	=	$3,975,000 + $150,000 - $70,000
	=	$4,055,000	(2 marks)
(b)	Real GDP in 2014
	=	GDP at market prices in 2014 ÷ GDP deflator in 2014 × GDP deflator in base year
	=	$4,055,000 ÷ 125 × 105
	=	$3,406,200	(2 marks)
(c)	(i)	Per capita real GDP in 2014
		= Real GDP in 2014 ÷ Population
		= $3,406,200 ÷ 8,400
		= $405.5	(2 marks)
		This figure reflects the average output enjoyed by each person in Country S.
	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Although the average output to each person has increased, the output may not be evenly distributed among the population.	(2 marks)
		(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
(a)	Define the general price level and price index.	(4 marks)
(b)	List TWO types of price indices which are most commonly used in Hong Kong.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The general price level is the weighted average of prices of all goods and services of a country or territory.	(2 marks)
A price index is a figure showing the price level of a basket of goods and services in a specified period relative to its price level in the base period.	(2 marks)
(b)	The consumer price index and	(1 mark)
the implicit price deflator of GDP (or GDP deflator)	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text: What are the consumer price index (CPI) and the GDP deflator? Give TWO differences between them.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
The consumer price index is a figure that shows the price level of consumer goods and services generally purchased by (domestic) households in a specified period relative to the price level in the base period.	(2 marks)
The GDP deflator is a figure that shows the price level of goods and services related to GDP in a specified period relative to the price level in the base period.	(2 marks)
Differences between them:
•	The CPI covers products generally purchased by domestic households but the GDP deflator covers products related to GDP. Thus, some goods not purchased by domestic households but that are related to GDP will be only covered by the GDP deflator.
•	Fixed weights are used in the CPI but variable weights are used in the GDP deflator.
(Accept any other reasonable answers. 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
Refer to the following information about Country A.

Year	Consumer price index	GDP deflator	
2013 (base year)	100	100	
2014	105	104	

(a)	Calculate the growth rates of the general price level by using the consumer price index and GDP deflator, respectively.	(2 marks)
(b)	Based on your answer in (a), what is the change in the cost of living in 2014?
	(1 mark)
(c)	Explain whether the consumer price index or the GDP deflator can better reflect the cost of living.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Growth rate of consumer price index
	= (105 - 100) ÷ 100 × 100%
	= 5%	(1 mark)
	Growth rate of GDP deflator
	= (104 - 100) ÷ 100 × 100%
	= 4%	(1 mark)
(b)	The cost of living increases by 5%.	(1 mark)
(c)	Consumer price index	(1 mark)
	The consumer price index shows the price level of products generally purchased by domestic households. Hence, it better reflects households' cost of living.
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following are data of Economy X for Year 4 and Year 5.

	Year 4	Year 5	
Nominal GDP ($ billion)	10	12	
Real GDP ($ billion)	11	13	

Find the price index for Year 4 and Year 5, respectively. Also find the growth rate of the price index between Year 4 and Year 5.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Price index for Year 4 = (10 ÷ 11) × 100	(1 mark)
= 90.9	(1 mark)
Price index for Year 5 = (12 ÷ 13) × 100	(1 mark)
= 92.3	(1 mark)
The growth rate of the price index between Year 4 and Year 5
= [(92.3 - 90.9) ÷ 90.9] × 100%	(1 mark)
= 1.5%	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following data refer to Economy A.

	Base Year	Year 5	
Nominal GDP	$1,000,000,000	$1,500,000,000	
Per capita real GDP	$10,000	$12,000	

Suppose the growth rate of the population is 10%. Find
(a)	the population in the base year.	(1 mark)
(b)	the per capita nominal GDP in the base year and Year 5.	(3 marks)
(c)	the growth rate of per capita nominal GDP between the base year and Year 5.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	In the base year, nominal GDP and real GDP are the same; dividing nominal GDP by per capita real GDP gives the population in the base year, which is 100,000.		(1 mark)
(b)	•	Per capita nominal GDP in Year 5
	= Nominal GDP ( Population
	= $[1,500,000,000 ( (100,000 ( 110%)]	(1 mark)
	= $13,636.4	(1 mark)
•	The per capita nominal GDP is equal to the per capita real GDP in the base year, that is, $10,000.	(1 mark)
(c)	The growth rate of per capita nominal GDP between the base year and Year 5
	= [(13,636.4 - 10,000) ( 10,000] ( 100%	(1 mark)
	= 36.4%	(1 mark)

The following table shows the GDP data (in $ billion) of a country in Year 7 and 
Year 8.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following table shows GDPs and the populations of a country in Year 7 and 
Year 8.

	Year 7	Year 8	
GDP	$100	$200	
Population	8	10	

(a)	Find the exact value of the growth rate of per capita GDP in Year 8.	(3 marks)
(b)	Find the approximate value of the growth rate of per capita GDP in Year 8.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:

Growth rate of per capita GDP in Year 8 = (20 - 12.5) ÷ 12.5 × 100%
= 60%	(1 mark)

	(1 mark)

Structured Questions

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
In a certain year, Silla's nominal GDP, price level and population decreased by 2%, 3% and 5%, respectively. Many people migrated to a neighbouring country. Kwangsu migrated to Baekje, while Jihyo stayed in Silla.
(a)	Kwangsu said, 'It is a difficult year for Silla. Silla produced less output than last year.' Do you agree with him? Explain your answer with calculations.	(4 marks)
(b)	Jihyo said, 'Thanks to those who left, the remaining compatriot (同胞) can enjoy more output on average than they did before.' Explain her statement with calculations.	(3 marks)
(c)	Suppose both the real GDP and the population of Silla and Baekje are the same. Explain which country's living standard is higher in each case.
	(i)	The average working hours in Silla are fewer than those in Baekje.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	The contribution of Silla's investment to GDP is much higher than that of Baekje.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.	(1 mark)
	Changes in real GDP reflect changes in output.	(1 mark)
	Percentage change in real GDP
	= Percentage change in nominal GDP - Percentage change in price level
	= -2% - (-3%) = 1%	
	Silla produced 1% more output than the year before.	(2 marks)

(b)	Per capita real GDP reflects the amount of output shared by each person.	(1 mark)
	Percentage change in per capita real GDP
	= Percentage change in real GDP - Percentage change in population
	= 1% - (-5%) = 6%	
	The average amount of output shared by each person in Silla increased by 6%.
	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	Longer working hours imply less leisure time and a lower living standard. The value of leisure is not counted in GDP.	(2 marks)
		Therefore, Silla's living standard is higher than that of Baekje.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	More investment means less retained for consumption. People in Silla enjoy fewer goods and services than those in Baekje in the current period.	(2 marks)
		Therefore, Baekje's living standard is higher than that of Silla.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following table gives information about Amestris.

Year	Nominal GDP
($ million)	Price index	
1550	340,000	110	
1551	346,800	121	

(a)	Edward said, 'The output of Amestris increased in 1551 because its nominal GDP increased.' Alphonse said, 'changes in nominal GDP cannot accurately reflect changes in aggregate output. We should look at real GDP instead.'
	(i)	Explain why nominal GDP CANNOT accurately reflect changes in aggregate output.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Calculate the real GDP of Amestris in 1550 and 1551 (assume the price index in the base year is 100). What do the results imply?	(4 marks)
(b)	Winry is a merchant who sells mechanical equipment. Recently, she decided to expand her business. Her grandmother has retired and takes care of their home.
	(i)	Suggest TWO indices measuring the general price level.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Explain which index is more important to Winry and her grandmother while considering their expenditure.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	A change in nominal GDP in different periods can be caused by a change in quantities of output and/or a change in prices. Thus, we do not know whether an increase in nominal GDP implies an increase in quantities.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Real GDP of Amestris in 1550
		= $340,000 million × 100 ÷ 110
		= $309,091 million	(1 mark)
		Real GDP of Amestris in 1551
		= $346,800 million × 100 ÷ 121
		= $286,612 million	(1 mark)
		The real GDP of Amestris in 1551 is smaller than that in 1550. This implies a decrease in the aggregate output.	(2 marks)

(b)	(i)	Consumer price index (CPI)	(1 mark)
		GDP deflator	(1 mark)
	(ii)	The GDP deflator is more important to Winry.	(1 mark)
		The GDP deflator covers the price level of capital goods, which is related to Winry's investment expenditure.	(2 marks)
		CPI is more important to Winry's grandmother.	(1 mark)
		CPI shows the price level of products generally purchased by (domestic) households. It better reflects households' basic living expenses.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following table gives information about Country A in Year 4 and Year 5.
	Year 4	Year 5	
Real GDP ($ billion)	100	200	
Population (billion)	0.1	0.1	
Price index	100	105	
(a)	Calculate nominal GDPs in Year 4 and Year 5.	(2 marks)
(b)	Based on the above data, explain the most probable change in the general standard of living between Year 4 and Year 5.	(2 marks)
(c)	Suggest THREE possible situations to explain why the change in the general standard of living is NOT necessarily the same as what is stated in (b).	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Nominal GDP in Year 4 = $100 billion	(1 mark)
Nominal GDP in Year 5 = $(200 × 105 ÷ 100) billion = $210 billion	(1 mark)

(b)	Since Country A's real GDP has increased by 100% between Year 4 and Year 5 and there is no change in its population, Country A's per capita real GDP must increase. All other things being equal, Country A's general standard of living will most likely improve.	(2 marks)

(c)	•	Income distribution becomes much more uneven.
•	There are many more unpaid services produced by households for self-consumption.
•	There is a large reduction in the proportion of private consumption expenditure in GDP.
•	There are more undesirable effects of production.
(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable explanations. 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch502 · The three basic economic problems
questions.text:
The following table gives information about Monkey Island in Year 1 and Year 2.
(in $ million)	Year 1	Year 2	
Private consumption expenditure	100	10	
Government consumption expenditure	50	120	
Gross domestic fixed capital formation	30	30	
Changes in inventories	20	20	
Depreciation	1	1	
Net exports	10	100	
Imports	2	2	
Indirect taxes	3	3	
Subsidies	4	4	
(a)	Define gross domestic product (GDP).	(2 marks)
(b)	Calculate the GDPs at market prices in Year 1 and Year 2.	(4 marks)
(c)	Suppose the total populations on Monkey Island in Year 1 and Year 2 are 1 million and 1.4 million, respectively.
(i)	Show the relationship between per capita nominal GDP and nominal GDP by an equation.	(1 mark)
(ii)	Calculate the per capita GDP at market prices for each year.	(2 marks)
(iii)	Explain why per capita nominal GDP is a better indicator of economic welfare, compared with nominal GDP.	(1 mark)
(d)	Suppose there are no changes in the general price level and populations on Monkey Island in Year 2.
(i)	What would be the most probable change in the economic welfare of Monkey Island in Year 2?	(3 marks)
(ii) Use the data in the above table to explain why the interpretation of national income statistics in (d)(i) may NOT be correct.	(2 marks)
(e)	Explain how the following events affect Monkey Island's GDP and economic welfare in Year 2, respectively.
*(i)	Some bananas produced in Year 1 are sold to domestic households in Year 2.
		(4 marks)
(ii)	More people participate in volunteer work in Year 2.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	GDP is the total value of production of all resident producing units of an economy in a specified period.	(2 marks)

(b)	GDP at market prices in Year 1 
	= $[100 + (30 + 20) + 50 + 10] million	(1 mark)
= $210 million	(1 mark)
GDP at market prices in Year 2 
= $[10 + (30 + 20) + 120 + 100] million	(1 mark)
= $280 million	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	Per capita nominal GDP = Nominal GDP ÷ Population	(1 mark)
(ii)	Per capita GDP at market prices in Year 1 = $(210 ÷ 1) = $210	(1 mark)
Per capita GDP at market prices in Year 2 = $(280 ÷ 1.4) = $200	(1 mark)
(iii)	Per capita nominal GDP eliminates the effect of population size while nominal GDP does not.	(1 mark)

(d)	(i)	As there is no change in the general price level, the increase in nominal GDP implies that there is an increase in real GDP in Year 2.	(1 mark)
As there is no change in population, the increase in real GDP implies that there is an increase in per capita real GDP in Year 2.	(1 mark)
Thus, economic welfare in Year 2 will probably increase.	(1 mark)
(ii)	An increase in private consumption expenditure can improve current economic welfare. Economic welfare in Year 2 may be lower as there is a decrease in private consumption expenditure.	(1 mark)
The increase in nominal GDP is due to the increase in net exports. The exported goods are consumed by non-local households. Thus, economic welfare in Year 2 may be overestimated.	(1 mark)

(e)	(i)	GDP is unaffected as the bananas are not produced in Year 2.	(2 marks)
As there is an increase in private consumption expenditure, economic welfare in Year 2 will improve.	(2 marks)
(ii)	GDP is unaffected as the value of volunteer services is not counted in the GDP.	(2 marks)
There is an improvement in economic welfare as volunteer work improves economic welfare.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The following graph shows the percentage changes in price levels in Mactata City.

Which of the following statements is correct?

B.	In Year 1, there was no inflationary effect.
C.	In Year 2, there was disinflation.
D.	From Year 4 to Year 5, recipients of fixed future payments lose.
questions.answerText:
To answer this question, students should first find the differences between the actual inflation rate and the expected inflation rate.

Then, students can use the concepts of unanticipated inflation and deflation in the textbook to tackle this question. If the difference is negative, the redistributive effect will be similar to the situation of unanticipated deflation. If the difference is positive, the redistributive effect will be similar to the situation of unanticipated inflation. If the difference is equal to zero, there is anticipated inflation / deflation and so no party gains or loses.

Short Questions

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is inflation?	(2 marks)
(b)	What is the difference between deflation and disinflation?	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
(b)	During deflation, the general price level decreases persistently (i.e., negative inflation rate).	(2 marks)
	During disinflation, the general price level still increases persistently but at a declining rate (i.e., positive but decreasing inflation rate).	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define inflation.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether the introduction of a general sales tax will cause inflation.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
(b)	•	No.	(1 mark)
•	Although the prices of all goods increase after the introduction of the tax, the increase in the prices is once-and-for-all, not a persistent increase.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define inflation.	(2 marks)
(b)	'After the government increases textbook assistance for students, the prices of textbooks increase persistently.' Explain whether this case is an example of inflation.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
(b)	•	No.	(1 mark)
•	The persistent increase in the price of textbooks cannot bring about a persistent increase in general prices. Thus, this case is not an example of inflation.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define disinflation and deflation.	(4 marks)

(b)	Study the following diagram about the change in the Composite Consumer Price Index (CCPI). Determine whether the economy experienced disinflation or deflation during the following period.
(i)	From Year 1 to Year 2	(1 mark)
(ii)	From Year 3 to Year 5	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Disinflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level but at a declining rate.	(2 marks)
Deflation is the phenomenon of a persistent decrease in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	Deflation	(1 mark)
(ii)	Disinflation	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define inflation and disinflation.	(4 marks)
(b)	Study the following diagram about the change in the GDP deflator.

Explain whether the economy experienced inflation during the following period.
(i)	From Year 1 to Year 2	(1 mark)
(ii)	From Year 3 to Year 5	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
Disinflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level but at a declining rate.	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	No. As the percentage changes in the GDP deflator are negative, the economy experienced deflation during the period.	(1 mark)
(ii)	Yes. As the percentage changes in the GDP deflator are positive, the economy experienced inflation during the period.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the following data about the Composite Consumer Price Index (CCPI) of Country H. The government increased the sales tax in April.

	March	April	May	June		CCPI	100	111	111	111	

(a)	Define inflation and inflation rate.	(4 marks)
(b)	Calculate the inflation rate in April.	(1 mark)
(c)	Explain whether the country experienced inflation during the period from March to June.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
Inflation rate is the (positive) percentage change in the general price level in a specified period.	(2 marks)
(b)	(111 - 100) ÷ 100 × 100% = 11%	(1 mark)
(c)	No. The increase in the sales tax only resulted in a once-and-for-all increase in the general price level. Since the general price level did not rise persistently, there was no inflation.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the following data about the GDP deflator of Country G. Oil prices in the country have increased persistently.

	Year 1	Year 2	Year 3	Year 4		GDP deflator	100	120	180	360	

(a)	Define inflation and inflation rate.	(4 marks)
(b)	Calculate the inflation rates in Year 2, Year 3 and Year 4.	(3 marks)
(c)	Explain whether the country experienced inflation during the period.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
The inflation rate is the (positive) percentage change in the general price level in a specified period.	(2 marks)
(b)	Year 2's inflation rate = (120 - 100) ÷ 100 × 100% = 20%	(1 mark)
Year 3's inflation rate = (180 - 120) ÷ 120 × 100% = 50%	(1 mark)
Year 4's inflation rate = (360 - 180) ÷ 180 × 100% = 100%	(1 mark)
(c)	Yes. As the general price level increased persistently, there was inflation.	(1 mark)

questions.text:
Study the following information about Hong Kong's economy.

Year	Composite consumer price index (CCPI)	
2011	106.0

(a)	Calculate the percentage changes in CCPI in 2012 and 2013 (correct to 1 decimal place). Determine whether Hong Kong experienced inflation or deflation in 2012 and 2013.	(4 marks)

	(2 marks)
(ii)	In 2011, John borrowed money from a bank to buy a luxury car as a gift to her girlfriend and agreed to repay a fixed monthly installment loan over ten years.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The percentage change in CCPI in 2012 = (110.3 - 106.0)/106.0 = 4.1%	(1 mark)
	Hong Kong experienced inflation in 2012.	(1 mark)
	The percentage change in CCPI in 2013 = (115.1 - 110.3)/110.3 = 4.4%	(1 mark)
	Hong Kong experienced inflation in 2013.	(1 mark)
(b)	CPI can better reflect households' cost of living as it only measures the prices of products generally purchased by domestic households.	(2 marks)
(c)	(i)	He will lose.	(1 mark)
		The real interest rate he receives is lower than he expected.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	He will gain.	(1 mark)
		The real value of the installments he pays is less than he expected.	(1 mark)

questions.text:
