	21st Oct, 2014

(a)	What is inflation? Based on the news extract, explain whether Hong Kong experienced inflation at that time.	(4 marks)
(b)	The government issued new inflation-linked bonds (iBonds) totalling $10 billion in July 2014. Explain whether the government or holders of iBonds will suffer from the change in the consumer price index mentioned in the news extract.
	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
	Hong Kong experienced inflation because there was an increase in the general price level over a year.	(2 marks)
(b)	Neither party will gain or lose.	(1 mark)
	The interest on iBonds will be adjusted based on actual inflation. As a result, the real value of interest income/payment remains unchanged under unanticipated inflation.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Express the real interest rate in terms of the nominal interest rate and the inflation rate.	(2 marks)
(b)	It was expected that there would be no inflation this year. However, the inflation rate has turned out to be 1%. Explain whether the following people will gain or lose.
	(i)	A lender who receives repayments at a fixed interest rate	(2 marks)
	(ii)	An employer who adjusts wages according to the expected inflation rate
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Inflation rate	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	He will lose.	(1 mark)
		The real interest rate he receives is lower than he expected.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	He will gain.	(1 mark)
		The real value of wages he pays is less than he expected.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Use ONE formula to show the relationship between the expected real interest rate and the expected inflation rate.	(2 marks)
(b)	In Year 1, Samuel deposited money into a bank and the bank agreed to pay him a nominal interest rate of 2%. He expected that there would be inflation in Year 2. Instead, there was deflation in Year 2. Explain whether the nominal interest rate will be higher than the actual real interest rate.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Expected real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Expected inflation rate
	(2 marks)
(b)	Actual real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Actual inflation rate	(1 mark)
As the actual inflation rate in Year 2 was negative, the nominal interest rate must be smaller than the actual real interest rate.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is deflation? What is indexation?	(4 marks)
(b)	How does deflation affect the economic welfare of the following parties?
(i)	Recipients of indexed future payments	(2 marks)
(ii)	Recipients of fixed future payments	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Deflation refers to a persistent decrease in the general price level.	(2 marks)
Indexation refers to the automatic adjustment of future payments according to a price index that reflects the cost of living.	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	As the future payments are indexed, they will be adjusted automatically according to the price index. Thus, deflation will not affect the purchasing power (or real value) of the future payments or the economic welfare of the recipients.	(2 marks)
(ii)	Deflation will increase the purchasing power of money and the purchasing power (or real value) of fixed future payments. As a result, the economic welfare of recipients of fixed future payments will increase during deflation.	
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define deflation.	(2 marks)
(b)	After the exemption of duties on wine, the price of wine decreases. Explain whether this is an example of deflation.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Deflation is the phenomenon of a persistent decrease in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
(b)	•	No.	(1 mark)
•	A fall in the price of a single good (wine) is not deflation.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What are nominal value and real value in a specified period?	(4 marks)
(b)	How can real value be determined from nominal value? Show this in an equation.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Nominal value in a specified period is value expressed in units of money in that period.	(2 marks)
Real value in a specified period is value expressed in units of money in the base period.	(2 marks)
(b)	Real value = Nominal value in a specified period ÷ Price index in the period × 100
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the following data.

Year	Price index	Mr Chan's nominal income ($ million)	
4	100	1	
5	120	1.3	

(a)	Find Mr Chan's real income in Year 4 and Year 5.	(2 marks)
(b)	Must Mr Chan's standard of living improve? Explain with ONE reason.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Mr Chan's real income in Year 4 = $1 million (as the price index = 100)	(1 mark)
Mr Chan's real income in Year 5 = $1.3 million ÷ 120 × 100 = $1.08 million
	(1 mark)
(b)	Not necessarily.	(1 mark)
The value of leisure is not counted. Mr Chan may give up more leisure in exchange for higher real income.	(2 marks)
(Any other reasonable answer.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the following data.

Year	Price index	Real GDP ($ million)	
4	110	100	
5	130	90	

(a)	Find nominal GDPs in Year 4 and Year 5.	(2 marks)
(b)	In which year is the purchasing power of nominal GDP greater? Explain.	(2 marks)
(c)	In light of the results in (a) and (b), explain why an increase in nominal GDP may NOT imply an improvement in economic welfare.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Nominal GDP in Year 4 = $100 million × 110 ÷ 100 = $110 million	(1 mark)
Nominal GDP in Year 5 = $90 million × 130 ÷ 100 = $117 million	(1 mark)
(b)	Year 4	(1 mark)
as the price level in Year 4 is smaller.	(1 mark)
(c)	An increase in nominal GDP may be caused by an increase in the general price level rather than an increase in the volume of production. Thus, even though there is an increase in nominal GDP, real GDP may still decrease. For example, in this case, nominal GDP increased from Year 4 to Year 5, but real GDP decreased in this period.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What are nominal and real interest rates?	(4 marks)
(b)	How can the real interest rate be found from the nominal interest rate? Show this in an equation.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Nominal interest rate is the rate of change in the nominal value (or money value) of an asset over a specified period.	(2 marks)
Real interest rate is the rate of change in the real value (or purchasing power) of an asset over a specified period.	(2 marks)
(b)	Real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Inflation rate	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose the expected deflation rate and the nominal interest rate are 1% and 2%, respectively.
(a)	Find the expected real interest rate.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose the actual inflation rate turns out to be 1%.
(i)	What would the actual real interest rate be?	(2 marks)
(ii)	Would debtors or creditors gain or lose in this case?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Expected real interest rate
= Nominal interest rate + Expected deflation rate	(1 mark)
= 2% + 1% = 3%	(1 mark)
(b)	(i)	Actual real interest rate
= Nominal interest rate - Actual inflation rate	(1 mark)
= 2% - 1% = 1%	(1 mark)
(ii)	In this case, debtors would gain (unexpectedly) as the actual real interest rate (1%) paid was lower than the expected real interest rate (3%).	(1 mark)
On the other hand, creditors would lose (unexpectedly) as the actual real interest rate (1%) received was lower than the expected real interest rate (3%).
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Explain how inflation affects the following items.
(a)	The purchasing power of money	(2 marks)
(b)	The competitiveness of domestic exports	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When the general price level increases, the same basket of goods and services will cost consumers more. This means that the purchasing power of money will decrease.	(2 marks)
(b)	Inflation increases the cost of domestic production and the prices of domestic exports. As a result, it lowers the competitiveness of domestic exports.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose people borrow from banks to finance the purchase of a home at a fixed interest rate.
(a)	Explain who will gain and who will lose during a period of unanticipated deflation.	(4 marks)
(b)	Explain who will gain and who will lose during a period of anticipated inflation.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Borrowers will lose,	(1 mark)
because the purchasing power of the money they repay to banks increases.
	(1 mark)
	•	Banks will gain,	(1 mark)
because the purchasing power of money they get back from borrowers increases.	(1 mark)
(b)	Under anticipated inflation, borrowers and banks have correctly anticipated the change in the real value of future payments. Since the actual change is expected, no party gains or loses due to the anticipated inflation.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose Peter lends $500,000 to Pan at an interest rate of 20% (per annum).
(a)	Explain who will gain and who will lose during a period of unexpected inflation.	(4 marks)
(b)	Suggest ONE method to avoid the wealth redistributive effects in (a).	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Peter will lose,	(1 mark)
because the purchasing power of the money he receives decreases with inflation.	(1 mark)
	•	Pan will gain,	(1 mark)
because the purchasing power of the money she pays back decreases with inflation.	(1 mark)
(b)	They can index the interest rate of the loan so that the interest rate will change　automatically along with a price index. This offsets the increase in the price level and maintains the purchasing power of the future payment.	(2 marks)
(Any other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the following diagram about the Composite Consumer Price Index (CCPI).

Explain whether the following parties would gain or lose during the period from Year 3 to Year 5.
(a)	A government which issued bonds at fixed interest rates	(2 marks)
(b)	The elderly who received a fixed amount of the Normal Old Age Allowance (普通高齡津貼)	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	As there was unexpected inflation during the period, the real value of fixed interest payments the government paid was lower than expected.	(1 mark)
Thus, the government would gain unexpectedly during the period.	(1 mark)
(b)	As there was unexpected inflation during the period, the real value of the allowance the elderly received was lower than expected.	(1 mark)
Thus, the elderly would lose unexpectedly during the period.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Salt City has many NEET youths (i.e., youths who are 'not in education, employment or training' 尼特族／啃老族). They have finished their studies and are old enough to work. However, they do not bother to look for jobs, but rely on their parents.
(a)	Explain whether NEET youths should be included in the unemployed population, according to the economic definition of unemployed persons.	(3 marks)
(b)	The government wants to tackle the problem. Explain the immediate effects on the unemployment rate of the following policies.
	(i)	Introduce vocational training programmes for NEET youths to continue their studies.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	Reward NEET youths who are successfully recruited.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No.	(1 mark)
	Although they do not have jobs, they do not actively look for work. They are neither included in the labour force nor in the unemployed population.	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	This policy does not immediately affect the unemployment rate.	(1 mark)
		Some of them may enrol in the programmes and become students. However, students are not included in the labour force and unemployed population. So, this does not affect the unemployment rate.	(2 marks)

	(ii)	The effect is uncertain.	(1 mark)
		This policy may encourage NEET youths to join the labour force and look for a job. However, some may be recruited and some may become unemployed persons. The effect on the unemployment rate depends on the percentage changes in the labour force and the unemployed population.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
'When the unemployment rate increases, the unemployed population must increase at a faster rate than that of the labour force.'
Explain whether this statement is correct.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	Incorrect. The rise in the unemployment rate may not imply that both the unemployed population and the labour force increase.	(1 mark)
Unemployment rate = 	(1 mark)
An increase in the unemployment rate may also be due to either one of the following:
•	a decrease in the labour force while the unemployed population remains unchanged;
•	both the unemployed population and the labour force decrease, but the unemployed population decreases at a slower rate than the labour force.
(Either one, 2 marks)

questions.text:

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text: In recent years, many Hong Kong residents have rushed to the mainland to find a job. Explain how this affects the unemployment rate in Hong Kong.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
•	The unemployed population will decrease.	(1 mark)
•	The labour force will decrease.	(1 mark)
•	The effect on the unemployment rate depends on the magnitude of the changes in the unemployed population and the labour force. 	(1 mark)
•	If the percentage decrease in the unemployed population is higher than the percentage decrease in the labour force, the unemployment rate will decrease.
OR
If the percentage decrease in the unemployed population is lower than the percentage decrease in the labour force, the unemployment rate will increase.
OR
If the percentage decrease in the unemployed population is equal to the percentage decrease in the labour force, the unemployment rate will remain unchanged.
(Any ONE of the above, 2 marks)

questions.text:

questions.answerText:

(b)	When some workers are unemployed, human resources which could have been used in production are wasted. As a result, the aggregate output of an economy is reduced.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Chun has been unemployed for one year. Recently, he succeeded in applying for admission to a full-time postgraduate programme. Under this programme, he will enjoy a scholarship (獎學金) but is not allowed to have any formal job attachment.
(a)	State TWO possible costs of unemployment to Chun.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether Chun is included in the following group.
(i)	Employed persons	(2 marks)
(ii)	Labour force	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Possible costs:
•	Lower standard of living
•	Family problems
•	Loss of skills
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers. 1 mark each)
(b)	(i)	The scholarshipship is not payment for work. Chun does not work for pay. He is not included in the groups of employed persons.	(2 marks)
(ii)	As Chun is neither an employed person nor an unemployed person, he is not included in the labour force.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define business cycles.	(2 marks)
(b)	Compare recession and peak in terms of real GDP.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Business cycles refer to short run cyclical fluctuations in the real GDP around the long run trend.	(2 marks)
(b)	Real GDP decreases when the economy is in recession.	(1 mark)
	Real GDP is at the highest point in a business cycle when the economy is at the peak.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the diagram below about the business cycle of a country and answer the following questions.

(b)	Apart from the level of real GDP, state TWO general phenomena that can be observed in this phase.	(2 marks)
(c)	Generally, economists use real GDP instead of nominal GDP to determine the phase of a business cycle. Explain the rationale behind this.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Peak	(1 mark)
(b)	(	High economic confidence and economic activities
	(	Low unemployment rate
	(	High real values of private consumption expenditure, investment expenditure, imports, sales receipts and tax revenue (either one)
	(	High inflation rate
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answer. 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(c)	This is because real GDP can better measure aggregate output as the effect of the price level on GDP has been eliminated.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Economy H experiences a great depression. Both the unemployment rate and the crime rate rise to a record high.
(a)	What are a trough and a depression?	(3 marks)
(b)	State TWO possible costs of unemployment to Economy H.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Trough is the lowest point of a business cycle in which economic activities are at their lowest level.	(1 mark)
The defining feature of a trough is that the real GDP is at its lowest.	(1 mark)
Depression is an extremely severe trough.	(1 mark)
(b)	Possible costs:
•	Loss of output
•	Social problems
(Any other reasonable answers. 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the following unemployment information for Country A.

Period	Unemployment rate (%)	
July 2013 - Sept. 2013	10	
Oct. 2013 - Dec. 2013	7	
Jan. 2014 - March 2014	3	

(a)	Define the unemployment rate in an equation.	(1 mark)
(b)	Based on the data above, explain how the number of unemployed persons in Country A changed during the period from October 2013 to December 2013 if the labour force did not change during the whole period.	(2 marks)
(c)	Explain which phase of a business cycle Country A was most likely in during the period from October 2013 to December 2013.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Unemployment rate = Unemployed persons ÷ Labour force × 100%	(1 mark)
(b)	As the labour force did not change, the decrease in the unemployment rate must imply a decrease in the number of unemployed persons.	(2 marks)
(c)	Recovery / expansion	(1 mark)
During the period, as the unemployment rate decreased, the real GDP most likely increased.	(1 mark)
However, it is not a peak as its unemployment rate is not at the lowest level.
	(1 mark)

questions.text:
Study the following information about an economy's price level in 2014 and 2015.

Year	Composite consumer price index (CCPI)	
2014	120

(b)	Suppose Rose made an investment in 2014 and expected no inflation. She expected the investment to generate a nominal rate of return of 8% after one year. Explain the investment's minimum actual nominal rate of return that would meet Rose's expectations on the real rate of return.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation rate in 2015 = (123 - 120)/120 × 100% = 2.5%	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
In 2015, Keith made an investment. He expected no change in the price level and a 2% nominal rate of return from the investment.
(a)	Find Keith's expected real rate of return from the investment.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose the nominal rate of return turns out to be 5%. Explain under what circumstances Keith's expectation of the real rate of return would not be met.
	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Expected real rate of return
	= Nominal rate of return - Expected inflation rate	(1 mark)
	= 2% - 0%
	= 2%	(1 mark)
(b)	Keith's expectation would not be met if the actual real rate of return from the investment is lower than 2%.	(1 mark)
	The actual real rate of return would be lower than 2% if inflation is 3% or higher.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Country C's consumer price index is shown as follows:
Year	Consumer price index	
2015	130	
2016	139	
(a)	Calculate the inflation rate of Country C in 2016.	(1 mark)
(b)	Given the situation in (a), would the nominal interest rate be higher than or lower than the real interest rate? Explain.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation rate = (139 - 130) ÷ 130 × 100% = 6.92%	(1 mark)
(b)	Nominal interest rate = Real interest rate + Inflation rate	(1 mark)
	With a positive inflation rate in 2016, the nominal interest rate would be higher than the real interest rate.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Express the real interest rate in terms of the nominal interest rate.	(1 mark)
(b)	Suppose people expect no inflation. By comparing the expected and actual real interest rates, explain whether lenders who receive fixed nominal interest rates will gain or lose when inflation occurs.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Inflation rate	(1 mark)
(b)	As there is no inflation is expected, the expected real interest rate is equal to the nominal interest rate.	(1 mark)
	When inflation occurs, the actual real interest rate is lower than the nominal interest rate.	(1 mark)
	As the actual real interest rate that lenders receive is lower than expected, lenders lose.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
City T has experienced deflation for three years. People in the city expect the price level to continue falling this year.
(a)	Explain whether the expected real interest rate is higher or lower than the nominal interest rate.	(3 marks)

(b)	Explain whether borrowers would gain or lose if inflation eventually occurs given that the borrowing rate is fixed.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Expected real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Expected inflation rate
	(1 mark)
	As people expect deflation, the expected inflation rate is negative. Hence, the expected real interest rate is higher than the nominal interest rate.	(2 marks)
(b)	Actual real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Actual inflation rate	(1 mark)
	The actual real interest rate is lower than the nominal interest rate when there is inflation.	(1 mark)
	Borrowers gain because the actual real interest rate they pay is lower than expected.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Explain whether the following people would gain or lose if unexpected deflation occurs.
(a)	Eric, who has a time deposit at a fixed nominal interest rate of 1.5%	(2 marks)
(b)	Marie, who has borrowed $100 million from a bank at a floating interest rate
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Gain, because	(1 mark)
	the purchasing power of the interest he receives would increase under unexpected deflation.	(1 mark)
(b)	No gain and no loss, because	(1 mark)
	the purchasing power of the interest would remain unchanged as the interest rate would be adjusted according to the inflation rate.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text: * 'Tenants paying fixed monthly rents lose when the expected real interest rate is higher than the nominal interest rate.' Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
No. It depends on the actual outcome.	(1 mark)
When there is unexpected inflation (or the actual deflation rate is smaller than the expected deflation rate), the purchasing power (real value) of the rental payments is lower than expected. In this case, tenants will gain.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
Sandy bought a bond with a 5% annual nominal interest rate in 2015. She expected 2% inflation that year.
(a)	Calculate Sandy's expected real rate of return from the bond.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose the inflation rate in 2015 turned out to be 1%. Explain whether Sandy would gain or lose, with reference to your answer in (a).	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Expected real rate of return
	= Nominal rate of return - Expected inflation rate	(1 mark)
	= 5% - 2%
	= 3%	(1 mark)
(b)	Actual real rate of return
	= Nominal rate of return - Actual inflation rate	(1 mark)
	= 5% - 1%
	= 4%	(1 mark)
	Sandy would gain because the actual real rate of return is higher than the expected real rate of return.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
The following table shows the price index of Country A.
Year	Price index	
1	200	
2	204	
(a)	Calculate the inflation rate in Year 2.	(1 mark)
(b)	Amber invested $100,000 in a project in Year 1 for an expected return of $20,000 in Year 2.
	If she expected the inflation rate to be 3% per year, explain whether she would gain or lose.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation rate = (204 - 200) ÷ 200 × 100% = 2%	(1 mark)
(b)	She would gain because	(1 mark)
	the actual inflation rate was lower than what she expected. The actual real rate of return (20% - 2% = 18%) was greater than the expected real rate of return

questions.topic: B5 · Ch503 · Demand and supply
questions.text:
* Country H's government issued a bond where the nominal interest rate is equal to the actual inflation rate. Bondholders are also guaranteed to receive a rate of at least 1%. The following table shows Country H's composite consumer price index (CCPI).
Year	CCPI	
1	100	
2	103.5	
3	102	
Suppose people expected the inflation rate to be 2% per year. Explain, in terms of the realised real interest rate, whether bondholders would gain or lose in Years 2 and 3, respectively.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Real interest rate = Nominal interest rate - Inflation rate	(1 mark)
In Year 2, the actual inflation rate was 3.5% and so was the nominal interest rate.
	(1 mark)
Therefore, the realised real interest rate was zero, which was the same as the expected real interest rate. They would not gain or lose.	(1 mark)
In Year 3, deflation occurred and the actual inflation rate was -1.45%.	(1 mark)
With a 1% nominal interest rate, the realised real interest rate was 2.45%, which was greater than the expected real interest rate. They would gain.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following can be an example to illustrate the relationship between the price level and the aggregate output demanded?
A.	When the central bank increases the interest rate, firms' investment expenditure decreases and the price level decreases.
B.	When the price level in a country decreases, foreign buyers import more from the country.
C.	When the price of a good increases, consumers buy less of the good.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements CANNOT explain the shape of an aggregate demand curve?
A.	When the price level increases, domestic products become less competitive than foreign products.
B.	When the price level increases, the purchasing power of people's wealth falls.
C.	When the price level decreases, output prices are more flexible than input prices.
D.	When the price level decreases, real interest rates decrease and this encourages people to increase present consumption.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following CANNOT explain the downward slope of an aggregate demand curve?
(1)	When the domestic price level increases, other things being equal, the real value of net exports decreases.
(2)	When nominal interest rates increase due to an increase in money supply, other things being equal, people will consume less and save more.
(3)	When people's real wealth increases due to an economic boom, people will consume more and their real private consumption expenditure increases.
A.	(3) only
B.	(1) and (2) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText:
Option (1) describes the net exports effect.
Options (2) and (3) are not the effects caused by changes in the price level. Thus, they cannot be used to explain the downward slope of an aggregate demand curve.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
When we explain the shape of an aggregate demand curve, which of the following correctly describes the net exports effect that occurs in the domestic economy?
A.	When the domestic price level increases, foreign economies import less from the domestic economy, holding price levels of foreign economies constant.
B.	When the price levels of foreign economies increase, the domestic economy exports more to foreign economies.
C.	When the domestic currency depreciates, the net exports of the domestic economy increase.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
The aggregate demand curve is __________ sloping because __________ when the price level increases.
A.	upward … people's total expenditure increases
B.	upward … the increase in interest rates attracts firms and households to invest
C.	downward … the domestic economy imports less due to the decrease in real wealth
D.	downward … fewer goods are bought due to the drop in purchasing power of cash

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Aggregate output is measured by

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
A.	The GDP deflator can be used to measure the price level.
B.	Aggregate output is measured by its total market value at current prices.
C.	Aggregate output demanded is negatively related to the price level.
D.	Aggregate output demanded is equal to the sum of real private consumption expenditure, real gross investment expenditure, real government consumption expenditure and the real value of net exports.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?
(1)	When the general price level decreases, aggregate demand will increase.
(2)	Aggregate demand is a value indicating the real expenditure on an economy's production at a particular price level.
(3)	When real consumption expenditure increases, aggregate output demanded will increase, other things being constant.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about the differences between aggregate output demanded and aggregate demand are correct?
(1)	Aggregate output demanded is a value while aggregate demand is a relation.
(2)	Aggregate output demanded is shown by a point while aggregate demand is represented by a curve or a table.
(3)	Aggregate output demanded is determined by the general price level alone while aggregate demand is determined by wealth alone.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
* Which of the following statements can explain why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping?
(1)	When the price level rises, fewer quantities of goods and services can be bought with the same amount of cash and deposits.
(2)	When the price level falls and with the same nominal amount of money in the economy, the real interest rate will decrease.
(3)	When the price level rises and with the same quantities of exports, the real value of net exports will decrease.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
Options (1) and (2) are the wealth effect and interest rate effect, respectively.
Option (3) is not correct. When the price level rises and with international prices remaining at the same level, the volume of exports falls while the volume of imports rises. As a result, the real value of net exports falls and so does the aggregate output demanded.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following can explain why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping?
A.	The substitution effect on demand 
B.	The law of demand
C.	The interest rate effect
D.	The wealth redistributive effect

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
When the general price level rises, ________ remains unchanged. This is why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping.
A.	the nominal value of exports
B.	the purchasing power of money
C.	the nominal value of goods and services
D.	the nominal value of cash

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements can explain why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping?
A.	According to the law of demand, aggregate output demanded and the general price level are inversely related.
B.	When the general price level rises, income distribution will become more uneven. This will lower labour productivity and the aggregate output demanded.
C.	When the general price level rises, there are substitution effects on consumption. The relative prices of final products to financial assets will increase. As a result, people will buy fewer final products and more financial assets.
D.	When the prices of domestic products rise relative to the prices of their foreign substitutes, the volume of our exports fall while the volume of our imports rise. Thus, the real value of net exports will increase.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
A.	The wealth effect on consumption exists only if the total nominal value of wealth remains unchanged when the price level changes.
B.	The aggregate output demanded is also called real aggregate expenditure.
C.	Aggregate demand describes the aggregate outputs demanded at different price levels, holding other factors constant.
D.	There are three effects to explain why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping, namely the wealth effect, the interest effect and the net exports effect.
questions.answerText: Option A is incorrect. When the price level rises, the real value of people's wealth declines as the nominal value of monetary assets (e.g., cash and deposits) remains unchanged. However, the nominal value of non-monetary assets (e.g., gold and properties) may increase.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
* Which of the following can be an example to illustrate the downward sloping shape of the aggregate demand curve?
A.	Alex buys less ice cream when its price increases.
B.	Boyle saves less money when the general price level increases.
C.	Cathy buys fewer imported goods when the domestic general price level increases.
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText: Option B can be an example to illustrate the interest rate effect. When many people save less money as Boyle does when faced with an increase in the general price level, real interest rates will increase. As a result, real private consumption expenditure and gross investment expenditure drop, and the aggregate output demanded also falls.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about the wealth effect on consumption is correct?
A.	It exists as consumption is only determined by wealth.
B.	People will consume fewer goods when the purchasing power of their wealth declines due to the decline in income.
C.	It cannot explain the downward sloping shape of the aggregate demand curve if the purchasing power of people's wealth increases when the general price level rises.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:

A.	When the general price level rises and the nominal money supply remains the same, households and firms need more money to finance transactions. This leads to an increase in real interest rates.
B.	When the general price level rises and the same nominal interest rates are in 
effect, real interest rates will decrease. Thus, consumption and investment decrease with real interest rates.
C.	It can explain the slope of the aggregate demand curve.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following can explain why the short run aggregate supply curve is upward sloping?
(1)	Bound by contracts, employers cannot lower their employees' salaries immediately when output prices fall.
(2)	When the price level increases, firms expect the price level to rise further. Thus, they produce more now and sell their products later at higher prices.
(3)	When the price level increases, firms find it profitable to increase their output.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText: Option (2): The change in price expectations will lead to a rightward shift in the short run aggregate supply curve and so cannot explain why the short run aggregate supply curve is upward sloping.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following about an upward sloping aggregate supply curve is correct?
A.	It exists in both the short run and the long run.
B.	It only exists under imperfect information.
C.	It exists when input prices cannot be adjusted immediately with the price level due to the contracts signed.
D.	None of the above

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following events can lead to an upward sloping short run aggregate supply curve?
A.	A firm borrows at a fixed interest rate to increase production while the economy is experiencing inflation.
B.	The adjustment of wages is based on the inflation rate in the previous year.
C.	A restaurant raises its prices by 6% while the prices of raw materials increase by 2%.
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText: Option B is correct because this will result in a lower increase in wages than output prices if the inflation rate is increasing.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
The short run aggregate supply curve is __________ because __________ in the short run.
A.	upward sloping … factor costs increase more than the price level
B.	upward sloping … input prices are less flexible than output prices
C.	vertical … input prices are fixed
D.	vertical … it is not profitable for firms to increase their output level

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
A.	Aggregate output supplied is the total real value of all goods and services supplied in an economy at a particular price level over a specified period.
B.	Aggregate output demanded is the total real value of all goods and services demanded in an economy at a particular price level over a specified period.
C.	Aggregate output supplied is positively related to the general price level.
D.	Aggregate output demanded is negatively related to the general price level.
questions.answerText: Option C: Aggregate output supplied is positively related to the general price level in the short run but it is independent of the general price level in the long run.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?
(1)	When the general price level increases, aggregate output supplied must increase.
(2)	Aggregate supply is a value indicating the total real value of all goods and services supplied at a particular price level.
(3)	According to the law of supply, an aggregate supply curve is upward sloping.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText: Option (1): When the general price level increases, aggregate output supplied increases in the short run but remains unchanged in the long run.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:

(1)	Aggregate output supplied is a value while aggregate supply is a relation.
(2)	Aggregate output supplied is the same as aggregate supply when they are measured by real national income.
(3)	Aggregate supply can be represented by a curve or a table.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?
A.	There are two kinds of aggregate supply curves, the short run aggregate supply curve and the long run aggregate supply curve.
B.	There are two kinds of aggregate demand curves, the short run aggregate demand curve and the long run aggregate demand curve.
C.	In the short run, some prices are sticky and do not adjust to the change in economic conditions.
D.	In the long run, all prices are flexible.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Which of the following statements can explain why the short run aggregate supply curve is upward sloping?
(1)	According to the law of supply, when the general price level increases, the aggregate output supplied will increase.
(2)	When output prices increase, factor costs do not increase immediately. This leads to profits for producers. Hence, they increase their output.
(3)	When the general price level increases, input prices increase at the same time. To cover the increase in cost, aggregate output supplied increases.
A.	(2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only

questions.text:

questions.answerText: Option D is the answer. The adjustment of input prices is slower than that of output prices. questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is the effect of an increase in the price level on the real values of households' and firms' monetary assets? Why?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain how the effect in (a) is related to the slope of an aggregate demand curve.
	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When the price level increases, the real values of households' and firms' monetary assets decrease.	(1 mark)
	This is because the nominal values of monetary assets are constant.	(1 mark)
(b)	When the price level increases, as households' and firms' real wealth decreases, real private consumption expenditure and real investment expenditure decrease. Hence, aggregate output demanded drops.	(2 marks)
	The inverse relationship between the price level and the aggregate output demanded implies a downward sloping aggregate demand curve.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	In what sense is interest a cost of present consumption?	(2 marks)
(b)	Assume the nominal amount of the money supply remains unchanged. How does the price level affect real interest rates? Then, explain how the relationship between the price level and real interest rates is related to the downward slope of an aggregate demand curve.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	People have to pay interest when they borrow money for present consumption. / People have to forgo interest income if they spend money on present consumption.	(2 marks)
(b)	When the price level increases, more money is needed to finance transactions. Thus, saving decreases and borrowing increases. Both push up real interest rates.
	(2 marks)
The increase in real interest rates discourages consumption and investment. As a result, aggregate output demanded falls. This implies a downward sloping aggregate demand curve.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	When the price level of a country increases while foreign price levels remain constant, how do the country's net exports change? Briefly explain.	(2 marks)
(b)	What is the shape of an AD curve? How does the relationship between the price level and net exports explain the shape?	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When the domestic price level increases, domestic goods and services become less competitive than foreign goods and services.	(1 mark)
	Exports decrease while imports increase. As a result, net exports decrease.
	(1 mark)
(b)	Downward sloping.	(1 mark)
When the price level increases, net exports decrease, driving down aggregate output demanded. The negative relationship implies a downward sloping aggregate demand curve.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define aggregate output demanded and aggregate demand.	(4 marks)
(b)	State ONE difference between them.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Aggregate output demanded is the total value of an economy's production demanded (measured by real gross domestic product or real national income) at a particular price level over a specified period.	(2 marks)
Aggregate demand is the relation between the price level and the aggregate output demanded in an economy. It describes the aggregate outputs demanded at different price levels, holding other factors constant.	(2 marks)
(b)	Aggregate output demanded is a value while aggregate demand is a relation between two variables.
(Accept any other reasonable answer. 1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
Suggest TWO reasons why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping.
	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
The aggregate demand curve is downward sloping because the following effects occur simultaneously as the price level changes.
(	The wealth effect - When the price level rises (falls), the purchasing power of people's monetary assets decreases (increases). Other things remaining constant, the real wealth of households and firms drops (rises). Hence, real private consumption and investment expenditure drop (rise) and so does the aggregate output demanded.
(	The interest rate effect - When the price level rises (falls), as more (less) money is needed to finance transactions, saving decreases (increases) while borrowing increases (decreases). This raises (lowers) the real interest rate. Thus, real private consumption and investment expenditure decrease (increase) and so does the aggregate output demanded.
(	The net exports effect - When the domestic price level rises (falls), prices of domestic products rise (fall) relative to the prices of their foreign substitutes. The volume of our exports falls (rises) while the volume of our imports rises (falls). As a result, the aggregate output demanded falls (rises).
(Briefly describe any TWO effects of the above, 3 marks × 2 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: The wealth effect can be used to explain why the aggregate demand curve is downward sloping. Explain how this effect works if there is a decrease in the general price level.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText: When the price level falls, people can buy more quantities of goods and services with the same amount of cash and deposits. Hence, the purchasing power or the real value of people's monetary assets increases due to the fall in the price level. Since people's real wealth has increased, they have a greater ability to consume. Their real private consumption expenditure increases. Consequently, aggregate output demanded increases.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: The interest rate effect is one of the effects that account for the downward sloping shape of the aggregate demand curve. Explain how this effect works if there is a decrease in the general price level.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText: When the price level decreases and with nominal money supply remaining unchanged, households and firms need less money to finance their transactions. Thus, saving increases and borrowing decreases. Both will push down real interest rates. The fall in the real interest rate increases both real private consumption expenditure and real gross investment expenditure. As a result, aggregate output demanded increases.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is aggregate demand?	(2 marks)
(b)	Given that foreign price levels remain unchanged, explain how the aggregate output demanded changes when there is a fall in the general price level.	(3 marks)
(c)	Based on the result in (b), what is the shape of an aggregate demand curve?
	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Aggregate demand is the relation between the price level and the aggregate output demanded in an economy. It describes the aggregate outputs demanded at different price levels, holding other factors constant.	(2 marks)
(b)	When the general price level falls but foreign price levels remain unchanged, the prices of domestic products fall relative to the prices of their foreign substitutes. The quantities of our exports rise while the quantities of our imports fall. As a result, aggregate output demanded rises.	(3 marks)
(c)	The shape is downward sloping as the aggregate output demanded increases when the general price level falls.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Give ONE example to explain why wages may be less flexible than output prices in the short run.	(1 mark)
(b)	Use 'sticky wages' to explain the upward sloping shape of a short run aggregate supply curve.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Wages may be fixed by contracts. (Accept other reasonable examples.)	(1 mark)
(b)	When output prices increase while wages remain sticky in the short run, it is profitable for firms to employ more labour to raise their outputs.	(2 marks)
	As a result, the aggregate output supplied increases with the price level in the short run. This implies that the short run aggregate supply curve is upward sloping.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define full employment GDP.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suggest ONE reason to explain why the long run aggregate supply curve is vertical at the full employment real GDP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Full employment GDP is the GDP when all of an economy's resources are used efficiently.	(2 marks)
(b)	(	Flexible prices: In the long run, both input and output prices are flexible. It is not profitable for firms to produce at an output level higher than the original output level. Therefore, in the long run, any change in the price level would have no effect on the aggregate output supplied. Moreover, as all input prices are fully flexible, all factor markets attain full employment. Thus, the economy produces at the full employment output level in the long run.
	(	Capacity constraint: The full employment output level of an economy is determined by its quantity and quality of resources, as well as the level of technology available. With resources and production technology remaining unchanged, full employment real GDP is a constant at any price level.
	(Either ONE of the above, 3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	Define aggregate output supplied and aggregate supply.	(4 marks)
(b)	State ONE difference between them.	(1 mark)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Aggregate output supplied is the total value of an economy's production supplied at a particular price level over a specified period.	(2 marks)
Aggregate supply is the relation between the price level and the aggregate output supplied in an economy. It describes the aggregate outputs supplied at different price levels, holding other factors constant.	(2 marks)
(b)	Aggregate output supplied is a value while aggregate supply is a relation between two variables.
(Accept any other reasonable answer. 1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: Discuss ONE difference between short run and long run in macroeconomics in terms of prices.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
In macroeconomics, short run is a period within which some prices do not fully adjust to the change in economic conditions.	(2 marks)
In macroeconomics, long run is a period within which all prices are fully flexible.
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: Why is the short run aggregate supply curve upward sloping?	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
When the price level increases, input prices increase at a slower pace than output prices in the short run. It becomes profitable for firms to employ more inputs to raise their outputs. Hence, the aggregate output supplied increases with the price level in the short run. This implies that the short run aggregate supply curve is upward 
sloping.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: Explain why the aggregate supply curve can be upward sloping or vertical.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
The aggregate supply curve is upward sloping in the short run but vertical in the long run.	(1 mark)
In the short run, when the price level increases, input prices increase at a slower pace than output prices. It becomes profitable for firms to employ more inputs to raise their outputs. Hence, the aggregate output supplied increases with the price level in the short run. This implies that the short run aggregate supply curve is upward sloping.
	(3 marks)
In the long run, all prices are fully flexible. All input prices would rise by the same proportion as output prices. It is not profitable for firms to produce at an output level that is higher than the original output level. Firms would restore their original production plans. Full employment real national income is always achieved at any price level. Thus, the long run aggregate supply curve is represented by a vertical line.
	(4 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: The imperfect adjustment of input and output prices can account for the shape of the short run aggregate supply curve. Explain how this effect works when the price level falls.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
In the short run, input prices are less flexible than output prices.	(1 mark)
When output prices decrease while input prices remain sticky, firms suffer decreases in profits. Firms will lower their outputs to minimise losses. Hence, the short run aggregate output supplied decreases when the price level falls.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
* 'As input prices adjust more slowly than output prices, firms increase their output when there is an increase in the general price level in order to maximise profits. Thus, other factors being constant, the equilibrium real national income will increase in the short run. This implies that inflation is good for an economy.'
Explain whether this statement is correct.	(10 marks)
questions.answerText:
Incorrect.	(1 mark)
The imperfect adjustment of input and output prices cannot be used to explain the relationship between the equilibrium real national income and the general price level.	(2 marks)
The short run equilibrium real national income is determined by the intersection of the short run aggregate supply curve and the aggregate demand curve.	(1 mark)
Other factors being constant, if there is an increase in the general price level, there will be an excess supply of aggregate output. The short run equilibrium real national income will not change.	(1 mark)
Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(1 mark)
There is no exact relationship between a persistent increase in the equilibrium price level (i.e., inflation) and an increase in the equilibrium real national income.	(1 mark)
However, there are adverse effects of inflation. The following are some of the adverse effects:
(	The cost of living rises and the purchasing power of money drops;
(	The standard of living may fall;
(	Resources are reallocated;
(	The volume of exports drops while the volume of imports rises.
(One of the above or any reasonable adverse effect, 2 marks)
Thus, inflation may be bad for an economy.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:

Year	GDP deflator	Nominal wage index	
1	100	150

3	120	170	

(a)	Calculate the percentage changes in the GDP deflator in Year 2 and Year 3, respectively.	(2 marks)

questions.answerText:
(a)	The percentage change in the GDP deflator in Year 2
= (110 - 100) ÷ 100 = 10%	(1 mark)
The percentage change in the GDP deflator in Year 3
= (120 - 110) ÷ 110 = 9.09%	(1 mark)
(b)	The percentage change in the nominal wage index in Year 2
= (160 - 150) ÷ 150 = 6.67%	(1 mark)
The percentage change in the nominal wage index in Year 3
= (170 - 160) ÷ 160 = 6.25%	(1 mark)
(c)	From the results of (a) and (b), the percentage increase in the nominal wage index was smaller than the percentage increase in the GDP deflator.	(2 marks)
It became profitable for firms to employ more labour to raise their outputs. Hence, the aggregate output supplied increased with the price level between Year 2 and Year 3. The short run aggregate supply curve within the period was upward sloping.	(2 marks)
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: Suppose there is a rise in the price level. What would happen to the aggregate output supplied in the short run and long run? State ONE underlying reason for each of the cases.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
In the short run, when the price level rises, the aggregate output supplied will 
increase.	(1 mark)
Underlying reason:
Imperfect adjustment of input and output prices: The adjustment of input prices is slower than the adjustment of output prices in the short run. This makes it profitable for firms to employ more inputs to increase output in the short run.	(2 marks)
In the long run, when the price level rises, the aggregate output supplied will remain unchanged.	(1 mark)
Underlying reason:
In the long run, the increase in input prices catches up with the increase in output prices. It is not profitable for firms to increase output beyond the original level.
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: Draw a short run aggregate supply curve and a long run aggregate supply curve. Explain with ONE reason why they have different shapes.	(4 marks)

(2 marks)
They have different shapes because some input prices are less flexible than output prices in the short run while all prices are fully flexible in the long run.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text: Explain why the long run aggregate supply curve is vertical.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Two underlying reasons explain why it is vertical.
(	Flexible prices: All input prices are fully flexible, and so all input markets attain full employment.	(2 marks)
(	Capacity constraint: The full employment output level of an economy is determined by its quantity and quality of resources, as well as the level of technology available. With resources and production technology remaining unchanged, full employment real national income is a constant at any price level.	(2 marks)
(Marks will be given only when explanations are provided.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply
questions.text:
In City T, the minimum wage is reviewed every two years. Most employers follow this practice when reviewing employees' wages. Suppose there is 10% inflation this year and wages were reviewed last year.
(a)	Suggestion ONE effect of inflation on real private consumption expenditure and real investment expenditure.	(3 marks)
(b)	(i)	In City T, does the adjustment of wages and output prices during this year belong to a short run or long run phenomenon? Why?	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Use the phenomenon in (b)(i) to explain the shape of the corresponding aggregate supply curve.	(3 marks)
(c)	Explain how the change in wage rates differs in the long run. Then, explain the shape of the long run aggregate supply curve.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(	Wealth effect: When the price level increases, the real values of households' and firms' monetary assets decrease. As a result, they are less able to spend and the real values of private consumption expenditure and investment expenditure decrease.
	(	Interest rate effect: When the price level increases, more money is needed to finance transactions. Thus, saving decreases and borrowing increases. Both push up real interest rates. The increase in real interest rates decreases real private consumption expenditure and real investment expenditure.
	(Either ONE of the above. 3 marks)

(b)	(i)	Short run.	(1 mark)
In the short run, wage rates are less flexible than output prices.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Since wages remain unchanged this year, it is profitable for firms to employ more labour to raise their output.	(1 mark)
Hence, the short run aggregate output supplied increases with the price level.
	(1 mark)
The short run aggregate supply curve is upward sloping.	(1 mark)

(c)	In the long run, workers ask for a wage rise equal to the increase in the price level.	(1 mark)
It is not profitable for firms to produce at an output level that is higher than the original output level. Firms would restore their original production plans. Therefore, in the long run, any change in the price level would have no effect on the aggregate output supplied. 	(3 marks)
This implies that the long run aggregate supply curve is vertical.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch504 · Changes in demand and supply

Refer to the following figures.
Year	Percentage change in real wage index	Percentage change in nominal wage index	
1	0%	2%

3	-1%	4%	
(a)	Suppose the real wage index in each year was deflated by its current GDP deflator. Find the approximate value of the percentage change in the GDP deflator in each year.	(3 marks)
(b)	Define inflation and disinflation. Was there disinflation during the period? Explain.	(6 marks)
(c)	It was found that firms employed more workers in Year 3 than in Year 2.
(i)	Why did firms have an incentive to employ more workers?	(2 marks)
(ii)	Between Year 2 and Year 3, what was the shape of the short run aggregate supply curve? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The approximate value of the percentage change in GDP deflator in Year 1
= 2% - 0% = 2%	(1 mark)
The approximate value of the percentage change in GDP deflator in Year 2
= 3% - 0% = 3%	(1 mark)
The approximate value of the percentage change in GDP deflator in Year 3
= 4% - (-1%) = 5%	(1 mark)
(b)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
Disinflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level but at a declining rate.	(2 marks)
No, there was no disinflation during the period.	(1 mark)
This is because the general price level increased at an increasing rate.	(1 mark)
(c)	(i)	The increase in nominal wages was smaller than the increase in the price level. If firms employ more workers to increase output, they could enjoy greater profit.	(2 marks)
(ii)	Upward sloping	(1 mark)
Firms increased output as the price level increased. This implied a positive relationship between the price level and the aggregate output supplied.
	(2 marks)

questions.text:
* Which of the following statements are INCORRECT?
(1)	When the government lowers the unit tax of a good and given the same aggregate output demanded, the price level drops. Thus, the aggregate demand curve shifts downwards.
(2)	When people desire to invest more, they will consume less. As a result, private consumption expenditure falls and the aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.
(3)	When people's wealth increases and given the same price level, individuals have a greater ability to consume. Thus, private consumption expenditure rises and the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
Option (1) is the answer. The decrease in unit tax will shift the short run aggregate supply curve (instead of aggregate demand curve) downwards. Moreover, the decrease in the unit tax of a particular good may only have a small (or even negligible) effect on the short run aggregate supply.
Option (2) is the answer. When people desire to invest more, gross investment expenditure will increase. Even if they cut their consumption and save more money to finance their investment, aggregate demand may not decrease. Thus, the aggregate demand curve may not shift leftwards.

questions.text:
Which of the following will lower aggregate demand and long run aggregate supply?

Options B and C are not the answers. If Doomsday is expected, people would tend to increase present consumption, instead of saving. If a storm is expected, people would rush to buy necessities (like water, food, batteries). Hence, it is possible that both events would raise aggregate demand.
Option D is not the answer. This does not affect long run aggregate supply.

* Which of the following statements about the introduction of minimum wage laws is INCORRECT?
A.	The introduction of minimum wage laws will lead to a decrease in the short run aggregate supply as it makes production less profitable.
B.	The introduction of minimum wage laws may increase the long run aggregate supply if it raises low-skilled workers' incentive to work.

questions.answerText:
Option B is a correct statement. If the introduction of minimum wage laws can increase low-skilled workers' incentive to work, the supply of labour will increase and so will the potential real national income and the long run aggregate supply.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: * Which of the following best represents the effect of an increase in the number of infants born this year?
questions.answerText:
The increase in the number of infants born means the labour force in 16 years (but not this year) will increase. Therefore, (short run and long run) aggregate supply in 16 years will increase.
On the other hand, the increase in the number of infants born means there will be more spending by people this year and 16 years from now. Therefore, aggregate demand this year and 16 years from now will increase.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Country A and Country B are trading partners. If the price level in Country B increases, Country A's real GDP will ________ in the short run.
A.	increase
B.	remain unchanged
C.	decrease
D.	be indeterminate
questions.answerText: When Country B's price level increases, the products that Country B makes will become more expensive. Country B's consumers will buy a larger quantity of Country A's goods and Country A will import a smaller quantity of Country B's goods. The real value of Country A's net exports rises and Country A's aggregate demand curve will shift to the right. As a result, Country A's real GDP will increase in the short run.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
* Which of the following would likely lower unemployment in Hong Kong?
(1)	The Community Care Fund (CCF, 關愛基金) provides a one-off subsidy to low-income households.
(2)	Many US businesspeople are optimistic about business prospects in the mainland of China.
(3)	Price levels in European countries increase rapidly.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
Option (1): After receiving the subsidy, low-income households will increase their consumption. As a result, aggregate demand increases and so does real GDP. The increase in real GDP will increase employment and lower unemployment.
Option (2): US businesspeople will increase their investment in the mainland of China. As a result, real GDP in the mainland of China will increase. The mainland of China is Hong Kong's trading partner. The increase in the mainland of China's real GDP will stimulate Hong Kong's economy and reduce unemployment here.
Option (3): When price levels in European countries increase, products in those countries become more expensive. Consumers there will buy a larger quantity of Hong Kong's goods while Hong Kong will import a smaller quantity of goods from European countries. The real value of Hong Kong's net exports rises and the aggregate demand curve will shift to the right. As a result, Hong Kong's real GDP will increase and unemployment will decrease.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: With the aid of a diagram, explain the effect of an increase in the foreign price level on local output and the price level in the short run.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in equilibrium output and the price level in the short run	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
•	An increase in the foreign price level means foreign products become more expensive.	(1 mark)
•	Therefore, net exports increase.	(1 mark)
•	As a result, aggregate demand increases, leading to an increase in output and the price level in the short run.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose an economy is facing unemployment. Explain with an AS-AD diagram how an income tax rebate (入息稅退稅) from the government will lower unemployment.
	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	The original short run equilibrium output is smaller than the full employment output, indicating the economy is facing unemployment	(1 mark)
•	Rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in short run equilibrium output / The difference between full employment output and short run equilibrium output (i.e., deflationary gap) is reduced or eliminated	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
•	Unemployment exists when the short run equilibrium output is smaller than the full employment output (Yf).	(1 mark)
•	The income tax rebate will increase people's disposable income. This will increase private consumption expenditure.	(2 marks)
•	Therefore, aggregate demand increases, leading to an increase in short run output.	(1 mark)
•	The difference between full employment output and short run equilibrium output decreases (from YfY1 to YfY2), meaning a decrease in unemployment.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
As a result of quantitative easing (QE) (量化寬鬆措施) in the US, the Hong Kong dollar depreciated against the renminbi.
(a)	Briefly explain why QE would increase both Hong Kong's real income and price level in the short run.	(3 marks)
(b)	As a Hong Kong resident, would you welcome QE in the US? Give ONE reason.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When the Hong Kong dollar depreciates against the renminbi as a result of QE, Hong Kong's products become cheaper in renminbi.	(1 mark)
	Therefore, Hong Kong's net exports increase and this increases Hong Kong's aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
	As a result, both Hong Kong's real income and price level increase in the short run.
(b)	I would welcome QE. This is because QE increases Hong Kong's real income, which means unemployment is lower in the short run.
OR
	I would not welcome QE.
The increase in real income is caused by an increase in net exports. This cannot improve current economic welfare.
	(Choose either ONE stand. Explain with ONE relevant reason. 2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Explain whether the following events will lead to a shift in the aggregate demand curve or a movement along the aggregate demand curve.
(a)	An increase in income taxes	(2 marks)
(b)	An increase in real consumption expenditure due to the wealth effect of a decrease in the price level	(2 marks)
(c)	An increase in real exports due to a decrease in the domestic price level	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	After an increase in income taxes, people will have less disposable income. Thus, given the same price level, the aggregate output demanded drops. Aggregate demand decreases and the aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(2 marks)
(b)	The wealth effect is caused by a decrease in the general price level. Thus, there is a downward movement along the aggregate demand curve.	(2 marks)

(c)	As the increase in real exports is caused by a decrease in the domestic price level, there is a downward movement along the aggregate demand curve.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Explain whether the following events will affect real aggregate expenditure. If they will, state which components they affect and how the aggregate demand curve shifts.
(a)	The government reduces profits taxes.	(3 marks)
(b)	The central bank increases interest rates.	(3 marks)
(c)	It is expected that the economy will experience a recession.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When the government reduces profits taxes, it is more profitable for firms to invest. At the same price level, real gross investment expenditure increases and so does real aggregate expenditure.	(2 marks)
As a result, the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
(b)	When interest rates rise, the cost of present consumption and investment increases. Thus, given the same price level, real private consumption expenditure and real gross investment expenditure decrease, and so does real aggregate expenditure.
	(2 marks)
As a result, the aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
(c)	When firms are pessimistic about economic prospects, they will cut their investment. Thus, real gross investment expenditure decreases and so does real aggregate expenditure.	(2 marks)
As a result, the aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is aggregate demand?	(2 marks)
(b)	What will happen to the aggregate demand curve if there is a decrease in the foreign price level? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(5 marks)
(c)	Do we have the same result as in (b) if there is an increase in the domestic price level (and thus the foreign price level becomes relatively lower)? Show your answer in a diagram.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Aggregate demand is the relation between price levels and the aggregate outputs demanded in an economy. It describes the aggregate outputs demanded at different price levels, holding other factors constant.	(2 marks)

(b)	When the price level of our trading partners decreases, foreign products become cheaper relative to our products. Foreigners buy a smaller quantity of our exports while we import a larger quantity of foreign goods.	(2 marks)
Hence, at the same domestic price level, net exports decrease.	(1 mark)
As a result, the domestic aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
	(1 mark)
(c)	No. There is an upward movement along the aggregate demand curve as the decrease in aggregate output demanded is caused by an increase in the domestic price level.	(2 marks)
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Suppose there are only two countries: Monkey Island (MI) and Weapon States (WS). They are close trading partners. The currency of MI (called Bana) appreciates against the currency of WS (called Dona) because the WS government prints a large amount of money in order to increase its expenditure.
(a)	How does the appreciation of Bana affect the real national income of MI in the short run? Explain with a diagram.	(8 marks)
(b)	How does the increase in the WS government's expenditure affect the real national income of WS in the short run? Explain with a diagram.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When Bana appreciates against Dona, people in WS have to use more units of Dona to buy MI's exports while people in MI can use fewer units of Bana to buy MI's imports.	(2 marks)
Thus, MI's real exports decrease while MI's real imports increase.	(2 marks)
As a result, MI's aggregate demand curve will shift leftwards.	(1 mark)
The real national income of MI will decrease in the short run.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

(b)	When the WS government increases its expenditure, aggregate demand increases and so the aggregate demand curve will shift rightwards.	(2 marks)
The real national income of WS will increase in the short run.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: In Apple City, because consumerism (消費主義) is advocated, people save less and consume more. With the aid of a diagram, explain how this affects the short run equilibrium real national income and price levels.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
If people desire to save less, they will consume a larger proportion of their disposable income. Hence, private consumption expenditure increases and so does aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
The aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
In the short run, both equilibrium real national income and price level will increase.
	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
With the aid of diagrams, explain how the following events will affect real national income and price level in the short run.
(a)	Our disposable income increases due to a tax rebate.	(7 marks)
(b)	Our trading partner's national income decreases.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When people have more disposable income, they will increase their private consumption expenditure. At the same price level, aggregate output demanded rises.	(2 marks)
Hence, aggregate demand increases and the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
As a result, both real national income and the price level increase.	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

(b)	When our trading partner's national income decreases, it will consume less. As its decreased consumption includes our exports, the real value of our exports decreases.	(2 marks)
Hence, the domestic aggregate demand decreases and the domestic aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
As a result, both real national income and the price level decrease.	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

questions.text: Electricity tariffs in Hong Kong have increased recently. With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, briefly explain the effect of the increase in electricity tariffs on Hong Kong's real GDP and price level in the short run.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
