•	Decrease in real GDP and increase in the price level	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
•	The increase in electricity tariffs will increase the cost of production.	(1 mark)
•	As a result, firms will reduce their output and the short run aggregate supply curve will shift leftwards.	(1 mark)
•	The price level will increase and the real GDP will decrease in the short run.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
An economy is operating at full employment. Suppose the only railway network in the economy closes for one week after a fire at the station. Would there be an inflationary gap or a deflationary gap in the short run? Explain with a well-labelled diagram.
	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Leftward shift of the short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
•	New short run equilibrium real GDP is lower than the full employment level / Deflationary gap exists	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
•	The temporary closure of the railway network decreases the short run aggregate supply. The short run aggregate supply curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
•	This lowers the short run equilibrium real GDP from Yf to Ye.	(1 mark)
•	As a result, a deflationary gap exists in the short run as the short run equilibrium real GDP (Ye) is lower than the full employment level (Yf).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Briefly explain whether the following events in Country A will affect its short run aggregate supply and long run aggregate supply.
(a)	A spill (漏油事故) leads to permanent environmental damage.	(3 marks)
(b)	A 10-year drought causes persistent crop failure. Famine (饑荒) causes half of the population to die.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The environmental damage will lower both the quantity and the quality of land (a type of factor of production). Thus, both the short run aggregate supply and the long run aggregate supply will decrease.	(3 marks)

(b)	The decrease in population implies that the quantity of labour available decreases. Thus, both the short run aggregate supply and the long run aggregate supply decrease.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Explain whether the following events will lead to a shift in the short run aggregate supply curve or a movement along the short run aggregate supply curve.
(a)	A rise in the general sales tax leads to a once-and-for-all rise in the general price level.	(3 marks)
(b)	Businesspeople expect stock prices to rise. 	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A shift in the short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
Reason: A rise in the general sales tax will raise production costs. At the same price level, firms have to cut their outputs. Therefore, the short run aggregate supply decreases and thus the short run aggregate supply curve shifts leftwards.
	(2 marks)
(b)	A shift in the short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
Reason: To earn more money, businesspeople will invest less in capital goods and put more money into the stock market. Thus, fewer capital goods will be available. As a result, the short run aggregate supply curve will shift leftwards.	(2 marks)
(Accept any other reasonable answer.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Read the following news report on Country X's economy.

Ming said, 'Some fresh graduates are unemployed. This implies that the labour market is not efficient. The long run aggregate supply will decrease and the long run aggregate supply curve will shift leftwards.'
Do you agree? Explain your answer.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
No.	(1 mark)
In the short run, there may be the problem of unemployment. However, in the long run, the problem will be settled. The existence of unemployment in the short run does not imply the labour market is inefficient.	(2 marks)
The long run aggregate supply is determined by the quantity of available factors, instead of employed factors. The unemployment of fresh graduates will not affect the quantity of labour available and so it has no effect on the long run aggregate supply and the long run aggregate supply curve.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: In Country A, there is an investment entrant scheme (投資入境計劃). Suppose the government increases the threshold (門檻) of investment for admission to Country A. Briefly explain how this will affect the aggregate supply and the long run equilibrium real national income of Country A. (To simplify, no need to consider the demand-side effects.)	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
The increase in the threshold will restrict the admission of quality migrants. As a result, Country A will have fewer high quality migrants.	(1 mark)
The quantity of labour will be lower (than the situation without increasing the threshold).	(1 mark)
The long run aggregate supply will be lower (than the situation without increasing the threshold).	(1 mark)
The long run equilibrium real national income is determined by the long run aggregate output supplied. As the long run aggregate output supplied is lower, the long run equilibrium real national income will be lower (than the situation without increasing the threshold).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: With the aid of a diagram, explain how a typhoon will affect the equilibrium real GDP and price level of Hong Kong in the short run and long run. Describe the adjustment process from the short run to the long run as well.	(11 marks)
questions.answerText:
A typhoon will affect the aggregate output supplied without affecting the full employment output level. Thus, it will only shift the short run aggregate supply curve leftwards.	(1 mark)
Suppose the economy is initially at Point A.
In the short run, the equilibrium real GDP will decrease from Yf to YS2 and the equilibrium price level will increase from P1 to PS2.	(2 marks)
In the long run, since the short run equilibrium real GDP (YS2) is smaller than the full employment real GDP (Yf), there is a deflationary gap and an excess supply of inputs.	(2 marks)
Input prices will decrease and this will shift the short run aggregate supply curve downwards until the deflationary gap is closed and long run equilibrium is achieved.	(1 mark)
As a result, both the equilibrium real GDP (Yf) and equilibrium price level (P1) will be restored to the original level in the long run.	(2 marks)
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: How will the real national income and price level change in the short run and long run if both the short run aggregate supply and the long run aggregate supply decrease? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
Suppose initially the aggregate demand curve, short run and long run aggregate supply curves intersect with each other at Point A.
When the short run aggregate supply decreases from SRAS1 to SRAS2, the price level increases from P1 to PS2 but the real national income decreases from Yf1 to YS2 in the short run.	(2 marks)
When the long run aggregate supply decreases from LRAS1 to LRAS2, the price level increases from P1 to PL2 while the real national income decreases from Yf1 to Yf2 in the long run.	(2 marks)
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
To save money, many Hong Kong people used to go to Shenzhen to shop because the prices of goods in Shenzhen were far cheaper than those in Hong Kong. Because of inflation in the mainland and the appreciation of the renminbi, fewer Hong Kong people shop in Shenzhen while some people from Shenzhen now travel to Hong Kong to shop.
With the aid of a diagram, explain how the above event affects the equilibrium real GDP and price level of Hong Kong in the short run and long run. Describe the adjustment process from the short run to the long run as well.	(13 marks)
questions.answerText:
Because of inflation in the mainland and appreciation of the renminbi, goods in the mainland have become more expensive relative to Hong Kong's goods. Thus, people in the mainland will buy a larger quantity of Hong Kong's exports while Hong Kong people will import a smaller quantity of goods from the mainland. As a result, the real value of Hong Kong's net exports will increase.	(2 marks)
The aggregate demand will increase and the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
In the short run, both the equilibrium real GDP and price level will increase.	(2 marks)
In the long run, as the short run equilibrium real GDP (YS2) is larger than the full employment real GDP (Yf), there is an inflationary gap and an excess demand for inputs. Input prices will rise. The rise in input prices shifts the short run aggregate supply curve upwards (from SRAS1 to SRAS2) until the inflationary gap is closed.
	(3 marks)
As a result, the equilibrium real GDP will be restored to Yf and the equilibrium price level rises from P1 to PL2 in the long run.	(2 marks)
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Determine whether the following items are a demand-side factor or / and a supply-side factor affecting Hong Kong's GDP, and briefly explain how Hong Kong's equilibrium real GDP will change in the short run.
(a)	There is a boom in the US stock market. 	(3 marks)
(b)	Under CEPA (內地與香港關於建立更緊密經貿關係的安排), the mainland of China imposes zero tariffs on Hong Kong's products.	(3 marks)
(c)	Electricity prices for commercial use rises.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Demand-side factor	(1 mark)
As the wealth of people in the US increases, they will spend more on imported goods from Hong Kong. Thus, Hong Kong's real exports will increase and so will Hong Kong's equilibrium real GDP.	(2 marks)
(b)	Demand-side factor	(1 mark)
Due to zero tariffs, the prices of Hong Kong's products in the mainland of China will be lower. Thus, Hong Kong's real exports will increase and so will Hong Kong's equilibrium real GDP.	(2 marks)
(c)	Supply-side factor	(1 mark)
At the same price level, an increase in electricity prices would make firms reduce their outputs. The short run aggregate supply will decrease and so will Hong Kong's equilibrium real GDP.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
(a)	What is an inflationary gap?	(2 marks)
(b)	How will the price level change when there is an inflationary gap? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	An inflationary gap refers to a situation when the short run equilibrium real national income is greater than the full employment real national income.
	(2 marks)
(b)	When there is an inflationary gap (at Point A), an excess demand for inputs occurs. Input prices will rise. The short run aggregate supply curve shifts upwards until the inflationary gap is closed.	(3 marks)
As a result, the price level will increase.	(1 mark)
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: John said, 'Other things being equal, an increase in the output level of an economy must be accompanied by an increase in the factor employment level. Thus, if there is an increase in real national income, the unemployment rate of labour will decrease.' Comment.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Other things being equal, firms need to employ more factors of production in order to raise the output level. Thus, factor employment and output level are positively related. The first statement is correct.	(2 marks)
The second statement is incorrect. If the percentage increase in the quantity of labour available is greater than the percentage increase in the quantity of labour employed, the unemployment rate of labour will increase.	(2 marks)
(Accept other reasonable answer.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: Between 2014 and 2015, the Japanese yen depreciated against major foreign currencies. With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain the short run effects on Japan's economy.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Rightward shift in aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Increases in price level and output level	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
•	As the Japanese yen depreciated, Japan's volume of exports increased and its volume of imports decreased. Hence, Japan's net exports increased.	(1 mark)
•	The aggregate demand increased from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
•	In the short run, the price level increased from P1 to P2 and the output level increased from Y1 to Y2.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Country C and Country G are heavily-industrialised economies which are major consumers of steel in the international market. Country C is suffering from an economic downturn, therefore its demand for steel has decreased sharply.
(a)	Explain how the price of steel will change in the international market.	(2 marks)
(b)	With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain the effects of the change in steel price on the price and output levels of Country G in the short run.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	As Country C's demand for steel decreases, the steel price in the international market decreases.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Rightward shift in short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in price level and increase in output level	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	•	As the steel price (i.e., an input price) decreases, Country G's short run aggregate supply increases from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(1 mark)
	•	In the short run, the price level decreases from P1 to P2 and the output level increases from Y1 to Y2.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Businessmen believe investing in Country H carries more political risks.
With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain how the above event affects Country H's output and price levels in the short run.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Leftward shift in aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in output level and price level	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
•	Businessmen will be less willing to invest in Country H. This lowers its investment expenditure and aggregate demand.	(1 mark)
•	In the short run, Country H's output level and price level will decrease.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: The mainland of China and Macau are close trading partners. Some people believe the mainland will face an economic downturn. Explain, with the aid of a diagram, the short run effect on Macau's output and price levels as a result of an economic downturn in the mainland.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Leftward shift of aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in both output and price levels	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The mainland's economic downturn lowers Macau's net exports,	(1 mark)
and thus Macau's aggregate demand decreases.	(1 mark)
Therefore, Macau's output and price levels decrease in the short run.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: Country Q is a small island country. Due to global warming, 30% of the land in Country Q has been submerged (淹沒). With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain the long run effect of the above event on Country Q's economy.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Leftward shift of long run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in output and increase in price level	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
•	As some of the land is submerged, the amount of natural resources in Country Q decreases.	(1 mark)
•	Therefore, long run aggregate supply decreases.	(1 mark)
•	As a result, output level decreases while the price level increases in the long run.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
To develop its Far East, the Russian government has offered each citizen one hectare of land free of charge, as long as they use the assigned land. The plan has attracted some residents of the United Kingdom and China into migrating to Russia.
With the aid of a diagram, explain the long run effect of the land-offer scheme on Russia's aggregate output.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Rightward shift of aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Rightward shift of vertical long run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in aggregate output	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The land-offer scheme stimulates investment in Russia's Far East.	(1 mark)
Gross investment expenditure, and thus aggregate demand, increase.	(1 mark)
The development of Russia's Far East and immigration of foreign residents increase the quantity of factor endowment.	(1 mark)
Long run aggregate supply increases.	(1 mark)
Output level increases in the long run.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text: Country A faces the problem of unemployment. People suggest that the government should adopt protectionist policies on imported goods to solve the problem. Explain how this policy may work, using an AS-AD diagram.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Original unemployment at short run equilibrium (Y1 < Yf)	(1 mark)
•	Rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Increase in output level to Yf	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
Protectionist policies will raise net exports and aggregate demand.	(1 mark)
Output level may increase to the full employment output level, solving the problem of unemployment.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Country K is facing a high risk of terrorist attacks. Businesspeople are pessimistic about the country's business prospects.
(a)	With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain how the risk of terrorist attacks affects Country K's price and output levels in the short run.	(5 marks)
(b)	Suppose Country K's government raises its production subsidies to firms. Using the same diagram in (a), explain whether the measure can offset the effects on the price and output levels you described in (a).	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Leftward shift in aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	•	Decreases in price level and output level	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	•	Investment expenditure decreases due to pessimistic business prospects.
	(1 mark)
	•	Aggregate demand decreases from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
	•	The price level decreases from P1 to P2 and output level decreases from Y1 to Y2.	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Rightward shift in short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in price level and increase in output level	(1 mark)

	Verbal elaboration:
	•	No.	(1 mark)
	•	An increase in production subsidies reduces production costs.	(1 mark)
	•	Short run aggregate supply increases from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(1 mark)
	•	The output level returns to the original level, but the price level further decreases.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Japan is initially at the short run equilibrium at Point E.

(a)	From the diagram above, what economic problem does Japan face? Explain.
	(2 marks)
(b)	The British pound depreciated against the Japanese yen when the United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union. With the aid of the above diagram, explain whether the depreciation of the pound may help Japan return to its long run equilibrium output level.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Unemployment, because	(1 mark)
	there is a deflationary gap / the short run equilibrium output level (Y1) is smaller than the full employment output level (Yf).	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Leftward shift of AD curve	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in output level	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	No.	(1 mark)
	The depreciation of the British pound (i.e., appreciation of Japanese yen) will lower Japan's net exports. Japan's aggregate demand will decrease. So, the output level will decrease further from the potential output (Yf).	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Hong Kong had originally faced a deflationary gap, as shown in the following diagram.

(a)	The Hong Kong government often provides tax rebates for salaries tax as a relief measure. WITHOUT using a diagram, explain how the above tax measure can help Hong Kong reach Yf.	(2 marks)
(b)	Even without the above tax measure, Hong Kong can still reach Yf in the long run. Explain with the aid of the above diagram.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The measure can raise people's disposable income, resulting in an increase in private consumption expenditure and aggregate demand. The short run equilibrium output will increase to Yf.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Downward shift of the short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Increase in aggregate output	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	With the deflationary gap, there is an excess supply of inputs.	(1 mark)
	This will lower input prices. The short run aggregate supply curve will shift downwards, until the aggregate output reaches Yf in the long run.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
The following shows Hong Kong's economic situation.

Many people suffer losses from their investments when there is financial market instability. With reference to the market adjustment mechanism from the short run to the long run equilibrium, explain the long run effect of the above event on Hong Kong's price level, using the above diagram.	(9 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Leftward shift of aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
•	Decrease in price level in the short run	(1 mark)
•	Rightward shift of short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
•	Further decrease in price level to reach long run equilibrium	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
As people suffer losses from their investments, private consumption expenditure decreases, and so does aggregate demand.	(1 mark)
Both price and output levels decrease in the short run.	(1 mark)
The resulting deflationary gap will eventually lower input prices.	(1 mark)
The short run aggregate supply will increase until the deflationary gap is closed.
	(1 mark)
The price level will drop further in the long run.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Economy X is facing an inflationary gap.
(a)	Use an AS-AD diagram to show the current situation of Economy X.	(2 marks)
(b)	With the aid of the diagram in (a), explain how market forces can help eliminate the inflationary gap.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Short run output level (Y1) > Full employment output level (Yf)	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Upward shift in short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in output level to the full employment level	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	•	As there is an inflationary gap (Y1 > Yf), the excess demand for inputs raises input prices.	(1 mark)
	•	Therefore, the costs of production increase.	(1 mark)
	•	The short run aggregate supply decreases from SRAS1 to SRAS2. The inflationary gap is closed and the full employment output level is attained.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Country A is initially at long run equilibrium. Suppose property prices in Country A decrease rapidly.
(a)	With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain the short run effects of the above event.	(5 marks)
(b)	Using the same diagram in (a), explain how the economy adjusts to long run equilibrium under the market mechanism.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Leftward shift in aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	•	Decreases in price level and output level	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	•	The decrease in property prices causes people's wealth to decrease. Consumption expenditure decreases and thus aggregate demand decreases from AD1 to AD2.	(2 marks)
	•	In the short run, the price level decreases from P1 to P2 and the output level decreases from Yf to Y2.	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Rightward shift in short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Further decrease in price level and increase in output level	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	•	Country A faces a deflationary gap. The excess supply of inputs drives down input prices.	(2 marks)
	•	Short run aggregate supply increases from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(1 mark)
	•	In the long run, the price level further decreases to P3 and the output level returns to the full employment output level (Yf).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Between 2015 and 2016, Brazil's economy was badly hit by the Zika virus (寨卡病毒). Unemployment rate was high. In August 2016, Brazil hosted the Olympic Games. Visitors from around the world went to Brazil to watch the games.
(a)	With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain how the Olympic Games could have relieved unemployment in Brazil in 2016.	(6 marks)

(b)	Without using a diagram, explain how market forces could restore the output level to long run equilibrium even if Brazil did not host the Olympic Games.
	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Short run output level (Y1) < Full employment output level (Yf)	(1 mark)
	•	Rightward shift in aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	•	Increase in output level	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	•	More visitors travelled to Brazil because of the Olympic Games. Exports of services increased.	(1 mark)
	•	The aggregate demand increased from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
	•	As a result, the output level increased. Hence, unemployment was relieved.		(1 mark)
(b)	A deflationary gap existed when there was unemployment.	(1 mark)
	The excess supply of inputs would cause input prices to decrease.	(1 mark)
	Therefore, the costs of production would decrease.	(1 mark)
	The short run aggregate supply would increase and the output level would be restored to long run equilibrium.	(1 mark)



Structured Questions

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Per capita real GDPs of most countries were relatively stable in human history until the Industrial Revolution (工業革命), after which per capita real GDPs increased dramatically. The Industrial Revolution changed the production method from hand-made to machine-manufactured and created many new business opportunities.
(a)	The Industrial Revolution facilitated specialisation. Briefly explain TWO advantages of specialisation.	(4 marks)
*(b)	Explain, with the aid of TWO separate diagrams, how the Industrial Revolution affected real GDP in the short run and long run, respectively. (Hint: You should consider both demand-side and supply-side factors.)	(12 marks)
(c)	It has been said that many people suffered from a severe reduction in their standard of living during the Industrial Revolution. Give TWO reasons to account for the inability of per capita real GDP to reflect this situation.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The advantages include:
	•	Assigning the right person to do the right job: This can increase productivity.
	•	Practice makes perfect: As workers do the same job repeatedly, their productivity increases.
	•	Saving time in training: As each worker focuses only on a part of the production process, training time for workers can be reduced.
	•	Saving time in shifting from one part of a job to another: Each worker can focus only on one task and does not have to shift from one part of a job to another.
	•	Fewer capital goods are needed in production: As each worker focuses only on one task, workers do not need to use tools for other tasks.
	•	Capital goods are used efficiently: Tools can remain in use all the time by the most appropriate workers.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers. 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram (short run situation):
	•	Rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	•	Rightward shift of the short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Increase in short run equilibrium real GDP	(1 mark)


	Indicate on the diagram (long run situation):
	•	Rightward shift of the aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	•	Rightward shift of the long run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Increase in long run equilibrium real GDP	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
	•	With the introduction of machinery for production, the quality and quantity of factors increased.	(1 mark)
	•	Therefore, both short run and long run aggregate supply increased.	(2 marks)
	•	Since the Industrial Revolution created many new business opportunities, gross investment expenditure increased.	(1 mark)
	•	Therefore, aggregate demand increased.	(1 mark)
	•	As a result, real GDP increased in both the short run (from YS1 to YS2) and the long run (from YL1 to YL2).	(1 mark)


(c)	Per capita real GDP failed to reflect the situation because it does not consider the following factors:
	•	Distribution of output: Although per capita real GDP increased, output distribution during the Industrial Revolution might have been more uneven.
	•	The value of leisure: People might have had to work longer hours during the Industrial Revolution. However, the longer working hours were not reflected in per capita real GDP.
	•	Undesirable effects of production: Workers might have had to work in dangerous working environments. However, this was not reflected in per capita real GDP.
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers. 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
A typhoon destroys several cities in Country A.
(a)	Suppose many buildings and facilities were destroyed. With the aid of a diagram, explain how the typhoon affects Country A's output in the short run.	(5 marks)
(b)	Suppose people invest to rebuild the destroyed cities. With the aid of a diagram, explain how this affects Country A's output in the short run.	(5 marks)
(c)	'From the results of (a) and (b), a typhoon may stimulate the economy.' Justify the statement.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Leftward shift of the short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	•	Decrease in short run equilibrium output	(1 mark)



Verbal elaboration:
	•	As many buildings and facilities were destroyed, the quantity of factors decreases.	(1 mark)
	•	Therefore, short run aggregate supply decreases.	(1 mark)
	•	As a result, output decreases from Y1 to Y2 in the short run.	(1 mark)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:

	•	Increase in short run equilibrium output	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:

	•	As a result, output increases from Y1 to Y2 in the short run.	(1 mark)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Region H is a small and open economy and Country C is its major trading partner. Recently, the income level of Country C has been increasing. Suppose Region H is operating at full employment.
(a)	How will the increase in Country C's income affect Region H's real GDP and price level in the short run? Explain with the aid of a diagram.	(6 marks)
(b)	Cindy, an economist, says, 'The increase in Country C's income will not benefit Region H in the long run.' Support Cindy's claim with the aid of the diagram you drew for part (a).	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	The aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
	•	Real GDP increases (to Y2) in the short run.	(1 mark)
	•	The price level increases (to P2) in the short run.	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
	•	When Country C's income increases, its consumption, including imports from Region H, increases.	(1 mark)
	•	Therefore, Region H's real value of exports increases.	(1 mark)
	•	As a result, Region H's aggregate demand increases, leading to an increase in its real GDP and price level.	(1 mark)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	The short run aggregate supply curve shifts upwards.	(1 mark)
	•	Real GDP reverts to its full employment level (Y1).	(1 mark)
	•	The price level increases (to P3).	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
	•	As the short run equilibrium real GDP is larger than the full employment real GDP, an inflationary gap results. The excess demand for resources will eventually raise input prices.	(2 marks)
	•	Therefore, the short run aggregate supply curve will shift upwards until long run equilibrium is achieved.	(1 mark)
	•	In the long run, the real GDP will go back to the original full employment level (Y1), while the price level will increase to P3.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
A self-fulfilling prophecy (自我實現的預言), a well-known sociological and psychological phenomenon, is a prediction that makes itself come true, due to the feedback between the belief and behaviour of the prophet. In this question, we will investigate whether the self-fulfilling prophecy applies to economic analyses.
(a)	Suppose people expect that there will be an increase in the price level. How does this affect price levels in the short run and the long run? Is the result consistent with a self-fulfilling prophecy? Explain with the aid of TWO diagrams.	(10 marks)
(b)	Suppose people expect that there will be a decrease in real national income. How does this affect real national income in the short run and the long run? Is the result consistent with a self-fulfilling prophecy? Explain with the aid of a diagram.
	(10 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	If people expect the price level to rise, they will consume more before prices increase to save money. Thus, private consumption expenditure increases and so does the aggregate demand. The aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.
		(2 marks)
If firms expect the price level to rise, they will think that it is more profitable to retain their present supply for future sale. Thus, the short run aggregate supply decreases, and the short run aggregate supply curve shifts leftwards.	(2 marks)
In the short run, the price level rises (from P1 to PS2). This is consistent with a self-fulfilling prophecy.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)
In the long run, as there is an increase in aggregate demand, the price level will also rise (from P1 to PL2). This is also consistent with a self-fulfilling prophecy.
	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)


(b)	If people expect that their income will decrease, they will decrease their present consumption and aggregate demand falls. The aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(2 marks)
If firms are pessimistic about economic prospects, they invest less and aggregate demand decreases. The aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(2 marks)
In the short run, real national income decreases (from Yf to YS2). This is consistent with a self-fulfilling prophecy.	(1 mark)
However, the long run aggregate supply is not affected. As a result, real national income remains unchanged in the long run. This is inconsistent with a self-fulfilling prophecy.	(2 marks)
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Consumerism (消費主義) preaches the concept of happiness through consumption. Suppose people desire to save less and consume more due to the promotion of consumerism.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain how this event affects real national income and the general price level in the short run.	(7 marks)
(b)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the adjustment from short run equilibrium to long run equilibrium.	(9 marks)
(c)	From the result in (b) about the change in the general price level, what economic phenomenon can be observed? Define the economic phenomenon.	(3 marks)
(d)	Give ONE reason to support consumerism and ONE reason to oppose it.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	As people consume more, private consumption expenditure increases and so does aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
Thus, the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
In the short run, both real national income and the price level will increase.
	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

(b)	Consumerism would not affect the long run aggregate supply.	(1 mark)
	As the short run equilibrium real national income (YS2) is larger than the full employment real national income (Yf), there is an inflationary gap and an excess demand for inputs. Input prices will rise. The rise in input prices shifts the short run aggregate supply curve upwards (from SRAS1 to SRAS2) until the inflationary gap is closed.	(3 marks)
As a result, real national income is restored to Yf and the price level rises to PL2 in the long run.	(2 marks)
	(3 marks)

(c)	Inflation	(1 mark)
This is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)


(d)	Reason to support:
It can increase real national income in the short run.	(1 mark)
Reason to oppose:
In the long run, it causes inflation / fluctuations in real national income.	(1 mark)
(Accept any other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Study the following diagram about the economic situation of Fishing City.

(a)	What is a business cycle? List the FOUR phases of a business cycle.	(4 marks)
(b)	Identify in which phase of a business cycle Point F is.	(1 mark)
(c)	Determine whether each of the following items is a demand-side factor or supply-side factor affecting GDP. With the aid of a diagram, explain how each can lead to the situation shown in the above diagram and affect the general price level.
(i)	The government raises production subsidies.	(7 marks)
(ii)	The government lowers income taxes.	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Business cycles refer to short run fluctuations in real GDP around the long run trend.	(2 marks)
	The four phases are recession (contraction), trough, recovery (expansion) and peak (prosperity or boom).	(2 marks)

(b)	Recovery / expansion	(1 mark)
(c)	(i)	Supply-side factor	(1 mark)
A rise in production subsidies would reduce production costs. At the same price level, it is profitable for firms to raise their outputs. Hence, the short run aggregate supply curve shifts rightwards.	(2 marks)
As a result, real GDP increases. This helps the economy achieve Point F.
	(1 mark)
The general price level will decrease.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)
(ii)	Demand-side factor	(1 mark)
When the government lowers income taxes, people have more disposable income. At the same price level, the aggregate output demanded rises. Hence, the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(2 marks)
As a result, real GDP increases. This helps the economy achieve Point F.
	(1 mark)
The general price level will increase.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Britain held a referendum on June 23, 2016 on its withdrawal from the European Union (EU). Some economists forecasted that leaving the EU would create uncertainty about Britain's future trading arrangements, both with the rest of Europe and other major economies. Ultimately, 51.9% of the voters opted to leave the EU.
(a)	Suppose the EU imposed trade barriers on British goods after the country leaves the EU. Explain how Britain's total export value (in British pounds) would change after the withdrawal.	(2 marks)
(b)	With the aid of the following diagram, explain the short run and long run effects of Britain's withdrawal from the EU, according to the economists' forecast.		(9 marks)
	
(c)	An economist said that the withdrawal from the EU would lead to a significant depreciation of the British pound. Explain how this would affect Hong Kong tourists' total expenditure on British goods and services in terms of Hong Kong dollars.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Due to the trade barriers, Britain's export volume would decrease. As a result, Britain's total export value (in British pounds) would decrease.	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift in aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Short run: Decreases in price level and output level	(1 mark)
	(	Rightward shift in short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Long run: Further decrease in price level and output level is restored to Yf
	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	Due to the uncertainty of future trading arrangements, firms' investment would decrease.	(1 mark)
	Hence, aggregate demand would decrease from AD to AD'.	(1 mark)
	In the short run, the price level would decrease from P1 to P2 and the output level would decrease from Yf to Y2.	(1 mark)
	As the output level is lower than the full employment output level, the excess supply of inputs would lead to a decrease in input prices. Short run aggregate supply would increase from SRAS to SRAS'.	(1 mark)
	In the long run, the price level would further decrease to P3 but the output level would be restored to Yf.	(1 mark)

(c)	As the British pound depreciates against the Hong Kong dollar, the price of British goods and services in terms of Hong Kong dollars would decrease.	(1 mark)
	Hong Kong tourists' quantity demanded for British goods and services would increase.	(1 mark)
	The change in total expenditure would be uncertain, depending on the price elasticity of Hong Kong tourists' demand for British goods and services.	(1 mark)

questions.text:

(c)	Most departing flights from the Hong Kong International Airport fly over Ma Wan. Residents in Ma Wan are annoyed by the noise from aircrafts flying above the area. Explain how the implementation of the Three-runway System would affect the problem of externality.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:

	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Rightward shift of aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Increases in price level and output level	(1 mark)

	The construction of the third runway increases investment expenditure.	(1 mark)

(c)	The implementation of the Three-runway System will increase the number of flights from Hong Kong International Airport. Noise pollution in Ma Wan will worsen.	(2 marks)

compensation.	(1 mark)

questions.text:
In 2016, the renminbi depreciated against the US dollar.
(a)	Explain how the depreciation of the renminbi would affect the number of mainland visitors to Hong Kong.	(3 marks)
(b)	With reference to your answer in (a) and using the diagram below, explain the short run and long run effects on Hong Kong's price and output levels under the market adjustment mechanism.	(9 marks)
	
(c)	Suppose mainlanders can now travel to more Asian countries with looser visa (簽證) requirements. Explain how this may affect the elasticity of mainlanders' demand for Hong Kong's tourism services.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Under the linked exchange rate system, when the renminbi depreciated against the US dollar, it simultaneously depreciated against the Hong Kong dollar.	(1 mark)
	It became more expensive for mainland visitors to visit Hong Kong.	(1 mark)
	Hence, the number of mainland visitors to Hong Kong would decrease.	(1 mark)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift of aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Short run: Decreases in price level and output level	(1 mark)
	(	Rightward shift of short run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
	(	Long run: Further decrease in price level and increase in output level	(1 mark)


	
	Verbal elaboration:
	As the number of mainland visitors decreased, the aggregate demand decreased from AD to AD'.	(1 mark)
	As a result, the price level decreased from P1 to P2 and the output level decreased from Y1 to Y2 in the short run.	(1 mark)
	The resulting excess supply of inputs would cause input prices to decrease.
	(1 mark)
	In the long run, the short run aggregate supply would increase from SRAS to SRAS'.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch505 · Price elasticity of demand and supply
questions.text:
Carlos Slim, a Mexican billionaire, suggested the following changes in work arrangements.
(	From working five days per week to working three days per week
(	Increase in retirement age to 75
(a)	Explain how above changes in work arrangements will affect labour productivity.
	(2 marks)
(b)	Discuss the overall effect of Slim's proposal on long run aggregate supply.
	(4 marks)
(c)	'Slim's proposal for a three-day work week allows workers to have time to take training courses. This can reduce income inequality.' Do you agree? Why?
	(3 marks)
(d)	Suppose the number of jobs in an economy is fixed. Explain why the unemployment rate may decrease as a result of a three-day working week.
	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Labour productivity will increase	(1 mark)
	because people tend to have more leisure time and become healthier.	(1 mark)

(b)	Uncertain.	(1 mark)
	The decrease in work days per week reduces labour supply, leading to a decrease in the long run aggregate supply.	(1 mark)
	However, the increase in productivity of the working population raises the long run aggregate supply.	(1 mark)
	Increasing the retirement age increases the labour force, leading to an increase in long run aggregate supply.	(1 mark)

(c)	No. Both high-income workers and low-income workers can choose to receive training during their extra leisure time. This could not reduce the income gap by increasing only the income of low-income workers.
	OR
	No. Low-income workers may have to find an additional job to earn enough money to live. As high-income workers receive more training than low-income workers, the income gap may widen instead.
	OR

	(Accept other reasonable answers. 3 marks)

(d)	Unemployment rate = (Unemployed persons / Labour force) × 100%	(1 mark)
	Firms will employ more people under the 3-day working week arrangement.
	(1 mark)

questions.text:
* Study the following table about the income tax system in Lucky Town.

Taxable income ($)	Total tax payment ($)	
Below 1,000	800	
1,000 - 1,999	500	
2,000 - 2,999	100	
Above 3,000	0 - 50
(Determined by a lucky draw 
at the time of payment)	
All people should pay their taxes in person at a specified time.	

Based on the table above, we can conclude that the income tax violates
(1)	the equity principle.
(2)	the certainty principle.
(3)	the convenience principle.
(4)	the economy principle.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(3) and (4) only
C.	(1), (2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
Under the income tax system, the higher the taxable income, the lower the total tax payment. Thus, the income tax system violates the equity principle.
The income tax system violates the certainty principle as the total tax payment (for the taxpayers who have taxable incomes above $3,000) is not certain.
The income tax system violates the convenience principle as the timing and the method of payment are not convenient for taxpayers.
The income tax system violates the economy principle as the government has to incur the unnecessary cost of holding lucky draws. The cost may be even higher than the tax payment (which can be zero).

questions.text:

A.	Direct tax refers to a tax which cannot be paid by a party other than the taxpayer.
B.	Indirect tax is a tax which is paid by the taxpayer indirectly.
C.	Profits tax is an indirect tax as businesspeople can shift part of their profits taxes to consumers by raising prices.
D.	Some indirect taxpayers might not shift their tax burden to another party.
questions.answerText: The tax burden of an indirect tax is determined by the elasticity of demand and the elasticity of supply. For example, when a sales tax is imposed on a good, if the demand is perfectly elastic or the supply is perfectly inelastic, sellers will not shift their tax burden to consumers.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
* Let C, Y and c% be the consumption expenditure on Good X, total income and percentage of consumption expenditure on Good X in total income, respectively. The percentage tax rate on Good X is 5%.
Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
(1)	If all people have the same c%, the tax is a proportional tax.
(2)	If c% increases, C must increase.
(3)	If c% of the higher-income group is smaller than that of the lower-income group, Good X must be an inferior good.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	All of the above
questions.answerText:
Average tax rate =  =  = c% × 5%
Option (1) is a correct statement. If all people have the same c%, they will have the same average tax rate. Thus, the tax is a proportional tax.
Option (2) is an incorrect statement. c% will also increase if Y decreases or the percentage decrease in Y is greater than the percentage decrease in C.
Option (3) is an incorrect statement. The demand for inferior goods will decrease as income increases. Suppose both income groups pay the same price for Good X. Even if c% of the higher-income group is smaller than that of the lower-income group, C (i.e., consumption expenditure on Good X) of the higher-income group may still be greater than that of the lower-income group. This implies that the higher-income group's demand for Good X is greater than the lower-income group's demand for Good X. In this case, Good X cannot be an inferior good.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
* Which pair of economic goals CANNOT be achieved at the same time by adjusting direct taxes?
A.	Stimulating long run economic growth and stabilising the price level
B.	Stabilising the price level and solving the problem of overheating
C.	Stimulating long run economic growth and reducing income inequality
D.	Stabilising the price level and solving the problem of unemployment
questions.answerText:
Option A is not the answer. Suppose there is deflation. The government can stabilise the price level by cutting the salaries tax. At the same time, it can stimulate long run economic growth by reducing the progressivity of the salaries tax. Then, both goals will be achieved.
Option B is not the answer. When there is a problem of overheating, an inflationary gap exists. The government can relieve inflationary pressure and solve the problem of overheating at the same time by raising the salaries tax.
Option C is the answer. To reduce income inequality by adjusting direct taxes, the government can raise the progressivity of direct taxes. However, this will reduce input suppliers' incentive to supply factors of production and cannot stimulate long run economic growth.
Option D is not the answer. When there is unemployment, a deflationary gap exists. The government can stabilise the price level and solve the problem of unemployment at the same time by cutting the salaries tax.

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
(a)	State the FOUR principles of taxation suggested by Adam Smith.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain how the four principles are applied to the salaries tax system in Hong Kong.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Equality principle, certainty principle, convenience principle and economy principle	(2 marks)
(b)	Equality principle -- In Hong Kong, tax rates for salaries tax increase with taxpayers' taxable income.	(2 marks)
Certainty principle -- In Hong Kong, the amount, the due date and the method of salaries tax payment are clearly described in the Notice of Assessment and Demand for Salaries Tax.	(2 marks)
Convenience principle -- In Hong Kong, salaries taxes can be paid in two instalments separated by a quarter of a year. In addition, the government provides different methods by which taxpayers can pay their taxes.	(2 marks)
Economy principle -- In Hong Kong, employers are required to inform the government about the salaries and pensions of their employees. This reduces the government's cost of collecting information on salaries.	(2 marks)
(Accept any other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Study the following table.

Taxable income	Tax payment	Average tax rate	
$10,000	$500		
$20,000	$2,000		
$30,000	$6,000		

(a)	Complete the above table.	(3 marks)
(b)	Explain whether the tax is a progressive tax, proportional tax or regressive tax.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)
Taxable income	Tax payment	Average tax rate	
$10,000	$500	5%	
$20,000	$2,000	10%	
$30,000	$6,000	20%	
	(3 marks)
(b)	The tax is a progressive tax.	(1 mark)
Because the average tax rate increases with taxable income.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Study the following table.

Taxable income	Marginal tax rate	
First $10,000	40%	
Next $10,000	30%	
Next $10,000	20%	
Remainder	10%	

(a)	Based on the table above, draw the corresponding curve in the space provided below.	(2 marks)

(b)	Explain whether the tax agrees with the equity principle of taxation.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)
	(2 marks)
(b)	The tax is a regressive tax.	(1 mark)
