questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
(a)	Give ONE example of a progressive tax and proportional tax in Hong Kong, respectively.	(2 marks)
(b)	In the space provided below, draw THREE curves to illustrate a progressive tax, proportional tax and regressive tax.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Progressive tax: Salaries tax
Proportional tax: General rates, property tax and profits tax
(ONE example for each type of tax. Accept other reasonable answers. 
1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(b)	
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
(a)	What are a direct tax and an indirect tax? Give ONE example in Hong Kong for each type.	(4 marks)
(b)	Explain whether a goods and services tax is
(i)	a direct tax;	(1 mark)
(ii)	a regressive tax.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A direct tax is a tax where the taxpayer cannot shift the tax burden to another party.	(1 mark)
An indirect tax is a tax where the taxpayer can shift the tax burden to another party.	(1 mark)
Examples of direct tax: profits tax, salaries tax and property tax
(ONE of the above, 1 mark)
Examples of indirect tax: stamp duty, bets and sweeps tax, general rates, duties on four dutiable goods, royalties and concessions, motor vehicles first registration tax and air passenger departure tax
(ONE of the above, 1 mark)
(b)	(i)	A goods and services tax is not a direct tax as the taxpayer (e.g., a seller) can shift the tax burden to another party (e.g., customers).	(1 mark)
(ii)	A goods and services tax is levied on most goods and services. The higher income group spends a smaller proportion of its total income on the consumption of most goods and services than the lower income group. Thus, the higher income group has a smaller proportion of its income taxed under a goods and services tax. The tax rate for the higher income group is lower than that for the lower income group. Thus, a goods and services tax is a regressive tax.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
The Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) (買家印花稅) was introduced to combat the overheated property market in Hong Kong. An extra stamp duty of 15% is charged for residential property acquired by any person (including an incorporated company) except a Hong Kong permanent resident.
(a)	Explain whether the BSD is a direct tax or an indirect tax.	(3 marks)
(b)	With the aid of a diagram, briefly explain how the introduction of the BSD will affect the commercial property market.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	It is an indirect tax.	(1 mark)
•	Buyers of residential property can shift the tax burden by bargaining for a lower price. 	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
•	Both the price and quantity transacted increase.	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
•	Commercial property and residential property are close substitutes.	(1 mark)
•	After the introduction of the BSD, the prices of residential property for foreign investors increase. This will lead to the increase in the demand for commercial property.	(2 marks)
•	As a result, both the price and quantity transacted of commercial property increase.	(1 mark)
(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: Explain why the Hong Kong government usually has more revenue from salaries tax during inflation.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
During inflation, people's nominal salaries will most likely increase. If the tax allowances of the salaries tax remain unchanged, a larger proportion of nominal income exceeds the tax allowances and becomes taxable.	(2 marks)
If the salaries tax rates remain unchanged, the larger taxable income means more tax revenue.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
(a)	What is fiscal policy?	(1 mark)
(b)	Give TWO examples of fiscal policy tools.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Fiscal policy is a government measure aimed at achieving certain economic goals by adjusting government revenue and/or government expenditure.	(1 mark)
(b)	Any two items in government revenue (e.g., income taxes) or government expenditure (e.g., government consumption expenditure)	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: Country X's government would like to stimulate economic growth by cutting general sales taxes. With the aid of diagrams, briefly explain whether the policy works in the short run.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
When the government cuts general sales taxes, the short run aggregate supply curve shifts downwards from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(2 marks)
The output level rises in the short run. The policy works.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
(a)	What is an inflationary gap?	(2 marks)
(b)	With the aid of a diagram, briefly explain how a government closes the gap by raising the salaries tax.	(5 marks)
(c)	With the aid of a diagram, briefly explain how a market adjustment mechanism closes the gap.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	An inflationary gap refers to a situation when the short run equilibrium output level is larger than the full employment output level.	(2 marks)
(b)	If the government raises the salaries tax, people will have less disposable income. Thus, private consumption expenditure will decrease and so will aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
The aggregate demand curve will shift leftwards from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
As a result, the inflationary gap is closed.
	(2 marks)
(c)	When there is an inflationary gap, there is an excess demand for inputs.	(1 mark)
The excess demand for inputs raises input prices. The short run aggregate supply curve shifts upwards until the inflationary gap is closed.	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Suppose an economy faces the problem of overheating. With the aid of a diagram, explain how the government can solve the problem by adjusting profits taxes.
	(7 marks)
questions.answerText:
As the economy faces the problem of overheating, an inflationary gap exists, i.e., the equilibrium output level is greater than the full employment output level.	(2 marks)
If the government raises profits taxes, it is less profitable for firms to invest. Gross investment expenditure will decrease and so will aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
The aggregate demand curve will shift leftwards from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
As a result, the inflationary gap is closed and so the problem is solved.
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: Suppose there is demand-pull inflation. With the aid of a diagram, explain why cutting the general sales tax may solve the problem in the short run but leave the problem unsolved in the long run.	(10 marks)
questions.answerText:
Demand-pull inflation is a problem of inflation caused by a continuous increase in aggregate demand.	(1 mark)
Suppose the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards from AD1 to AD2 and the short run equilibrium price level and output level become P1 and Y1, respectively. 
If the government cuts the general sales tax, production costs of firms will decrease. Hence, the short run aggregate supply curve shifts downwards from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(2 marks)
In the short run, the price level will decrease from P1 to P2.	(1 mark)
In the long run, as there is an inflationary gap, the excess demand for inputs will raise input prices. The short run aggregate supply curve shifts upwards until the inflationary gap is closed.	(2 marks)
The price level will increase from P2 to P3. Thus, cutting the general sales tax cannot solve the problem in the long run.	(1 mark)
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: Suppose there is cost-push inflation. With the aid of a diagram, explain why raising the salaries tax may solve the problem in the short run but lead to deflation in the long run.	(10 marks)
questions.answerText:
Cost-push inflation is a problem of inflation caused by a continuous decrease in short run aggregate supply.	(1 mark)
Suppose the short run aggregate supply curve shifts upwards from SRAS1 to SRAS2 and the short run equilibrium price level and output level become P1 and Y1, respectively.
If the government raises the salaries tax, people's disposable income will decrease. Hence, the aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards from AD1 to AD2.	(2 marks)
In the short run, the price level will decrease from P1 to P2.	(1 mark)
In the long run, as there is a deflationary gap, the excess supply of inputs will lower input prices. The short run aggregate supply curve shifts downwards until the deflationary gap is closed.	(2 marks)
The price level will decrease from P2 to P3. Thus, raising the salaries tax may lead to the problem of deflation in the long run.	(1 mark)
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: * Sunset City faces a problem of unemployment. To solve this problem, the government decides to adjust either general sales taxes or transfer payments. With the aid of TWO separate diagrams, explain which measures should be chosen if the city also suffers from inflation.	(14 marks)
questions.answerText:
The government can solve the problem of unemployment by cutting general sales taxes or raising transfer payments.	(1 mark)
If the government chooses to cut general sales taxes, production costs will decrease. Hence, the short run aggregate supply curve shifts downwards from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(2 marks)
Both the output level and the employment level rise.	(1 mark)
The price level will decrease.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)
If the government chooses to raise transfer payments, people's disposable income will increase. At the same price level, private consumption expenditure increases. Hence, the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards from AD1 to AD2.	(2 marks)
Both the output level and the employment level rise.	(1 mark)
The price level will also increase.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)
The government should choose to cut general sales taxes as this can relieve inflationary pressure at the same time.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Animal Farm (AF) has a presidential election. There are three candidates: Sheep, Wolf and Pig.
(a)	Explain whether the following should be counted in AF's GDP.
(i)	Salary paid by AF's government to count votes	(2 marks)
(ii)	Lunch fees paid by Wolf to bribe the voters	(2 marks)
(iii)	Cash given by Pig to bribe the voters	(2 marks)
(b)	AF faces a serious problem of unemployment. Sheep promises that he will solve the problem by cutting the profits tax if he wins the election. Explain with the aid of a diagram how Sheep's proposal will work.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	It should be counted	(1 mark)
	because the salary is paid by the government, which is AF's resident producing unit.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	It should be counted	(1 mark)
	because it is the amount spent on the current production of a resident producing unit.	(1 mark)
	(iii)	It should not be counted	(1 mark)
	because it is just a transfer of money, which involves no production.	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Original short run equilibrium real GDP which is smaller than full employment real GDP / Deflationary gap	(1 mark)
•	Aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
•	Real GDP increases to its full employment level.	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
•	As the economy faces a serious problem of unemployment, its real GDP is smaller than the full employment level / there is a deflationary gap.	(1 mark)
•	After cutting the profits tax, it is more profitable for firms to invest. Thus, gross investment expenditure increases and the aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards. The problem of unemployment will be solved.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Study the following news report about Rich City.

(a)	What is the Gini coefficient? Based on the Gini coefficient, explain whether income distribution in the city is fair.	(3 marks)
(b)	Suppose the government wants to relieve the problem of income inequality and stimulate long run economic growth.
Explain briefly why the measure suggested by the news report CANNOT help the government achieve both goals at the same time.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The Gini coefficient is the ratio of the area between the 45-degree line and the Lorenz curve to the total area below the 45-degree line.	(2 marks)
The Gini coefficient can be used to measure the degree of income inequality but it cannot tell us whether income distribution is fair or not.	(1 mark)
(b)	If the government raises the progressivity of the salaries tax, the income gap between the rich and the poor will be narrowed. Thus, this measure can reduce income inequality.	(1 mark)
However, this measure will lower the input suppliers' incentive to provide inputs. Thus, long run aggregate supply will decrease and so will the potential real GDP. As a result, this measure cannot stimulate long run economic growth.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
'In the long run, real national income will be restored to its long run equilibrium level. Thus, the government cannot stimulate long run economic growth by a fiscal policy.'
Do you agree? Briefly explain your answer with ONE example.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
No. The government can stimulate long run economic growth by implementing a fiscal policy which can increase the quantity of factors, the quality of factors or productivity.	(2 marks)
Examples:
•	Providing education subsidies
•	Provision of tax relief to encourage investment
•	Reducing the progressivity of direct taxes
•	Cutting indirect taxes on producer goods
(Any ONE of the above or other relevant tool of fiscal policy with brief explanation, 
2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
In King Kong City, land sales are the only source of government revenue. The source of government revenue has been criticised as being too narrow. To deal with this problem, the government is considering whether to introduce a general sales tax or a salaries tax.
(a)	What are a direct and an indirect tax? Determine whether the above taxes are a direct tax or an indirect tax.	(3 marks)
(b)	Which of the above taxes more likely satisfies the equality principle of taxation suggested by Adam Smith? Explain.	(3 marks)
(c)	In the end, the government chooses to introduce a general sales tax. Briefly explain how this measure will affect real national income in the short run.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A direct tax is a tax where the taxpayer cannot shift the tax burden to another party.	(1 mark)
An indirect tax is a tax where the taxpayer cannot shift the tax burden to another party.	(1 mark)
Salaries tax is a direct tax while a general sales tax is an indirect tax.	(1 mark)
(b)	Salaries tax.	(1 mark)
This is because salaries tax is usually proportional or progressive while a general sales tax is usually regressive.	(2 marks)
(c)	The introduction of a general sales tax will lead to a decrease in the short run aggregate supply. Real national income will decrease in the short run.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: In Country A, the government increases its consumption expenditure and income taxes at the same time. The rise in government expenditure is exactly the same as the increase in tax revenue. With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain how this would affect the real national income and price level in the short run.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
•	Aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
•	Both the real national income and price level increase.	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
•	As the expansionary effect of increasing government consumption expenditure is greater than the contractionary effect of raising income taxes, aggregate demand increases.	(2 marks)
•	As a result, both real national income and the price level increase in the short run.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
(a)	What is a budget?	(2 marks)
(b)	What is a balanced budget?	(1 mark)
(c)	'The overall effect of a balanced budget is neutral.'
Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A budget is a financial statement of a government's estimated revenue and expenditure in a financial or fiscal year.	(2 marks)
(b)	A balanced budget refers to a budget in which estimated government revenue is equal to estimated government expenditure.	(1 mark)
(c)	No.	(1 mark)
As the expansionary effect of government expenditure is greater than the contractionary effect of the same amount of government revenue, the overall effect of a balanced budget is expansionary.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
(a)	What is a budget?	(2 marks)
(b)	How can we measure the size of a government?	(2 marks)
(c)	Briefly explain the overall effect of a surplus budget.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A budget is a financial statement of a government's estimated revenue and expenditure in a financial or fiscal year.	(2 marks)
(b)	The size of a government can be measured by:
Public expenditure ÷ GDP × 100%	(2 marks)
(c)	In a surplus budget, estimated government revenue is greater than estimated government expenditure.	(1 mark)
As the expansionary effect of government expenditure is greater the contractionary effect of the same amount of government revenue, the overall effect of a surplus budget can be expansionary, neutral or contractionary.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Tiger Country has a large fiscal deficit. The government considers introducing either a goods and services tax or a profits tax.
(a)	What is a fiscal deficit? Must it be equal to a budget deficit?	(3 marks)
(b)	Is a goods and services tax a direct tax? How about the profits tax? Explain.
	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A fiscal deficit is the difference between actual government revenue and actual government expenditure when the former is smaller than the latter.	(1 mark)
A budget deficit is the difference between estimated government revenue and estimated government expenditure when the former is smaller than the latter.
	(1 mark)
A fiscal deficit is an actual figure while a budget deficit is an estimated figure. Thus, they may not be the same.	(1 mark)
(b)	A goods and services tax is not a direct tax as the taxpayers of this tax can shift their tax burden to another party.	(2 marks)
A profits tax is a direct tax as the taxpayers of this tax cannot shift their tax burden to another party.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Suppose the Hong Kong government raises the profits tax rate.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the effects on Hong Kong's price and output levels in the short run.	(5 marks)
(b)	With reference to your answer in (a), explain whether the rise in profits tax rate will necessarily improve the fiscal balance.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
•	Output level and price level decrease.	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The rise in profits tax rate lowers firms' after tax profits.	(1 mark)
Gross investment expenditure and thus aggregate demand decrease.	(1 mark)
The price level decreases from P1 to P2 and the output level decreases from Y1 to Y2 in the short run.	(1 mark)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
	Although the tax rate increases, national income decreases. This will result in a decrease in firms' profits. If the increase in the tax rate is smaller than the percentage decrease in profits, government tax revenue will decrease. Therefore, the fiscal balance may not improve.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Suppose the government reduces the standard tax rate for the salaries tax.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the effects on price and output levels in the short run.	(6 marks)
(b)	Explain how income distribution will change.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
•	Both price and output levels increase.	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
People's disposable income increases when the standard tax rate decreases.
	(1 mark)
Private consumption expenditure increases.	(1 mark)
Aggregate demand increases from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
Therefore, the price level increases from P1 to P2 and the output level increases from Y1 to Y2 in the short run.	(1 mark)
(b)	Income distribution will become more uneven.	(1 mark)
	This is because the post-tax income of the high-income group will increase while that of the low-income group will remain unchanged.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: An economist proposed that the government increase the salaries tax for the rich and spend all the extra tax revenue on education and medical services. Discuss the effect on the aggregate output in the short run.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Aggregate output will increase.	(1 mark)
Increasing the salaries tax will lower private consumption expenditure, resulting in a decrease in aggregate demand. However, an increase in expenditures on education and medical services will raise government consumption expenditure, and thus aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
The expansionary effect of the increase in government expenditure is greater than the contractionary effect of the decrease in private consumption expenditure because households seldom spend all of their disposable income.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Suppose the government lowers the maximum income limit for applying for low income cash assistance.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the effect of the policy change on price and output levels in the short run.	(5 marks)
(b)	Discuss the effect on income inequality.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
	(	Price and output levels decrease in the short run.	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	Lowering the maximum income limit means fewer people can get the cash assistance. The income of affected people decreases. This lowers private consumption expenditure and thus aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
	Price and output levels decrease in the short run.	(1 mark)
(b)	The policy change worsens income inequality. Some people become ineligible for the cash assistance. The income of the lower income group decreases.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Singapore provides an infant and child care subsidy to parents. Working parents of children aged from 2 months to 7 years old pay less to use child care services under the subsidy.
(a)	With the aid of a diagram, explain the effects of the infant and child care subsidy on output and price levels in the short run.	(5 marks)
(b)	Discuss the possible effect of the subsidy on the output level in the long run.
	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
•	Output level and price level increase.	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
The subsidy raises working parents' disposable income.	(1 mark)
Their consumption expenditure and thus aggregate demand increase.	(1 mark)
The price level increases from P1 to P2 and the output level increases from Y1 to Y2 in the short run.	(1 mark)
(b)	The subsidy may encourage more parents to enter the labour market / may result in an increase in the birth rate.	(1 mark)
	Therefore, the size of the labour force grows.	(1 mark)
	Long run aggregate supply increases and so does the output level.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: The Japanese government has announced a series of measures to stimulate the economy. To deal with the increase in government expenditure, the government may increase the sales tax rate from 8% to 10%. State TWO undesirable effects of raising the sales tax rate.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(	Raising the sales tax will increase production costs. The short run aggregate supply decreases, resulting in a decrease in output level and an increase in the price level.
(	The unemployment problem worsens due to a decrease in the output level.
(	Income distribution will become less even because the sales tax is regressive.
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers. 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: During an economic downturn, a politician suggests that the government lower the salaries of government officials, legislative council members, and civil servants. Explain whether a decrease in salaries can help the economy return to the full employment output level.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Lowering their salaries will lower their disposable income.	(1 mark)
Private consumption expenditure decreases.	(1 mark)
Aggregate demand decreases.	(1 mark)
Aggregate output decreases further from the full employment output level.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
In February 2016, the unemployment rate among those aged 15 to 29 was 12.5% in Korea. Suppose the government encourages unemployed youths to go back to school by providing subsidies.
(a)	Explain how the unemployment rate among youths will be affected.	(3 marks)
(b)	Discuss the effect of the above measure on the long run aggregate output.
	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When some of the unemployed go back to school, both the labour force and unemployed persons will decrease by the same amount.	(1 mark)
	The unemployment rate will decrease because the percentage decrease in unemployed persons will be larger than the percentage decrease in the labour force.	(2 marks)
(b)	As government expenditure on education increases, human capital will improve.
	(1 mark)
	Long run aggregate supply will increase.	(1 mark)
	Hence, aggregate output will increase in the long run.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: The government of Country T has faced a serious fiscal deficit for years. The government decides to reduce unemployment benefits by half to relieve the problem. With the aid of a diagram, explain the effects of the policy on the price level and output level in the long run.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
Indicate on the diagram:
(	Leftward shift in aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
(	Vertical long run aggregate supply curve	(1 mark)
(	Decrease in price level	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
When unemployment benefits decrease, people's disposable income decreases.
	(1 mark)
Private consumption expenditure decreases.	(1 mark)
Hence, aggregate demand decreases from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
In the long run, the price level decreases from P1 to P2 while the output level remains unchanged at Yf.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
* In June 2016, a basic income referendum (公投) was held in Switzerland. The proposal called for giving every citizen a basic income per month (2,500 Swiss francs for every adult and 625 for every child). Evaluate the effects of the proposal on Switzerland's short run output level, long run output level and Gini coefficient.
	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
Short run output level:
(	As citizens' disposable income increases, aggregate demand would increase. Hence, output level would increase in the short run.	(2 marks)
Long run output level:
(	The basic income would create disincentive effects. Some people may quit their jobs. The labour force would decrease. The long run aggregate supply would decrease. Hence, the long run output level would decrease.
(	As children would be included in the basic income, parents would be encouraged to have more children. The population and the labour force would increase in the long run. The long run aggregate supply would increase. Hence, the long run output level would increase.
(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answer. 2 marks)
Gini coefficient:
(	Due to the basic income, the percentage increase in income of the low-income group would be higher than that of the high-income group. Therefore, the income gap between the low-income group and the high-income group would be smaller. The Gini coefficient would decrease.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Country G is initially operating at long run equilibrium. Country G relies heavily on imported natural gas. Suppose the import price of natural gas has sharply increased recently.
(a)	With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain the short run effect of the above event on Country G's price level and output level.	(6 marks)
(b)	After the increase in the price of natural gas, Country G's government decides to grant firms a tax refund. With the aid of the same diagram, explain how the tax refund can help restore the country to long run equilibrium.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Correct position of initial long run aggregate output (Yf)	(1 mark)
	•	Short run aggregate supply curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
	•	Price level increases and output level decreases.	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	When the price of natural gas increases, the input price increases.	(1 mark)
	Hence, short run aggregate supply decreases from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(1 mark)
	As a result, the price level increases from P1 to P2 and the output level decreases from Yf to Y1 in the short run.	(1 mark)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
	•	Output level increases to Yf.	(1 mark)
	Verbal elaboration:
	As firms receive the tax refund, investment expenditure increases.	(1 mark)
	Hence, aggregate demand increases from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
	Output level increases from Y2 back to the full employment level (Yf).	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
In 2016, the Financial Secretary announced that an extra allowance would be provided to social security recipients.
(a)	Explain the effect of the measure on income inequality.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose Point E is Hong Kong's initial equilibrium.
	
	With the aid of the above diagram, explain how the measure can adjust the employment level to long run equilibrium.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The measure helps reduce income inequality. It equalises income as the allowance is provided to the low-income group only.	(2 marks)
(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
	(	Aggregate output increases.	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	The measure raises people's disposable income.	(1 mark)
	This raises private consumption expenditure and thus aggregate demand.	(1 mark)
	Aggregate output increases, implying a higher employment level.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
A government considers spending a certain amount of its fiscal reserves on either one of the following proposals:
Proposal 1: Providing a subsidy to low-income elderly people
Proposal 2: Building a railway that connects with its trading partner
Evaluate the two proposals in terms of their effects on income inequality and long run aggregate output.	(8 marks)
questions.answerText:
Proposal 1:
•	The subsidy for low-income elderly people raises their income while the income of the high-income group remains unchanged. This can narrow the income gap between the rich and the poor.	(2 marks)
•	The subsidy does not affect long run aggregate supply. Therefore, long run aggregate output is unaffected.	(2 marks)
Proposal 2:
•	The railway construction can create more employment opportunities for the unemployed. This can narrow the income gap.	(2 marks)
•	The completion of the railway raises the economy's production capacity, leading to an increase in the long run aggregate supply and aggregate output.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text: Country A is facing enormous national debts. A legislator in Country A suggests that the government should decrease government expenditure on education in order to reduce the fiscal deficit in the long run. Evaluate his proposal.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Decreasing government expenditure (G) on education will decrease national income (Y) in the long run.	(2 marks)
(	If the decrease in tax revenue (due to the decrease in Y) is smaller than the decrease in G, the fiscal deficit will decrease. The policy will be effective.
	(2 marks)
OR
(	If the decrease in tax revenue (due to the decrease in Y) is larger than the decrease in G, the fiscal deficit will increase. The policy will be ineffective.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
A government devalues its currency against foreign currencies to stimulate the economy. This results in criticism from foreign economies.
(a)	Explain ONE possible undesirable effect of the currency devaluation on foreign economies.	(2 marks)
(b)	A politician stated, 'Using an expansionary fiscal policy instead of currency devaluation will worsen the fiscal balance.' Explain why the statement is NOT necessarily correct.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	This will lower the volume of exports of foreign economies, resulting in a drop in aggregate demand and national income.	(2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)
(b)	Increasing government consumption expenditure and tax revenue by the same amount will not worsen the fiscal balance. However, the effect is expansionary because households seldom spend all of their disposable income.	(3 marks)


Structured Questions

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
In August 2011, the US Congress passed the Budget Control Act of 2011 in order to cut the budget deficit. According to the Act, the US government needed to cut its defense and domestic spending greatly in 2013. In addition, some direct tax relief expired at the same time so that the government needed to increase taxes. This situation is known as a 'fiscal cliff' (財政懸崖).
(a)	What is a direct tax? Give ONE example of a direct tax in Hong Kong.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain how the following events under the 'fiscal cliff' would affect income inequality in the US.
(i)	The cut in unemployment benefits	(2 marks)
(ii)	The expiration of the Child Tax Credit which reduces the tax liability for families making less than US$130,000	(2 marks)
(c)	Suppose the US failed to jump over the 'fiscal cliff'. With the aid of a diagram, explain how this would affect the US's real national income and price level in the short run and long run.	(9 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A direct tax is a tax where the taxpayer cannot shift the tax burden to another party.	(1 mark)
Examples of a direct tax in Hong Kong: Profits tax, salaries tax and property tax
(Either one)	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	Unemployment benefits are a transfer payment for the poor. A cut in unemployment benefits would worsen income inequality in the US.	(2 marks)
(ii)	As the tax liability of the poor increases, income inequality would worsen.
	(2 marks)

(c)	Indicate on the diagram:
	•	Aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
	•	Short run situation: Both the real national income and price level decrease.
	(1 mark)
	•	Short run aggregate supply curve shifts downwards.	(1 mark)
	•	Long run situation: The real national income returns to Yf and the price level decreases further to P3.	(1 mark)

Verbal elaboration:
	•	The increase in taxes and decrease in government spending would decrease the US's aggregate demand.	(1 mark)
	•	In the short run, both real national income and the price level would decrease.	(1 mark)
	•	As the short run equilibrium real national income was smaller than its full employment level, there was a deflationary gap / an excess supply of resources.	(1 mark)
•	This would lead to a decrease in short run aggregate supply.	(1 mark)
•	As a result, real national income returns to Yf and the price level decreases further to P3.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Country X has experienced a serious problem of unemployment. Its government plans to build the tallest hotel in the world to stimulate the economy. However, the hotel was abandoned before the construction work was completed. The hotel is neither usable nor being demolished.
(a)	The president said, 'Although the hotel has been abandoned, its construction helped us solve the problem of unemployment.' With the aid of a diagram, explain why this statement is correct.	(7 marks)
(b)	Suppose the government can choose to complete the hotel or build offices on the land where the hotel is located. Explain whether the following would affect the cost of completing the hotel.
	(i)	Office rental values increase.	(3 marks)
	(ii)	The unfinished building has started to deteriorate, doubling the expected time to complete the hotel.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
•	Original short run equilibrium real GDP which is smaller than full employment real GDP / Deflationary gap	(1 mark)
•	Aggregate demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
•	Real GDP increases to its full employment level.	(1 mark)


Verbal elaboration:
•	As the economy faced a serious problem of unemployment, its real GDP was smaller than the full employment level / there was a deflationary gap.	(1 mark)
	•	The construction of the hotel has increased gross investment expenditure.
	(1 mark)
•	Therefore, Country X's aggregate demand has increased.	(1 mark)
•	Country X's real national income has increased and the problem of unemployment has been solved.	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	•	If the government chooses to complete the hotel, it cannot build offices on the site. Thus, the value of building offices is the cost of completing the hotel.	(2 marks)
•	The increase in office rental values increases the value of building offices and the cost of completing the hotel.	(1 mark)
(ii)	•	As the expected length of time to complete the hotel increases, the money cost (e.g., wage payments) and time cost (e.g., the rental income from the land) involved increase.	(2 marks)
•	As a result, the cost of completing the hotel rises.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
With the aid of diagrams, explain whether the overall effect of each set of the following fiscal policies is expansionary in the short run.
(a)	The government raises the monthly old age allowance by $500 and waives the hotel accommodation tax.	(10 marks)
(b)	The government raises the salaries tax and uses the additional tax revenue to finance its expenditure on new production subsidies.	(10 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The increase in the old age allowance will increase the disposable income of old people. Thus, private consumption expenditure will increase and so will aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
The aggregate demand curve will shift rightwards from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
Waiving the hotel accommodation tax will lower the costs of providing hotel services. Firms will provide more hotel services.	(2 marks)
The short run aggregate supply curve will shift downwards from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(1 mark)
As a result, real national income will increase from Y1 to Y2. This implies that the overall effect is expansionary in the short run.	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

(b)	When the government raises the salaries tax, people will have less disposable income. Private consumption expenditure will decrease and so will aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
The aggregate demand curve will shift leftwards from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
When the government provides more production subsidies, firms' production costs will decrease. Firms will increase their outputs and so the short run aggregate supply will rise.	(2 marks)
The short run aggregate supply curve will shift downwards from SRAS1 to SRAS2.	(1 mark)
The change in real national income is uncertain. Therefore, we cannot conclude whether the overall effect is expansionary in the short run.	(2 marks)


(Diagram showing either ONE of the possible cases. 2 marks)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Refer to the following diagram about the economic situation in Material Country.

Suppose the initial long run equilibrium is at Point F. In order to win the next presidential election, President Herbert raises transfer payments substantially.
(a)	Explain how the measure will affect real national income in the short run and how the economy achieves long run equilibrium. Show the changes in the AD curve and/or SRAS curve in the diagram above and label the new long run equilibrium point as 'G'.	(10 marks)
(b)	Suppose the country is at Point G now. Herbert loses his position. New president Old Bema also raises transfer payments.
(i)	Show the new long run equilibrium in the diagram drawn in (a) and label the new long run equilibrium point as 'H'. [Remark: No need to repeat your explanations in (a).]	(2 marks)
(ii)	What economic phenomenon can we observe from the change in the price level? Define the phenomenon.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	When the government raises transfer payments, people's disposable income will increase. Private consumption expenditure will increase. Thus, aggregate demand will increase.	(2 marks)
The aggregate demand curve will shift rightwards from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
In the short run, real national income will increase from Y1 to Y2.	(1 mark)
In the long run, as there is an inflationary gap, there is excess demand for inputs. Excess demand for inputs will raise input prices. Thus, the short run aggregate supply curve will shift upwards until the inflationary gap is closed.	(2 marks)
Real national income will be restored to its full employment level (Y1).	(1 mark)
	(3 marks)

(b)	(i)

(1 mark for label 'H', 0.5 marks for AD3 and 0.5 marks for SRAS3.)
(ii)	Inflation as the price level increases continuously.	(1 mark)
Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Donald, a candidate for president of Country U, suggests cutting corporate profits tax by 20% and personal income tax by 6%. He thinks this can improve the country's economy and attract other corporations to invest in the country.
(a)	Discuss the effects of cutting taxes on Country U's output level
	(i)	in the short run, and	(3 marks)
	(ii)	in the long run, respectively.	(3 marks)
(b)	Explain why the cut in the income tax rate may NOT necessarily reduce government tax revenue.	(4 marks)
(c)	Explain how Country U's Gini coefficient may be affected by the cut in personal income tax.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	Cutting taxes leads to an increase in consumption and investment expenditures.
	(1 mark)
		Aggregate demand increases.	(1 mark)
		As a result, Country U's output level increases in the short run.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Cutting corporate profits tax raises firms' incentive to invest and increase capital stock.	(1 mark)
		Long run aggregate supply will increase.	(1 mark)
		Hence, Country U's output level will increase in the long run.	(1 mark)

(b)	The cut in the tax rate leads to an increase in the output level. Hence, total taxable income will increase.	(2 marks)
	Tax revenue may increase if the effect of the increase in total taxable income outweighs the effect of the decrease in the tax rate.	(2 marks)

(c)	The high income group pays more income taxes. Therefore, the high income group benefits more from the cut in personal income tax. The income of the high income group will increase more than that of the low income group.	(2 marks)
	The income gap will become larger and the Gini coefficient will increase.
	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
Canada imposes a new property transfer tax on foreigners who buy properties in Vancouver.
(a)	Explain how the new property transfer tax would affect Canada's output and price levels in the short run.	(6 marks)
(b)	'When a mainland investor sells his property in Vancouver to a Canadian, Canada's balance of payments will improve.' Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
(c)	Suppose the Canadian government uses the extra tax revenue to provide rental assistance to low-income working families.
	(i)	Discuss the effect of the rental assistance on income inequality.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Explain ONE possible undesirable effect of the rental assistance on Canada's economy.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Leftward shift of aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Decrease output and price levels	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	The property transfer tax will lower the income of property agencies and other related workers due to a decrease in the quantity transacted of properties.	(1 mark)
	Private consumption expenditure decreases	(1 mark)
	and thus aggregate demand decreases.	(1 mark)
	Both output and price levels decrease in the short run.	(1 mark)

(b)	No.	(1 mark)
	The sale of a property owned by a mainland investor to a Canadian implies a capital outflow for Canada, which worsens Canada's capital and financial account balance, and thus Canada's market balance of payments.	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	The rental assistance helps reduce income inequality because it increases the income of low-income working families while the income of high-income families remains unchanged.	(2 marks)

	(ii)	The rental assistance may discourage people from working longer hours, causing a disincentive effect on labour supply. This may lead to a loss of output.	(2 marks)
		(Accept other reasonable answers.)

questions.topic: B5 · Ch506 · Market intervention (I)
questions.text:
The Shenzhen-Hong Kong stock connect is expected to be launched soon. This raises the prices of Hong Kong's stocks in general.
(a)	Discuss the effect of the above policy on government tax revenue.	(2 marks)
(b)	With the aid of a diagram, explain how the increase in stock prices would affect Hong Kong's price and output levels in the short run.	(5 marks)
(c)	(i)	What is the cost of holding money instead of these stocks?	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Suppose people expect the risk of investing in the stock market to increase. How will the demand for money change? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	As transactions in the stock market increases, government revenue from stamp duty will increase.	(2 marks)

(b)	Indicate on the diagram:
	(	Rightward shift of aggregate demand curve	(1 mark)
	(	Increase in price and output levels	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	As stock prices increase, people's wealth increases.	(1 mark)
	This raises private consumption expenditure, and thus the aggregate demand.
	(1 mark)
	Both the price and output levels increase in the short run.	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	The cost of holding money is the nominal rate of return of holding these stocks.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	The asset demand for money increases.	(1 mark)
		The higher risk of investing in the stock market means less desirable to hold stocks. People can avoid a loss by holding a larger amount of money as a store of wealth.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Which of the following exists in a barter economy?
	(1)	Price
	(2)	Interest
	(3)	Deflation

C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Mr Chin lives in a barter economy. He has produced two swords and wants to exchange his swords for other goods. Which of the following can explain why it is difficult for him to trade with other people?
	(1)	It is too costly for him to set exchange ratios for different trading partners.
	(2)	It is not easy to find a trading partner who wants Mr Chin's swords and at the same time has the goods that Mr Chin wants.
	(3)	The swords produced by Mr Chin differ in quality.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
In a barter economy, buying and selling usually occur at the same time because
A.	a double coincidence of wants is required.
B.	there is no generally accepted medium of exchange.
C.	there is no paper money.
D.	there is no specialisation.

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Refer to the following dialogue between Miss A and Mr B.
Miss A said, 'I have some apples. I'd like to exchange them for your fish.'
Mr B said, 'I don't want any fruit now. I prefer a stone axe instead.'
They would not trade because
A.	Miss A's apples are valueless to Mr B.
B.	apples are not durable.
C.	they do not have money.
D.	they do not have a double coincidence of wants.

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

(1)	Difficult to satisfy a double coincidence of wants

A.	(1) and (4) only
B.	(2) and (3) only

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Nick is a chicken farmer (雞農). He wants to exchange his chickens for other goods he needs. It is difficult for him to achieve this goal because
(1)	chickens are heterogeneous.

A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(2) and (3) only

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
When a barter economy is transformed into a monetary economy, the economy is expected to have

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

	(1)	The use of money in exchange improves living standards.

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about money is correct?

questions.answerText: Option A is incorrect. If salted fish is generally accepted as a medium of exchange, though it does not have all the desirable properties of money, it is money.

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Which of the following statements about money is INCORRECT?
(1)	Legal tender must be money.
(2)	Money must be generally accepted in exchange.
(3)	The face value and intrinsic value of money may not be equal.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only

questions.answerText: Option (1) is an incorrect statement. Legal tender may not be generally accepted by the public on some occasions (e.g., in times of hyperinflation).

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
* Ka Ming said, 'In economics, banknotes must be money but money may not be banknotes.' This statement is
A.	correct. As banknotes do not include other types of money like deposits, money may not be banknotes but banknotes must be money
B.	correct. As banknotes are declared by the government to be money, banknotes must be money.
C.	incorrect. As only banknotes are legal tender, money must be banknotes.
D.	incorrect. Banknotes may not be money as banknotes may not be generally accepted as a medium of exchange during hyperinflation.

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
* Which of the following statements about money is correct?
A.	Without money, there will be no indirect exchange.
B.	Without money, there will be no problem of inflation.
C.	Without money, there will be no future payments.
D.	The types of money must be dictated by the government.
questions.answerText: Option B is correct. If there is no money, the value of goods is expressed in terms of other goods. Thus, the prices of all goods will only be measured in real value, instead of nominal (monetary) value. The problem of inflation will not exist as there is no monetary value.

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
* Which of the following statements about money is correct?
A.	Money raises the cost of exchange because people have to make change.
B.	Inflation occurs when the money supply keeps increasing.
C.	Sufficient money supply is a precondition for exchange.
D.	Only the central bank can issue money.
questions.answerText: Option B is correct. When the money supply increases, the value of money falls, and each unit of money can buy fewer goods. That is, the purchasing power of money will decrease and the price of goods in terms of money will increase. Thus, when the money supply keeps increasing, the general price level will keep increasing and inflation occurs.

questions.text:

	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:

	(	Eggs are not homogeneous. Buyers and sellers may have disputes on exchange ratios because the qualities of different eggs are not the same.

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
(a)	Explain why monetary exchange does NOT require a double coincidence of wants.	(3 marks)
(b)	How does the use of money promote trading activities in an economy?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Money is the medium commonly accepted in exchange in a monetary economy. Buyers who pay with money can exchange money for anything they desire, if they can find sellers with the goods they want. Hence, a double coincidence of wants is not required.	(3 marks)
(b)	The use of money greatly reduces the costs involved in transactions, e.g., the costs of finding a trading partner and determining exchange ratios. This makes trade easier and more profitable.	(2 marks)

	Different shells differ in quality and size. Silver coins are more homogeneous so that disputes over exchange ratios can be avoided.	(2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)
(b)	It is very costly to carry a large amount of silver coins for high-value transactions.	(2 marks)
	(Accept other reasonable answers.)

		As people lose confidence in the legal tender, it is no longer generally accepted as a medium of exchange.	(2 marks)

(c)	(	The use of a medium of exchange can reduce the number of exchange ratios.
	(1 mark)
(	Therefore, the total exchange cost will be lower and the gains from trade will be higher.	(1 mark)

(	Stable in supply: The yield of apples is unstable and so the purchasing power of apples may fluctuate greatly.
(	Durable: Apples decay quickly.
(	Portable: It is inconvenient to carry apples in large transactions.
(	Homogeneous: Apples are not homogeneous.
(Any THREE of the above, 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Suppose some people in a village are willing to use live cattle in exchange for goods.
(a)	Explain whether live cattle are money in this village.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suggest TWO reasons to explain why live cattle are NOT good money.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Uncertain, because we do not know whether live cattle are generally accepted as a medium of exchange in the village.	(2 marks)
(b)	The reasons are:
(	Their supply is unstable: the number of live cattle may change with the weather and the natural environment. This will affect their function as a medium of exchange.
(	They have low divisibility: live cattle will die soon after being cut.
(	They are not portable: it is very inconvenient for people to carry a large number of live cattle during large-value transactions.
(	They are not homogeneous: they do not possess uniform physical characteristics.
	(Any TWO of the above, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
In October 2014, the US Federal Reserve (美國聯邦儲備局) ended the quantitative easing policy (量化寬鬆政策). Many investors decided to convert other currencies into US dollars as their relative prices against the US dollar decreased.
(a)	What function of money of the US dollar was strengthened in the above case? Explain.	(3 marks)
(b)	The US dollar is used in most international transactions. Explain TWO functions that the US dollar performs in international trade.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	As a store of value	(1 mark)
	This is because the value of US dollars in terms of other currencies increased. Investors keep more US dollars as an asset for accumulating wealth or preserving purchasing power.	(2 marks)
(b)	(	As a medium of exchange because the US dollar is exchanged for goods.
	(	As a unit of account because the prices of goods are quoted in US dollars.
	(	As a standard of deferred payment because future payments involved in international trade are set in terms of the US dollar.
	(Explain any TWO of the above, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
In order to shorten the queuing time for public medical services, the government intends to give medical coupons to low-income earners so that they can see private doctors. The beneficiaries can receive free private out-patient services by presenting the coupons. The coupons can be accumulated and have no expiry date.
(a)	Explain why the medical coupons are NOT money.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether the medical coupons can perform the following functions.
(i)	A standard of deferred payments	(2 marks)
(ii)	A store of value	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Because they are not a generally accepted medium of exchange. They can be used to pay for private out-patient services only.	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	No, because future receipts or payments are not expressed in terms of the coupons.	(2 marks)
(ii)	Yes, because the beneficiaries can accumulate the coupons and store their purchasing power.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
(a)	Explain if a gift coupon issued by a department store can perform the same function of being a medium of exchange as money.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain whether a gift coupon is a better store of value than money when there is inflation.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	No. This is because a gift coupon is not accepted as a medium of exchange other than in the department store.	(2 marks)
(b)	(	No. When there is inflation, a gift coupon can be exchanged for fewer goods than before.	(1 mark)
(	Thus, similar to money, the purchasing power of a gift coupon will decrease with inflation.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
(a)	Explain why gold and silver were preferred to bronze coins (銅錢) as a medium of exchange in large transactions in ancient China.	(2 marks)
(b)	Later, gold and silver certificates were invented in China. The holders of those certificates could withdraw a corresponding amount of gold and silver from the goldsmiths (金號).
	However, during wars, people were usually unwilling to accept gold and silver certificates to settle payments. Explain why.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(	Because significantly more bronze coins are required in large transactions.
	(1 mark)
(	Silver and gold are more portable than bronze coins and are better forms of money in this case.	(1 mark)
(b)	(	The value of the certificates depends on the value of the gold and silver into which they can be converted.	(1 mark)
	(	During wars, it is very likely that the issuers of the certificates would be unable to convert them into gold and silver.	(1 mark)
	(	The function of a store of value would be lost and so would their function as a medium of exchange.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
* Electronic money is stored and transferred electronically and does not have a physical form.
Based on the definition of money, use ONE example in Hong Kong to explain why electronic money may be money nowadays.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Money is anything that is generally accepted as a medium of exchange.	(2 marks)
In Hong Kong, electronic money may be money. For example, the electronic money stored on Octopus cards is accepted as a medium of exchange by many shops and public transport providers.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Mr Lo has recently purchased an apartment in Shatin. He has made a down payment (首期) of $487,000 to the property developer.
(a)	Explain the function of money performed by the apartment.	(2 marks)
(b)	Mr Lo used a cheque instead of banknotes to pay the down payment.
	(i)	Explain ONE function of money performed by a cheque in this case.
	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Explain ONE reason why a cheque is preferred to banknotes in this case.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(	As a store of value	(1 mark)
	(	Because it can be sold in future and hence provide purchasing power to the holder in future.	(1 mark)
(b)	(i)	(	As a medium of exchange	(1 mark)
		(	It is accepted by the developer in making the down payment.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	(	Because the down payment involves a large amount, cheques are more portable than banknotes and serve as a better medium of exchange in this case.
(	A cheque can save the cost of counting as a cheque payment can be drawn for the exact amount.
(	The risk of theft is lower when the payment is made by a cheque.
(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answer, 2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
HSBC is a listed company in Hong Kong. It performs some of the functions of a central bank in Hong Kong. However, it is not the central bank of Hong Kong. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is generally regarded as the central bank of Hong Kong.

questions.answerText:

(b)	HSBC is privately-owned while a central bank is government-owned.	(1 mark)
	The main objective of HSBC is profit-maximising while the main objective of a central bank is to serve society.	(1 mark)
(c)	(	Being the government's adviser
	(	Managing official reserves
	(	Being a lender of last resort
	(	Supervising the banking system
	(	Issuing coins and $10 notes
	(	Carrying out monetary policy

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:

questions.text:
(a)	Explain TWO central banking functions performed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.	(4 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Great Oceania is a closed economy ruled by a dictator. Its legal tender is called the Great Dollar (GD). Due to the failure of government policies and serious natural disasters, Great Oceania is extremely poor. 
The dictator believes that printing more money can boost the economy. After the increase in money supply, serious inflation occurs. As a result, most citizens of Great Oceania engage in barter and avoid using GD. 
(a)	What is inflation? State ONE possible effect of inflation in Great Oceania.
	(3 marks)
(b)	Winston said, 'Although GD is the legal tender of Great Oceania, it is no longer money.' Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
(c)	How will people's standard of living change after the failure of GD? Explain your answer.	(3 marks)
(d)	Due to the lack of food, corn has become more valuable in Great Oceania. Now, corn is widely used in transactions. Explain which function of money corn performs in each of the following cases.
	(i)	Instead of spending the corn, Julia saves up the corn she has for future transactions.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	O'Brien promises to give Winston 5 kg of corn after he finds out who is spreading rumours against the dictator.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Inflation is the phenomenon of a persistent increase in the general price level.
	(2 marks)
Possible effects of inflation on Great Oceania:
(	Income is redistributed.
(	The cost of living rises and the purchasing power of money drops.
(	The standard of living may fall.
(	Resources are reallocated.
(	The volume of exports drops while the volume of imports rises.
(Any ONE of the above, 1 mark)

(b)	Yes.	(1 mark)
	Money is anything that is generally accepted in an economy as a medium of exchange. As GD is no longer generally accepted in transactions, it is no longer money.	(2 marks)

(c)	The living standard will decrease.	(1 mark)
	After the failure, people widely engage in barter. The costs involved in transactions, e.g., the costs of finding trading partners and determining exchange ratios, will increase.	(1 mark)
	This will hinder the exchange of goods. The volume of exchange will decrease and so people's standard of living will decrease.	(1 mark)

(d)	(i)	Corn functions as a store of value. It preserves its purchasing power and Julia uses it to accumulate wealth.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Corn functions as a standard of deferred payments. The future payment from O'Brien to Winston is expressed in terms of corn.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
After the implementation of the Individual Visit Scheme, more and more mainlanders are visiting Hong Kong. As a result, some shops in Hong Kong quote their prices in both Hong Kong dollars (HKD) and renminbi (RMB).
(a)	Explain the functions of money that RMB performs at those shops in the above example.	(4 marks)
(b)	Some people claim that the influx of mainland visitors has pushed Hong Kong price levels upwards. Explain which function of money weakens during inflation.	(3 marks)
(c)	Hong Kong is an international financial centre. Due to Hong Kong's advantage in financial services over the mainland, many mainland companies want to list their shares on the Hong Kong stock market.
	(i)	List TWO factors that contribute to Hong Kong's development as a financial centre.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Chi Kwong said, 'The development of the financial industry cannot benefit Hong Kong because the values of financial assets are not counted in Hong Kong's GDP.' Explain why he is INCORRECT.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	RMB performs as a unit of account as the prices are quoted in RMB.	(2 marks)
	RMB performs as a medium of exchange as people can use RMB to buy goods at those shops.	(2 marks)

(b)	The function as a store of value weakens.	(1 mark)
	During inflation, the purchasing power oreserved in money decreases. Money has less ability to accumulate wealth.	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	(	Favourable time zone location
		(	Strong local and regional demand for financial services
		(	Favourable government policies
		(	Excellent financial infrastructure
		(	Adequate supply of financial professionals
		(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers. 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
	(ii)	The value of services involved in the transactions of financial assets should be included in Hong Kong's GDP. This means the development of the financial industry can benefit Hong Kong.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Marshall was a fisherman on Fishing Island. He would like to exchange his fish for a knife. He met Jordon, the only cutler (刀匠) on the island.
Marshall said, 'I would like to have your knife. I will give you four fish in return.'
Jordon said, 'Sorry, I don't eat fish. I would like to have 10 apples for my wife instead.'
Marshall said, 'Only a few people love to eat apples and grow apples. I need time to find them.'
One month later, Marshall found a farmer and exchanged his fish for 10 apples. Then he went back to Jordon.
Marshall said, 'Here are your 10 apples. May I have your knife?'
Jordon said, 'No. Sorry, I have received 10 apples in another transaction. Now, what I want is 10 oranges.'
Marshall said, 'Curses! Why did I exchange my fish for these 10 apples which you and I don't want?'
(a)	Explain ONE problem of barter in the above story.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain ONE similarity and ONE difference between the role of apples in the above story and the role of money in the real world.	(4 marks)
(c)	Explain why the emergence of money can improve the situation in the above story.	(3 marks)
(d)	List TWO benefits of the emergence of money other than the one discussed in (c).	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Difficult to satisfy a double coincidence of wants	(2 marks)

(b)	Similarity:
	(	Both serve as a medium of exchange.
	(	Both serve as a store of value. Apples preserve the purchasing power of fish.
	(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answer, 2 marks)
Difference: Apples are not generally accepted but money is generally accepted.
	(2 marks)

(c)	If there is money, Marshall can exchange his fish for money and then exchange his money for Jordon's knife. This is because money is generally accepted in exchange. In this case, Marshall need not bear a risk that the good which serves as a medium of exchange (i.e., apples) would not be accepted by Jordon.	(3 marks)

(d)	The following are the benefits of the emergence of money:
(	The volume of exchange can grow tremendously.
(	Specialisation can be widely practised.
(	Wealth can be accumulated at lower cost.
(	People's living standards can be greatly improved.
(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
Study the following diagram about the economic situation of Country A.

(a)	(i)	What is a business cycle? List the FOUR phases of a business cycle.	(4 marks)
(ii)	Explain which phase of a business cycle Point B is in.	(2 marks)
(b)	Ming had a garment factory in Country A. He found that, on average, the output level was lower than other factories although the total working hours of his workers were greater than other factories.
(i)	Explain what method of wage payments was most likely used by Ming.
	(2 marks)
(ii)	Suppose it was easy for Ming to measure his workers' contribution and monitor the quality of the products. Suggest a method of wage payment that should be used by Ming and list TWO advantages of this method of wage payment to Ming.	(3 marks)
(c)	In Year 3, Ming lost a lot of money in the stock market. He decided to close his factory and use garments to pay his workers all wages in arrears (欠薪). Some workers accepted the arrangement.
(i)	List and define TWO functions of the garments similar to those of money in this case.	(4 marks)
(ii)	Explain why garments are NOT money.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	(	The business cycle refers to short run fluctuations in real GDP around the long run trend.	(2 marks)
(	The four phases are contraction, trough, expansion and peak.
(0.5 marks for each phase)
(ii)	Contraction as the real GDP is declining.	(2 marks)

(b)	(i)	Time rate (hour rate). The workers have an incentive to work longer and produce fewer goods.	(2 marks)
(ii)	Piece rate.	(1 mark)
Advantages:
(	It could raise workers' incentive to work and their productivity.
(	It could reduce the need for supervision against shirking.
(Accept other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

(c)	(i)	(	As a medium of exchange: Something accepted for the exchange of goods and services
(	As a store of value: Something used to preserve purchasing power and accumulate wealth
(	As a unit of account: Something used to express prices, values, incomes and expenditures
(Any TWO of the above, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)
(ii)	Money is anything that is generally accepted as a medium of exchange.
	(2 marks)
Since garments are not generally accepted, they are not money.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch607 · Market intervention (II)
questions.text:
In a remote area, people live self-sufficiently. Recently, they have decided to specialise in producing goods that can be exchanged for dried fruit. Then, they will use their dried fruit to exchange for other goods they want.
(a)	Explain whether people who are self-sufficient need money.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose dried fruit is accepted in all transactions. Explain whether dried fruit is money in the above case.	(2 marks)
(c)	Explain the functions of money served by dried fruit in the cases below.
	(i)	A hawker said, 'My chickens are fresh, each costing 50 pieces of dried fruit.'	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Mary stored a lot of dried fruit in her warehouse for future purchase.	(2 marks)
(d)	State THREE desirable properties of money which dried fruit does not have.
	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	They do not need money because there is no exchange.	(2 marks)

(b)	Yes	(1 mark)
	because dried fruit is a generally accepted medium of exchange.	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	Unit of account,	(1 mark)
		because the price of another good (chickens) is expressed in terms of dried fruit.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	Store of value,	(1 mark)
		because dried fruit is used to preserve purchasing power and accumulate wealth.	(1 mark)

(d)	Dried fruit does not have the following desirable properties of money:
(	Durable: Dried fruit is perishable.
(	Portable: Dried fruit is not portable, especially in large transactions.
(	Homogeneous: Dried fruit is not homogeneous because it does not possess uniform physical characteristics.
(	Stable in supply: The supply of dried fruit is unstable and its value may fluctuate greatly.
(Any THREE of the above, 2 marks × 3 = 6 marks)

questions.text:
* Which of the following statements about the monetary base is INCORRECT?
A.	The monetary base will not change during the money creation process.
B.	An increase in the monetary base will increase the maximum possible amount of money supply in the economy.
C.	Cash leakage will not affect the value of the monetary base.
D.	When there is no cash leakage, the monetary base is the same as reserves held by the banking system.
questions.answerText:
Option A is a correct statement. During the money creation process, only credit and deposits are created, and the total amount of legal tender issued in the economy (i.e., the monetary base) remains unchanged.
Option B is a correct statement. When members of the public deposit cash into the banking system, the money supply will increase after the money creation process. Hence, the monetary base determines the maximum amount of cash that can be used for money creation, and also determines the maximum possible amount of money supply in the economy. When the monetary base increases, the maximum possible amount of money supply will increase.
Option D is the answer. No cash leakage means all the loans from banks are redeposited into the banking system. This does not mean that the public does not hold cash.

Suppose the banking system holds $100 in excess reserves. Which of the following statements is correct when the central bank lowers the required reserve ratio by 10%?
A.	The excess reserves will remain unchanged.
B.	The amount of reserves will decrease by $100.
C.	The maximum amount of deposits will increase by $1,500.
D.	The maximum amount of loans will increase by $1,000.
questions.answerText:
The original required reserve ratio = ($200 - $100) ( $500 ×100% = 20%
The new required reserve ratio = 20% - 10% = 10%
The original maximum amount of deposits = $200 × (1 / 20%) = $1,000
The new maximum amount of deposits = $200 × (1 / 10%) = $2,000
The original maximum amount of loans = $1,000 - $200 = $800
The new maximum amount of loans = $2,000 - $200 = $1,800
Both the maximum amounts of deposits and loans increase by $1,000.

questions.text:
* A lady deposits $5 million cash into the banking system. After the money creation process, the amount of loans in the banking system increases by $25 million.

	(1)	The maximum banking multiplier is 6.
	(2)	Deposits have increased by $30 million.
	(3)	The money supply has increased by $25 million.

Option (2) is incorrect. If there is cash leakage, the change in reserves will be less than $5 million. Hence, we have insufficient information to conclude what the change in deposits will be.
Option (3) is incorrect. Since there may be cash leakage, we do not know what the change in the amount of cash held by the public will be, and hence we cannot conclude how the money supply will change.

questions.answerText:

questions.answerText: Option D is the answer. When a certain amount of cash (say, $1,000) is deposited into a bank, the bank can lend out excess reserves (say, $800). Hence, during the deposit creation process, only the amounts of loans and deposits increase, not reserves. The maximum increase in reserves is equal to the initial deposit. questions.topic: B6 · Ch608 · Ownership of firms
questions.text:
* Suppose a banking system never holds excess reserves. After $1,200 is deposited into a bank, the total amount of loans in the banking system increases by $3,600 eventually.
Which of the following conclusions can be drawn?
	(1)	The minimum reserve ratio is 25%.
	(2)	The actual banking multiplier is 4.
	(3)	The money supply increases by $2,400.
A.	(1) only
B.	(2) only
C.	(1) and (2) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
Option (1) is incorrect. The actual increase in loans is the same as the maximum increase in loans only when the assumptions of maximum creation of money (i.e., there are no excess reserves, enough borrowing, and no cash leakage) are satisfied. Since the question only mentions that there are no excess reserves, we cannot draw the conclusions in Option (1).
Option (3) is incorrect as we do not know whether the initial deposit comes from cash held by the public or not.
Option (2) is correct. The increase in deposits is $4,800, which is equal to the sum of the increase in reserves (i.e., the initial deposit of 1,200) and the increase in loans (i.e., $3,600). Therefore, the actual banking multiplier is 4 (= $4,800 / $1,200).

questions.topic: B6 · Ch608 · Ownership of firms
questions.text:
* If $200 is withdrawn from a bank, the total amount of deposits in the banking system will decrease by $800. Which of the following statements is true?
A.	The actual reserve ratio of the banking system must be 25%.
B.	The maximum banking multiplier must be 4.
C.	The money supply must decrease by $800.
D.	None of the above
questions.answerText: Options A and B are incorrect. When the actual reserve ratio and the required reserve ratio are both 25% (i.e., banks do not hold excess reserves) and there is no cash injected into the banking system, a $200 withdrawal will result in a fall in deposits by $800 in the banking system. The actual banking multiplier and the maximum banking multiplier in the banking system are both equal to 4. However, if banks hold excess reserves (i.e., the actual reserve ratio is greater than the required reserve ratio), we cannot draw the conclusions in Options A and B.

questions.text:
* The following is the balance sheet of Bank H.

Assets ($)	Liabilities ($)	
Reserves	200	Deposits	1,600	
Loans	1,400			

Suppose the required reserve ratio is 20%. Which of the following events can help Bank H fulfil the reserve requirement?
	(1)	Bank H calls back $120 in loans.
	(2)	Bank H borrows $120 from other banks.
	(3)	Members of the public deposit $120 cash into Bank H.
A.	(1) and (2) only
B.	(1) and (3) only
C.	(2) and (3) only
D.	(1), (2) and (3)
questions.answerText:
Options (1) and (2) are correct. When Bank H calls back $120 in loans or borrows $120 from other banks, reserves increase to $320 while deposits remain unchanged. As a result, the actual reserve ratio becomes 20% (= $320 / $1,600).
Option (3) is incorrect because deposits also increase by $120. When deposits increase to $1,720, required reserves increase to $344. In other words, Bank H is still short of reserves (= $344 - $320 = $24) after the deposit of $120.

questions.text:
(a)	What is the difference between money supply and the monetary base?	(3 marks)
