questions.topic: B6 · Ch613 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
The following table shows the exchange rates between the Hong Kong dollar (HKD) and the renminbi (RMB).

Date	Exchange rate	
2014/5/3	HKD 1 = RMB 0.805	
2015/5/3	HKD 1 = RMB 0.801	

(a)	Explain whether RMB has appreciated or depreciated against HKD within the period.	(2 marks)
(b)	With the aid of separate diagrams, explain the effects of the above change in the exchange rate on Hong Kong's
	(i)	total import value from the mainland in terms of Hong Kong dollars.
	(6 marks)
	(ii)	total export value to the mainland in terms of Hong Kong dollars.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	RMB has appreciated against HKD because	(1 mark)
	the same amount of HKD can only be exchanged for fewer RMB.	(1 mark)

(b)	(i)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Price increases, quantity demanded decreases	(1 mark)
(	Correct areas of increase and decrease in total import value	(1 mark)
		

		Verbal elaboration:
		The price (in terms of Hong Kong dollars) of imports from the mainland increases after the appreciation of RMB.	(1 mark)
		The quantity demanded decreases.	(1 mark)
		The change in total import value is uncertain. It depends on the price elasticity of demand for imports from the mainland.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Demand curve shifts rightwards.	(1 mark)
(	Total export value increases.	(1 mark)
		
		Verbal elaboration:
		The price (in terms of RMB) of exports to the mainland decreases after the appreciation of RMB (assuming the HKD price remains the same).	(1 mark)
		Hence, the volume of exports from Hong Kong to the mainland increases.
	(1 mark)
		This brings a rightward shift of the demand curve and an increase in the total export value.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch613 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Hong Kong imports toys, as well as produces its own toys.
(a)	Some Hong Kong merchants import toys from Japan. The imported toys are used as a reference when designing their own products. To which factor of production do the imported toys belong? Explain.	(2 marks)
(b)	Suppose there is a rumour that some Hong Kong toys are dangerous for children.
(i)	Explain, with the aid of a diagram, how the price, quantity and total revenue of imported toys in Hong Kong would change.	(6 marks)
(ii)	Based on your result in (i), explain how Hong Kong's market balance of payments and accounting balance of payments would be affected.	(4 marks)
(c)	Suppose the US dollar appreciates against the Japanese yen. Explain, with a diagram, the effect on the total value (in terms of Hong Kong dollars) of Japanese toys imported to Hong Kong.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The imported toys are capital. They are man-made resource used to help in the production of Hong Kong-made toys.	(2 marks)

(b)	(i)	Since Hong Kong toys and imported toys are close substitutes, the demand for imported toys will rise (from D0 to D1).	(1 mark)
			(2 marks)
	The equilibrium price of imported toys increases from P0 to P1.	(1 mark)
	The equilibrium quantity of imported toys increases from Q0 to Q1.	(1 mark)
	Therefore, the total revenue of imported toys increases.	(1 mark)
	(ii)	As the imported toys are recorded as debits in the current account, the increase in the total revenue of imported toys would worsen the market balance of payments.	(2 marks)
	Since the accounting balance of payments must be zero, it is not affected by the matter.	(2 marks)

(c)	According to the linked exchange rate system, the HK dollar also appreciates against the Japanese yen.	(1 mark)
	As the price (in terms of HK dollars) of Japanese toys decreases (from Pd1 to Pd2), according to the law of demand, the quantity demanded of Japanese toys increases (from QM1 to QM2).	(2 marks)
	The total value (in terms of HK dollars) of Japanese toys imported may increase or decrease, depending on the price elasticity of demand for Japanese toys.
	(1 mark)
	
		(2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch613 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
The currency of Country L (LD) is under a pegged exchange rate system. The currency of Country T (TP) is under a flexible exchange rate system. Country T urges Country L to revaluate LD.
(a)	Country L imports oranges from Country T in addition to its domestic supply. Explain, with the aid of a diagram, the effects of an appreciation of LD on the total revenue of Country L's domestic orange growers.	(6 marks)
(b)	Remi, a citizen of Country T, says, 'The appreciation of LD relieves our current account deficit against Country L.' Explain why he may NOT be correct.
	(5 marks)
(c)	Country T has been facing a persistent market balance of payments deficit.
	(i)	What is the difference between accounting balance of payments and market balance of payments?	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Ka Ming says, 'The market balance of payment deficit implies that Country T has a current account deficit.' Do you agree? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Indicate on the diagram:
(	Demand curve shifts leftwards.	(1 mark)
(	Total revenue decreases.	(1 mark)
	
	Verbal elaboration:
	After the appreciation of LD, the price (in terms of LD) of Country T's oranges in Country L decreases.	(1 mark)
	As domestic oranges are substitutes for imported oranges, the demand for domestic oranges decreases.	(2 marks)
	As a result, the total revenue of domestic orange growers decreases.	(1 mark)

(b)	The appreciation of LD raises the price (in terms of TP) of Country L's goods in Country T. This will lower the quantity demanded of Country L's goods. As a result, the change in Country T's total import value (in terms of TP) from 
Country L is uncertain.	(2 marks)
	On the other hand, the appreciation of LD lowers the price (in terms of LD) of Country T's goods in Country L. This causes the quantity demanded of 
Country T's goods to increase. As a result, Country T's total export value to Country L (in terms of TP) increases.	(2 marks)
	Remi may not be correct as the overall effect on the current account of Country T is uncertain.	(1 mark)

(c)	(i)	The accounting balance of payments includes the transactions of central banks and must be balanced, while the market balance of payments does not include the transactions of central banks and may not be balanced.	(2 marks)

	(ii)	Disagree.	(1 mark)
		Market BoP = Current account balance + Net change in capital and financial non-reserve asssets 	(1 mark)
		If the 'Net change in capital and financial non-reserve assets' is negative and greater than the current account surplus, Country T will also have a market BoP deficit.	(2 marks)
		(Accept any correct explantion.)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch613 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Country J has been affected by radioactive contamination (核污染). Due to this catastrophe, fewer of Country H's people travel to Country J. In addition, Country H imports fewer goods from Country J.
(a)	With the aid of a supply-demand diagram, explain how the above event affects the equilibrium price and quantity in Country H of tours to Country J.	(5 marks)
(b)	With the aid of an AS-AD diagram, explain how the above events affect
Country J's real GDP and price level in the short run.	(7 marks)
(c)	Suppose Country J's currency depreciates against Country H's currency as a result of the above events. With the aid of a diagram, analyse how the depreciation of Country J's currency affects the price (in Country H's currency) and quantity of imports from Country J in Country H. (Remark: You are NOT required to discuss the effects of radioactive contamination.)	(4 marks)
(d)	To help the economy recover, Country J's government raises tax revenue to finance its increased government expenditure on infrastructure. Explain whether this policy can stimulate real GDP growth in the short run.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	The demand for tours to Country J decreases. The demand curve of tours to Country J shifts leftwards from D1 to D2.	(1 mark)
•	Both the equilibrium price and quantity of tours to Country J decrease.
	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

(b)	•	The fall in the number of tourists and the volume of exports to Country H will lead to a decrease in Country J's real exports and aggregate demand.	(2 marks)
•	The aggregate demand curve shifts leftwards from AD1 to AD2.	(1 mark)
•	Country J's real GDP decreases from Y1 to Y2.	(1 mark)
•	Country J's price level decreases from P1 to P2.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)


(c)	•	As Country J's currency depreciates, the prices of imports from Country J (in Country H's currency) decrease from P1 to P2.	(1 mark)
•	According to the law of demand, Country H's quantity demanded of imports from Country J increases from Q1 to Q2.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

(d)	•	Since the contractionary effect from an increase in government revenue is smaller than the expansionary effect from an increase in government expenditure of the same amount, aggregate expenditure increases.	(2 marks)
•	Thus, the overall effect of this policy is expansionary. It can stimulate real GDP growth in the short run.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch613 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Wendy is a university graduate in Hong Kong. She travels to Japan for three months before seeking a job.
(a)	Explain whether the following items will be affected by Wendy's Japan trip.
(i)	Hong Kong's goods account balance	(2 marks)
(ii)	Hong Kong's services account balance	(2 marks)
(b)	Wendy has exchanged US$10,000 for Japanese yen (¥) at a rate of ¥100 : US$2. Now, the exchange rate changes to ¥100 : US$1.
(i)	What is the effect of the above change on the exchange rate between Japanese yen and Hong Kong dollars? Explain.	(2 marks)
(ii)	Explain how the change in the exchange rate between Japanese yen and Hong Kong dollars mentioned in (b)(i) will affect Japanese goods' prices paid by Hong Kong tourists in terms of Hong Kong dollars.	(1 mark)
(iii)	Wendy talked to her friend, 'If I buy Japanese yen now instead, I can save US$5,000 and get the same amount of Japanese yen. Thus, my US$5,000 is my opportunity cost of holding ¥500,000 earlier.' Do you agree? Explain your answer.	(3 marks)
(c)	(i)	Explain whether Wendy is classified as an unemployed person when she travels to Japan.	(3 marks)
(ii)	State TWO costs of unemployment to the unemployed.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(i)	No external transactions of goods are involved. Thus, there is no effect on Hong Kong's goods account balance.	(2 marks)
(ii)	Wendy's expenditure in Japan will be recorded as imports of services. This will worsen Hong Kong's services account balance.	(2 marks)

(b)	(i)	•	Under the linked exchange rate system, the changes in market exchange rates of non-US currencies against the Hong Kong dollar closely follow those against the US dollar.	(1 mark)
•	Thus, the exchange rate of Japanese yen against Hong Kong dollars will decrease by about 50%.	(1 mark)
(ii)	As the Japanese yen depreciates against the Hong Kong dollar, Japanese goods' prices paid by Hong Kong tourists in terms of Hong Kong dollars decrease.	(1 mark)
(iii)	•	Disagree.	(1 mark)
•	The cost of holding (i.e., buying) ¥500,000 earlier is the highest-valued alternative use of the amount spent, which would not be changed by any events that happened after the decision was made.	(2 marks)

(c)	(i)	•	Unemployed persons are those who want a job but fail to find one. They are available for and seeking work.	(2 marks)
•	As Wendy was neither available for work nor seeking work during the period, she is not regarded as an unemployed person.	(1 mark)
(ii)	Costs of unemployment to the unemployed are as follows:
•	Lower living standard
•	Family problems
•	Loss of skills
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers. 2 × 1 mark = 2 marks)

questions.topic: B6 · Ch613 · Market and market structure
questions.text:
Suppose there are only two countries: Chive and United Space. Both countries are self-sufficient. Recently, they have decided to partly open their economies as an experiment. They will only trade the following two goods: machines and food. The following shows their absolute advantages and comparative advantages.

Country	Absolute advantage	Comparative advantage	
Chive	―	Machines	
The United Space	Machines, Food	Food	

(a)	Suppose both countries engage in specialisation. What determines the pattern of specialisation? Which goods should Chive specialise in? Which goods should United Space specialise in? Explain the principle applied.	(5 marks)
(b)	The experiment is successful. Both countries decide to further open their economies. Afterward, Chive has a huge balance of payments (BoP) surplus while United Space has a huge BoP deficit. Suppose Chive adopts a fixed exchange rate system.
*(i)	Suppose United Space's demand for Chive's exports is elastic. With the aid of TWO supply-demand diagrams, explain whether the revaluation of Chive's currency will improve United Space's trade balance (in United Space's currency).	(14 marks)
(ii)	To determine the overall effect of the revaluation of Chive's currency on United Space's current account balance, what information do we need besides the visible and invisible trade balances? What further information do we need to determine the overall effect of the revaluation of Chive's currency on United Space's BoP?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	•	Comparative advantage	(1 mark)
•	Chive should specialise in producing machines while United Space should specialise in producing food.	(2 marks)
•	The principle behind this is the principle of comparative advantage. It states that if each country specialises in producing the good in which it has a comparative advantage, total world output will increase.	(2 marks)


(b)	(i)	•	The revaluation of Chive's currency lowers the price of United Space's exports in terms of Chive's currency.	(1 mark)
•	Since the price of United Space's exports in terms of Chive's currency decreases, United Space's export volume (QX) increases from QX1 to QX2.	(1 mark)
•	The price of United Space's exports in terms of its domestic currency (PdX) is assumed to be independent of the exchange rate. At the same price in terms of United Space's currency, the increase in the export volume implies that Chive's demand for United Space's exports increases.
	(2 marks)
•	The demand curve for United Space's exports shifts rightwards from DX1 to DX2.	(1 mark)
•	Therefore, the total value of exports in United Space's domestic currency (VX) rises.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

•	The revaluation of Chive's currency raises United Space's import price in terms of its domestic currency (PdM).	(1 mark)
•	Since PdM increases, according to the law of demand, United Space's volume of imports (QM) decreases from QM1 to QM2.	(1 mark)
•	As United Space's demand for imports is elastic, the percentage drop in QM is larger than the percentage rise in PdM. Thus, the total value of imports in its domestic currency (VM) drops.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)
•	As VX rises and VM drops, United Space's trade balance will improve.
	(1 mark)
(ii)	•	Determining the overall effect on current account balance: the changes in net income from abroad and net current transfers OR the change in the capital and financial account balance (with an opposite sign)
	(Any one, 1 mark)
•	Determining the overall effect on BoP: net change in capital and financial non-reserve assets OR net change in reserve assets (with an opposite sign)	(Any one, 1 mark)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
(a)	What does a production possibilities frontier (PPF) show?	(2 marks)
(b)	What are the assumptions of constructing a PPF?	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A PPF shows all combinations of two goods that a country can produce with all of its resources and the best technology available.	(2 marks)
(b)	The country produces only two goods.	(1 mark)
	Resources available are given.	(1 mark)
	Technology is given.	(1 mark)
	The country uses all of its resources and the best technology available.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
Country X produces only medicine and rice with its only input, labour. It is self-sufficient. The following shows the PPF of the country. Suppose Country X wants to consume at Point A.

(a)	Explain why the country cannot consume at Point A.	(3 marks)
(b)	Explain which economic concept is illustrated by (a).	(2 marks)
(c)	Suggest TWO possible changes that allow Country X to consume at Point A.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Country X is self-sufficient, so its consumption point is the same as its production point.	(1 mark)
	Point A is beyond the PPF, which means the current resources and technology level are not enough to attain this output.	(2 marks)
(b)	Scarcity	(1 mark)
	The amount of output that Country X can produce and consume (shown by the PPF) is less than the output the country wants (shown by Point A).	(1 mark)
(c)	•	Country X's production technology improves.
	•	Country X's labour force increases.
	•	Country X engages in trade with other countries.
	(Any TWO of the above, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text: Define the production possibilities frontier (PPF). Draw a PPF and show the area of attainable production combinations.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
The production possibilities frontier shows all combinations of two goods that a country can produce with all of its resources and the best technology available.
	(2 marks)
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
The following diagrams show the PPFs of Country A and Country B. Suppose the two countries use different resources in production.

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
(a)	Under what situation will the production possibilities frontier (PPF) become linear?	(2 marks)
(b)	Under what situation will the PPF become concave to the origin?	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	The PPF is linear if the marginal cost of production of goods (in terms of another good) is constant.	(2 marks)
(b)	The PPF is concave to the origin if the marginal cost of production of goods (in terms of another good) is increasing.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text: Explain the differences between absolute advantage and comparative advantage by using PPFs. 	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
If countries have the same amount of resources, a country has an absolute advantage in producing the good on the x-axis (y-axis) when its PPF has an x-intercept (y-intercept) further from the origin.	(1 mark)
A country has a comparative advantage in producing the good on the x-axis (y-axis) when its PPF has a smaller (greater) slope than the other country's PPF.	(1 mark)
Any correct diagram and elaboration which illustrate absolute advantage and comparative advantage:	(3 marks)
In the following diagram, suppose both countries possess the same amount of resources. We can see that Country B has an absolute advantage in producing both goods, while Country A enjoys a comparative advantage in producing Good X.

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
Refer to the following diagram:

Country A has 10 units of resources while Country B has 30 units of resources. 
Which country has an absolute advantage in producing Good X? Which country has an absolute advantage in producing Good Y? 	(4 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text: Suppose there are only two countries producing two goods. The slopes of their PPFs are the same, yet one of the countries possesses an absolute advantage in producing both goods. Can they benefit from international trade? Explain. 	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
No.	(1 mark)
This is because the slopes of their PPFs are the same, which means their costs of production are the same. There is no comparative advantage for both countries.

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
The following diagram shows the production possibilities frontier (AA') of a small open economy, Country Q. Point K and Point J are the production points of Country Q under autarky and after specialisation, respectively. Point L is the consumption point after trade.

(a)	What is meant by a 'small open economy'?	(2 marks)
(b)	How will the marginal production cost of Good Y change when Country Q produces more Good Y? Explain.	(2 marks)
(c)	Suppose CC' is the terms of trade line. Explain how Country Q gains from trade.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	A small open economy refers to an economy which engages in international trade but cannot affect the world price no matter how much it imports or exports.
	(2 marks)
(b)	The marginal production cost will increase as the economy's PPF is concave to the origin.	(2 marks)
(c)	Country Q gains as Point L has more of both goods than Point K.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text: Explain, with the aid of a diagram, why a small open economy with increasing marginal cost will produce at a point where the terms of trade line is tangent to its PPF.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
For the segment (Segment A) where the slope of the PPF is greater than the slope of the TOT line, the economy will decrease the production of Good X. 	(1 mark)
For the segment (Segment C) where the slope of the PPF is smaller than the slope of the TOT line, the economy will increase the production of Good X. 	(1 mark)
Therefore, the economy will produce at the point where the TOT line is tangent to its PPF (Point B). At this point, the economy has no tendency to change its output of Good X.	(1 mark)
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:

Suppose there is technological advancement that only increases the economy's productivity of Good X. Show the new production point on the diagram above and briefly explain your answer.	(5 marks)
questions.answerText:
Technological advancement will increase the maximum amount of Good X produced with existing resources. This can be represented by a shift from PPF to PPF2.
	(1 mark)
As there is no change in the terms of trade, the slope of the TOT line remains unchanged. To find the new production point, we shift the TOT line parallel to the right. The new production point, A', is where the TOT line is tangent to PPF2.
	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
(a)	What is globalisation from economic perspectives?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain how the concept of comparative advantage helps promote globalisation.
	(3 marks)
(c)	Suggest TWO costs of globalisation.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	From economic perspectives, globalisation refers to increasing international trade and capital flows between countries.	(2 marks)
(b)	If countries engage in international trade based on comparative advantage, they can gain from trade and enjoy a higher standard of living. This encourages countries to adopt a free trade policy. As the volume of world trade and investment expands, the degree of globalisation increases.	(3 marks)
(c)	•	Increasing income inequality
	•	Labour exploitation
	•	Exhaustion of natural resources
	•	Pollution and environmental damages
	•	Loss of autonomy
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text:
(a)	Define globalisation in terms of economic aspects.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain any TWO driving forces of globalisation in terms of economic aspects.
	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	In terms of economic aspects, globalisation refers to increasing international trade and capital flows between countries.	(2 marks)
(b)	Major driving forces:
Expansion of international trade based on comparative advantage
Outsourcing of multinational corporations' production processes to other countries
	(Accept other reasonable answers. 2 marks each.)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch714 · Profit maximisation and output determination
questions.text: Explain the relationship between globalisation and comparative advantage.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
Specialisation and trade based on the principle of comparative advantage can allow countries to enjoy a higher standard of living. This encourages countries to adopt a free trade policy. The increased adoption of a free policy among countries leads to a higher degree of globalisation.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
(a)	What is economic growth?	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain why it is better to measure economic growth by per capita real GDP than real GDP.	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Economic growth refers to an increase in the real value of an economy's production.	(2 marks)
(b)	An increase in an economy's real GDP may be due to an increase in population. Per capita real GDP eliminates the effect of changes in population.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: Briefly explain why the Human Development Index is a better measurement of economic development than per capita real GDP.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText: Per capita real GDP can be used to measure economic growth. However, economic development takes into account aspects other than economic growth. Besides economic growth, the HDI also takes into account an economy's level of health and educational attainment.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: List the three measures of the Human Development Index (HDI) and briefly explain how they reflect a country's standard of living.	(6 marks)
questions.answerText:
HDI is based on the following three measures:
(	Life expectancy at birth - If an economy has better healthcare, its people can enjoy a longer, healthier life. As a result, the country's productivity and living standards will be higher.	(2 marks)
(	Years of schooling - This consists of two indicators, mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling. More and better education can increase people's living standards.	(2 marks)

(	Per capita GNI (PPP) - Countries with higher per capita GNI (PPP) generally have higher living standards.	(2 marks)

(a)	(	Increase in the stock of physical capital
	(	Increase in labour supply
	(	Increase in human capital
	(	Technological advancement
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 2 = 2 marks)
(b)	(	As many citizens have migrated to other countries, Country K's labour supply decreases.
	(	Due to the famine, the health of Country K's citizens may worsen. This adversely affects labour productivity in Country K.

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
Explain whether the following policies favour economic growth.
(a)	Strict immigration requirement on applicants' educational levels	(3 marks)
(b)	Higher profits tax rate for foreign companies	(3 marks)
(c)	Exempting interest income and dividend income from income taxes	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Uncertain.	(1 mark)
	This may hinder the growth in labour supply and therefore economic growth. However, this may also increase workers' average productivity and thus favour economic growth (in terms of per capita real GDP).	(2 marks)
(b)	No.	(1 mark)
	This reduces foreign companies' incentive to invest. Less foreign direct investment will hinder economic growth.	(2 marks)
(c)	Yes.	(1 mark)
	This can encourage people to save and invest as they can keep all of their investment income.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: Student A says, 'Since a higher level of saving will reduce consumption and hence aggregate demand, a higher level of saving will harm economic growth.' Do you agree? Explain.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText: No. If the savings are used for investment purposes, the increase in investment will compensate for the decrease in consumption. As a result, the economy's real income may not fall, while the increase in investment will help increase the economy's future income.	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
Explain how the following policies will affect a country's economic growth.
(a)	Enhancing the protection of private property rights	(2 marks)
(b)	Extending the years of free and compulsory education	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Private property rights provide owners with incentives to make the best use of their property. Enhancing the protection of private property rights can facilitate investment activities and promotes economic growth.	(2 marks)
(b)	This can improve labour productivity and thus stimulate the country's economic growth.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: Country B's government wants to promote economic growth. Suggest THREE possible policies to the government and briefly explain each of them.	(6 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
(a)	Explain ONE possible benefit of economic growth to people.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain which type of worker is LESS likely to benefit from economic growth.
	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	(	Economic growth can improve people's living standards. They can enjoy more goods and services.
(	With economic growth, more resources can be devoted to educational, medical and social services. This can help people who are living in poverty.
(Any ONE of the above or other reasonable answer, 2 marks.)
(b)	Low-skilled workers.	(1 mark)
	They may lose their jobs or suffer wage cuts due to the use of new technologies and capital goods.	(1 mark)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text: 'Since economic growth can improve people's living standards, income inequality tends to decrease.' Do you agree? Explain.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
Disagree.	(1 mark)
Since the rich can save more than the poor, they are able to accumulate more capital and earn more income from their capital investments. Hence, it is more likely that the rich benefit more from economic growth, resulting in higher income inequality.
	(3 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
The following chart shows the Human Development Index and income figure for Country H and Country S in Year 1.

(a)	Country H's income is lower than Country S. However, Country H's HDI is higher than Country S. Explain TWO possible reasons for this.	(4 marks)
*(b)	Jimmy said, 'The HDI of Country H is higher than that of Country S. Therefore, the living standard of Country H's people is higher.' Explain why Jimmy may be WRONG, giving TWO reasons.	(4 marks)
(c)	The income figures have been converted by exchange rates before comparison. What is the reason for converting the income figures before comparison?	(2 marks)
(d)	Explain whether a high saving rate can promote economic growth. 	(3 marks)
(e)	State THREE costs of economic growth.	(3 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Country H's people have a longer life expectancy at birth than those of Country S.
	(2 marks)
	Country H's people have longer mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling than those of Country S.	(2 marks)
(b)	The HDI ignores the distribution of income. Despite a higher HDI, the income disparity in Country H may be larger than Country S. Country H's people may not have a higher living standard.
	Due to inadequate information, the value of some unreported production activities cannot be reflected by the HDI. Therefore, the HDI may not accurately reflect the economic welfare of both countries.
	The value of some unpaid services is not reflected by the HDI. However, these production activities improve people's standard of living.
	(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers, 2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)
(c)	Different currencies have different values. Therefore, the income figures have to be converted into one single currency for easier comparison.	(2 marks)
(d)	Yes. Investment comes from savings. If people save more of their income, then more funds will be available for investment. As a result, capital will accumulate, which will stimulate economic growth.	(3 marks)
(e)	(	Lower current consumption
	(	Uneven income distribution
	(	Unemployment of low-skilled workers
	(	Economic instability
	(	Exhaustion of natural resources
	(	Pollution and other environmental damage
	(Any THREE of the above or other reasonable answers, 1 mark × 3 = 3 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
Country X has experienced very slow economic growth for the past few years.
(a)	Explain whether it is better to use real GDP or per capita real GDP to measure economic growth.	(2 marks)
(b)	Explain how the following events hinder Country X's economic growth.
	(i)	Five years ago, Country X was struck by a great tsunami.	(2 marks)
	(ii)	To prevent a rise in prices, the government of Country X imposes price ceilings on most necessities.	(2 marks)
	(iii)	Country X has been politically unstable in recent years.	(2 marks)

(c)	An official of the immigration department suggested, 'We should relax the immigration requirement. With a larger labour force, we can boost our country's economic growth.' Explain why the official may NOT be correct.	(2 marks)
(d)	The following are some of the policies suggested by the president of Country X. Explain how they can promote economic growth.
	(i)	Raise the penalty for breaking copyright laws (版權法)	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Lower the profits tax rate	(2 marks)
	(iii)	Grant more subsidies for technological research and development through the innovation and technology fund	(2 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Per capita real GDP is a better measure because it eliminates the effect of a population change.	(2 marks)
(b)	(i)	The tsunami might have destroyed a lot of production facilities and killed many workers. This would reduce Country X's production capacity.
	(2 marks)
	(ii)	Government intervention generally results in inefficiency in resource allocation and leads to a deadweight loss.	(2 marks)
	(iii)	Political instability would likely lead to a reduction in investment and immigration of professionals.	(2 marks)
(c)	Economic growth is often measured by per capita real GDP. If the new immigrants are less productive, the population's growth rate will exceed the real GDP's growth rate.	(2 marks)
(d)	(i)	This raises the cost of breaking the laws and protects copyrights better. Businesspeople will have greater incentives to develop new products.
	(2 marks)
	(ii)	A lower profits tax rate means companies can retain more of their earnings. This attracts investment.	(2 marks)
	(iii)	These subsidies promote research and development. This may bring technological advancement and hence stimulate economic growth.	(2 marks)

questions.topic: B7 · Ch715 · Consumer surplus and producer surplus
questions.text:
The following table shows information about Country A and Country B in Year 1:

	Country A	Country B	
GNI (PPP)	US$80 billion	US$95 billion	
Population	2 million	3 million	
Years of schooling on average	22 years	18 years	
Life expectancy at birth	75 years	73 years	
Foreign direct investment	US$20 million	US$10 million	
Expenditure on research and development to GDP	3%	1%	
Rule of law index	Ranking: 12	Ranking: 48	
* The rule of law index ranking is higher if the country has a higher degree of rule of law.

(a)	Compare the per capita GNI (PPP) of the two countries.	(3 marks)
(b)	Which country has a higher Human Development Index (HDI)? Explain.
	(2 marks)
(c)	Which country has better prospects for economic growth? Provide THREE reasons to support your answer.	(4 marks)
(d)	Country C used to be a closed socialist economy. The leader of the country decides to open up the country in an attempt to increase its national income.
	Suggest THREE economic policies that the government of Country C can use to promote external trade.	(3 marks)
(e)	Other than the problem of unemployment, explain TWO possible costs of economic growth.	(4 marks)
questions.answerText:
(a)	Per capita GNI (PPP):
	Country A = US$80 billion ÷ 2 million = US$40,000	(1 mark)
	Country B = US$95 billion ÷ 3 million = US$31,666.67	(1 mark)
	Country A has a higher per capita GNI (PPP).	(1 mark)
(b)	Country A has a higher HDI because its per capita GNI (PPP) is higher; citizens in Country A have longer years of schooling on average; and life expectancy at birth is higher in the country. 	(2 marks)

(c)	Country A.	(1 mark)
	This is because:
(	the country has a more educated labour force;
(	longer life expectancy implies that people in Country A are in better health;
(	a larger proportion of its GDP is used for investment in research and development;
(	the country has a higher degree of rule of law. 
	(Any THREE of the above, 1 mark each.)
(d)	The government can: 
(	introduce favourable tax policies to attract foreign direct investment in the external trade sector;
(	develop infrastructure related to export and import activities. This can facilitate the flows of goods and people, and increase the volume of trade;
(	improve human capital in order to improve labour productivity. This can strengthen the competitiveness of domestic products;
(	promote research and development in order to strengthen the competitiveness of domestic products.
(Any THREE of the above, 1 mark each. Accept other reasonable answers.)
(e)	Possible costs of economic growth include:
(	Lower current consumption: When we accumulate capital, we give up current consumption for future consumption.
(	Uneven income distribution: Rapid economic growth may produce more uneven income distribution.
(	Economic instability: Foreign trade and investment are the major driving forces of economic growth. However, they may affect a country's economic stability (e.g., income and price stability).
(	Exhaustion of natural resources: A lot of natural resources used in production are exhaustible and may be used up one day. Economic growth may speed up the exhaustion of these resources.
(	Pollution and other environmental damage: Some production activities have harmful effects on the environment and people. As economic growth means more production activities and output, it can cause greater damage to the environment.
(Any TWO of the above or other reasonable answers with brief explanations, 
2 marks × 2 = 4 marks)
